# Independent repository reviews

This ledger covers 717 catalog-owned repository reviews. Evidence levels apply to each classification. Source review alone does not establish successful compilation or numerical verification. Specific local driver checks are identified explicitly; imported playground verification remains separate.

**License: Apache-2.0**

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `bab71767cb166ef878002b806c8360fe21307765`.

**C — documentation-reviewed**

The README describes circular loops and straight current segments; the pinned mod_cel interface documents a complete elliptic integral and excludes zero complementary parameter. Polygon/filament approximations are not exact arbitrary finite-width conductors. Floating-point error and asymptotic-accuracy claims were not independently checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `bab71767cb166ef878002b806c8360fe21307765`.

[abscab/mod_cel.f90](https://github.com/jonathanschilling/abscab-fortran/blob/bab71767cb166ef878002b806c8360fe21307765/abscab/mod_cel.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `3c14d5c4e63b892bd67479ca0b3fc8545bbc40c938b7d53dbfa1ac0c01ef84fb`.

**C14 — source-reviewed**

The public CEL function evaluates Bulirsch complete elliptic integral cel(kc,p,a,b) using a duplication iteration, transforming the p<=0 branch before iteration. The integral definition is explicitly given in source. This mapping covers the reusable special-function routine, not the domain-specific magnetic-field APIs or a claim of all elliptic-integral forms. Source finding: the kc=0 branch tests local B before assigning B_IN, so that branch reads undefined state; the declaration already requires nonzero kc. The loop has no explicit iteration limit/status output. Positive p and nonzero kc avoid the inspected singular-branch issue; the negative-p branch is not presented as an ordinary nonsingular integral.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `bab71767cb166ef878002b806c8360fe21307765`.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

bmdfsaneacc::dfsaneacc solves a square system: the residual callback maps x(n) to res(n), with no Jacobian callback. It combines residual-direction nonmonotone steps with QR-based sequential-secant acceleration built from iterate/residual history. Success requires dot_product(res,res)<=epsf**2, so epsf bounds the residual Euclidean norm; iteration exhaustion is a distinct return. F2 is already a GAMS leaf: there is no official derivative-free or acceleration child to add. Internal least-squares acceleration is not evidence for a general rectangular least-squares solver, and this does not enumerate all roots or certify uniqueness. The Fortran example supplies a three-variable exponential system; the reviewed Fortran path does not require running R or CUTEst. Memory/rank limits, singular cases and the author example were not tested.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `2e879f8b0baf7de75de8382e65d619b02bc5c7b6`.

Public module subroutine for square nonlinear systems. Supply n residuals for n REAL(KIND=8) unknowns through evalr; x is updated and res, iter, fcnt and istop are returned. epsf controls the residual 2-norm, ndiis the acceleration interval and nhlim the history capacity. pdataptr is optional.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dfsaneacc(evalr, n, x, res, epsf, maxit, ndiis, nhlim, &
               iter, fcnt, istop, pdataptr)
```

**L8h — source-reviewed**

The selected SUPSMU entry smooths ordered weighted observations with running local linear fits. Positive module SPAN selects the fixed-span path; zero invokes candidate spans, cross-validation residual smoothing and interpolated locally selected spans. It is an EDA smoother, not the complete ACE/AVAS transformation estimator. The sketch explicitly uses IPER=1 and fixed SPAN=0.5: the periodic branch in SMOOTH reads X(J) before correcting a negative wrapped index and needs repair/bounds checking before use. SUPSMU has no status output, divides by total weight for constant x and accesses quartile indices, so supply sufficiently many finite sorted data and positive total weights. Module control state is shared; no accuracy or smoothing-selection experiment was performed. SMOOTH also combines J<N with X(J+1)<=X(J) in a logical expression: Fortran does not guarantee short-circuit evaluation, so tied terminal abscissae can expose X(N+1). The sketch uses strictly increasing x; this is not a fix or bounds-safety proof.


**L10a2a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected real-data path zero-pads and transforms file columns, multiplies each spectrum by its conjugate, inverse-transforms and divides lag k by N-k. L10a2a1 records autocorrelation/autocovariance summaries. Values are not divided by lag-zero variance and therefore are not necessarily unit-normalized correlations. The default mean path sums the entire allocated capacity, including undefined unused tail entries; the sketch uses -nave and already-centered data. Contrary to README wording, oversized nacf is not clamped and can divide by zero or exceed valid sample ranges. Lag time is copied from the time column without checking uniform spacing. Complex paths/FFTW kernels are outside this review. No correlation was executed.

Link FFTW legacy Fortran entry points and supply fftw3.f. Enforce 1<=lag_count<=sample count yourself. Output index one is zero lag, so ten outputs cover lags 0 through 9, not 0 through 10.

Implementation helper `real_fft_2_acf`: [real.f90:1–92](https://github.com/lingtikong/ACFbyFFT/blob/bdfe202ffccd21aff3fdaaabbd482fb464f525c1/real.f90#L1-L92).

**L10b2a — source-reviewed**

The inspected real-data path zero-pads and transforms file columns, multiplies conjugate(first spectrum) by the second spectrum, inverse-transforms and divides lag k by N-k. L10b2a records two-series cross-correlation summary statistics. Values are not divided by lag-zero variance and therefore are not necessarily unit-normalized correlations. The default mean path sums the entire allocated capacity, including undefined unused tail entries; the sketch uses -nave and already-centered data. Contrary to README wording, oversized nacf is not clamped and can divide by zero or exceed valid sample ranges. Lag time is copied from the time column without checking uniform spacing. Complex paths/FFTW kernels are outside this review. No correlation was executed.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The ACRS interface accepts finite lower/upper bounds and an objective-value callback, with no gradient or Hessian callback. Its Price iteration randomly selects working-set points, computes a weighted centroid/reflection, projects onto the box and replaces a worse objective value. G2i describes this global nonconvex search; there is no finer GAMS subclass here. Bounds are restricted by implementation checks (lower bounds must exceed -1e6 and upper bounds must be below 1e16). Termination by objective spread, iteration count or CPU budget does not certify global optimality. The supplied acrs_main/FUNCT_ACRS example is a possible future driver starting point; it was not run.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed real adjac_double path records local first-derivative dependencies in module-wide tape arrays. Multiplication records the product rule through sum_taylor_a; get_dense_jacobian_a seeds dependent variables in blocks and traverses those dependencies backward to assemble Jacobian rows. adjac_set_independent seeds variable indices. This establishes operator-overloaded first differentiation, not higher derivatives or a numerical finite-difference method. The scoped review covers real variables and dense extraction; complex, sparse-COO, tapeless and FFT variants remain outside this source mapping. The shared storage and mode flag require coordinated lifecycle management and are not independently thread-local. Reset without product_mode preserves the previous mode. Fatal errors STOP rather than return status. No numerical derivative test was run.

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

Public TRAPECIO/SIMPSON generics dispatch to private precision-specific functions. The reviewed DP paths sort finite bounds, repeatedly halve trapezoid spacing (SIMPSON extrapolates (4*Tnew-Told)/3), stop on absolute change below EPS and restore reversed-bound signs. This is automatic finite-interval function quadrature, not a grid-only routine or general singular/infinite-interval guarantee. EPS defaults to 1e-2 and is an absolute successive-estimate test, not a rigorous error bound. MAXITER=26 is fixed; nonconvergence prints and STOPs the host process. Equal-zero estimates can cause early acceptance; no oscillatory-integrand or floating-point edge tests were run. Other Integration module algorithms and imported Linear routines remain outside this source review.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

setup forms segment slopes, extrapolated endpoint slopes and Akima weighted nodal slopes, then local cubic coefficients; interp selects an interval and evaluates its cubic. This establishes univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation. abs_smooth rounds the absolute-value weights when delta_x is positive, so that variant differs from unsmoothed Akima. The source assumes ordered distinct nodes and at least three points without checking them. Queries outside the data range continue the nearest end polynomial; this is not a reliable general extrapolation method. No shape-preservation, monotonicity or accuracy guarantee is inferred from the README, and no spline was run.

External evaluator returning values, argument derivatives and data sensitivities. All coefficient-sensitivity matrices are required, shaped (npt-1,npt); transpose the appropriate SETUP_DV direction blocks as the Python wrapper does. Output data sensitivities have shape (n,npt). Out-of-range queries use the nearest end polynomial.

```fortran
CALL interp(npt, n, x, xpt, p0, p1, p2, p3, dp0dxpt, dp1dxpt, dp2dxpt, dp3dxpt, dp0dypt, dp1dypt, dp2dypt, dp3dypt, y, dydx, dydxpt, dydypt)
```

External tangent-mode constructor specialized to the spline setup. Supply xptd and yptd as (nbdirs,n) seed arrays; each coefficient derivative is (nbdirs,n-1). Use positive delta_x for smooth data sensitivities. It is not a general differentiation engine for arbitrary user functions.


**H1 — source-reviewed**

The Tapenade-generated SETUP_DV propagates caller-supplied tangent directions through slope differences, smoothed Akima weights and cubic coefficients. interp then forms analytic derivatives with respect to the query argument and original abscissae/ordinates, including the derivative of the local coordinate. The Python wrapper seeds 2*n directions with identity/zero blocks and transposes their coefficient sensitivities. This mapping is differentiation of this particular interpolant, not a general-purpose AD package, finite-difference estimator or derivative of an unknown sampled function. delta_x is held fixed; its derivative is not computed. Positive smoothing is needed for the intended smooth data sensitivities. No derivative comparison was executed.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The reviewed UVIPIA general path (ND>=5) locates successive intervals, estimates endpoint derivatives from weighted neighboring three-point slope estimates, forms cubic coefficients for NP<=3 or higher-degree basis factors, and evaluates the corresponding interval polynomial. This supports univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation E1a, not a global polynomial, spline-system solve or smoothing fit. Ordered distinct XD is checked; invalid input prints a message and leaves YI at -9999 without a status argument. End extrapolation is linear, using endpoint slope estimates. The sketch uses NP=3 and ND=7; selecting larger NP does not establish higher-order derivative-estimate accuracy or shape preservation. Material findings: the general query loop unconditionally prints the OpenMP thread number and query index; the separate ND=4 cubic a3 formula repeats yuse(1) in its second term where the distinct second ordinate would be expected. That small-data branch requires checking/correction and is excluded from the sketch. No accuracy, small-data case or OpenMP execution was verified.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `67875afd0df120590a49e1ef3a3fc25b5b3eaab5`.

External REAL(KIND=8) interpolation subroutine. NP, ND and NI are default INTEGER, XD/YD have length ND and XI/YI length NI. XD must be strictly increasing; XI can be unordered. The inspected general path requires ND>=5. NP<3 is promoted to three. Compile/link with OpenMP support because omp_lib and omp_get_thread_num are used even apart from directive handling. There is no success/status output.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL uvipia(np, nd, xd, yd, ni, xi, yi)
```

Argument declarations: [src/uvipia_omp.f90:45–75](https://github.com/NRLMMD-GEOIPS/akima86/blob/67875afd0df120590a49e1ef3a3fc25b5b3eaab5/src/uvipia_omp.f90#L45-L75).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: uvipia
integer, parameter :: nd=7, ni=2
integer :: i
real(8) :: xd(nd), yd(nd), xi(ni), yi(ni)
xd=[(real(i-1,8),i=1,nd)]
yd=xd*xd
xi=[1.5d0,4.5d0]
call uvipia(3,nd,xd,yd,ni,xi,yi)
```

Uncompiled fragment for in-range queries and seven nodes. Expected quadratic values are 2.25 and 20.25, but no comparison was performed. Do not treat -9999 as an unambiguous failure status because it can also be a legitimate data value. The pinned general path writes per-query thread/index diagnostics. The four-node cubic branch has a source-formula discrepancy and is not demonstrated. There is no missing-data treatment or monotonicity/positivity guarantee established by this review.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The public DERIVATIVE generic selects private 1D/2D functions. The inspected 1D path computes centered differences with initial width one, halves the width and stops after at least five iterations when ABS(DNEW/DOLD-1)<ACC. It has a fixed 100-iteration maximum and STOPs on exhaustion. Arithmetic and callback use default REAL, not the separate precision module. Zero previous derivative estimates lead to division by zero, and a relative successive-estimate test is not a rigorous derivative error bound. The finite-difference path is numerical differentiation, not automatic differentiation or a review of the library integration/domain modules.

**D2e — source-reviewed**

The public real-double multilevel preconditioner type constructs an algebraic multilevel hierarchy and its level smoothers for a distributed PSBLAS sparse matrix. The build binding dispatches hierarchy_build followed by smoothers_build; init selects ML rather than the separate diagonal/block-Jacobi/Schwarz options. The associated apply implementation contains V/W/K cycle paths. This is a concrete associated linear-system operation, not a claim that build itself solves A*x=b or that a generic multigrid cycle is a particular Krylov method. MPI/PSBLAS context, assembled matrix/descriptor, level settings and optional coarse-solver configuration must already be consistent. INFO and the configured PSBLAS error policy govern failures; some policies terminate rather than returning. Review covers initialization, public binding/build dispatch and cycle entry documentation, not every smoother, coarse solver or parallel scaling claim.

**P — documentation-reviewed**

The README explicitly expands ANN as Approximate Nearest Neighbors, not artificial neural networks. The underlying algorithms/data structures are C++, with Fortran access provided here. Approximation guarantees, high-dimensional performance and current build compatibility were not checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `7ea83844834fa602ea3ed9a38b67c36998e44ace`.

[README](https://github.com/Box-Tools/ANN-Fortran/blob/7ea83844834fa602ea3ed9a38b67c36998e44ace/README)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `6d3a4e0cf880789f1d3288eabc947f0dd618d70d60fead2d84354fa00a6dcf39`.

**P — source-reviewed**

The Fortran ANN module forwards point-cloud construction and single-query k-nearest-neighbor search to the C++ ANN kd-tree. The bridge copies a Fortran point matrix with ROWS points and COLS coordinates using input offset I+J*ROWS; QUERY has DIM coordinates, compatible with the built tree. The backend uses EPS to relax search and returns zero-based point indices with squared Euclidean distances; EPS=0 selects exact search under the native algorithm. Require 1<=K<=ROWS and nonnegative EPS. Important reviewed defects prevent treating this as a ready-to-use ownership API: NNIDX/DISTS pointers are written into but never allocated by the bridge, so callers must supply live K-entry buffers; C++ temporary arrays are freed with scalar DELETE rather than matching array deallocation; the public Fortran destroy routine only nulls its handle, with its C destroy call commented out; construction point storage ownership is not released by that public path. The C destroy declaration also passes a pointer reference while the C++ definition takes a pointer value. Native search state uses file-scope globals, so independent concurrent search is not assumed. This is a mapping of the implemented kd-tree bridge with defects recorded, not a successful build, leak-free lifecycle, numerical verification or batch-query interface.

**C19 — source-reviewed**

The selected external HYP_2F1 and HYP_2F1_SUBROUTINE evaluate the Gauss (nonconfluent) hypergeometric function for complex parameters and argument. The driver selects transformed power expansions near zero, one or infinity, with a remaining complex-plane path. Real z>=1 is shifted to an infinitesimal negative imaginary part, explicitly choosing a side of the branch cut. Undefined denominator parameters call REXIT and there is no returned numerical-status/error-estimate argument. C19 is used because the GAMS C11 branch is specifically confluent hypergeometric functions; this is not that class. The selected wrapper/dispatch review does not validate every expansion, singular limit or the separate Appell F1 ODE path.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `f1bfd62382ad8d3e965eadd01ca60be83e66d399`.

**G1b1c — source-reviewed**

The arp::arp_solve path is unconstrained (zero general constraints, unbounded variable arrays) and evaluates user gradient and Hessian callbacks for p=2 or p=3, adding user third-derivative tensors for p=3. arp_model::model_evalf constructs a quadratic/cubic Taylor model with cubic/fourth-order regularization; model minimization delegates to bundled ALGENCAN. G1b1c is the most specific available GAMS class for the reviewed second-/third-order modes: there is no third-derivative child. This is not automatic differentiation, and the p=3 default needs more than the first and second derivatives named by the class. The sparse and dense fourth-order regularizers have different formulas in source; numerical equivalence is not asserted. The advertised p=1 mode, generic constrained problems, and all bundled ALGENCAN algorithms are outside this mapping. No optimizer or author MGH driver was executed.

Public module solver for unconstrained minimization. x is an assumed-shape REAL(KIND=dp) initial point overwritten by the result; param is an arp_param and output an arp_output. The mapped p=2/3 paths require gradient and Hessian callbacks; p=3 additionally requires third derivatives. Model minimization delegates to ALGENCAN.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL arp_solve(x, param, output)
```

**D4a4 — source-reviewed**

The adapted local ZNAUPD implements implicitly restarted Arnoldi reverse communication for a few eigenpairs of a general complex operator. The selected standard mode uses OP=A and B=identity; requests for operator products are returned through IDO and WORKD offsets, followed by ZNEUPD Ritz-value/vector extraction. This is complex non-Hermitian ordinary eigenproblem scope D4a4, not a dense all-eigenpair routine or a claim that every operator is sparse. N, NEV, NCV and work sizes must satisfy the documented bounds; initialization and every requested operation must be handled. This rewrite gives V and IPNTR INTENT(OUT) in ZNAUPD although Arnoldi basis/state and pointer information must survive reverse-communication reentry. Those attributes need inspection/repair before relying on standard-conforming persistence; preserving caller arrays alone does not repair their undefined-on-entry semantics. Saved locals/debug/stat modules also prevent assuming independent concurrent solves. Review covers the adapted driver/state dispatch and extraction interface, not upstream ARPACK validation or the parallel variant. ZNEUPD also declares IPNTR INTENT(OUT) while consuming saved pointer offsets; its extraction contract needs the same persistence review.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `b3d655207d2e8caebcb09f0eb2d90397a81e66f4`.

**A3c — source-reviewed**

The public MP_REAL type and arithmetic operator extensions expose multiword extended-precision real arithmetic from Fortran. MPINIT configures precision/constants, the plus generic dispatches MP_REAL addition, and the native Fortran wrapper passes the component representation through the F_MPADD C++ bridge. This is a binding over the ARPREC arithmetic implementation, not an intrinsic compiler REAL kind, interval arithmetic or a standalone all-Fortran library. The reviewed module has a fixed maximum digit capacity (MPIPL=2000) and runtime working precision must fit the compiled storage; every module/backend must agree on the representation and ABI. Decimal text assignment avoids losing decimal input precision in a machine-real literal before conversion. Global precision/error settings require care around mixed-precision and concurrent calls. Review follows selected addition/conversion and initialization interfaces, not all operator variants or a proof of correctly rounded results.

**H2a2a1 — source-reviewed**

The supplied QUADTS component integrates a callback on a finite interval using tanh-sinh abscissas/weights, nested refinements and an estimated-error stopping test. Its open-interval evaluations support the demonstrated integrable endpoint singularities; arbitrary interior singularities and unevaluated infinite-interval transformations are not assumed. INITQTS precomputes tables with lower bound -1 and metadata in negative-index slots. QUADTS returns MP_REAL but accepts MP_REALX interval bounds/callback arguments and switches global working precision between primary and secondary word counts. The shared QUADGLOBAL state must be configured consistently with both module capacities and table sizes. Reaching the maximum level or insufficient secondary precision can print a warning and return an approximation without a nonzero NERROR; NERROR=0 is therefore not an accuracy certificate. Review covers table generation, callback/refinement and stopping logic from the supplied demonstration, not a production library packaging claim or a rigorous quadrature error bound.

```fortran
! X1/X2 use MP_REALX; WK/XK use MP_REAL with bounds -1:NQ2.
! Extract/link the selected quadrature components with their matching helpers.
nerror=0
call initqts(nq1,nq2,wk,xk)
if(nerror/=0) error stop "quadrature table initialization failed"
result=quadts(fun07,x1,x2,nq1,nq2,wk,xk)
! FUN07 is the supplied endpoint-singular example on [0,1].
! Inspect warnings and repeat with greater level/precision; NERROR=0 is insufficient.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-configuration component fragment, not a standalone driver. The supplied file also contains the demonstration F_MAIN and callbacks; integrate the selected components without conflicting application entry points and initialize bounds for the chosen integrand. No integral, error estimate, precision scaling or endpoint evaluation was run.

**L15 — source-reviewed**

PLESTM forms a product-limit survival estimator from sorted uncensored/censored arrays, accumulates pointwise standard-error terms, and computes a mean and its error. The implementation first converts largest censored observations to detections until the tail is uncensored, mutating U, NU and NC and reporting ICHANGE/NCHANGE. This is an explicit tail convention, not an assumption-free estimate of an unidentified unrestricted mean. NTOT-sized arrays need spare space for moved observations; all-censored input is unsafe because U(NU) is read before NU is checked. Tied/small samples also expose loops reading U(I+K) before a bound test, and Fortran does not guarantee short-circuit evaluation. No recoverable status output certifies valid inputs. Higher-level ASURV wrappers handle censoring direction/data transformation separately. Review covers the product-limit implementation and tail conventions, not the complete interactive package or validation of survival inference.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `c2b1e0d5405507c958a605aca4c7f8e58a8c69a4`.


```fortran
external :: PLESTM

call PLESTM(u,c,nu,nc,s,v,ntot,mean,mean_error,ichange,nchange,ranks)
! Check ICHANGE/NCHANGE before interpreting a mean based on tail conversions.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. A post-validation interface fragment, not a statistically checked survival example. Censoring direction must match the higher-level ASURV transformations. Repair/validate all-censored, tied-tail and small-sample bounds before use. No survival curve, mean or standard error was tested.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed FG_t branch stores a REAL64 value and an allocatable gradient vector. Its ordinary product overload propagates the product rule for operands using the same independent-variable basis; addition adds their gradient vectors. Unit-vector seeds therefore propagate a first gradient without finite-difference step sizes. H1 is the differentiation leaf. This review covers the same-basis product/addition and assignment paths, not all intrinsic overloads, the distinct concatenating .mul. operator, or the separate Hessian/Laplacian modules. Both operands need allocated, conformable seed vectors; no shape/domain/status validation is supplied. No derivative, example optimizer or numerical comparison was executed.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

AUTO is an initialized continuation application, not a drop-in stateless equation solver. Its framework supplies AUTOPARAMETERS, active parameter indices, weights, callbacks, restart/start data, output units and configured MPI state; prefer its supported run/CLUI workflow for ordinary use. Direct-call sketches below are post-framework-initialization contracts only. AE::AUTOAE controls continuation of real nonlinear algebraic systems through CNRLAE and SOLVAE. The corrector forms a bordered system from FUNI values/Jacobians and the continuation constraint, solves it with pivoted GEL, and tests relative parameter/state corrections against EPSL/EPSU within ITNW iterations. A failed corrector restores the old state and returns NIT=0 internally; AUTOAE itself has no scalar success dummy or returned solution array, since state and files are managed by the framework. The interface takes internal FUNI/STPNAEI/FNCI callbacks from interfaces.h, not the shorter user FUNC signature. Non-root ranks return immediately on this algebraic path. This mapping covers real nonlinear-system continuation and its Newton corrector, not a guarantee of finding every root, branch, bifurcation or global solution.

**I1b2 — source-reviewed**

AUTO is an initialized continuation application, not a drop-in stateless equation solver. Its framework supplies AUTOPARAMETERS, active parameter indices, weights, callbacks, restart/start data, output units and configured MPI state; prefer its supported run/CLUI workflow for ordinary use. Direct-call sketches below are post-framework-initialization contracts only. BVP::AUTOBV dispatches to general nonlinear ODE boundary-value continuation. NEWTONBV forms predictor states and repeatedly calls SOLVBV for collocation linearizations, using parameter and state correction tolerances with configured Newton/chord refresh and iteration limits. SOLVBV constructs interpolation/derivative weights and divides derivative weights by each mesh interval length before building the equation blocks. The driver accepts boundary and integral-condition callbacks, starting/restart data and test functions through the explicit internal interfaces; satisfying the dimension/free-parameter/condition balance is the framework setup responsibility. Mesh values are normalized to the AUTO interval and physical period/scale enters through the problem formulation. No direct INFO/result-array dummy is provided by AUTOBV, and continuation stopping or small corrections do not replace an independent differential/boundary residual check. Periodic-orbit and bifurcation specialties require their own problem setup and are not certified by this general BVP entry review.

**I1c — source-reviewed**

MESH::ADAPT2 is a public service routine for retabulating AUTO solution/tangent data while changing the number of mesh intervals and/or collocation points. NEWMSH equidistributes a monitor based on differences of high-order derivative estimates; INTERP uses local Lagrange weights to transfer both UPSR and VPSR. If old and new counts agree it copies rather than adapts the mesh. Use positive strictly increasing interval meshes, at least two old intervals on the selected nonperiodic path, supported collocation orders 2..7, adequate zero-based sample storage and NDIM=NDOLD in the selected sketch. When dimensions differ only MIN(NDIM,NDOLD) components are assigned, so added components remain undefined. IPER selects periodic versus extrapolated endpoint monitor treatment, not a general interpolation extrapolation policy. No status or verified error bound is returned; the monitor and interpolation do not prove ODE/BVP solution accuracy. ADAPT2 is selected instead of ADAPT to avoid conflating this serial retabulation interface with the latter distributed scatter protocol.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

MESH::INTWTS forms Lagrange cardinal weights for nodes numbered 0..N. The caller evaluates the interpolating polynomial by a dot product of WTS with N+1 nodal samples; DT1DT is expressed in node-index units, not normalized physical coordinates. For an interval [a,a+h] sampled at a+j*h/N, pass N*(x-a)/h. The public GENWTS companion generates value/derivative weights at fixed collocation points, while private INTERP demonstrates actual piecewise sample transfer using INTWTS. Restrict N to the small supported AUTO collocation orders (2..7 in the sketch): the integer factorial/product denominators are not overflow guarded and arbitrary high degree is unsafe. There is no barycentric stabilization, shape preservation, conditioning estimate or status output. This mapping is polynomial interpolation of already sampled values, not fitting noisy data or selecting an adaptive degree.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

MESH::GENWTS constructs both value weights WT and first-derivative weights WP of the polynomial through NCOL+1 equally spaced samples on the normalized interval [0,1], evaluated at NCOL interior Gauss-Legendre collocation points. The caller obtains derivatives by DOT_PRODUCT(WP(:,IC),VALUES); physical interval width h requires division by h, as shown in SOLVBV. This is numerical differentiation of sampled data through the interpolating polynomial, not automatic/symbolic differentiation of a user routine. Use NCOL in 2..7 and arrays with first index 0:NCOL. Unsupported orders are not rejected: the private CPNTS SELECT CASE has no default and leaves collocation nodes undefined. No accuracy, noise sensitivity or error estimate is returned. Integer products are safe for the selected small orders only; avoid extending the order contract based on the explicit-shape signature alone.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

MESH::WINT returns fixed closed Newton-Cotes integration weights for NCOL+1 equally spaced values on [0,1], with hardcoded orders NCOL=2..7. The caller supplies the grid samples and forms their weighted sum, multiplying by physical interval width h; a composite rule sums those panel contributions. NCOL=2 gives the three-point Simpson weights. This is nonautomatic quadrature of grid data, not an adaptive integrand-callback driver or Gauss-Legendre quadrature merely because other routines in this module use Gauss collocation points. WINT has no default case or status: unsupported NCOL leaves WI undefined. No error estimator, tolerance control, singularity treatment or irregular-grid support is supplied; physical scaling and adequate smoothness must be assessed by the caller.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected scalar reverse-mode path builds pointer-linked nodes with local product/addition/exponential derivatives. tree_t%backward seeds the output adjoint to one, then recursively distributes local-derivative products; shared input nodes accumulate contributions. get_grad reads the stored scalar adjoint. H1 describes this reverse differentiation path rather than a finite-difference approximation. Repeated backward calls do not clear reachable gradients, and there is no reviewed zero-grad operation. Real assignment allocates a new node without releasing the old one; destructors recurse/nullify links without deallocating the node targets. Copy ownership, repeated graph reuse and cleanup therefore need validation. The configured rk is REAL32, despite some printed double-looking example output. No graph or gradient was executed.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected src/avd.f90 implementation propagates derivatives through overloaded products and elementary-function composition. The avd_d4 inheritance chain stores a value and first through fourth raw derivatives with respect to one scalar parameter; the product and Q4_f chain rules contain the corresponding binomial/composition coefficients. This is forward differentiation, not finite differencing or symbolic expression manipulation. CALL init() must populate the module function-pointer table before elementary functions are used. H1 is the differentiation leaf; there is no finer automatic-differentiation child in this taxonomy. The review covers the fourth-order product/exponential path, not every overload or the older root autodiff.f90 implementation. Source requests an eight-byte default REAL build; module and caller settings must agree. No author tests or derivative comparisons were executed.

**M1b — source-reviewed**

BAM_FIT constructs a packed initial inference vector and proposal scales from already loaded model/data/prior state, then forwards the model posterior callback to the external ADAPTIVE_METRO_OAAT sampler. This is adaptive one-at-a-time Metropolis posterior simulation through a framework entry point, not a standalone arbitrary-density sampler or proof of posterior convergence. The reviewed wrapper validates top-level parameter/remnant-vector sizes against private INFER state, obtains headers/derived-parameter storage and passes adaptation/cycle/move-rate/scale controls and output/monitor file names through. Build and initialize the full BaM, BMSL and miniDMSL dependencies with matching MRK/MIK kinds and valid priors/likelihood/model configurations; INFER is module-global and independent concurrent contexts are not assumed. ERR>0 is an error, ERR<0 a warning and MESS provides context. Samples go to named files. M1b records continuous-parameter Markov-chain simulation; this source review covers the entry, packing/dispatch and status contract, not the external proposal acceptance/adaptation kernels, chain diagnostics, detailed balance or effective sample size.

**L13a — source-reviewed**

The public update_factor_normal component draws latent Gaussian factor scores conditional on the supplied loadings, dedicated-factor assignments, idiosyncratic precisions and factor covariance distribution. It adds loading-weighted diagonal contributions to the factor precision, inverts this precision, forms the conditional mean and adds a Cholesky-transformed normal draw. This is a factor-analysis component, not a complete Bayesian fit or evidence that one draw constitutes a converged posterior analysis. DEDIC values must lie in 0..NFAC, with zero denoting an inactive measurement; precisions and covariance must be valid. The module uses the package MT19937-64-based probability generator, while matrix failures call R error helpers and inversion uses LAPACK. Consequently this is not a standalone standard-library routine or a routine governed by R RNG state alone. Review covers this conditional update and its constructors/numerical dependencies; it does not assert that this particular type is the full BEFA driver path.

**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

The public bddcml_solve method selector 0 dispatches to preconditioned conjugate gradients for SPD systems using the multilevel BDDC preconditioner. The native Krylov module applies level preconditioning and distributed matrix/vector operations; this is not a classification inferred solely from an external sparse factorization dependency. Initialize MPI, upload the global or subdomain FEM problem and construct the preconditioner with a compatible matrix type first. A direct-only level configuration overrides the selected iterative method with a direct solve, so the mapping requires an iterative configuration. CONVERGED_REASON=0 means the relative-residual criterion was met, -1 means the iteration limit and -2 the nondecreasing-residual limit. Solution values remain in internal state until downloaded. The condition-number estimate belongs to the PCG path and is not an independent conditioning/accuracy guarantee. Shared level/Krylov state and MPI collectives require consistent calls across participating ranks. Review covers public dispatch and selected recurrence/preconditioner paths, not every mesh decomposition, singular problem or scalability case.

**J — source-reviewed**

HankelJ0Transform/HankelJ1Transform evaluate fixed logarithmic digital-filter sums of a kernel callback at lambda_i=10**(a+(i-1)*s)/r, then divide the weighted sum by r. Fast variants use shorter tables. J records numerical Hankel integral transforms; the original GAMS J subtree has no dedicated Hankel child, so neither Fourier nor Laplace classification is invented. The exact convention is integral_0^infinity K(lambda)*J_order(r*lambda) d(lambda), without an additional lambda measure factor. Callers using the common lambda*d(lambda) convention must incorporate lambda into K. R must be positive and finite, with a kernel defined over the sampled positive range; extreme R can overflow/underflow sampling. No error estimate, convergence status or adaptive quadrature is returned. Ogata/Bessel-zero paths are not included in this digital-filter review. No transform or published example was run.

**C10a3 — source-reviewed**

bessel_eval accepts nonnegative real order up to 1e9 and positive real argument, dispatching J_nu/Y_nu evaluation among tabulated expansions, small-argument series and asymptotic routines. In the inspected table path, bivariate Chebyshev coefficients represent phase/phase derivative in the oscillatory region or log magnitudes in the nonoscillatory region; values are recovered by trigonometric/exponential formulas. C10a3 is the real-argument, real-order cylindrical Bessel scope, not complex-argument or modified Bessel functions. Call bessel_eval_init first; it reads fixed relative binary filenames into shared module state using unit 20. Repeated init returns without assigning DSIZE. Missing tables or invalid parameter ranges STOP rather than return an error; binary layout, real-kind promotion and endianness must match. Auxiliary phase/log outputs are branch-dependent and initially zero, not universally valid derivatives/logarithms. No accuracy, binary-portability or advertised timing result was tested; series/asymptotic coefficient derivations were not fully audited.

**L6b3 — source-reviewed**

DRAW_JU generates correlation-matrix draws using sequential beta-distributed partial correlations and the Joe construction. The output stores the strict lower-triangle correlations in row-by-row order (2,1),(3,1),(3,2),(4,1),(4,2),(4,3),..., with unit diagonal implicit; NUMCORRGROUP must equal P*(P-1)/2. FISHER=1 transforms each correlation with atanh. Internal RANDOM_BETA draws from the R UNIF_RAND stream, so a running/initialized R runtime and GetRNGstate/PutRNGstate lifecycle are required. FINDINV uses LAPACK LU/inversion on intermediate correlation blocks, but its ERROR1 output is not checked by the caller, and no status is returned to users for invalid dimensions, roundoff-induced square-root failure or extreme Fisher transforms. This maps the concrete random-correlation generator, not all Bayes-factor hypotheses supported by the R package. Review covers the selected full generator and its contained numerical helpers.

The selected DRGLG entry performs unconstrained NL2SOL-like iterations for an objective composed from model values R and their first derivatives DR, dispatching to DG7LIT_M and QR/curvature-update machinery. In this R-package revision the linked RHO is specifically weighted/unweighted negative log probability, with derivatives -1/R and 1/R**2; it is not a freely supplied RHO callback argument or arbitrary least-squares objective by default. The caller supplies model values/Jacobians at reverse-communication requests and must interpret IV(1) according to the package protocol, including diagnostic requests. Require positive finite model probabilities and valid initialized work/state arrays. The BIND(C) interface passes LRHOI/LRHOR by VALUE while most scalars are by reference: an explicit matching interface is essential. This is driver dispatch/source structure, not a full audit of all trust-region, covariance or diagnostic kernels or a maximum-likelihood accuracy check.

**D2a4 — source-reviewed**

SOLVERS_BASE dispatches real sparse square linear systems in one-based CSR storage to BCGSTAB or unrestarted GMRES. ITOL=1 compares relative residual to the RHS norm, while ITOL=2 uses an absolute norm. X is both the starting guess and returned approximation; ITER is not a comprehensive success status. The BCGSTAB path has no visible denominator/breakdown or early-small-S safeguard. GMRES divides by the initial residual and Arnoldi subdiagonal without happy-breakdown handling, forms a Hessenberg inverse rather than a triangular backsolve, and can use ITER=ITMAX+1 in array slices after loop exhaustion. These limitations prevent treating the calling sketch as a checked solver example. **D4a1 — source-reviewed**

DBLZDRV standard symmetric mode requests A*U by reverse communication, then orchestrates block-Lanczos recurrence, orthogonality control and projected-eigenproblem convergence dispatch. The inspected DBLZSTP controls recurrence/reorthogonalization helper calls, stores basis/projected coefficients and schedules Ritz evaluation/restarts; this is driver/step-control review, not a complete kernel or convergence proof. D4a1 covers real symmetric ordinary problems. The interface is matrix-free and can accept sparse products, but no particular sparse storage format is claimed. Initialize control/work arrays according to documented dimensions before LFLAG=0; service every positive request with NVOPU columns and reenter with the same flag. LFLAG=0 after a call is normal completion, negative is abnormal/early; partial eigenpairs and work-array warning/error reports require inspection. Workspace sizing includes control prefixes, and low memory can create temporary files. No eigenpairs, inertia or residuals were checked by execution.

External double-precision block-Lanczos reverse-communication driver. ISTOR holds integer controls/work, RSTOR real controls/work, U/V blocks, EIG(LEIG,2) eigenvalue data and X(LNI,LEIG) vectors. SIGMA/NNEIG carry shift/inertia; LFLAG and NVOPU control caller operations.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DBLZDRV(ISTOR, RSTOR, SIGMA, NNEIG, U, V, LFLAG, NVOPU, EIG, X)
```

DBLZDRV generalized symmetric mode uses reverse-communication products with B and shifted solves (A-SIGMA*B)*V=B*U, with caller factorization/inertia information on flag 3. Initialize control/work arrays according to documented dimensions before LFLAG=0; service every positive request with NVOPU columns and reenter with the same flag. LFLAG=0 after a call is normal completion, negative is abnormal/early; partial eigenpairs and work-array warning/error reports require inspection. Workspace sizing includes control prefixes, and low memory can create temporary files. No eigenpairs, inertia or residuals were checked by execution.

**L4a1b2 — source-reviewed**

KDE estimates a univariate density by averaging scaled kernels at (u-X(i))/h and dividing by n*h. The inspected default Gaussian kernel uses the ordinary normal-density formula; uniform, triangular and other compact kernels are also dispatched. If H is omitted, the routine requests empirical standard deviation and applies the 1.06*std*n^(-1/5) bandwidth rule. Nonpositive bandwidth is rejected, but empty samples, NaN inputs and boundary bias are not comprehensively handled. The sketch supplies a positive bandwidth and nonempty finite sample. ERR/MESS distinguish fatal errors and warnings; no bandwidth choice, normalization or statistical optimality is certified. Review covers the public wrapper and kernel dispatch rather than the full statistics library.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `97c70294fd4bb01219da5e7a2e0f9a6cf1ede2f3`.

**L13b — source-reviewed**

PCA optionally centers/scales observation-row data, decomposes a cross-product covariance matrix or a transposed-data SVD, and returns eigenvalues, retained eigenvectors, projections and centering/scaling metadata in PCATYPE. X is overwritten when transformations are requested. STANDARD uses X-transpose*X/N whereas SVD scales by sqrt(N-1), so reported variances differ between these branches; they should not be treated as numerically identical implementations. A fixed absolute 1e-6 threshold defines numerical rank (on eigenvalues or singular values respectively), and NDim defaults to four. Zero-variance scaling and rank-deficient/boundary cases need validation. The selected sketch uses centering, no scaling and STANDARD with NDim=1. Review covers preprocessing/decomposition dispatch/projection, not the external DMSL eigensolver/SVD kernels, kernel PCA or a verified reconstruction.

**D2b1b — source-reviewed**

The external CHOLESKY_FACTOR routine overwrites the lower triangle of a dense real matrix with a Cholesky factor by square-rooting pivots, scaling the column and applying rank-one trailing updates. The upper triangle is left as original input. This is the real symmetric positive-definite factorization scope, not a complete solve. The declared INTENT(OUT) ERROR is never assigned; it is undefined on return and cannot report failure. There is no positive-pivot/symmetry/size validation, so indefinite or zero-pivot inputs can produce invalid arithmetic and N=0 still references A(N,N). No numerical factorization or failure was reproduced; the catalog records an educational implementation with these limitations.

**I2b1a1 — source-reviewed**

LBFMM2D wraps the legacy eighth-order adaptive box-code volume-potential solver for a two-dimensional free-space Poisson problem. This is a volume-potential tool with the library kernel normalization, not an arbitrary prescribed-boundary-value interface; the mapping stays at the Poisson/Laplace class without selecting a rectangular Dirichlet/Neumann subclass. Input is a level-restricted quadtree and density values on each leaf box 8-by-8 Chebyshev grid; the active wrapper loops over ND density components and dispatches FMMSTART8_WRAP. The latter hardcodes IPERIOD=0 and allocates/maps legacy FMM tables/workspace. Require NORDER=8, NPBOX=64, IPERIOD=0, positive box counts and a valid tree. The wrapper does not enforce its apparent NORDER/IPERIOD parameters, and TIMEINFO is never assigned; do not infer timing/status outputs from its dummy list. Source-declared IPTR(8) is default INTEGER despite the header calling it INTEGER(8); the converter also contains explicit INTEGER*4 data, so use the compatible default-four-byte integer build rather than blindly promoting all integers. FVALS/POT actually have rank three (ND,NPBOX,NBOXES), unlike the rank-two prose summary. Centers/sizes are normalized by BOXSize(0) without a visible final physical potential rescaling: the selected fragment requires a unit-side root and leaves general physical scaling to separate verification. Only leaf potential entries are within the documented output scope. Review covers wrapper shapes, tree conversion and core dispatch; the author legacy core test is linked as usage context but has not been compiled or run for this catalog, nor has the modern wrapper, near-field behavior or all FMM kernels. The legacy core wrapper reserves 64000*NBOXES entries in each real and integer workspace; check memory capacity and default-integer size arithmetic before using large trees.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

CHEBEXPS with ITYPE=1 constructs Chebyshev-root nodes in ascending order on [-1,1] and weights for unweighted interpolatory quadrature. The degree recurrence accumulates even-Chebyshev moments into the weights, which the caller applies to sampled integrand values. This is fixed-order quadrature for grid data (H2a1b2), not an adaptive callback integrator or the weighted Gauss-Chebyshev measure dx/sqrt(1-x**2). Match REAL*8 arrays and default INTEGER arguments with the selected legacy GNU build, provide X/WHTS length N and U/V(N,N) buffers, and choose N>=2 for the selected contract. ITYPE=1 leaves U/V unassigned; only node/weight outputs are used. There is no status or accuracy-estimate output. The original routine and companion source use length-one dummy arrays for larger actual storage; the unmodified legacy object was compiled without bounds instrumentation, while the catalog main program used bounds checks. No claim of modern Fortran conformance or full-file memory safety follows from the numerical checks. A complete driver verifies all monomial moments through degree N-1 for N=2,4,8,16, plus node ordering, interval membership and positive weights. All 30 moments passed absolute tolerance 2e-13; maximum error was 1.7347e-16. Transform-matrix mode ITYPE=2 and the Poisson wrapper retain separate unverified scopes.

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
! GAMS H2a1b2. Unweighted polynomial quadrature on [-1,1].
program check_cheb_quadrature
  implicit none
  interface
    subroutine chebexps(itype,n,x,u,v,w)
      integer :: itype,n
      real(kind=8) :: x(*),u(n,n),v(n,n),w(*)
    end subroutine
  end interface
  integer,parameter :: orders(4)=[2,4,8,16]
  real(kind=8),allocatable :: x(:),w(:),u(:,:),v(:,:)
  real(kind=8) :: exact,error,maxerr
  integer :: n,i,k,cases
  cases=0; maxerr=0d0
  do i=1,size(orders)
    n=orders(i)
    allocate(x(n),w(n),u(n,n),v(n,n))
    call chebexps(1,n,x,u,v,w)
    if(.not.all(x(2:n)>x(1:n-1)))error stop 'nodes not ascending'
    if(.not.all(abs(x)<1d0))error stop 'nodes outside open interval'
    if(.not.all(w>0d0))error stop 'weights not positive'
    do k=0,n-1
      exact=0d0
      if(mod(k,2)==0)exact=2d0/real(k+1,8)
      error=abs(sum(w*x**k)-exact)
      if(.not.(error<2d-13))error stop 'unweighted polynomial moment failed'
      maxerr=max(maxerr,error); cases=cases+1
    enddo
    deallocate(x,w,u,v)
  enddo
  print '(a,i0)','Polynomial moments checked: ',cases
  print '(a,es12.4)','Maximum absolute moment error: ',maxerr
  print '(a)','PASS Chebyshev-node quadrature: 30 moments and node/weight checks'
end program check_cheb_quadrature
```

Complete main program compiled and run locally on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), 2026-11-06. The unmodified upstream object used -O0 -g -std=legacy -ffixed-line-length-none -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow, with no bounds instrumentation because of its legacy length-one dummy declarations. The binary64 main program used -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow. Thirty unweighted polynomial moments and node/weight checks passed; maximum absolute moment error was 1.7347e-16. Both per-source flag sets and all compiler warnings are saved under drivers/boxcode-quadrature/. This result does not verify companion routines or the separate Poisson solver.

**E3c — source-reviewed**

With ITYPE=2, CHEBEXPS constructs U mapping values at N ascending Chebyshev-root nodes to N ordinary Chebyshev-series coefficients, and V mapping coefficients back to nodal values. This is a dense basis change, not an FFT or a monomial-basis conversion. Tests use each T_k(x)=cos(k*acos(x)), k=0,...,N-1, to check that U returns the corresponding unit coefficient vector and V reconstructs its independently evaluated values. For N=2,4,8,16 all 60 coefficient/value cases passed, with maximum normalized error 3.275158e-15. Use default INTEGER and REAL*8 arrays with a compatible ABI, N>=2 and Chebyshev-root nodes on [-1,1]. There is no status or error-estimate result. The upstream source uses legacy length-one dummy arrays and internal work-array remapping; several helper declarations are smaller than the scratch regions actually used. The unmodified legacy object was compiled without bounds instrumentation, while each catalog main program retained bounds checks and floating-point traps. The numerical results do not certify modern Fortran conformance, full-file memory safety or every companion routine. The source is linked and downloaded at a pinned hash, not redistributed here; its existing scoped license absence finding remains. The complete catalog driver was compiled and run on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental); tolerance was 2e-11 for these finite tests.

```fortran
! Catalog-owned analytic checks of GAMS E3c using CHEBEXPS.
! Upstream source is downloaded at a pinned revision; it is not bundled here.
program basis
 use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 implicit none
 integer :: n,k,j,count
 real(real64), allocatable :: x(:),weights(:),u(:,:),v(:,:),a(:,:),d(:,:),w(:),ending(:),values(:),want(:),got(:)
 real(real64) :: error,maximum,endpoint
 real(real64), parameter :: tolerance=2.e-11_real64
 external :: chebexps,chebinmt
 maximum=0
 count=0
 do j=1,4
   n=2**j
   allocate(x(n),weights(n),u(n,n),v(n,n),a(n,n),d(n,n),w(3*n*n+2*n+50), &
      ending(n),values(n),want(n),got(n))
   call chebexps(2,n,x,u,v,weights)
   do k=0,n-1
     values=cos(real(k,real64)*acos(x))
     got=matmul(u,values)
     want=0;want(k+1)=1
     call verify()
     got=matmul(v,want)
     want=values
     call verify()
   end do
   deallocate(x,weights,u,v,a,d,w,ending,values,want,got)
 end do
 print '(a,i0)', 'Checked polynomial cases: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS basis'
contains
 subroutine verify()
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(got))) error stop 'nonfinite result'
   error=maxval(abs(got-want))/max(1._real64,maxval(abs(want)))

 end subroutine
end program
```

**E3a2 — source-reviewed**

With ITYPE=2, CHEBINMT constructs ADIFF so MATMUL(ADIFF,F) gives the derivatives of the degree-at-most-N-1 interpolating polynomial at the N Chebyshev-root nodes. Allocate ADIFF(N,N), AINTE(N,N), X/WHTS/ENDINTER(N) and W(3*N*N+2*N+50); AINTE is unassigned in this mode and must not be read. ENDINTER maps nodal values to the interpolating polynomial at x=1, outside the open set of root nodes. The helper transforms values to coefficients, differentiates the expansion and transforms back. The driver checks all monomial derivatives through degree N-1 for N=2,4,8,16 and independently checks endpoint evaluation against 1. All 30 derivative cases and 30 endpoint checks passed; maximum normalized derivative error was 8.668621e-13. Use default INTEGER and REAL*8 arrays with a compatible ABI, N>=2 and Chebyshev-root nodes on [-1,1]. There is no status or error-estimate result. The upstream source uses legacy length-one dummy arrays and internal work-array remapping; several helper declarations are smaller than the scratch regions actually used. The unmodified legacy object was compiled without bounds instrumentation, while each catalog main program retained bounds checks and floating-point traps. The numerical results do not certify modern Fortran conformance, full-file memory safety or every companion routine. The source is linked and downloaded at a pinned hash, not redistributed here; its existing scoped license absence finding remains. The complete catalog driver was compiled and run on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental); tolerance was 2e-11 for these finite tests.

```fortran
program derivative

 implicit none
```

**E3a3 — source-reviewed**

With ITYPE=1, CHEBINMT constructs AINTE so MATMUL(AINTE,F) gives the integrated polynomial representation at each Chebyshev-root node, with lower-limit convention -1 in the selected checked regime. Allocate AINTE(N,N), ADIFF(N,N), X/WHTS/ENDINTER(N) and W(3*N*N+2*N+50); ADIFF is unassigned in this mode and must not be read. Integration raises the polynomial degree, but the nodal matrix retains only N coefficients; the omitted higher coefficient can affect data with degree N-1. The checked contract therefore restricts input polynomials to degree at most N-2, and does not claim exact integration of the highest interpolating degree or arbitrary-data error bounds. The driver compares against (x**(k+1)-(-1)**(k+1))/(k+1) for k=0,...,N-2 at N=2,4,8,16. All 26 polynomial cases passed, with maximum normalized error 4.451610e-16. This is integration of a fitted polynomial, not adaptive callback quadrature. Use default INTEGER and REAL*8 arrays with a compatible ABI, N>=2 and Chebyshev-root nodes on [-1,1]. There is no status or error-estimate result. The upstream source uses legacy length-one dummy arrays and internal work-array remapping; several helper declarations are smaller than the scratch regions actually used. The unmodified legacy object was compiled without bounds instrumentation, while each catalog main program retained bounds checks and floating-point traps. The numerical results do not certify modern Fortran conformance, full-file memory safety or every companion routine. **D2a1 — source-reviewed**

These are precision-generated Fortran APIs: the pinned template names are transformed by PrecisionPreprocessing.sh into d_ (DAT=1, REAL(8)) or z_ (DAT=0, COMPLEX(8)) module/procedure/type names. Use the matching generated module files, data kinds and BLAS/LAPACK/MPI ABI; template DT is not a Fortran type. Initialize the configured MPI environment or library MPI dummy layer, process tree, options, statistics, mesh/permutation and compressed matrix collectively before these calls. Local vectors must follow the constructed distributed ordering; undo the permutation for results in original coordinates. The selected real general square-system path sets OPTION%PRECON=DIRECT, factors a constructed HODLR, HMAT/BLR or HSS representation, then applies its stored inverse/factors to multiple right-hand sides. No symmetry or Hermitian property is required by this selected general interface. BPACK_Solution dispatches DIRECT to BPACK_Inv_Mult; other PRECON values invoke an iterative route whose local error/iteration diagnostics are not exposed as output arguments here. The factorization and solve are relative to a compressed approximation: rank tolerances and conditioning affect error, and this is not an exact uncompressed LU guarantee or a sparse-storage solver merely because the representation is compressed. No INFO dummy is returned; unsupported FORMAT has no default diagnostic in these selected dispatches. Preserve original operator/RHS for an independent residual and restrict calls to constructed, supported formats. Review covers public dispatch and precision generation, not every hierarchical factorization kernel or scalability/accuracy claims.

Local vectors must follow the constructed distributed ordering; undo the permutation for results in original coordinates. The selected complex general square-system path sets OPTION%PRECON=DIRECT, factors a constructed HODLR, HMAT/BLR or HSS representation, then applies its stored inverse/factors to multiple right-hand sides. No symmetry or Hermitian property is required by this selected general interface. BPACK_Solution dispatches DIRECT to BPACK_Inv_Mult; other PRECON values invoke an iterative route whose local error/iteration diagnostics are not exposed as output arguments here. The factorization and solve are relative to a compressed approximation: rank tolerances and conditioning affect error, and this is not an exact uncompressed LU guarantee or a sparse-storage solver merely because the representation is compressed. No INFO dummy is returned; unsupported FORMAT has no default diagnostic in these selected dispatches. Preserve original operator/RHS for an independent residual and restrict calls to constructed, supported formats. Review covers public dispatch and precision generation, not every hierarchical factorization kernel or scalability/accuracy claims.

[README.md](https://github.com/YoushanLiu/Butterworth-Filter/blob/7ad7f7086a165e169597fad651cf2077f2a613a4/README.md)

**L10a1c3 — source-reviewed**

The inspected low-pass design prewarps the cutoff with cot(pi*f*dt), assembles first/second-order Butterworth factors and expands their polynomials into coefficient vectors. buttfilt applies a causal recursive linear difference equation with input numerator coefficients b and feedback denominator coefficients a, overwriting samples 0:nt after zero-state initialization. L10a1c3 records this autoregressive-linear filtering path, not statistical AR-model parameter estimation. The forward routine omits division by a(0), so it requires a(0)=1; the separate filtfilt implementation divides by a(0) and uses forward/reverse zero-state passes, which is not an equivalent endpoint-transient policy to every other library filtfilt. Positive order/dt and cutoff below Nyquist are caller checks; only near-zero cutoff is rejected in buttlp. High-order direct-form conditioning, stability and frequency response were not measured. No signal or author driver was run.

```fortran
a = a/a(0)

```

[README.md](https://github.com/dingshutong/BVARmml/blob/b68a4001d2f9c67cad4b904ee81136c3f74423da/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `c8405bf04de320e4d4571e4a5fbfe6756fc7480654aa0cebcb08dcbd0487fb72`.

**L10c — source-reviewed**

The public VARUTILS VARFORECAST routine recursively forecasts a vector autoregression from a supplied lag vector and coefficient matrix, optionally adding multivariate-normal innovations. Deterministic regressors enter through optional X; absence of VC/VCROOT/VCDIAG selects deterministic point forecasts. Optional variance selection prefers VCDIAG, then VCROOT, then VC. The lag vector groups the most recent M-vector first, and B uses matching coefficient rows; each forecast replaces the first lag block and shifts older values. Dimension checks use STOP and do not validate all zero-lag/finite/covariance cases; the full-covariance branch computes a Cholesky factor via IMSL without enforcing returned rank. The sketch uses a stable two-series VAR(1) with no deterministic regressors or stochastic innovations. The module itself includes Intel/IMSL linkage and other routines, so absence of optional noise does not make the whole object dependency-free. Review covers recursive forecasting and the associated AR-to-MA recurrence, not Bayesian variable selection or model estimation.

Carlson RC(X,Y): require X>=0 and Y>0; this interface does not provide the negative-Y principal-value extension. Import CARLSON_ELLIPTIC_MODULE_WP to match the preprocessed real kind (REAL64 by default). Optional integer IER should be supplied: 0 is normal; positive values flag domain or machine-range limits. The mathematical sign restrictions alone are insufficient at extreme magnitudes; consult the linked LOLIM/UPLIM tests. The result is a scalar, with no caller workspace or tolerance argument. Invalid input initializes the result to zero, so zero alone cannot distinguish failure.

Usage:

```fortran
VALUE = drc(X,Y[,IER])
```

**L8c — source-reviewed**

QUANTILELASSONET1 computes a penalized smooth quantile-regression coefficient path by generalized coordinate descent. At TAUX=0.5 the loss is a smoothed median/L1-regression surrogate; this is not an exact linear-programming LAD fit. C controls smoothing and LAM2 adds a quadratic penalty alongside the lasso path. The wrapper excludes constant/JD-listed columns, centers/scales X in place, clips PF/PF2, calls the path routine and restores coefficient/intercept scale. JD(1) counts excluded indices; IBETA and NBETA encode compressed active coefficients, not a dense NVAR-by-NLAM output. Initialize JERR=0 before entry because allocation statuses are added to it. Positive and negative JERR require inspecting completed NALAM and the path failure convention. Review covers this lasso/median branch, not every SCAD/MCP variant, a statistical selection guarantee or nonsmoothed quantile accuracy. The broad multiple-linear-regression class is retained because a smoothed penalized quantile loss is not an exact unpenalized Lp solver.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `0b2946cc1759deffabbde6321bd639d0d8eb09de`.

**D2e — source-reviewed**

The selected native BoxMG restriction and correction-prolongation entries are associated operations used inside a structured-grid multigrid linear solver. BMG2_SymStd_restrict accumulates a fine-grid vector to coarse interior points using transpose interpolation weights CI; periodic cases update input ghost cells in Q. BMG2_SymStd_interp_add adds coarse corrections to existing fine Q and also adds residual/diagonal terms at noninjection nodes: it is not pure interpolation of arbitrary data. It divides interior RES by the stencil diagonal in place, requiring nonzero diagonals and fresh residual storage before repeated calls. Provide matching BoxMG hierarchy extents/coarsening, initialized CI/stencil/boundary constants and ghost layers; these routines do not construct CI, solve a system, check convergence or return an error status. ModInterface defines len_t=C_INT and real_t=C_DOUBLE. Both external routines are BIND(C) with VALUE scalar dimensions/selectors, so Fortran callers need an exact explicit interface; USE ModInterface alone does not declare these external entries. The selected sketches cover serial 2-D transfer contracts, not MPI/3-D kernels or complete multigrid convergence.

**E1b — source-reviewed**

The reviewed CGL path generates Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto nodes mapped to [a,b], produces alternating barycentric weights with half endpoint weights, and evaluates a single univariate global Lagrange polynomial by the barycentric quotient. A near-node isclose test returns the stored sample rather than dividing by a small node difference. E1b records a single polynomial, not a piecewise interpolant or noisy-data fit. n is polynomial degree and arrays need n+1 elements despite some abbreviated shape comments. bary_weights only implements CGL weights, so the sketch does not combine it with CG/CGR nodes. Explicitly pass is_descending=.false.: the node generator default flag has declaration initialization and therefore retains a prior supplied value between calls. Positive n, distinct endpoints and adequate array extents are caller responsibilities; no error estimate/status is returned. Module imports require MKL BLAS95/F95_PRECISION even though this reviewed scalar interpolation path uses no BLAS operation. No interpolation result, extrapolation behavior or alternate node family was verified by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `6cf9f7de551072ba71435052b850d57371157394`.

Public module barycentric interpolation function. x, w and f each need n+1 REAL(rp) elements. Source documents ascending x. A query sufficiently close to a node returns its sample directly, using relative tolerance 1e-12 and absolute tolerance 1e-14. Otherwise the weighted numerator is divided by the weight sum.

Usage:

```fortran
value = lag_intrp(n, x, w, f, p)
```

Argument declarations: [src/chebyshev_m.f90:944–960](https://github.com/saridut/chebpak/blob/6cf9f7de551072ba71435052b850d57371157394/src/chebyshev_m.f90#L944-L960).

```fortran
use constants_m, only: rp
```

**H1 — documentation-reviewed**

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1`.

[README.md](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `89df696f996361d2b7f620e461b13bd564390cc0d0462b73067528adc0731c6d`.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

DPO2FT walks the lower Cholesky factor backward, propagating supplied factor adjoints through diagonal division, BLAS matrix/vector updates and diagonal halving. DPOFRT performs the corresponding blocked updates and delegates diagonal blocks to DPO2FT. This is a reverse first-derivative primitive for a scalar objective depending on an already-computed positive-definite Cholesky factor, not a factorization, solve or complete automatic-differentiation system. Only UPLO=L is implemented in the nonempty paths; the upper branches call XERBLA without reliably setting the advertised INFO=-8. Input checks omit LDC, so the caller must enforce it. The blocked path may overwrite entries above the selected triangle. Preserve the author triangular-adjoint convention when passing sensitivities onward. BLAS/LAPACK support routines and matching integer ABI are required. No adjoint identity or finite-difference comparison was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1`.

Public entry point `DPO2FT`: [dpo2ft.f:1–164](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpo2ft.f#L1-L164).

External unblocked double-precision reverse primitive. A holds a valid lower Cholesky factor; C holds the lower factor sensitivities on entry and is overwritten with input-matrix sensitivities in the author triangular convention. Supply UPLO=L, N >= 0 and both leading dimensions >= MAX(1,N); check INFO. A and C must be separate valid arrays.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DPO2FT(UPLO, N, A, LDA, C, LDC, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [dpo2ft.f:9–15](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpo2ft.f#L9-L15).

Author example (not run): [python/chol_diff.py:153–166](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/python/chol_diff.py#L153-L166).

Public entry point `DPOFRT`: [dpofrt.f:1–219](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpofrt.f#L1-L219).

External blocked variant with the same double-precision input/output convention, lower-factor restriction and required leading dimensions. Calls DPO2FT for small problems and diagonal blocks. C is modified in place, including some upper entries; retain only the meaningful triangle. INFO is not an accuracy estimate.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DPOFRT(UPLO, N, A, LDA, C, LDC, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [dpofrt.f:9–15](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpofrt.f#L9-L15).

Author example (not run): [python/chol_diff.py:261–274](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/python/chol_diff.py#L261-L274).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dpofrt
double precision :: factor(2,2), adjoint(2,2)
integer :: info
factor = reshape([2.0d0,1.0d0,0.0d0,3.0d0],[2,2])
adjoint = 0.0d0
adjoint(1,1) = 1.0d0
adjoint(2,2) = 1.0d0
call dpofrt("L",2,factor,2,adjoint,2,info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "reverse Cholesky failed"
```

Uncompiled calling sketch. The supplied lower factor defines X=factor*transpose(factor); adjoint initially seeds the sum of the factor diagonal. Link these reverse routines with ABI-compatible BLAS and LAPACK support; this is not a standalone single-file program. The output uses the author triangular sensitivity representation, so do not automatically symmetrize or double off-diagonals without matching the subsequent contraction convention. No numerical check was performed.

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

ADAPGAUSS generates an M-point Gauss-Legendre rule and adaptively bisects a finite interval, comparing a parent rule value with the sum of child values. The callback is a SUBROUTINE FUN(X,PAR1,PAR2,VAL), despite some comments calling it a function. Use matching REAL*8 parameter arrays/callback arguments; do not infer type-safe arbitrary integer user-data passing from historical comments. M must be positive and <=100 because local node/weight arrays have 100 entries. EPS>0 is compared independently against each accepted leaf difference: it is not divided among leaves and therefore is not a guaranteed global absolute-error bound. Depth is limited to 200 and the work loop to 100000 steps; IER=8/16 indicates those respective limits and RINT can be partial. MAXREC/NUMINT describe the traversal, not proof of error control. The rule differences can miss unresolved singularities/oscillations; no special weighted-integrand or rigorous error certificate is implied.

Reviewed 2026-11-06 at `e70b8ce97e337c8d20b1e9712bf40590eeda9994`.

Usage:


**H2a1a2 — source-reviewed**

LEGEWHTS constructs nodes and optional weights for a fixed-order Gauss-Legendre rule on [-1,1]. It starts from cosine root approximations, uses up to ten Newton corrections and exploits symmetry; weights come from a sum-of-squared-Legendre orthogonality relation. IFWHTS=1 computes weights, 0 returns nodes alone. Choose the quadrature order yourself; no tolerance-driven integrand adaptation or error estimate is returned. Positive N and caller-owned TS/WHTS storage of at least N elements are required. The old dummy declarations TS(1)/WHTS(1) are indexed beyond their declared extent, a legacy source convention requiring attention under bounds/conformance checking. Newton termination is not reported by a separate status, so do not infer successful roots/weights for every order. The calling sketch shows how this rule would be applied to a smooth scalar integrand, not a checked polynomial-exactness test.

Reviewed 2026-11-06 at `e70b8ce97e337c8d20b1e9712bf40590eeda9994`.

**C3a2 — source-reviewed**

LEGEPOL uses the Legendre three-term recurrence to return P_N(X), then computes its first derivative through N*(X*P_N-P_(N-1))/(X**2-1). Degree 0 and 1 have explicit value/derivative branches. Require N>=0; negative degree is not rejected. For N>=2, X=+/-1 gives a zero denominator and near-endpoint evaluation can lose derivative accuracy. Use interior finite arguments or separately supply mathematically appropriate endpoint limits; this pin does not implement such a special branch. This is evaluation of one Legendre polynomial and derivative, not evaluation of a whole fitted series, associated Legendre functions or a spherical-harmonic transform.

Reviewed 2026-11-06 at `e70b8ce97e337c8d20b1e9712bf40590eeda9994`.

**I2a2 — source-reviewed**

The selected pointwise routines solve scalar interface Riemann problems used in wave-propagation finite-volume methods for one-dimensional hyperbolic conservation laws. rp1_advection_ptwise uses constant velocity from REAL(KIND=8) COMMON /cparam/ u, returns the state jump, speed and signed flux fluctuations. rp1_burgers_ptwise uses the Roe average speed for flux q**2/2 and applies an always-enabled entropy fix to transonic rarefactions. Require NUM_EQN=1 and NUM_WAVES=1; the checked drivers use NUM_AUX=1 with unused auxiliary arrays. All numerical arrays are REAL(KIND=8), integers use the matching default ABI, and the pointwise declarations are INOUT even for quantities only read by these implementations. There is no status/dimension validation; larger arbitrary systems are not implied by dimension arguments. The two files export the same external symbol and are alternative link selections. Source review covers the full selected small kernels. Two complete catalog-owned main programs were compiled and run with bounds/FPE checks: nine advection cases and eight Burgers cases verify exact interface fluxes, fluctuation conservation, jumps and reported speeds. The results establish those cases, not a complete Clawpack time integrator, boundary treatment, convergence order or all solvers in the repository.

Reviewed 2026-11-06 at `008d4921ea46878a97a96c8b8daa399a2e7b9078`.

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
! GAMS I2a2; scalar advection interface checks.
! Upstream pin: 008d4921ea46878a97a96c8b8daa399a2e7b9078
program check_advection
  implicit none
  interface
    subroutine rp1_ptwise(ne,na,nw,ql,qr,al,ar,w,s,am,ap)
      integer, intent(in) :: ne,na,nw
      real(kind=8), intent(inout) :: ql(ne),qr(ne),al(na),ar(na)
      real(kind=8), intent(inout) :: w(ne,nw),s(nw),am(ne),ap(ne)
    end subroutine
  end interface
  real(kind=8) :: u
  common /cparam/ u
  real(kind=8) :: ql(1),qr(1),al(1),ar(1),w(1,1),s(1),am(1),ap(1)
  real(kind=8), parameter :: speeds(3)=[-2d0,0d0,3d0]
  real(kind=8), parameter :: left(3)=[1d0,-1d0,2d0],right(3)=[4d0,2d0,2d0]
  real(kind=8) :: flux,err,maxerr,tol
  integer :: i,j
  maxerr=0d0; al=0d0; ar=0d0
  do i=1,size(speeds)
    u=speeds(i)
    do j=1,size(left)
      ql=left(j); qr=right(j); w=0d0; s=0d0; am=0d0; ap=0d0
      call rp1_ptwise(1,1,1,ql,qr,al,ar,w,s,am,ap)
      if(u>=0d0)then
        flux=u*left(j)
      else
        flux=u*right(j)
      endif
      err=max(abs(u*left(j)+am(1)-flux),abs(u*right(j)-ap(1)-flux), &
              abs(am(1)+ap(1)-u*(right(j)-left(j))), &
              abs(w(1,1)-(right(j)-left(j))),abs(s(1)-u))
      tol=2d-13*max(1d0,abs(flux),abs(u*left(j)),abs(u*right(j)))
      if(.not.(err<=tol))error stop 'advection flux/speed/jump check failed'
      maxerr=max(maxerr,err)
    enddo
  enddo
  print '(a,es12.4)','Maximum absolute error: ',maxerr
  print '(a)','PASS advection: 9 positive/negative/zero-speed and state cases'
end program check_advection
```

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
! GAMS I2a2; scalar burgers interface checks.
! Upstream pin: 008d4921ea46878a97a96c8b8daa399a2e7b9078
program check_burgers
  implicit none
  interface
    subroutine rp1_ptwise(ne,na,nw,ql,qr,al,ar,w,s,am,ap)
      integer, intent(in) :: ne,na,nw
      real(kind=8), intent(inout) :: ql(ne),qr(ne),al(na),ar(na)
      real(kind=8), intent(inout) :: w(ne,nw),s(nw),am(ne),ap(ne)
    end subroutine
  end interface
  real(kind=8) :: ql(1),qr(1),al(1),ar(1),w(1,1),s(1),am(1),ap(1)
  real(kind=8), parameter :: left(8) =[1d0,-3d0,-2d0,1d0,2d0,1d0,2d0,0d0]
  real(kind=8), parameter :: right(8)=[3d0,-1d0,1d0,-1d0,-1d0,-2d0,2d0,0d0]
  real(kind=8) :: fl,fr,flux,err,maxerr,tol
  integer :: i
  maxerr=0d0; al=0d0; ar=0d0
  do i=1,size(left)
    ql=left(i); qr=right(i); w=0d0; s=0d0; am=0d0; ap=0d0
    call rp1_ptwise(1,1,1,ql,qr,al,ar,w,s,am,ap)
    fl=0.5d0*left(i)**2; fr=0.5d0*right(i)**2
    ! Independent exact Godunov flux from the scalar Riemann solution.
    if(left(i)>right(i))then
      flux=max(fl,fr)
    elseif(left(i)>=0d0)then
      flux=fl
    elseif(right(i)<=0d0)then
      flux=fr
    else
      flux=0d0
    endif
    err=max(abs(fl+am(1)-flux),abs(fr-ap(1)-flux), &
            abs(am(1)+ap(1)-(fr-fl)), &
            abs(w(1,1)-(right(i)-left(i))), &
            abs(s(1)-0.5d0*(left(i)+right(i))))
    tol=2d-13*max(1d0,abs(fl),abs(fr),abs(flux))
    if(.not.(err<=tol))error stop 'Burgers Godunov flux/entropy check failed'
    maxerr=max(maxerr,err)
  enddo
  print '(a,es12.4)','Maximum absolute error: ',maxerr
  print '(a)','PASS Burgers: 8 shock, rarefaction, transonic and constant-state cases'
end program check_burgers
```

Complete main program compiled and run locally on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), 2026-11-06. Flags: -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow.
