**L14a1b — source-reviewed**

The selected DCDB-Clust directory provides incremental minimum-sum-of-squares clustering, with OPTIM dispatching the DC-Clust local nonsmooth optimizer for the configured auxiliary or real clustering objective. For NS=2, CLUSTERFUNC sums each record squared distance to its nearest of NC centers, packed feature-first within each center. The public OPTIM interface takes MAXDIM-sized start/result arrays, with data matrix A, MF, NC, NRECORD and method controls supplied through shared modules. It has no arbitrary objective callback or returned termination code; printed FVALUE is not a global-optimum certificate. Other directory algorithms and the alternative DCD-Bundle method are not inferred from this one path. Review covers the public dispatcher, objective and selected local search structure, not clustering accuracy, initialization quality or every bundled implementation.

**C11 — source-reviewed**

The external HYG0F1 evaluates the confluent hypergeometric limit series 0F1(;A;Z), accumulating positive terms through logarithms of the rising factorial and ordinary factorial. The actual log formulation requires A>0 and Z>0 on the selected real branch; it does not implement general negative/complex arguments, analytic continuation or poles. It stops on an absolute term threshold 1e-15 or before iteration 1000, without returning a convergence flag or rigorous tail bound. Overflow, finite-precision loss and truncation are not diagnosed. This scoped mapping records the positive-real confluent limit function, not the separate Gauss 2F1 implementation or all special-function regimes in the package.

**L5a1b — source-reviewed**

BETACDF returns the regularized incomplete beta ratio for positive shape parameters and X in [0,1], calling its BRATIO implementation and exposing IER. BRATIO switches by parameter/input regime between power series, continued fractions, recurrences and asymptotic routines; its lower/complementary result is selected to reduce cancellation. The wrapper returns the lower-tail W, collapses nonzero inner statuses to IER=1, and uses IER=3 for an out-of-range result. Several internal BGRAT calls use IERR1 without propagating it through the wrapper status, so IER=0 is not an independently established accuracy guarantee. The binomial part of the shared GAMS class is not claimed. Review covers wrapper validation and regime dispatch, not every approximation kernel or all tails.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `21e9a3f878f632a145ca81b7c66ea4a6f6fbef5b`.

**A3a — source-reviewed**

The selected eq generic compares absolute differences with a tolerance, including default-real scalars, REAL64 scalars, default complex scalars and real arrays. Even the REAL64 overload takes a DEFAULT REAL tolerance; the default is 1e-8. Array overloads reduce to one logical and return false for size mismatch and also for two empty arrays. setTol returns its optional argument or the default; it does not change module state. There is no relative scaling or dedicated nonfinite/negative-tolerance validation; equal infinities can fail via infinity-minus-infinity. The complex ordering functions elsewhere compare real parts and are excluded from this equality mapping. No runtime comparison tests were performed.

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The scalar FZERO overload dispatches to NEWTON_INTERPOL, which uses two nearby initial function values and secant interpolation to solve a scalar equation without a supplied derivative. It is not a bracketing Brent solver despite other optimization routines in the toolbox. The selected cosine-minus-x example is a nonpolynomial equation and supports F1b. X is overwritten; the optional CHECK_RETURN is false on a residual-based return and true on stagnation or exhausted iterations. Shared module tolerance/iteration settings affect calls. The iteration has no interval or domain safeguard and can encounter a vanishing secant denominator; callers must supply a valid initial neighborhood and independently check the final residual. Review covers the scalar generic/implementation, not the distinct vector Broyden overload or global root isolation.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `dd70a86a02e45b6b5f9576216f280475c1b3b40b`.

```fortran
program scalar_root_sketch
use toolbox, only: fzero
implicit none
real(kind=kind(1d0)) :: x
logical :: failed
x=0.5d0
call fzero(x,residual,failed)
if(failed) error stop "root iteration stagnated or reached its limit"
print *,x,residual(x)
contains
function residual(x) result(value)
 real(kind=kind(1d0)),intent(in) :: x
 real(kind=kind(1d0)) :: value
 value=cos(x)-x
end function
end program
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build the pinned toolbox and match its REAL*8 interface. The scalar overload does not bracket a root or prove uniqueness; inspect the residual even after CHECK_RETURN is false. No root, stagnation or domain-error case was run.

**E1b — source-reviewed**

The scalar POLY_INTERPOL generic evaluates the global Lagrange interpolating polynomial through supplied univariate nodes. The implementation builds each product basis directly and sums YI times the bases; it is not piecewise interpolation, a spline or a barycentric implementation. Equal node/value counts are asserted, but duplicate nodes are not rejected before division. Distinct well-scaled nodes and modest degree are appropriate for the calling sketch; polynomial interpolation does not imply stable extrapolation or freedom from Runge oscillation. The node/value dummy arrays have lower bound zero, which is reflected in the usage fragment. Review covers scalar evaluation and generic visibility, not the separate vector-query implementation or fitted-error guarantees.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

LEGENDRE generates Gauss-Legendre abscissas and weights on a finite interval, selecting order from the output-array size. It uses symmetric initial root guesses, recurrence evaluation of Legendre polynomials/derivatives, Newton corrections and symmetric mapping of roots/weights to the target interval. The concrete mapping is quadrature service routine H2c: this API does not itself accept or integrate a user function, and the sketch performs the fixed-order weighted sum separately. Array-size mismatch or exhausted root iterations invokes the toolbox error handler; no numerical status is returned. The source caps root iteration at ten steps. A positive order and increasing finite endpoints are assumed by the sketch. The source explicitly identifies Numerical Recipes adaptation, which is retained as a licensing/provenance qualification rather than silently treating every component as original GPL code.

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The public BRENTZERO generic selects single/double bindings. The reviewed double binding tests endpoint roots/signs, maintains a bracket, attempts secant or inverse-quadratic interpolation and falls back to bisection when acceptance conditions fail. It returns an interval-scale convergence test or exact computed zero, evaluation count and explicit error code. The routine is for one continuous scalar equation with a sign-changing bracket, not guaranteed root enumeration, polynomial complex roots or discontinuous functions. The initial FA*FB sign test can overflow/underflow, and finite values/positive tolerances/iteration limits are not validated. No accuracy or pathological-bracket behavior was checked by execution.

Public entry point `ForsytheMalcolmMoler::BrentZero`: [fmm.f90:3076–3223](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90#L3076-L3223).

Public module generic; reviewed double binding uses SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50). Callback F(X) has a scalar real input with INTENT(IN) and scalar real result. ERRCode=0 normal, 1 iteration budget, 2 endpoints have the same sign; NEVAL counts endpoint and iteration evaluations.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL BrentZero(AX, BX, F, TOL, MAXITER, NEVAL, ERRCODE, XZERO, FZERO)
```

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: BrentZero
integer, parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50)
real(dp) :: root, residual
integer :: neval, status
! Provide F(x)=x*x-2 with a matching REAL(dp) scalar interface.
call BrentZero(1.0_dp,2.0_dp,f,1.0e-10_dp,100,neval,status,root,residual)
if (status /= 0) error stop "BrentZero failed"
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Provide the callback, finite endpoint values, a continuous bracketed problem and positive controls. Compare ROOT with sqrt(2) and independently evaluate the residual. Convergence in bracket width is not a universal residual guarantee; ERRCODE=2 returns HUGE sentinels. No other textbook solver is promoted to source-reviewed by this mapping.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The public FMMspline and NaturalSpline generics construct univariate interpolating cubic splines; Seval evaluates the fitted polynomial. Provide equal-length X,Y,B,C,D arrays, strictly increasing distinct knots and N>=2; there is no general size/ordering validation or returned fit status. FMMspline uses divided-difference end conditions derived from four endpoint data points when N>3, with lower-order special cases for N=2/3. NaturalSpline enforces zero second derivative at both ends and needs N>=2 even though the other constructor has a one-point branch. These are different boundary conditions; natural splines do not generally reproduce a cubic. Coefficients are in powers of U-X(i), not B-spline basis coefficients. SEVAL/SEVAL3 extrapolate the first/last polynomial beyond the knot range without clipping or a warning. Their cached interval index is SAVE state; the serial tests do not establish thread safety. The complete main checks FMM polynomial reproduction through degree MIN(3,N-1) and natural constant/linear reproduction on nonuniform grids of 2,3,4,6,9 knots, at interior queries, knots and exterior points in a nonmonotone order. An independent three-knot natural spline through (0,0),(1,1),(2,0) supplies non-affine reference pieces 1.5*x-0.5*x**3 on the left and 1-1.5*(x-1)**2+0.5*(x-1)**3 on the right. All 499 value checks passed; maximum normalized error was 2.220446e-16. The selected double overload uses DP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50), binary64 on the recorded GNU build. Match this kind in inputs, outputs and callbacks; DP is private, so the main declares the same selection. Tests compile the complete unmodified module and each main with -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow. These finite serial checks do not certify all textbook routines, all input regimes, other compilers or single precision. Existing root MIT and inherited-source scope findings are retained; only original catalog mains and a pinned-source downloader are bundled.

Public entry point `ForsytheMalcolmMoler::FMMspline`: [fmm.f90:55–57](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90#L55-L57).

Public generic; selected double-precision cubic constructor with FMM end conditions.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL FMMspline(X,Y,B,C,D)
```

Argument declarations: [fmm.f90:2061–2075](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90#L2061-L2075).

Argument declarations: [fmm.f90:55–57](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90#L55-L57).

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
! GAMS E1a: checked ForsytheMalcolmMoler spline interface.
program spline
 use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: FMMspline,NaturalSpline,Seval,Seval3
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 implicit none
 integer,parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50),sizes(*)=[2,3,4,6,9]
 real(dp),parameter :: queries(*)=[-1.2_dp,-1._dp,-.9_dp,-.5_dp,0._dp,.25_dp,.5_dp,1._dp,1.3_dp,1.7_dp,2._dp,2.2_dp,-.3_dp]
 integer :: mode,k,n,degree,i,j,maxdegree,count
 real(dp),allocatable :: x(:),y(:),b(:),c(:),d(:)
 real(dp) :: q,expected(4),got(4),error,maximum
 maximum=0;count=0
 do k=1,size(sizes)
  n=sizes(k)
  allocate(x(n),y(n),b(n),c(n),d(n))
  do i=1,n
   x(i)=-1._dp+3._dp*(real(i-1,dp)/real(n-1,dp))**1.3_dp
  end do
  do mode=1,2
   maxdegree=min(3,n-1)
   if(mode==2) maxdegree=1
   do degree=0,maxdegree
    y=x**degree
    if(mode==1) then
     call FMMspline(x,y,b,c,d)
    else
     call NaturalSpline(x,y,b,c,d)
     if(abs(c(1))+abs(c(n))>5.e-11_dp) error stop 'natural endpoint curvature'
    end if
    do j=1,size(queries)+n
     if(j<=size(queries)) then
      q=queries(j)
     else
      q=x(j-size(queries))
     end if
     expected=0
     expected(1)=q**degree
     if(degree>=1) expected(2)=degree*q**(degree-1)
     if(degree>=2) expected(3)=degree*(degree-1)*q**(degree-2)
     if(degree>=3) expected(4)=degree*(degree-1)*(degree-2)*q**(degree-3)
     got=0;got(1)=Seval(q,x,y,b,c,d)
     expected(2:)=0
     if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(got))) error stop 'nonfinite spline'
     error=maxval(abs(got-expected))/max(1._dp,maxval(abs(expected)))
     maximum=max(maximum,error)
     if(error>5.e-11_dp) error stop 'spline polynomial mismatch'
     count=count+1
    end do
   end do
  end do
  deallocate(x,y,b,c,d)
 end do
 ! Three-knot non-affine natural spline: exact piecewise cubic, no second solver used.
 allocate(x(3),y(3),b(3),c(3),d(3))
 x=[0._dp,1._dp,2._dp];y=[0._dp,1._dp,0._dp]
 call NaturalSpline(x,y,b,c,d)
 do j=-1,9
  q=0.25_dp*j
  if(q<1._dp) then
   expected=[1.5_dp*q-0.5_dp*q**3,1.5_dp-1.5_dp*q*q,-3._dp*q,-3._dp]
  else
   expected=[1._dp-1.5_dp*(q-1)**2+0.5_dp*(q-1)**3,-3._dp*(q-1)+1.5_dp*(q-1)**2, &
     -3._dp+3._dp*(q-1),3._dp]
  end if
 got=0;got(1)=Seval(q,x,y,b,c,d);expected(2:)=0
  if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(got))) error stop 'nonfinite natural spline'
  error=maxval(abs(got-expected))/max(1._dp,maxval(abs(expected)))
  maximum=max(maximum,error)
  if(error>5.e-11_dp) error stop 'natural spline reference mismatch'
  count=count+1
 end do
 deallocate(x,y,b,c,d)
 print '(a,i0)', 'Checked spline queries: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS spline'
end program
```

**E3a2 — source-reviewed**

The public SEVAL3 generic evaluates the spline value and up to three derivatives, using PRESENT tests for its optional F,FP,FPP,FPPP outputs. The outputs are analytic derivatives of the fitted local cubic, not finite differences or direct derivatives of arbitrary underlying data. At an exact interior knot the selected right-hand polynomial determines the third derivative; a natural spline is C2 and its third derivative may jump. Provide equal-length X,Y,B,C,D arrays, strictly increasing distinct knots and N>=2; there is no general size/ordering validation or returned fit status. FMMspline uses divided-difference end conditions derived from four endpoint data points when N>3, with lower-order special cases for N=2/3. NaturalSpline enforces zero second derivative at both ends and needs N>=2 even though the other constructor has a one-point branch. These are different boundary conditions; natural splines do not generally reproduce a cubic. Coefficients are in powers of U-X(i), not B-spline basis coefficients. SEVAL/SEVAL3 extrapolate the first/last polynomial beyond the knot range without clipping or a warning. Their cached interval index is SAVE state; the serial tests do not establish thread safety. The complete main checks all four outputs against analytic polynomial derivatives using the same nonuniform grids and nonmonotone query orders as the value driver, including a separately derived non-affine three-knot natural spline. All 499 output-vector comparisons passed; maximum normalized error was 5.667141e-15. The selected double overload uses DP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50), binary64 on the recorded GNU build. Match this kind in inputs, outputs and callbacks; DP is private, so the main declares the same selection. Tests compile the complete unmodified module and each main with -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow. These finite serial checks do not certify all textbook routines, all input regimes, other compilers or single precision. ! GAMS E3a2: checked ForsytheMalcolmMoler spline interface.
```fortran
program derivatives
 use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: FMMspline,NaturalSpline,Seval,Seval3
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 implicit none
 integer,parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50),sizes(*)=[2,3,4,6,9]
 real(dp),parameter :: queries(*)=[-1.2_dp,-1._dp,-.9_dp,-.5_dp,0._dp,.25_dp,.5_dp,1._dp,1.3_dp,1.7_dp,2._dp,2.2_dp,-.3_dp]
 integer :: mode,k,n,degree,i,j,maxdegree,count
 real(dp),allocatable :: x(:),y(:),b(:),c(:),d(:)
 real(dp) :: q,expected(4),got(4),error,maximum
 maximum=0;count=0
 do k=1,size(sizes)
  n=sizes(k)
  allocate(x(n),y(n),b(n),c(n),d(n))
  do i=1,n
   x(i)=-1._dp+3._dp*(real(i-1,dp)/real(n-1,dp))**1.3_dp
  end do
  do mode=1,2
   maxdegree=min(3,n-1)
   if(mode==2) maxdegree=1
   do degree=0,maxdegree
    y=x**degree
    if(mode==1) then
     call FMMspline(x,y,b,c,d)
    else
     call NaturalSpline(x,y,b,c,d)
     if(abs(c(1))+abs(c(n))>5.e-11_dp) error stop 'natural endpoint curvature'
    end if
    do j=1,size(queries)+n
     if(j<=size(queries)) then
      q=queries(j)
     else
      q=x(j-size(queries))
     end if
     expected=0
     expected(1)=q**degree
     if(degree>=1) expected(2)=degree*q**(degree-1)
     if(degree>=2) expected(3)=degree*(degree-1)*q**(degree-2)
     if(degree>=3) expected(4)=degree*(degree-1)*(degree-2)*q**(degree-3)
     call Seval3(q,x,y,b,c,d,f=got(1),fp=got(2),fpp=got(3),fppp=got(4))
     if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(got))) error stop 'nonfinite spline'
     error=maxval(abs(got-expected))/max(1._dp,maxval(abs(expected)))
     maximum=max(maximum,error)
     if(error>5.e-11_dp) error stop 'spline polynomial mismatch'
     count=count+1
    end do
   end do
  end do
  deallocate(x,y,b,c,d)
 end do
 ! Three-knot non-affine natural spline: exact piecewise cubic, no second solver used.
 allocate(x(3),y(3),b(3),c(3),d(3))
 x=[0._dp,1._dp,2._dp];y=[0._dp,1._dp,0._dp]
 call NaturalSpline(x,y,b,c,d)
 do j=-1,9
  q=0.25_dp*j
  if(q<1._dp) then
   expected=[1.5_dp*q-0.5_dp*q**3,1.5_dp-1.5_dp*q*q,-3._dp*q,-3._dp]
  else
   expected=[1._dp-1.5_dp*(q-1)**2+0.5_dp*(q-1)**3,-3._dp*(q-1)+1.5_dp*(q-1)**2, &
     -3._dp+3._dp*(q-1),3._dp]
  end if
 call Seval3(q,x,y,b,c,d,f=got(1),fp=got(2),fpp=got(3),fppp=got(4))
  if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(got))) error stop 'nonfinite natural spline'
  error=maxval(abs(got-expected))/max(1._dp,maxval(abs(expected)))
  maximum=max(maximum,error)
  if(error>5.e-11_dp) error stop 'natural spline reference mismatch'
  count=count+1
 end do
 deallocate(x,y,b,c,d)
 print '(a,i0)', 'Checked spline queries: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS derivatives'
end program
```

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

The public QUANC8 generic adaptively integrates a finite-interval callback using closed eight-panel Newton-Cotes rules, repeated interval subdivision and a difference-based error estimate/correction. The callback must accept a scalar of the selected real kind with INTENT(IN) and return the same kind; it is sampled at endpoints as well as interior points, so selected integrands are finite and smooth there. Supply positive ABSERR/RELERR and inspect the real-valued FLAG, error estimate ERREST and evaluation count NOFUN; FLAG=0 is the normal return, while nonzero values indicate depth/evaluation-limit conditions. ERREST is an estimate rather than a certified upper bound. Equal limits return zero without evaluating the callback; reversed limits were independently checked. LEVMAX has initialized local SAVE state and is reduced by the resource-limit path without being reset at entry, so a difficult earlier call can alter later limits. That resource-limit behavior, singular/discontinuous integrands and concurrent calls were not executed. The complete main checks degree-0-through-12 monomials on [0,1], [-1,2], [2,-1] and [1,1], plus exponential, sine and rational integrals. All 55 comparisons passed, using 1738 callback evaluations; maximum normalized analytic error was 9.219847e-13. Requested absolute/relative controls were 1e-11, and the independent check tolerance was 5e-10. The selected double overload uses DP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50), binary64 on the recorded GNU build. Match this kind in inputs, outputs and callbacks; DP is private, so the main declares the same selection. Tests compile the complete unmodified module and each main with -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow. Locally checked main program:

```fortran
! GAMS H2a1a1: adaptive QUANC8 checked against analytic definite integrals.
program quadrature
 use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: Quanc8
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 implicit none
 integer,parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50)
 integer :: power,which,interval,nofun,count,total_evaluations
 real(dp) :: a,b,expected,value,errest,flag,error,maximum
 maximum=0;count=0;total_evaluations=0;which=0
 do power=0,12
  do interval=1,4
   select case(interval)
   case(1);a=0;b=1
   case(2);a=-1;b=2
   case(3);a=2;b=-1
   case(4);a=1;b=1
   end select
   expected=(b**(power+1)-a**(power+1))/real(power+1,dp)
   call check()
  end do
 end do
 do which=1,3
  select case(which)
  case(1);a=-1;b=1;expected=exp(1._dp)-exp(-1._dp)
  case(2);a=0;b=acos(-1._dp);expected=2
  case(3);a=0;b=1;expected=acos(-1._dp)/4
  end select
  call check()
 end do
 print '(a,i0)', 'Analytic integral comparisons: ',count
 print '(a,i0)', 'Function evaluations: ',total_evaluations
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS quadrature'
contains
 function integrand(x) result(y)
  real(dp),intent(in) :: x
  real(dp) :: y
  select case(which)
  case(0);y=x**power
  case(1);y=exp(x)
  case(2);y=sin(x)
  case(3);y=1/(1+x*x)
  end select
 end function
 subroutine check()
  call Quanc8(integrand,a,b,1.e-11_dp,1.e-11_dp,value,errest,nofun,flag)
  if(.not.ieee_is_finite(value) .or. .not.ieee_is_finite(errest) .or. .not.ieee_is_finite(flag)) error stop 'nonfinite quadrature'
  if(flag/=0 .or. errest<0 .or. nofun<0) error stop 'quadrature status'
  if(a==b .and. nofun/=0) error stop 'zero interval evaluation count'
  if(a/=b .and. nofun<=0) error stop 'missing function evaluations'
  error=abs(value-expected)/max(1._dp,abs(expected))
  maximum=max(maximum,error)
  if(error>5.e-10_dp) error stop 'analytic integral mismatch'
  total_evaluations=total_evaluations+nofun
  count=count+1
 end subroutine
end program
```

**D6 — source-reviewed**

The public SVD generic implements a real rectangular singular-value decomposition through Householder bidiagonalization and QR iteration, with optional left/right vectors. The checked contract uses positive dimensions M>=N, separate A(M,N), W(N), U(M,N), V(N,N) buffers and both vector selectors true. A is preserved; singular values are nonnegative but not sorted. Reconstruct A as U*diag(W)*transpose(V), and pair each column with its corresponding unsorted W. U is scratch even when MATU is false; the source only guards U dimensions conditionally, so do not infer that a dummy-sized U is sufficient when vectors are disabled. IERR=0 is normal, negative statuses indicate some undersized output buffers, and a positive index reports nonconvergence after the iteration limit. Wide/empty cases, output aliasing, disabled-vector flags, extreme dynamic range and every error-return path were not executed. The complete main checks 48 square/tall matrices: N=1..4 and M=N or N+2, with diagonal known spectra, dense matrices, zero/rank-one cases and dense matrices scaled by 1e-30 or 1e30. It independently verifies unchanged input, finite nonnegative singular values, reconstruction, orthogonality, scaled Frobenius energy and selected analytic spectra. Maximum scaled reconstruction, orthogonality and relative energy errors were 6.661338e-16, 1.110223e-15 and 8.889787e-16, below 5e-11. Use the public generic with the selected DP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50) double-precision interface, binary64 on the recorded compiler. DP is private, so the catalog main declares the same kind selection. The complete unmodified module and main were compiled and run with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), Windows, at -O0 with bounds checks and invalid/zero/overflow traps. No source repair or permissive argument-mismatch flag was used. These finite tests do not establish every input regime, optimized-build behavior, other compilers or single precision. Existing root MIT/inherited-source license findings remain scoped; no upstream numerical source is bundled.

```fortran
! GAMS D6: SVD checked by reconstruction, orthogonality and known spectra.
program check_svd
 use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: SVD
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 implicit none
 integer,parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50)
 integer :: n,m,extra,kind,i,j,k,status,count
 real(dp),allocatable :: a(:,:),original(:,:),u(:,:),v(:,:),w(:),scaled(:,:),gram(:,:)
 real(dp) :: scale,residual,orthogonality,energy,maximum,maximum_orth,maximum_energy,known
 real(dp),parameter :: tolerance=5.e-11_dp
 maximum=0;maximum_orth=0;maximum_energy=0;count=0
 do n=1,4
  do extra=0,2,2
   m=n+extra
   allocate(a(m,n),original(m,n),u(m,n),v(n,n),w(n),scaled(m,n),gram(n,n))
   do kind=1,6
    a=0
    select case(kind)
    case(1)
     do i=1,n
      a(i,i)=i
     end do
    case(2,5,6)
     do j=1,n
      do i=1,m
       a(i,j)=sin(real(3*i+2*j,dp))+0.3_dp*cos(real(i*j,dp))
       if(i==j) a(i,j)=a(i,j)+2
      end do
     end do
     if(kind==5) a=a*1.e-30_dp
     if(kind==6) a=a*1.e30_dp
    case(3)
     a=0
    case(4)
     do j=1,n
      do i=1,m
       a(i,j)=real(i,dp)*real(j,dp)
      end do
     end do
    end select
    original=a
    call SVD(a,w,.true.,u,.true.,v,status)
    if(status/=0) error stop 'SVD status'
    if(any(a/=original)) error stop 'SVD modified input'
    if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(w)) .or. any(w<0)) error stop 'SVD spectrum'
    if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(u)) .or. .not.all(ieee_is_finite(v))) error stop 'SVD vectors'
    scale=maxval(abs(original));if(scale==0) scale=1
    do j=1,n
     scaled(:,j)=u(:,j)*(w(j)/scale)
    end do
    residual=maxval(abs(matmul(scaled,transpose(v))-original/scale))
    gram=matmul(transpose(u),u)
    do i=1,n
     gram(i,i)=gram(i,i)-1
    end do
    orthogonality=maxval(abs(gram))
    gram=matmul(transpose(v),v)
    do i=1,n
     gram(i,i)=gram(i,i)-1
    end do
    orthogonality=max(orthogonality,maxval(abs(gram)))
    energy=abs(sum((w/scale)**2)-sum((original/scale)**2))/max(1._dp,sum((original/scale)**2))
    if(kind==1) then
     ! Singular values need not be sorted; compare their power sums with the known diagonal.
     do k=1,3
      known=sum([(real(i,dp)**k,i=1,n)])
      if(abs(sum(w**k)-known)>tolerance*max(1._dp,known)) error stop 'diagonal spectrum'
     end do
    else if(kind==3) then
     if(maxval(abs(w))>tolerance) error stop 'zero spectrum'
    else if(kind==4) then
     known=sqrt(sum([(real(i,dp)**2,i=1,m)])*sum([(real(j,dp)**2,j=1,n)]))
     if(abs(maxval(w)-known)>tolerance*known) error stop 'rank-one spectrum'
     if(sum(w)-maxval(w)>tolerance*known) error stop 'rank-one null spectrum'
    end if
    if(max(residual,orthogonality,energy)>tolerance) error stop 'SVD invariant'
    maximum=max(maximum,residual);maximum_orth=max(maximum_orth,orthogonality);maximum_energy=max(maximum_energy,energy)
    count=count+1
   end do
   deallocate(a,original,u,v,w,scaled,gram)
  end do
 end do
 print '(a,i0)', 'Checked SVD matrices: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum scaled reconstruction error: ',maximum
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum orthogonality error: ',maximum_orth
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum relative energy error: ',maximum_energy
 print '(a)', 'PASS svd'
end program
```

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The public RKF45 generic integrates explicit nonstiff initial-value ODE systems with a Fehlberg fourth/fifth-order Runge-Kutta pair and adaptive step control. Provide Y(NEQN), WORK(3+6*NEQN), IWORK(5), mutable T/TOUT/RELERR, a nonnegative ABSERR, and an exact-kind callback F(T,Y,YP) using assumed-shape input/output vectors. Initialize IFLAG=1 for interval output or -1 for one-step mode; preserve work arrays and returned state for continuation. Status 2 means TOUT was reached, -2 means an accepted single step, and 3 adjusts an overly small relative tolerance and requires a subsequent call; statuses 4..8 and misuse of recovery state need separate handling and can lead to STOP. This is not a stiff solver, global-error certificate or event locator. IMPORTANT PORTABILITY CAVEAT: RkfsDouble declares preserved H, NFE, KOP and some saved tolerance arguments INTENT(OUT), yet continuation paths read retained values before redefining them. Entry makes such dummy values undefined under Fortran semantics; successful GNU -O0 runs do not establish portable or optimized continuation correctness. No repair was applied. The driver checks scalar exponential decay and a harmonic oscillator forward/backward, eight interval outputs per trajectory, 176 accepted one-step returns, initial equal-time requests, and explicit status-3 tolerance recovery. All 211 analytic-state comparisons passed, with 2507 callback evaluations and maximum normalized error 8.110344e-10 below 5e-8. Normal controls were RELERR=1e-9 and ABSERR=1e-11; the single status-3 case intentionally starts RELERR=0. Stiffness, resource-limit recovery, concurrency and optimized builds remain unverified. Use the public generic with the selected DP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50) double-precision interface, binary64 on the recorded compiler. DP is private, so the catalog main declares the same kind selection. The complete unmodified module and main were compiled and run with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), Windows, at -O0 with bounds checks and invalid/zero/overflow traps. No source repair or permissive argument-mismatch flag was used. These finite tests do not establish every input regime, optimized-build behavior, other compilers or single precision. Existing root MIT/inherited-source license findings remain scoped; no upstream numerical source is bundled.

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
! GAMS I1a1a: RKF45 continuation and one-step modes against analytic IVPs.
program check_ode
 use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: RKF45
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 implicit none
 integer,parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50)
 integer :: problem,direction,mode,j,iflag,iw(5),calls,count,steps,evaluations
 real(dp),allocatable :: y(:),work(:),expected(:)
 real(dp) :: t,tout,relative,previous,error,maximum
 maximum=0;count=0;steps=0;evaluations=0
 do problem=1,2
  allocate(y(problem),work(3+6*problem),expected(problem))
  do direction=-1,1,2
   do mode=1,2
    y=0;y(1)=1;work=0;iw=0;t=0;relative=1.e-9_dp
    iflag=1;if(mode==2) iflag=-1
    if(mode==1) then
     do j=1,8
      tout=direction*0.25_dp*j
      call RKF45(rhs,y,t,tout,relative,1.e-11_dp,iflag,work,iw)
      if(iflag/=2 .or. t/=tout) error stop 'RKF45 interval status'
      call verify()
     end do
    else
     tout=direction*2._dp
     do calls=1,10000
      previous=t
      call RKF45(rhs,y,t,tout,relative,1.e-11_dp,iflag,work,iw)
      if(iflag/=-2 .and. iflag/=2) error stop 'RKF45 step status'
      if(direction*(t-previous)<=0) error stop 'RKF45 no directional progress'
      call verify()
      steps=steps+1
      if(iflag==2) exit
     end do
     if(iflag/=2 .or. t/=tout) error stop 'RKF45 step target'
    end if
   end do
  end do
  ! Initial zero-length request is allowed and must preserve the initial state.
  y=0;y(1)=1;work=0;iw=0;t=0;tout=0;relative=1.e-9_dp;iflag=1
  call RKF45(rhs,y,t,tout,relative,1.e-11_dp,iflag,work,iw)
  if(iflag/=2 .or. t/=0) error stop 'RKF45 initial equal-time request'
  call verify()
  deallocate(y,work,expected)
 end do
 ! Explicitly check the documented too-small-relative-tolerance recovery.
 problem=1;allocate(y(1),work(9),expected(1))
 y=1;work=0;iw=0;t=0;tout=1;relative=0;iflag=1
 call RKF45(rhs,y,t,tout,relative,1.e-11_dp,iflag,work,iw)
 if(iflag/=3 .or. relative<=0 .or. t/=0) error stop 'RKF45 tolerance adjustment'
 call RKF45(rhs,y,t,tout,relative,1.e-11_dp,iflag,work,iw)
 if(iflag/=2 .or. t/=tout) error stop 'RKF45 tolerance recovery'
 call verify()
 print '(a,i0)', 'Analytic ODE state comparisons: ',count
 print '(a,i0)', 'Accepted one-step returns: ',steps
 print '(a,i0)', 'Derivative evaluations: ',evaluations
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized solution error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS ode'
contains
 subroutine rhs(time,state,derivative)
  real(dp),intent(in) :: time,state(:)
  real(dp),intent(out) :: derivative(:)
  evaluations=evaluations+1
  if(problem==1) then
   derivative=-state
  else
   derivative(1)=state(2);derivative(2)=-state(1)
  end if
 end subroutine
 subroutine verify()
  if(.not.ieee_is_finite(t) .or. .not.all(ieee_is_finite(y))) error stop 'nonfinite ODE result'
  if(problem==1) then
   expected=exp(-t)
  else
   expected=[cos(t),-sin(t)]
  end if
  error=maxval(abs(y-expected))/max(1._dp,maxval(abs(expected)))
  maximum=max(maximum,error)
  if(error>5.e-8_dp) error stop 'ODE analytic mismatch'
  count=count+1
 end subroutine
end program
```

**G1a1a — source-reviewed**

The public BrentMin and Fmin generics implement smooth scalar minimization without supplied derivatives. The inspected double overload searches a finite interval by safeguarded parabolic interpolation and golden-section steps, using only callback function values. G1a1a is the derivative-free smooth univariate class, not a multivariate, gradient-supplied or guaranteed global optimizer. Caller must supply an appropriate unimodal interval, ordered finite endpoints, positive tolerance and finite callback values. The stopping expression combines SQRT(EPSILON)*ABS(X) and TOL/3; TOL is not an achieved accuracy certificate. The complete unmodified-source main checks both APIs on quadratic, quartic, exp(t)-t-1 and asymmetric positive-quartic objectives, across three centers, widths and amplitude scales, totaling 216 known-minimum comparisons. Width-normalized location error must be <=5e-5, amplitude-normalized objective error <=1e-8, values finite and estimates inside the interval. Maximum errors were 7.381406e-8 and 2.664535e-15. Independently counted callback calls agree with NEVAL, and BrentMin returned values agree with fresh evaluations. Important source and executed limitation: BrentMin initializes ERRCODE=0 but never assigns the documented exhaustion code when MAXITER is reached. A deliberate one-iteration quadratic probe returns zero status while the minimizer location is wrong by 3.606801e-2. Fmin fixes its budget at 100 and discards error status and counts. Zero status is therefore not evidence of convergence. The probe is a reproduced defect, separate from successful known-minimum cases. GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 experimental on Windows ran both module and main at O0 with bounds checks and floating-point traps; no upstream source was repaired. The callback uses SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50); single overloads, endpoint minima, multimodal/noisy/nonsmooth objectives, invalid brackets, extreme scales, optimized builds and other compilers remain unchecked. Existing RKF45 state-intent and inherited-source license findings remain in force.

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
program minimization
  use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: BrentMin, Fmin
  use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50)
  real(dp), parameter :: centers(3)=[-3.0_dp,0.0_dp,4.0_dp]
  real(dp), parameter :: widths(3)=[0.25_dp,1.0_dp,3.0_dp]
  real(dp), parameter :: scales(3)=[1e-6_dp,1.0_dp,1e6_dp]
  real(dp) :: center,width,amplitude,x,fx,a,b,location_error,value_error
  real(dp) :: max_location,max_value,fresh
  integer :: ic,iw,is,shape,api,calls,neval,status,count,total_calls,probe_calls
  max_location=0; max_value=0; count=0; total_calls=0
  do ic=1,3
    center=centers(ic)
    do iw=1,3
      width=widths(iw); a=center-width; b=center+1.5_dp*width
      do is=1,3
        amplitude=scales(is)
        do shape=1,4
          do api=1,2
            calls=0
            if(api==1)then
              call BrentMin(a,b,objective,1e-10_dp*width,500,neval,status,x,fx)
              if(status/=0)error stop 'Unexpected minimizer status'
              if(neval/=calls)error stop 'Objective evaluation count differs'
            else
              x=Fmin(a,b,objective,1e-10_dp*width)
              fx=objective(x)
            end if
            total_calls=total_calls+calls
            if(.not.ieee_is_finite(x).or..not.ieee_is_finite(fx))error stop 'Nonfinite result'
            if(x<a.or.x>b)error stop 'Result outside search interval'
            location_error=abs(x-center)/width
            fresh=objective(x)
            value_error=abs(fresh)/amplitude
            if(location_error>5e-5_dp)error stop 'Known minimizer location check failed'
            if(value_error>1e-8_dp)error stop 'Known minimum value check failed'
            if(abs(fx-fresh)>1e-12_dp*amplitude)error stop 'Reported objective disagrees'
            max_location=max(max_location,location_error)
            max_value=max(max_value,value_error)
            count=count+1
          end do
        end do
      end do
    end do
  end do
  ! Deliberately expose the pinned routine's misleading exhaustion status.
  center=0.2_dp; width=1; amplitude=1; shape=1; calls=0
  call BrentMin(-1.0_dp,1.0_dp,objective,1e-12_dp,1,neval,status,x,fx)
  probe_calls=calls
  if(status/=0.or.abs(x-center)<1e-3_dp)error stop 'Pinned exhaustion behavior changed'
  if(neval/=probe_calls)error stop 'Probe evaluation count differs'
  print '(a,i0)', 'Known-minimum API comparisons: ',count
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum width-normalized location error: ',max_location
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum amplitude-normalized objective error: ',max_value
  print '(a,i0)', 'Normal-case objective calls (excluding independent fresh checks): ',total_calls
  print '(a,i0,a,es14.6)', 'One-iteration probe status: ',status,'; location error: ',abs(x-center)
  print '(a)', 'WARNING: BrentMin does not report iteration exhaustion; Fmin discards status.'
  print '(a)', 'PASS minimization'
contains
  function objective(arg) result(value)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: arg
    real(dp) :: value,t
    calls=calls+1
    t=(arg-center)/width
    select case(shape)
    case(1)
      value=t*t
    case(2)
      value=t**4
    case(3)
      value=exp(t)-t-1.0_dp
    case(4)
      value=t*t*(1.0_dp+0.1_dp*t+0.05_dp*t*t)
    end select
    value=amplitude*value
  end function
end program
```

```fortran
            if(abs(fx-fresh)>1e-12_dp*amplitude)error stop 'Reported objective disagrees'
            max_location=max(max_location,location_error)
            max_value=max(max_value,value_error)
            count=count+1
          end do
        end do
      end do
    end do
  end do
  ! Deliberately expose the pinned routine's misleading exhaustion status.
  center=0.2_dp; width=1; amplitude=1; shape=1; calls=0
  call BrentMin(-1.0_dp,1.0_dp,objective,1e-12_dp,1,neval,status,x,fx)
  probe_calls=calls
  if(status/=0.or.abs(x-center)<1e-3_dp)error stop 'Pinned exhaustion behavior changed'
  if(neval/=probe_calls)error stop 'Probe evaluation count differs'
  print '(a,i0)', 'Known-minimum API comparisons: ',count
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum width-normalized location error: ',max_location
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum amplitude-normalized objective error: ',max_value
  print '(a,i0)', 'Normal-case objective calls (excluding independent fresh checks): ',total_calls
  print '(a,i0,a,es14.6)', 'One-iteration probe status: ',status,'; location error: ',abs(x-center)
  print '(a)', 'WARNING: BrentMin does not report iteration exhaustion; Fmin discards status.'
  print '(a)', 'PASS minimization'
contains
  function objective(arg) result(value)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: arg
    real(dp) :: value,t
    calls=calls+1
    t=(arg-center)/width
    select case(shape)
    case(1)
      value=t*t
    case(2)
      value=t**4
    case(3)
      value=exp(t)-t-1.0_dp
    case(4)
      value=t*t*(1.0_dp+0.1_dp*t+0.05_dp*t*t)
    end select
    value=amplitude*value
  end function
end program
```

Complete main program compiled and run locally on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), 2026-11-06. Both unmodified module and main use -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow. All 216 smooth known-minimum API comparisons passed independent location/objective checks. A separate intentionally exhausted one-iteration call reproduces zero ERRCODE despite a wrong minimizer; it is not counted as convergence. Fmin hides status entirely. Do not treat ERRCODE=0 as certification. See drivers/fmm-minimization/ for exact tolerances, source hashes, flags, compiler warnings, saved results and untested cases.

**Q — source-reviewed**

The regular-grid wrapper traces an isoline at a specified level through rectangular scalar samples using GCONTR, collects callback vertices into allocated polylines, then maps fractional grid indices to physical coordinates CORNER+(INDEX-1)*STEP. Closed contours repeat the starting point, with no guaranteed orientation. POLYLINE stores N_POINTS, CLOSED and POINTS(2,N_POINTS). This is contour extraction for plotting, not a complete rendering backend, an arbitrary unstructured mesh algorithm or certified topology at saddle/degenerate values. ZMAX excludes values above a threshold; NaNs need separate handling. Scratch arrays and contour counters are shared saved state, so simultaneous calls need serialization. Source dispatch, crossing tracing, collection and coordinate conversion were inspected; no contour image or topology test was executed.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The public INTERP_LINEAR generic implements adjacent-point piecewise-linear interpolation for scalar/vector queries; INTERP_SPLINE builds cubic piecewise-polynomial coefficients and evaluates them. Require equal nonempty X/Y lengths, finite strictly increasing distinct X and at least two points for the spline. Linear queries outside the interval clamp to endpoint values. Spline outside queries use reflection about the endpoint and a reflected value, rather than the same constant policy; farther outside reflected arguments may themselves leave the interval. The cubic helper solves a tridiagonal coefficient system with its own endpoint conditions, not a user-selectable natural/clamped boundary API. No status argument validates sorting, duplicate nodes or model error. The defining helper source credits an earlier Godunov interpolation implementation; component provenance remains scoped.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The public INTERP_BILINEAR generic selects a double-precision rectangular tensor-grid path which brackets each query on two ordered coordinate axes, linearly combines four neighboring values and preserves a missing sentinel where interpolation is unavailable. Z is shaped (SIZE(X),SIZE(Y)); the reviewed overload returns (SIZE(XOUT),SIZE(YOUT)), with MASK on the output grid. Strictly increasing axes with at least two nodes and matching finite data are required. Queries equal to either extreme coordinate are marked outside by the <=/>= tests; only strictly interior points are interpolated. Any sentinel-valued corner prevents interpolation. FILL is accepted/stored but the filling block in this overload is commented out; it does not fill missing outputs. This is a source review of the gridded overload, not the separate paired-query or nearest-neighbor variants, scattered triangulation or conservative remapping.

**K5 — source-reviewed**

The public LOESS_SMOOTH generic regularizes an irregular series onto a uniform grid, calls the native LOWESS local-linear smoother with two robustness iterations, then linearly maps the smoothed series back. It omits Y equal to the chosen missing sentinel, uses the minimum consecutive X spacing to allocate the uniform grid, and derives F from L, DX and grid size; require sorted distinct X, at least two points and a practical minimum spacing to avoid huge allocation. L is not simply a point-count window; the code uses (2*L+1) in both its availability gate and fraction formula. It prints L/F and returns the sentinel when its point-count gate fails. The double overload explicitly casts data/window to default real before computation; its output is not a full double-precision LOWESS calculation. The same repository offers FILTER_GAUSSIAN via normalized sampled Gaussian weights and reflected boundary patches. Explicitly supply positive DX: the float path starts with SIGMAP=SIGMAP and only assigns a value when DX is present, and the double wrapper evaluates REAL(DX) without a PRESENT guard. The double Gaussian overload also reduces the field to REAL(4). Kernel width must fit the convolution implementation; its four-pass fallback is not an unlimited large-kernel remedy. These are smoothing implementations, not uncertainty estimates, missing-NaN detection or a precision guarantee.

**J2 — source-reviewed**

The public CONVOLVE routine accumulates weighted two-dimensional patches after reflecting each side once. Its implementation multiplies weights in their stored orientation without reversing them: for general asymmetric weights this is a correlation-style operation; symmetric Gaussian weights implement the corresponding convolution. H2/J2-style scalar integral or Fourier transform APIs are not inferred from the name. Inputs, weights and outputs are REAL(4), output must match input shape and weights should have odd extents so patches conform. Each weight extent must be strictly less than the corresponding input extent+1 (checked with an assertion that can terminate). Without MASK it is a direct weighted patch sum. With MASK, excluded centers remain unchanged and weights of excluded neighbors are redistributed equally over included neighbors; this is not a general theorem of global field conservation. The kernel is not automatically normalized and no sentinel/NaN policy is provided.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

HGRAD returns the magnitude of a centered finite-difference horizontal gradient, not a two-component gradient array. Its private helpers divide by 2*DX and copy neighboring interior derivatives to boundaries. Require positive finite DX and at least three points in each direction. A concrete boundary-index defect is present: D_DX assigns DU(NY,:) rather than DU(NX,:), so nonsquare grids can leave the last row wrong or address beyond the first extent. Restrict the sketch to square grids or repair this before general rectangular use. NORM=.TRUE. divides by MAXVAL(ABS(DU)) without a zero guard, so constant fields may divide by zero. Review records the local stencil and its limitations, not a general nonuniform/curvilinear gradient, convergence study or corrected implementation.

**P — source-reviewed**

The public CREATE_POLYGON and POINT_IN_POLYGON generics build a planar polygon from coordinate arrays and classify query points by parity of ray/edge intersections. The selected constructors assemble sequential edges closing the polygon; the query creates a default-real point and counts intersections over stored index pairs. Supply matching finite coordinate vectors, at least three sensible vertices and a valid simple polygon. The implementation perturbs a query Y equal to a vertex Y by a fixed EPS=1e-5, and slope/vertical-edge comparisons use floating-point thresholds. Consequently boundary/vertex inclusion, scale dependence and degenerate/self-intersecting polygons are not certified exact predicates. This is planar point containment, not spherical geometry, triangulation or polygon Boolean operations. Allocatable polygon components carry copied points/edge indices; the explicit FREE_POLYGON helper is private.

**L6b — source-reviewed**

The serial RUN_SAMPLER implements an affine-invariant ensemble stretch proposal with a companion walker, stretch density proportional to 1/sqrt(z) on [1/2,2], and acceptance factor z**(NDIM-1)*exp(delta log posterior). LOG_PRIOR and LOG_LIKE callbacks supply scalar logs. RANGES initializes walkers only; the callbacks must enforce posterior support thereafter. CHAINS has shape (NDIM,NWALKERS,NSTEPS), LOG_PROBS (NWALKERS,NSTEPS). Require NWALKERS>=2 to avoid the distinct-partner loop hanging and NSTEPS>=10 because progress MOD uses integer NSTEPS/10. The inspected range-shape guard combines tests incorrectly, so the caller must enforce shape (2,NDIM). EVORTRAN supplies the RNG and must be initialized consistently with WP. The routine allocates the whole chain even if output is omitted; no burn-in, autocorrelation or effective-sample-size calculation is performed. This mapping covers the serial implementation, not the separate OpenMP samplers or a verified posterior sample.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The public linear_interp type inherits initialization and scalar/array interpolate methods. Initialization copies monotonic x/y data; scalar interpolation locates/hunts a neighboring interval and dispatches li_raw_interp, which evaluates the two-point affine formula. E1a records univariate piecewise-linear polynomial interpolation, not global high-degree polynomials or cubic spline boundary options. Equal interval endpoints return the first ordinate; the sketch instead requires distinct ascending nodes and in-range queries. The scalar wrapper calls raw_interp without checking a locate/hunt error, and locate references SIZE and endpoint elements before its allocation guard, so successful initialization is essential. Errors are managed through optional ferror objects, with default behavior controlled by that dependency. No interpolation value, extrapolation policy or error path was executed.

**K1a1a2 — source-reviewed**

The rank-one x/y overload of linear_least_squares initializes a zero result, checks matching lengths, copies y and calls polynomial%fit_thru_zero with degree one, then extracts coefficient two. K1a1a2 records this dispatch to an unconstrained univariate polynomial least-squares fit restricted to y=a*x. It does not estimate an intercept and is not the separate multivariable SVD overload. The polynomial kernel lives in the external nonlin dependency and is not independently audited here; the source review establishes the wrapper contract and dispatch, not rank detection or numerical accuracy. Error paths can return the initialized zero slope, so a zero result alone is not a success flag. No fit or supplied plotting example was run.

**S — documentation-reviewed**

CUTEst supplies optimization test infrastructure and decoded problem interfaces. It is placed under software tools, not labeled as an optimization algorithm. Problem-specific SIF decoding may be required.

[README.md](https://github.com/ralna/CUTEst/blob/acff7e033e4723fc40bc379033ca1e808355c963/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `59a388906a51eeacb3bf42fa52a3701983096143a5f60fe3790942ebb92b0a4a`.

**R — source-reviewed**

The external CUTEST_UOFG routine evaluates the objective and optionally its gradient for a previously decoded/setup unconstrained SIF problem. It dispatches through global CUTEST data/work state to element/group evaluation and derivative accumulation, updates work/counters and reports failures in STATUS. It does not minimize the objective, choose search directions or establish optimizer convergence, so the source mapping is a numerical problem-evaluation service rather than an optimization-solver leaf. GRAD=false leaves G unsuitable as a computed gradient. The default public names and kinds are selected by preprocessing: CUTEST_UOFG_R becomes CUTEST_UOFG, and the provided interface module becomes CUTEST_INTERFACE_DOUBLE in the normal double/32-bit build. A matching SIF-decoded OUTSDIF.d plus compiled ELFUN/GROUP/RANGE routines and a successful USETUP are prerequisites; the global wrapper is distinct from per-workspace threaded variants. No objective or derivative was numerically checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `acff7e033e4723fc40bc379033ca1e808355c963`.

**J — source-reviewed**

The inspected program evaluates Morlet or Mexican-hat kernels at each integer scale and translation, multiplies by sampled signal and applies a trapezoidal weighted sum before writing coefficient magnitudes. This is a direct demonstrative continuous-wavelet-transform implementation, kept in the verified broad integral-transform class J rather than inventing a finer wavelet code. Quadrature omits time-step factors, translations use sample indices rather than input times, and the Morlet path uses default COMPLEX even though times are real(kind=8). No inverse transform, phase-preserving output, arbitrary-grid normalization or acceleration is established. Internal procedures belong to the program and are not reusable public module interfaces. File/allocation controls are not robustly validated; a malformed input can STOP the process.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected serial DCTSV solves real square cyclic tridiagonal systems with multiple right-hand sides by paired endpoint elimination, small determinant solves for the even/odd terminal cases, and back substitution. DL(1) stores the top-right corner and DU(N) the bottom-left corner. Those corners make this a general real system rather than an ordinary tridiagonal matrix in the displayed ordering; D2a1 is used without implying a dense factorization. D/DL/DU are read-only and B is overwritten by solutions. N>=4 and leading-dimension checks precede work. No pivoting is implemented; exact-zero intermediate determinant checks do not prove singularity of the entire matrix, and INFO=0 is not a conditioning or accuracy certificate. The README recommends diagonal dominance and warns that error grows faster with N than LU. This review excludes general wider-band and OpenMP variants. No solve, residual or timing comparison was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a`.

External double-precision cyclic tridiagonal solver. Supply N>=4, NRHS>=0, DL(N), D(N), DU(N), and B(LDB,NRHS), with LDB>=N. The wrapped corner elements are part of DL/DU. B becomes the solution; diagonals are preserved. Check INFO, but also assess residuals independently. Link XERBLA (normally supplied by LAPACK).

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DCTSV(N, NRHS, DL, D, DU, B, LDB, INFO)
```

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dctsv
integer :: info
double precision :: dl(4), d(4), du(4), rhs(4,1)
dl=-1.0d0
d=4.0d0
du=-1.0d0
rhs(:,1)=2.0d0
call dctsv(4,1,dl,d,du,rhs,4,info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "cyclic elimination failed"
```

Uncompiled fragment for a strictly diagonally dominant cyclic system with expected constant solution one. No residual was checked. Retain a copy of the original RHS for that check. This routine does not return reusable LU factors. Default INTEGER and double precision must match the linked error-handler ABI; positive INFO is an elimination-breakdown indication, not proof that every possible solver would fail.

**D2a2a — source-reviewed**

The separate external thomas routine performs forward elimination and backward substitution for an ordinary real tridiagonal system with k right-hand sides. The lower diagonal a(i) is read for i=2..n, the upper c(i) for i=1..n-1; a(1) and c(n) are unused. It overwrites b and d while returning solutions in z. This supports D2a2a (ordinary tridiagonal systems), not periodic corner coupling. There is no pivoting, dimension validation or error-status output, and division by zero or small elimination pivots is not guarded. Use appropriate nonzero-pivot inputs; no stability theorem or numerical check is established by this source inspection.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a`.

External nonpivoted tridiagonal elimination. n and k are default INTEGER; a/b/c are double-precision length n arrays, d and z have shape (n,k). b and d are overwritten; a/c are declared INOUT but not changed in the inspected body. z receives the solution. There is no INFO argument.


**I1a2 — source-reviewed**

The vendored DDASKR driver solves implicit differential/algebraic systems G(t,y,yprime)=0 with variable-order BDF integration, direct dense/band or preconditioned Krylov linear solves, and optional root-event detection. Its own category header identifies I1A2. The selected sketch uses direct dense finite-difference Jacobians, consistent supplied initial Y/YPRIME, scalar tolerances and no events. RES(T,Y,YPRIME,CJ,DELTA,IRES,RPAR,IPAR) has a CJ argument that older DASSL residual interfaces lack. INFO has 20 entries and selects solver/initialization modes; work lengths depend on those choices and on NEQ/NRT. Positive IDID distinguishes intermediate, endpoint, root and initialization returns; negative values require the documented recovery protocol, not blind resubmission. Continuation preserves workspace/state and changes INFO(1) as documented. This review covers driver controls, DDSTP BDF step dispatch/acceptance and residual contract, not every Newton/Krylov/preconditioner kernel, DAE index or consistent-initialization mode.

**L1a1a — source-reviewed**

These external numeric routines belong to Dataplot and use implicit default REAL/INTEGER arguments unless explicitly declared otherwise, plus CHARACTER*4 controls/status where present. The inspected src/Makefile sets -fdefault-real-8 and -fdefault-double-8: callers must use that same ABI, not infer four-byte arguments from old single-precision comments. Include DPCOP2.INC consistently and initialize the Dataplot output/common environment; OFF controls suppress selected feedback/debug paths, but errors and some warnings still call DPWRST. Link the required Dataplot support, not just an isolated monolithic source file. No missing/NaN policy or independently packaged stable library API is inferred. MEAN returns an arithmetic mean using an explicit DOUBLE PRECISION sum; MEDIAN sorts into a distinct caller workspace and selects the middle observation or average middle pair. Inputs remain in their original order in the selected separate-buffer usage. Require N>=1 and MAXNXT>=N for MEDIAN. Singleton/constant inputs use direct early-return values, so the median workspace need not contain a sorted copy on those paths. IERROR is CHARACTER*4 NO/YES, not a logical/integer code; ignore result values after error. Summation is not compensated, and the even-median addition can overflow for extreme finite values. This mapping covers raw-data location summaries, not population inference, quantile conventions or a missing-data estimator.

NORCDF uses a fixed five-term polynomial in 1/(1+p*ABS(X)) multiplied by a normal density to approximate the standard normal CDF; NORPDF directly evaluates exp(-X**2/2)/SQRT(2*PI). The normal has mean zero and variance one; callers standardize other location/scale families themselves. Both use default REAL arguments and constants, with no INFO/error bound, NaN policy or accuracy-based precision selection. The CDF subtracts from one and mirrors negative X, so very small tail probabilities can be lost by cancellation; use a dedicated survival/log-tail routine when that is the quantity required. LOGCDF evaluates the standard logistic CDF with a sign split: EXP(X)/(1+EXP(X)) for negative X and 1/(1+EXP(-X)) otherwise. LOGPDF evaluates EXP(X)/(1+EXP(X))**2 without that sign split. POICDF returns a Poisson cumulative probability through a positive-term finite recurrence for 0<ALAMBA<500, and dispatches to a normal approximation at rates >=500. There is no scalar status/error bound; count conversion and 2*(1+count) must fit the integer kind. **L5a1t — source-reviewed**

Dataplot external Fortran routines, with implicit default REAL dummies except integer arguments and explicitly DOUBLE PRECISION kernel interfaces identified below. The pinned Makefile promotes default REAL to eight bytes with -fdefault-real-8 and keeps DOUBLE PRECISION eight bytes with -fdefault-double-8; match caller, common blocks and all dependencies to that build. Initialize the Dataplot output/common environment and machine-constant arrays before any SLATEC-derived helper is first called; saved FIRST-call constants make late initialization ineffective. Link required support, not just a monolithic source file. There is no general INFO/error-bound output, NaN policy or independently packaged library API. TCDF and TPDF implement central Student t distributions with REAL ANU>0. TCDF converts ANU to INTEGER first and selects an integer path within 1e-6; that path assigns ANU=NU, so supply a writable variable rather than a literal. Small integer degrees use parity recurrences, large integer degrees a normal-based expansion, and genuinely fractional degrees an incomplete-beta relation. TPDF uses parity products for integer degrees and log-gamma differences for fractional degrees. Both initial INT conversions must fit the integer kind; huge/NaN degree values are outside the contract. The selected sketch uses ANU=5.5 and moderate X to follow the fractional branch. No noncentral t probabilities or uniformly accurate extreme tails are claimed.

Dataplot external Fortran routines, with implicit default REAL dummies except integer arguments and explicitly DOUBLE PRECISION kernel interfaces identified below. The pinned Makefile promotes default REAL to eight bytes with -fdefault-real-8 and keeps DOUBLE PRECISION eight bytes with -fdefault-double-8; match caller, common blocks and all dependencies to that build. Initialize the Dataplot output/common environment and machine-constant arrays before any SLATEC-derived helper is first called; saved FIRST-call constants make late initialization ineffective. Link required support, not just a monolithic source file. There is no general INFO/error-bound output, NaN policy or independently packaged library API. TPPF computes central t quantiles with REAL ANU>=1 and 0<P<1. The selected genuinely fractional ANU=5.5 path brackets between normal and Cauchy quantiles, evaluates the beta-based t CDF and bisects with fixed width 1e-7 and probability-residual 1e-4 requirements and a 3000-iteration diagnostic. Invalid P can return PPF unassigned; there is no status output. Integer paths are materially different: closed forms for NU=1/2, five-update special formulas for 3-6, a Hill-labelled branch for 7-30 and a normal-quantile expansion thereafter. Source caution for 7-30: PT is made a symmetric two-tail probability, but the first XT uses D*P rather than D*PT; inspect/correct and test that inconsistency before relying on this branch. The mapping records that branch structure without certifying those integer approximations. The routine excludes fractional 0<ANU<1 even though a t distribution exists there.

Dataplot external Fortran routines, with implicit default REAL dummies except integer arguments and explicitly DOUBLE PRECISION kernel interfaces identified below. The pinned Makefile promotes default REAL to eight bytes with -fdefault-real-8 and keeps DOUBLE PRECISION eight bytes with -fdefault-double-8; match caller, common blocks and all dependencies to that build. Link required support, not just a monolithic source file. There is no general INFO/error-bound output, NaN policy or independently packaged library API. GAMPPF inverts the unit-scale gamma CDF for positive REAL shape. It constructs a small-probability starting estimate using an internally computed log-gamma expansion, seeks an upper bracket for at most 30000 multiples and bisects with an absolute 1e-10 midpoint-change or 100-iteration stop. The internally evaluated incomplete-gamma series has a 10000-term limit and returns PPF=0 with diagnostics on exhaustion. There is no returned convergence flag; exhausting the bracket search or bisection budget is not separately certified. Require 0<P<1, finite moderate positive shape and independent CDF-residual checks. This is a gamma quantile, not an inverse gamma-function or geometric-distribution routine.

**L5a1w — source-reviewed**

Dataplot external Fortran routines, with implicit default REAL dummies except integer arguments and explicitly DOUBLE PRECISION kernel interfaces identified below. The pinned Makefile promotes default REAL to eight bytes with -fdefault-real-8 and keeps DOUBLE PRECISION eight bytes with -fdefault-double-8; match caller, common blocks and all dependencies to that build. Initialize the Dataplot output/common environment and machine-constant arrays before any SLATEC-derived helper is first called; saved FIRST-call constants make late initialization ineffective. Link required support, not just a monolithic source file. There is no general INFO/error-bound output, NaN policy or independently packaged library API. WEICDF/WEIPDF implement unit-scale Weibull probability functions with positive REAL shape GAMMA and INTEGER MINMAX. MINMAX=1 (also zero as an alias) selects the usual nonnegative distribution, CDF=1-EXP(-X**GAMMA); MINMAX=2 selects its reflected nonpositive counterpart, CDF=EXP(-(-X)**GAMMA). The selected usage explicitly chooses 1 and X>0. The PDF formula is a direct power/exponential product; at X=0 the source returns 1 for all GAMMA<=1, which is not the infinite mathematical limit for shapes below one. CDF subtraction can lose small probabilities, and large powers can overflow before the exponential suppresses the value. Invalid MINMAX prints diagnostics and can leave PDF unassigned; validate the selector and shape yourself.

Dataplot external Fortran routines, with implicit default REAL dummies except integer arguments and explicitly DOUBLE PRECISION kernel interfaces identified below. The pinned Makefile promotes default REAL to eight bytes with -fdefault-real-8 and keeps DOUBLE PRECISION eight bytes with -fdefault-double-8; match caller, common blocks and all dependencies to that build. Link required support, not just a monolithic source file. There is no general INFO/error-bound output, NaN policy or independently packaged library API. WEIPPF uses closed-form unit-scale Weibull quantiles: [LOG(1/(1-P))]**(1/GAMMA) for MINMAX=1/0, and -[LOG(1/P)]**(1/GAMMA) for the reflected MINMAX=2 distribution. Require positive REAL shape, INTEGER selector and strictly interior probability in the selected sketch. The input check admits P=0, but the reflected formula then divides by zero; no endpoint-infinity handling is supplied. Ratios and logarithms are computed directly rather than LOG1P-based forms, so rounded endpoints and extreme-tail cancellation/overflow need separate handling. Invalid inputs print diagnostics and return zero without a status flag. Location and scale must be applied outside this interface.

Dataplot external Fortran routines, with implicit default REAL dummies except integer arguments and explicitly DOUBLE PRECISION kernel interfaces identified below. The pinned Makefile promotes default REAL to eight bytes with -fdefault-real-8 and keeps DOUBLE PRECISION eight bytes with -fdefault-double-8; match caller, common blocks and all dependencies to that build. DLBETA is the bundled SLATEC-derived DOUBLE PRECISION log complete beta function for positive A/B. It branches on MIN/MAX parameter sizes: a gamma-ratio expression when both are below ten, and log-gamma/asymptotic correction plus DLNREL formulas for larger parameters. It returns LOG(BETA(A,B)), not BETA or a probability, and has no separate error estimate/status. Nonpositive input prints diagnostics and returns zero, which is also a legitimate log-beta value for some valid inputs. The review covers this public function and size-based dispatch, not every DGAMMA, D9LGMC, DLNGAM or DLNREL dependency kernel. Selected usage uses moderate positive parameters and a compatible initialized Dataplot environment.

SENZADERGLOB constructs bounded random trial points and uses an exponential acceptance threshold before derivative-free local searches. RICERCA_LUNGO_ASSI delegates to box-search kernels; linesearchbox_cont enforces bounds and sufficient objective decrease using only function values. This supports global nonconvex optimization (G2i), not a requirement to provide derivatives. The inspected routine is a working-set implementation; its title does not establish an MPI/distributed-memory interface. Evaluation/step limits and comparisons with a supplied fglob are stopping criteria, not proofs of a global minimum. The upstream MAIN_GLOB driver and repeated-run statistics were not executed.

**P — source-reviewed**

The bundled DELAUNAYSPARSES routine locates Delaunay simplices containing specified query points and returns vertex indices and barycentric weights. Its native serial path constructs a starting simplex, performs a budgeted visibility walk, and optionally projects out-of-hull queries. It does not construct/export an entire triangulation or certify arbitrary geometric predicates. PTS and Q are shifted/rescaled in place; shapes are D by N and D by M, with D+1 vertex/weight rows per query. Per-query IERR=0 means interpolation, 1 means permitted projected extrapolation, and larger codes report invalid data, degeneracy, budget or dependency failures. EXACT controls diameter/duplicate-check strategy, not exact arithmetic. This source review selects the bundled Fortran geometry, not the Python Delaunay-density diagnostic or an execution check of high-dimensional conditioning.

**E2b — source-reviewed**

With INTERP_IN/INTERP_OUT supplied, the bundled serial DELAUNAYSPARSES routine evaluates multivariate scattered-data piecewise-linear interpolation by summing response values at the located Delaunay-simplex vertices with their barycentric weights. Multiple response components use rows of INTERP_IN/OUT; both optional arrays must be present together. The native path only accumulates response values for per-query statuses 0 or 1. This is scattered-data interpolation E2b, not a smooth spline, gridded interpolator or a statistical density estimate. Default extrapolation projects onto the convex hull and interpolates at the projection rather than extending an affine function beyond the hull; EXTRAP=0 rejects outside queries. Coordinates are modified by normalization, and degeneracy/budget failures must be inspected per query before consuming outputs.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

class_optimizer initializes MPI, RNG, configuration, history, trial processing and stopping objects, then loops over trial evaluation and history selection. The inspected DE/rand/1 strategy selects three distinct non-parent members, forms base+F*difference, crosses coordinates and retries until the trial is within bounds. History accepts greater-or-equal fitness: DEPP maximizes, so minimizing an objective requires an explicit sign transformation. G2i records stochastic global search in a rectangular domain, not proof of global optimality or an audit of optional response-surface strategies. init reads configuration and run finalizes MPI itself; this is not a pure function accepting an objective callback and returning a solution array. The external fitness path writes parameter files, executes a configured program and reads a fitness file. Trial bounds and some fitness retries have no local cap; require at least four population members and a viable domain. No optimization, MPI or external fitness process was run.

**G2c7 — source-reviewed**

SD_BOX alternates bounded continuous and discrete coordinate line searches according to INDEX_INT, accepts objective reductions and updates directional step lengths. This mapping selects mixed continuous/integer coordinates with unit lattice spacing on the second coordinate. The external FUNCT(N,X,F) symbol is linked at build time, not passed as a callback argument. Initial points must already satisfy bounds and the chosen lattice; positive SCALE_INT is required on discrete coordinates. NF and NI are input/output counters and must be initialized. ISTOP=1 means directional stopping tests, 2 evaluation budget exceeded, 3 iteration budget exceeded; budget tests use > and happen after line searches, so NF_MAX is not a strict maximum objective-call count. No nonlinear-constraint handling, integer/global-optimality certificate or nonsmooth convergence proof was established by this source review. The supplied main shares the same source file and must be separated when supplying another main.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `d5a282bbe05a34c9a89167e6c21c85dfcef3235f`.

**G2h3b — source-reviewed**

The legacy external DFO driver minimizes an objective with simple, linear and nonlinear constraints using quadratic interpolation/trust-region modeling. The inspected driver validates/setup dimensions, scales inputs, evaluates linked FUN, initializes interpolation points and dispatches DFOSLV; the outer solver file shows model/subproblem dispatch rather than an independent full kernel audit here. The mapping records nonlinear equality/inequality constrained optimization without claiming the fine derivative-supply classes or every backend path. This is not a modern callback object: FUN is a linked external, model/control state is in saved COMMON blocks and arrays are flattened column-major buffers. dfo_model_inc.inc limits the default model dimensions to 50 variables/constraints and 10000 functions. Trust-region subproblems require a compatible IPOPT/NPSOL path and build configuration. INFO, final objective/constraint values and independent feasibility checks are essential; no optimizer was compiled or run.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `bd57c2eb07729aa1671e408ce4d4b10541538c82737365f36ac40002d0254b85`.

**D5 — source-reviewed**

The Fortran bmqrf module supplies column-pivoted Householder QR support, not the nonlinear DFSANE algorithm implemented in R. bmqr overwrites A with a compact factorization, stores reflector factors in gam and column permutation in p, and estimates rank using a scaled threshold of about 100 machine epsilons. extractQ/extractR expose the rank-sized factors. Restrict this reviewed interface to n>=m>=1, lda>=n and mlim>=m; it is not a reviewed wide-matrix routine. Failure hooks call REXIT and need the R runtime or a deliberately compatible replacement. No standalone compilation or factorization residual was checked.

**D4a1 — source-reviewed**

DGL_DAVIDSON_DRIVER computes a few lowest eigenpairs of a real symmetric ordinary eigenproblem using caller block matrix-vector and preconditioner routines, subspace projection, Rayleigh-Ritz extraction, residual expansion and restart/locking. This mapping selects no METVEC argument, hence identity metric. Require 1<=N_TARG<=N_MAX with 2*N_MAX<N, a truly symmetric operator, compatible configured integer kind and suitable initial guesses. It checks both RMS and maximum residual components for targeted roots. OK reports convergence, whereas DGL_INFO reports API/numerical errors: budget exhaustion can leave INFO=0 with OK false and approximate eigenpairs. This is not a dense full-spectrum solver or a new eigenpair/orthogonality validation.

**D4b1 — source-reviewed**

The generalized DGL_LOBPCG_DRIVER path seeks a small set of real symmetric A*x=lambda B*x eigenpairs, with B symmetric positive definite supplied through an associated METVEC procedure pointer. It builds a locally optimal subspace from eigenvector/residual/search-direction blocks, applies preconditioning and metric orthogonalization, and locks converged roots. This mapping does not assume an arbitrary indefinite metric, a nonsymmetric problem or a complete spectrum. Callbacks must implement the actual symmetric A and SPD B and a suitable preconditioner, with matching configured kinds and block dimensions. OK and DGL_INFO remain separate convergence/error outputs. Source review covers the generalized dispatch and inspected subspace/metric update paths, not every orthogonalization fallback or fresh numerical validation.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

DIFF_EVOL implements a stochastic differential-evolution search using mutation, binomial-style crossover, greedy selection and optional population perturbation. It calls the module-specific Griewank OBJ_FTN directly rather than accepting an objective callback. Lower/upper bounds initialize/reinitialize the population but do not constrain later mutation trials. Source findings: donor rejection uses AND rather than OR, so indices need not be distinct/exclude the target; the forced crossover coordinate can be NOP+1; BH_BEST is assigned only after improvement over the initial minimum and can remain undefined. G2i records the intended global-search method, not a guarantee of a global solution, correct bounded DE, or fitness for production use. The fixed generation/progress logic prints each generation and exposes no status or evaluation count.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `efeb31150b35010c5bdb465d81fc0e56000f37b2`.

dirdfn combines a DIRECT-type global partition search with CS-DFN local minimizations. The inspected nuovoglobale block invokes sd_box and subdivides potentially optimal rectangles; objective and feasibility are tracked separately through value-only callbacks. Finite lower and upper bounds are required, as the author driver explicitly warns. This global constrained search maps to the G2i leaf; finite evaluation/interval budgets and a supplied target fglob do not certify a global optimum or feasibility. The author main_test/problem example is available as a future driver candidate, not a checked example.

**G2h3b2 — source-reviewed**

The local sd_box implementation is explicitly CS-DFN for nonsmooth nonlinear programming. It uses coordinate/dense search directions and value-only objective/constraint evaluation, while funct_pen adds positive inequality violations and absolute equality violations. funct_vinc calls both fconstrin and fconstreq. This supports G2h3b2, the leaf for general nonlinear functions with equality and inequality constraints without a smoothness assumption. Nonsmooth does not establish convergence for arbitrary discontinuities: regularity assumptions, penalty updates and numerical convergence remain unverified. The supplied problem contains nonlinear polynomial equalities; its existence is not a successful solve.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

nuovoglobale evaluates an objective-value callback on a bounded domain, selects potentially optimal rectangles and triggers sd_box local searches after the configured trigLS budget fraction. The local kernel projects its starting point onto bounds and uses function-value line searches; no user derivative interface is present in the inspected path. G2i is the most specific GAMS global nonconvex class. Internal discrete-search branches in the shared local-search source are not enough to advertise an integer-programming solver: index_int is initialized to zero. Known fglob and resource limits are termination conditions rather than global-optimality certificates. No benchmark or driver was run.
