```fortran
﻿program correlation
  use fftpack, only: xcorr
  use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
  implicit none
  integer :: nx, ny, n, pattern, i, j, lag, count
  complex(kind=8), allocatable :: x(:), y(:), reference(:), z(:)
  real(kind=8), allocatable :: r(:), real_reference(:)
  complex(kind=4), allocatable :: xs(:), ys(:), zs(:)
  real(kind=4), allocatable :: rs(:)
  real(kind=8) :: scale, error, max_double, max_single
  count=0; max_double=0; max_single=0
  do nx=1,7
    do ny=1,7
      n=max(nx,ny)
      allocate(x(nx),y(ny),reference(2*n-1),real_reference(2*n-1),xs(nx),ys(ny))
      do pattern=1,3
        do i=1,nx
          x(i)=cmplx(sin(real(2*i+nx,8)),cos(real(i+ny,8)),8)
        end do
        do i=1,ny
          y(i)=cmplx(cos(real(3*i+ny,8)),sin(real(i-nx,8)),8)
        end do
        if(pattern==2)then
          x=0; y=0
          x(nx)=cmplx(2.0_8,-1.0_8,8); y(1)=cmplx(-3.0_8,2.0_8,8)
        else if(pattern==3)then
          x=0
        end if
        reference=0; real_reference=0
        do lag=1-n,n-1
          do j=1,ny
            i=j+lag
            if(i>=1.and.i<=nx)then
              reference(lag+n)=reference(lag+n)+x(i)*conjg(y(j))
              real_reference(lag+n)=real_reference(lag+n)+real(x(i),8)*real(y(j),8)
            end if
          end do
        end do
        z=xcorr(x,y)
        call check_complex(z,reference,2e-12_8,.false.)
        r=xcorr(real(x,8),real(y,8))
        call check_complex(cmplx(r,0.0_8,8),cmplx(real_reference,0.0_8,8),2e-12_8,.false.)
        ! Round inputs before the single-kind reference comparisons.
        xs=cmplx(x,kind=4); ys=cmplx(y,kind=4)
        reference=0; real_reference=0
        do lag=1-n,n-1
          do j=1,ny
            i=j+lag
            if(i>=1.and.i<=nx)then
              reference(lag+n)=reference(lag+n)+cmplx(xs(i),kind=8)*conjg(cmplx(ys(j),kind=8))
              real_reference(lag+n)=real_reference(lag+n)+real(xs(i),8)*real(ys(j),8)
            end if
          end do
        end do
        zs=xcorr(xs,ys)
        call check_complex(cmplx(zs,kind=8),reference,2e-6_8,.true.)
        rs=xcorr(real(xs,4),real(ys,4))
        call check_complex(cmplx(rs,0.0_4,8),cmplx(real_reference,0.0_8,8),2e-6_8,.true.)
      end do
      deallocate(x,y,reference,real_reference,xs,ys)
    end do
  end do
  print '(a,i0)', 'Direct-sum cross-correlation comparisons: ',count
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized binary64 error: ',max_double
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized binary32 error: ',max_single
  print '(a)', 'PASS correlation'
contains
  subroutine check_complex(actual,expected,tolerance,single)
    complex(kind=8), intent(in) :: actual(:),expected(:)
    real(kind=8), intent(in) :: tolerance
    logical, intent(in) :: single
    if(size(actual)/=size(expected))error stop 'Wrong output size'
    if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(real(actual,8))))error stop 'Nonfinite real output'
    if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(actual))))error stop 'Nonfinite imaginary output'
    scale=max(1.0_8,maxval(abs(expected)))
    error=maxval(abs(actual-expected))/scale
    if(error>tolerance)then
      print *,nx,ny,pattern,error,tolerance
      error stop 'Cross-correlation differs from direct sums'
    end if
    if(single)then
      max_single=max(max_single,error)
    else
      max_double=max(max_double,error)
    end if
    count=count+1
  end subroutine
end program
```

Complete main program compiled and run locally on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), 2026-11-06. All 588 four-overload vector comparisons passed direct-sum references. The wrapper/main use -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow. The unchanged kernel uses -O0 -g -ffree-line-length-none -fallow-argument-mismatch -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow without bounds checks. See drivers/fftpack-correlation/ for hashes, saved results, warnings, tolerances and scope. This is not a normalized correlation coefficient or a verification of all backend memory accesses.

Complex rank-one transform returning an allocatable COMPLEX(rk) array. Import rk from fftpack; this pin defines rk=REAL64. Optional N defaults to SIZE(X), truncates if smaller and zero-pads if larger; use a positive transform length. FFT calls ZFFTF and IFFT calls ZFFTB, with no division by N in either wrapper: IFFT(FFT(X)) is N*X, so divide the inverse by N for a normalized round trip. X is not overwritten; work arrays are allocated internally. No status argument is exposed. The declarations are the generic public interface; separate submodules implement the functions.

Usage:

```fortran
VALUE = fft(X[,N])
```

Argument declarations: [src/fftpack.f90:223–227](https://github.com/fortran-lang/fftpack/blob/0fffe7c05a918363a7cc12ae138a695afd115f36/src/fftpack.f90#L223-L227).

**J1a2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected 1D COMPLEX(real64) dcfft1/dicfft1 bindings allocate FFTW-aligned complex storage, create an in-place FFTW_ESTIMATE plan, copy input after planning, execute the forward/backward FFTW call, copy output and destroy/free the plan/buffer. The public fft/ifft generics select these specifics for complex double vectors. Forward is unscaled; inverse divides by the requested length. Optional num(1) truncates input or pads trailing zeros; output is allocatable and replaced on entry. This supports J1a2 as an interface to an external complex DFT implementation, not a new FFT-kernel audit. Each call plans afresh; there is no persistent plan/wisdom reuse in this path. Nonpositive lengths are not validated before allocation/planning, failure uses STOP 1 rather than a status result, and module/caller precision and C interoperability must match the linked FFTW build. Real, other-rank, single-precision and shift families are outside this source review. No wrapper tests, FFTW execution, scaling comparison or timing was run.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use fftw3_wrapper, only: fft, ifft
complex(real64) :: input(4)
complex(real64), allocatable :: spectrum(:), restored(:)
input=cmplx(0.0_real64,0.0_real64,real64)
input(1)=cmplx(1.0_real64,0.0_real64,real64)
call fft(spectrum,input)
! Unscaled impulse spectrum is one in each bin.
call ifft(restored,spectrum)
```

Uncompiled fragment; no spectrum or round-trip error was checked. Outputs must be allocatable and must not alias the input. The distributed module references single- and double-precision FFTW symbols, so the documented build links both libfftw3 and libfftw3f and needs the FFTW fftw3.f03 include file. Use positive lengths representable in C_INT. Optional resizing changes the transformed sequence; an inverse after truncation is not recovery of discarded samples. No plan reuse or concurrency guarantee was tested.

**G2h3b1b — source-reviewed**

filterSD solves local nonlinear programming with two-sided bounds on variables and nonlinear constraint values. It maps workspace and dispatches filter_SD, whose inspected phase-one/phase-two control uses GLCPD linearized subproblems, feasibility/objective filter tests and projection/step evaluations. External functions and gradients callbacks provide objective/constraints and their first derivatives; a reduced-Hessian/limited-memory mechanism is internal, not a required user Hessian. G2h3b1b records smooth nonlinear equality/inequality constrained optimization with supplied first derivatives. Supply matching dense or sparse derivative backends, invariant sparse structure and COMMON block settings including workspace capacities. X needs N+M storage; multipliers and final violation are distinct from a success certificate. IFAIL=3 means a locally infeasible point, not proof that the original feasible set is empty. IFAIL>=7 can return before workspace is scattered into X/AL. No NLP, derivative checks or GLCPD/kernel accuracy audit was executed.

Protocol fragment requiring problem callbacks, array allocation, workspace/COMMON settings and linked BLOCK DATA defaults; copying the call alone is insufficient. **G4c — source-reviewed**

checkd perturbs one variable at a time by caller-supplied nonzero AL increments and compares each objective/constraint forward difference quotient with the supplied derivatives at both endpoints, using backend AIJ access. G4c records a first-derivative consistency diagnostic, not numerical certification of analytic derivatives. An inconsistency is printed and causes immediate RETURN without a machine-readable status or restoring the current perturbed X(i); preserve X before calling. Normal completion restores coordinates and prints an exit message. Insufficient workspaces STOP the process. A quotient between endpoint derivatives can pass despite an incorrect derivative, and cancellation/domain violations depend on the chosen increments/tolerance. No diagnostic was run.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected findiff and findiff_multiscale paths perturb each coordinate and combine symmetric 3-, 5-, 7- or 9-point stencils to approximate a square vector-function Jacobian. findiffhes instead differences a supplied square Jacobian callback and returns a rank-three derivative tensor; it does not directly compute a scalar Hessian from scalar function values. The order argument selects stencil point count, not derivative order or a certified accuracy order. All reviewed interfaces use iso_fortran_env real128, require nonzero suitable perturbations and provide no automatic step selection, error estimate or status. The generic stencil fallback is three-point with a printed warning. The author test files select real64 while the module selects real128 and need consistent kinds/imports before they can serve as drivers. The matrix-in-time and multiscale-tensor paths are not included in this review. No stencil error or compilation failure was reproduced.

**G2h3b1 — source-reviewed**

FIRD solves smooth nonlinear programs with equality/inequality constraints and variable bounds. The fird wrapper requires objective-value, constraint-value and constraint-Jacobian callbacks. dfoirfalg actually calls the user Jacobian to form linearized constraints and passes it to restoration, while the objective interface requests no derivatives. The author guide (doc/doc.tex, lines 99-123 at this revision) explicitly assumes continuously differentiable objective and constraint functions. G2h3b1 is retained deliberately: G2h3b1a would falsely imply no user derivatives, while G2h3b1b requires objective derivatives as well as constraint derivatives. No GAMS leaf exactly represents this mixed interface. Default restoration delegates to external ALGENCAN; source inspection does not establish a standalone solver or successful convergence. The HS14 author example is a future driver candidate, not a checked solve.

**L8 — documentation-reviewed**

**L8e1b3 — source-reviewed**

The public BOOTSTRAP workflow reads (x,y,sigma_y) observations, forms residuals (y-model)/sigma_y and invokes NL2SNO twice per fit, using finite-difference Jacobians rather than supplied derivatives. MONTE_CARLO_FIT_DATA first fits original data, then repeatedly perturbs each observation by independent Gaussian error scaled by its supplied sigma and refits, accumulating parameter/derived-property dispersion. These are parametric Monte Carlo perturbations, not resampling empirical rows. The pinned model is a+b*exp(-alpha*x); changing it requires editing private model/initialization/property procedures, not passing a callback to the public workflow. The fixed replication count is 100000. NL2SNO status IV is not checked between/after the two calls, so failed fits can enter reported summaries. Require positive observation errors and more observations than parameters for reduced chi-squared reporting. This is weighted nonlinear least-squares parameter estimation with model-specific simulation uncertainty, not a universal accuracy claim or the standard error of the Monte Carlo mean.

**D6 — source-reviewed**

ZHZL1SA is a public module procedure included into HIF_HZ, not a standalone external routine or LAPACK-compatible driver. Match DWP, default INTEGER, SIMD/alignment parameters and the JACSD/VN/JSTRAT and BLAS/OpenMP build; the GNU make fragment uses -fdefault-integer-8. H(LDH,N) and S(LDS,N) are overwritten, Z(LDZ,N) is initialized internally to identity then accumulated, and JVEC(M) encodes the diagonal signature with entries +1/-1. Selected usage requires M>=N>=2, even N, aligned leading dimensions/storage, a valid noncolliding JS/JSPAIR schedule generated through JSTRAT, NSWP>=1, valid CPR/TPC and enough stack storage for vector/thread scratch. The actual OpenMP team size must not exceed CPR because thread IDs index CPR-wide scratch arrays; disable dynamic team sizing and configure the matching team explicitly. Preserve original factors for residual checks. INFO<0 is an input rejection; for nonempty valid work INFO is the sweep index, so positive INFO<=NSWP can be normal and NSWP+1 means the sweep budget was exhausted. Internal STOPs and floating-point failures are not fully represented by INFO. The selected positive-signature JVEC=+1 case is a complex generalized singular-value decomposition of the factor pair (H0,S0), with S0 full column rank and suitable regularity. One-sided Hari-Zimmermann pair transformations act on H, S and the accumulated Z; final column normalization returns SY/SW and scales Z, giving factor relations H0*Z=H_out*diag(SY) and S0*Z=S_out*diag(SW). These generalized values/vectors use project conventions rather than ordinary singular values of one matrix. EY/EW are pre-normalization squared factor-column norms, EE=EY/EW, and SY/SW are normalized together with SS. This mapping remains at GAMS D6 because that hierarchy does not distinguish this generalized factor-pair decomposition cleanly. Review covers public contract, selected Gram accumulation, transformation application and final normalization; not every pair formula, hyperbolic degeneracy, rank-deficient case or convergence proof.

**D4b3 — source-reviewed**

ZHZL1SA is a public module procedure included into HIF_HZ, not a standalone external routine or LAPACK-compatible driver. Match DWP, default INTEGER, SIMD/alignment parameters and the JACSD/VN/JSTRAT and BLAS/OpenMP build; the GNU make fragment uses -fdefault-integer-8. H(LDH,N) and S(LDS,N) are overwritten, Z(LDZ,N) is initialized internally to identity then accumulated, and JVEC(M) encodes the diagonal signature with entries +1/-1. Selected usage requires M>=N>=2, even N, aligned leading dimensions/storage, a valid noncolliding JS/JSPAIR schedule generated through JSTRAT, NSWP>=1, valid CPR/TPC and enough stack storage for vector/thread scratch. The actual OpenMP team size must not exceed CPR because thread IDs index CPR-wide scratch arrays; disable dynamic team sizing and configure the matching team explicitly. Preserve original factors for residual checks. INFO<0 is an input rejection; for nonempty valid work INFO is the sweep index, so positive INFO<=NSWP can be normal and NSWP+1 means the sweep budget was exhausted. Internal STOPs and floating-point failures are not fully represented by INFO. The signature-weighted factor representation defines a complex Hermitian pencil A=H0^H*diag(JVEC)*H0 and B=S0^H*S0. With S0 full column rank, B is positive definite, and simultaneous diagonalization produces generalized eigenvalues EE=EY/EW and right directions in Z. EY is accumulated with JVEC and may be signed; EW is a nonnegative ordinary factor norm. This is a factor-based Hermitian-definite generalized eigenproblem, not a driver accepting arbitrary A/B arrays or general nonsymmetric pencils. The procedure normalizes H/S and scales Z after the sweep; original-pencil residuals must use original factors, not overwritten arrays. Require valid signature and regular/well-conditioned factors consistent with the method; unverified isotropic/degenerate pairs are outside the selected contract. Review covers signature Gram accumulation, common right transformations, ratio extraction and status/normalization, not all pair kernels or numerical eigenpair accuracy.

**C7a — source-reviewed**

The public FMZM GAMMA generic dispatches the real FM derived type to FMGAM, using configurable multiprecision arithmetic rather than machine-real GAMMA. The inspected core checks special/pole cases, caches nearby arguments, shifts to a larger argument, evaluates log-gamma/exponential and reverses the shift; negative noninteger arguments use reflection. Precision increases and retry logic respond to cancellation, subject to configured storage/exponent limits and global KFLAG diagnostics. The sketch restricts the domain to a positive real value, avoiding pole/reflection subtleties. FM_SET determines requested decimal precision; decimal strings avoid importing machine-precision literal rounding. Shared FMVALS scratch/caches and state mean ordinary concurrent calls need isolation. This is the pinned historical TOMS814 distribution, not a review of newer FM releases. Review covers the real generic and selected gamma paths, not every elementary or complex special function.

The public FMZM BETA generic dispatches two real FM arguments to FMBETA. The core uses gamma ratios in one branch and exponentiated log-gamma combinations in another to handle large arguments, with special cases and cancellation retries under the shared precision/diagnostic state. The sketch uses positive parameters, where beta is the standard complete beta function; incomplete beta, complex continuation and probability-tail accuracy are not inferred. This mapping records a concrete complete-beta implementation in the historical FM distribution. It is not merely the presence of GAMMA in a README, and no runtime accuracy/overflow comparison was performed.

**G1a1a — source-reviewed**

The public FMIN function performs smooth scalar minimization without user derivatives over an initial interval. It uses safeguarded parabolic interpolation with golden-section fallback and a stopping scale SQRT(EPSILON)*ABS(X)+TOL/3. This modern package places F before AX/BX, unlike some textbook interfaces of the same name. The return is only a minimizer estimate; no convergence/status output or evaluation budget is exposed. This independent review records the public interfaces, dispatch and caller contracts, not a new numerical execution check or audit of every dependency/kernel. The existing problem-specific hosted drivers remain separate. No upstream numerical source is bundled.

Public entry point `fmin_module::fmin`: [src/fmin_module.F90:85–225](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/fmin/blob/3d094fba0e9b98d132414f8442c7c76d32da1d30/src/fmin_module.F90#L85-L225).

Scalar derivative-free minimizer combining golden-section and parabolic steps. The objective function F(X) is the first argument, followed by ordered interval endpoints AX/BX and nonnegative TOL; the result XMIN is an abscissa, not the minimum function value. Reevaluate F(XMIN) if its value is needed. Import fmin_rk to match the preprocessed real kind (REAL64 by default); callback argument and result have that kind. The source has no status, iteration-count or maximum-evaluation argument; its unbounded loop exits on an interval/machine-precision condition. Finite objective values and a suitable unimodal interval are caller responsibilities; multimodal, invalid-input and nontermination behavior are not certified by this review. The upstream source filename is case-sensitive fmin_module.F90.

Usage:

```fortran
XMIN = fmin(F,AX,BX,TOL)
```

Argument declarations: [src/fmin_module.F90:89–95](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/fmin/blob/3d094fba0e9b98d132414f8442c7c76d32da1d30/src/fmin_module.F90#L89-L95).

**A3c — source-reviewed**

The selected FMPFR interface wraps an allocated MPFR object with defined construction, assignment, arithmetic and finalization. The safe reviewed string constructor allocates storage and initializes it at the configured default BIT precision; addition allocates a result at the maximum operand precision and calls the C glue/MPFR add operation. A newly assigned result gets at least the default/source precision, but assigning into an already allocated lower-precision object does not automatically enlarge it. The module default rounding variable has no declaration initializer, so the sketch explicitly sets it before constructing values. Selected explicit-precision string and exponential wrappers elsewhere call MPFR initialization on an unallocated component and are excluded from this sketch. This is a binding/ownership/dispatch review, not a verification of MPFR arithmetic or the full generated configuration/ABI.

[README.md](https://github.com/giacrossi/FOLLIA/blob/892d23aaaa36b2fa27dbd524cf79b282dc1e31bd/README.md)

**E1b — source-reviewed**

The inspected type generates S separate degree-at-most-S-1 Lagrange polynomials on overlapping S-point stencils drawn from 2*S-1 nodes. compute_coefficients forms the product-form basis at one target, and compute_interpolations applies each stencil column to stored Y values, returning S estimates. E1b records single-polynomial interpolation within each stencil; the source does not choose or combine these estimates into one piecewise or WENO interpolant. Default coordinates are the integers -S+1..S-1; optional coordinates must provide the same 2*S-1 layout with distinct increasing values. S>=2 is required by the initializer accesses to x(-1), x(0) and x(1), but is not validated. The target must lie between the midpoints adjacent to x(0) and must not equal x(0); failure uses ERROR STOP. No duplicate-node, ordering or optional-array-size check is supplied, and no error estimate/status is returned. Recompute coefficients after changing coordinates/target. No polynomial reproduction or driver execution was checked.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

integrator_runge_kutta_ssp::integrate forms explicit Runge-Kutta stages using the integrand arithmetic and time-derivative binding, then accumulates the weighted derivative stages into U. Initialization selects a Butcher table and allocates stage storage using a concrete integrand prototype. I1a1a records explicit one-step ODE initial-value methods, scoped to standard three-stage third-order SSP stepping. The caller supplies DT and advances time; the optional NEW_DT is set equal to DT and supplies no adaptive control. An SSP label requires a compatible spatial operator and step restriction; it is not unconditional stability or positivity. Concrete integrands must implement the deferred arithmetic, assignment, description, dimension and derivative contracts. Fast mode, coarrays, other tables and multistep schemes are outside this review. No ODE solution or order/stability test was run.

**G1a1a — source-reviewed**

biss_1d compares objective values at two interior points separated by 20 percent of the current interval, then discards one side until interval width falls below tolerance. G1a1a records a derivative-free scalar minimization search on a suitable unimodal bracket, not a root bisection despite its name. imode=1 minimizes; other values maximize. The routine prints the estimate and optionally writes iteration data, but returns neither a minimizer argument nor a success flag. Initialized local tol/kmax/mode variables have implicit SAVE, so omitted optional settings can inherit previous calls. Iteration exhaustion uses STOP; no bracket/unimodality/NaN validation is supplied. The similarly named golden routine has an unguarded optional-unit write and is not the recommended entry here. No objective or bracket reduction was executed.

**G1a1c — source-reviewed**

newton_1d takes f0 as the objective, f as its first derivative and fprime as its second derivative, then performs x <- x - f/fprime until the first derivative is small. G1a1c records this derivative-supplied smooth scalar stationary-point search as a minimization primitive. It does not establish positive curvature or reject maxima/saddles. Zero second derivative and iteration exhaustion use STOP; initialized local tolerance/limit are saved across calls. The optional output unit id is used unconditionally inside the iteration, so supply a valid id. Results are printed rather than returned. No stationary point, minimum or Newton convergence was numerically checked.

**L10a2e — source-reviewed**

FA_KF_PREDICT applies x=F*x and P=F*P*F-transpose+Q. FA_KF_UPDATE computes innovations, gates individual measurements by squared innovation over diagonal innovation variance, extracts the retained full covariance submatrix, solves the SPD innovation system, and applies a Joseph-form covariance update. All C-boundary matrices are flat row-major, not ordinary Fortran column-major arrays. VALIDITY is output: +1 fused, 0 skipped above 9, -1 rejected above 16 (or degenerate diagonal); if no values are fused, state/covariance remain at prediction with INFO=0. Cholesky solve failure maps to INFO=4; invalid dimensions to 3. Covariance consistency/finite values are not comprehensively checked. Some helper calls alias input/output arrays despite differing INTENTs and need compiler/alias-contract review. The sketch uses a scalar model to avoid layout ambiguity. Review covers the linear KF path and matrix-solve helper, not every EKF/UKF/particle-filter variant.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `95abadba7c3e774ca58dc2fe1e7d6a572b7cb031`.

**H2a1a2 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed Newton-Cotes method evaluates a concrete integrand object at n+1 equally spaced nodes on a finite interval. init selects closed-rule weights for degrees 1..10, and integrate_1D performs a single fixed weighted sum without a tolerance or error estimate, supporting the nonautomatic callback quadrature leaf H2a1a2. Source finding: weights use the usual h=(b-a)/n normalization but the final multiplication uses (b-a)*k without dividing by n. Thus degrees above one appear scaled by n; the calling sketch is restricted to n=1 (trapezoidal rule). Unsupported degrees are not rejected and leave zero weights; no success status is returned. The inherited adaptive_integrate reads an INTENT(OUT) accumulator before defining it and is excluded from the calling sketch. 2D/3D bindings are empty result-returning stubs and receive no mapping. No quadrature output was run or checked.

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected 1D Romberg path starts with the endpoint trapezoidal rule, halves the mesh, evaluates newly introduced odd nodes, and builds Richardson extrapolation columns using 4**k. It stops when the absolute difference between the last two columns meets tol, within an n-level budget, supporting automatic finite-interval callback quadrature H2a1a1. This is global refinement, not local adaptive subdivision or a proven error bound. Important source finding: if the loop exhausts its budget without EXIT, i becomes n+1 and the returned R(i,i) is outside the allocated 0:n table. Nonpositive budgets/tolerances are not validated and no failure status is returned. Resolve this exhaustion path before relying on the routine. The 2D/3D methods are unimplemented stubs and are not mapped. No integration or failure case was reproduced by execution.

**L1a1a — source-reviewed**

The public MEAN generic selects single/double precision implementations computing an optionally masked arithmetic mean. The selected DP function divides SUM(DAT,MASK)/COUNT(MASK), without missing-value recognition beyond the caller mask. It checks mask shape via STOP but has no guard against an empty/all-false selection, whose count becomes zero. NaN handling and overflow/compensated summation are not supplied by this interface. This is location summarization, not an estimator of a fitted probability distribution. Review covers the double-precision masked mean and public generic, not every statistical utility.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `db2a6b255a2540b910cec369ed52144dd21867dd`.

**L1a1b — source-reviewed**

The public VARIANCE generic computes sample variance of optionally masked data using centered sums and the correction (SUM((x-mean)^2)-SUM(x-mean)^2/n)/(n-1). At least two selected observations are required; violations/mask mismatches use STOP rather than an INFO return. This selected function always uses n-1 and does not expose the population option of the separate MOMENT subroutine. Floating-point cancellation, nonfinite data and near-zero negative rounding outcomes are not independently validated. Review covers the DP function, not all optional-output combinations of MOMENT.

**L1b — source-reviewed**

The public COVARIANCE generic summarizes two arrays with an optional shared mask, subtracting each selected mean and dividing the product sum by n (population-style normalization). It requires at least two selected values and matching array/mask lengths. The CORRELATION sibling divides this n-normalized covariance by sample standard deviations from MOMENT, so its output is attenuated by (n-1)/n relative to the usual Pearson coefficient on finite nonconstant data; that normalization requires review before interpreting it as Pearson r. The promoted calling sketch therefore uses COVARIANCE only. No hypothesis test, missing-data policy beyond masking, or statistical inference is provided by this summary interface.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `db2a6b255a2540b910cec369ed52144dd21867dd`.

**P — source-reviewed**

The public S1850 wrapper exposes intersections between a SISL spline curve and a line in 2D or plane in 3D. It forwards the curve C pointer, point/normal, tolerances and dimension to the separately installed SISL C routine, copies isolated intersection parameters and transfers intersection-curve pointers into Fortran objects. This is computational geometry P; the catalog does not infer a root-finding or interpolation leaf from the external implementation. Review covers the actual binding and ownership/status path, not the C intersection algorithm. Important wrapper defects need repair: CINTCURVE is not initialized before ASSOCIATED is tested on all paths, and INTCURVECTOF is called with INTCURVE(I) after the loop leaves I beyond the allocated range when overlaps are returned. Zero-count branches can also leave previously allocated output arrays stale. Inspect counts and status, initialize/fix pointer handling and follow the package C/Fortran ownership helpers before reuse; return alone does not establish valid geometric output.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `dad6e123b70495ff627e14314c182b3118287b86`.

**L14a1b — source-reviewed**

The public KMEANS object fits dense nonhierarchical Euclidean clusters through repeated nearest-centroid assignments and centroid updates, with random/kmeans++ initialization, optional explicit initial centers, restarts and empty-cluster relocation. X has observation rows and feature columns; PREDICT returns one-based labels in an (N,1) allocatable INT64 matrix. SCORE returns a nonnegative-style sum of squared distances, not sklearn negative inertia. The selected sketch uses N_INIT=1 and default unchunked storage: the demo passes real-valued N_INIT/CHUNK_SIZE although the inspected constructor requires INT64, and the multi-restart chunked path passes the unallocated whole-distance matrix. The iteration helper also marks persistent input state INTENT(OUT) while reading it, and convergence checks can touch initially unset previous centroids. Those state contracts require repair/validation before relying on fits. OpenBLAS thread control and RNG state are global side effects. Review is source-based, not a validated clustering implementation.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

gauss_legendre builds nodes/weights by Newton iterations on the Legendre three-term recurrence and mirrors the half-rule. gauss_legendre_ab applies affine node/weight scaling; gauss_lobatto_legendre includes both endpoints and iterates on the derivative roots. H2c records quadrature-rule generation, not an automatic integrator or a requested-accuracy guarantee. Despite the header mentioning Golub-Welsch, the selected Legendre implementation is Newton/recurrence, not an eigenvalue solve. The Newton loops have a fixed 16-iteration cap with no returned nonconvergence flag; invalid point counts ERROR STOP. The Lobatto API requires N>=2, Legendre N>=1. The separate generalized-Laguerre/QL and derivative-product paths are outside this scoped mapping. No quadrature moments or convergence was checked by execution.

**D4a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected dense ordinary-problem path projects a real symmetric matrix into a basis, dispatches DSYEV on the projected matrix, forms Ritz vectors/residuals, appends diagonal-preconditioned corrections and reorthogonalizes/restarts the basis. This mapping is restricted to METHOD=DPR with SECOND_MATRIX absent; generalized and matrix-free paths remain outside this review. The convergence check uses residual norms, despite argument prose describing eigenvalue error. HAS_CONVERGED flags remain true across iterations, so ALL(HAS_CONVERGED) need not mean all current residuals satisfy tolerance. DPR divides by eigenvalue-minus-diagonal without a near-zero safeguard. Initial basis has 2*LOWEST columns and expansion can exceed limits without robust shape validation. No numerical convergence or complete LAPACK/helper audit was performed.

**C8 — source-reviewed**

The public FERF generic selects elemental real32/real64 approximations to erf. Both inspected bindings compute SIGN(1-(1+0.278393*abs(x)+0.230389*x**2+0.000972*abs(x)*x**2+0.078108*x**4)**(-4),x). This is a fixed-coefficient approximation, not a high-accuracy replacement for intrinsic ERF, ERFC or scaled tails. Extra precision in the DP interface does not add coefficient accuracy. Squaring/polynomial powers can overflow for large inputs, and no exceptional-value handling, error estimate or status is provided. Only FERF, not the library reductions/logarithm/trigonometric approximations, is source reviewed; neither speed nor numerical error was measured.

**G2h3b — source-reviewed**

FILTERSLP partitions real/integer workspaces and dispatches a legacy filter sequential-linear-programming method for the supported nonlinear model representation with two-sided variable/constraint bounds. SLP_MAIN obtains model function/gradient values, solves LP subproblems through EMSOL, compares objective/constraint-violation filter entries, and adjusts the trust region. It is a local nonlinear-programming method, not global optimization or a replacement for an arbitrary user-callback library. OBJFUN/CONFUN/GRADIENT operate on repository model/global state and packed USER/IUSER storage; bounds/scales/control COMMON blocks require initialization by the supplied driver. The broad equality/inequality nonlinear class is retained rather than asserting unsupported derivative-callback or Hessian options. IFAIL/RIFAIL and workspace exhaustion must be interpreted; allocated output arrays alone do not imply convergence. Review covers workspace dispatch and selected LP/filter/gradient paths, not EMSOL internals or all model-parser representations.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `32ede00787a65cb934356bd136f9b8a7f954f853`.

**L4c1a — source-reviewed**

The selected fit routine estimates a multivariate Gaussian mixture by alternating E-step log-density/log-sum-exp responsibilities and M-step weighted means/covariances, with BLAS products and Cholesky-derived precisions. This supports parametric analysis of independent multidimensional observations. It is not K-means or a proof of finding the global likelihood maximum. Components must be allocated and initialized before fit; empty-component responsibility sums can divide by zero and covariance factorization failures STOP. regCovar is a module variable initially zero. The stopping condition is a signed likelihood improvement per sample, with no iteration cap or returned convergence status, so a decreasing/nonfinite objective can also end iteration. No fit or statistical validation was run.

**D5 — source-reviewed**

The linalg::gramSchmidt routine extends an existing set of orthonormal columns using modified Gram-Schmidt: each new vector is repeatedly projected against prior columns using the CURRENT residual, then normalized. It returns orthonormal columns only, not an R factor. Require 0<=nu<=n<=d, normalized independent existing columns, and independent residual vectors. There is no rank detection, reorthogonalization, zero-norm check or returned status, so dependent/nearly dependent inputs need caller treatment. This selected small module routine is distinct from the repository mixture estimator and is not a BLAS/LAPACK eigenvalue review.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `473ff4e032ab0d8472c87b1f580fc82db1d73cf2`.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The program samples cell-center Cartesian grids, ranks objective misfits, retains a chosen number of best cells, and refines their coordinate intervals at successive levels, reusing central model values when applicable. G2i records global-search intent for nonconvex objectives, not a proof of global coverage or convergence after discarding cells. The supplied Example computes Euclidean distance to a three-component fixed aim; users replace source calls. MisExit is not initialized on the ordinary no-target-exit path before being read. ReadCLA tests arg before its first assignment, and Example uses optional arguments in logical expressions without guaranteed short-circuit safety. No run, target flag or search accuracy was checked.

**N6a2a — source-reviewed**

The sort generic dispatches to integer int8/int16/int32/int64 routines that overwrite arr, so this is active internal integer sorting (N6a2a), not passive ranking. The inspected int32 implementation and shared templates partition around a pivot, switch to binary insertion sorting for short ranges and to heapsort at the depth limit. History-enabled variants carry caller-provided labels along with moved values; they still sort arr actively. The actual module name at this pin is mod_introsort, differing from the README usage snippet. The wrapper computes log(size(arr)) before handling empty input; zero-length behavior, stability, concurrency of module max_depth and performance were not checked. No external/file sorting or character/complex-key interface is claimed.

**N6a2a — source-reviewed**

The public quicksort generic dispatches the INTEGER overload to iterative range-stack processing and last-element Lomuto partitioning with <= comparisons. Values are sorted in place in ascending order. The stack is supplied by the caller, avoiding recursive calls and allocations in the core. push_pair silently ignores a range when two more stack slots do not fit, so an undersized stack can return partially unsorted data without a status flag; use the documented 2*N default-integer workspace. Last-element pivots retain quadratic worst cases for ordered/equal data; nonrecursive does not mean bounded linearithmic work. The other kind has its own mapping; no upstream sort/test or timing was run.

Public generic, shown for default INTEGER values and a default-INTEGER work_stack. Both dummies are INTENT(INOUT); stack contents are scratch. For N>=2 use workspace of at least 2*N entries. Empty/singleton arrays return before stack use; there is no success/error output.

Usage:


**N6a2b — source-reviewed**

The public quicksort generic dispatches the REAL overload to iterative range-stack processing and last-element Lomuto partitioning with <= comparisons. Values are sorted in place in ascending order. The stack is supplied by the caller, avoiding recursive calls and allocations in the core. push_pair silently ignores a range when two more stack slots do not fit, so an undersized stack can return partially unsorted data without a status flag; use the documented 2*N default-integer workspace. Last-element pivots retain quadratic worst cases for ordered/equal data; nonrecursive does not mean bounded linearithmic work. NaN handling is not defined for the default-REAL branch. The other kind has its own mapping; no upstream sort/test or timing was run.

**D9b1 — source-reviewed**

The legacy NNLS routine initializes x=0, selects columns using the largest positive dual-gradient component, applies Householder transformations, solves the passive triangular system, and uses a feasibility interpolation/Givens update loop to move nonpositive coefficients back to the zero set. It returns a residual norm and mode, supporting constrained L2 linear least squares D9b1 with x>=0. A and b are overwritten by orthogonal transformations. Mode=1 succeeds, 2 rejects nonpositive M/N, and 3 reports the 3*N iteration limit. Leading dimensions/workspace extents remain caller obligations. This review follows active-set control and the included transformation helpers, not a numerical proof or a complete audit of all package solvers. The simplified module wrapper was inspected but shares a file with a test main; the calling sketch uses the independently linkable legacy routine. No fit or KKT/residual check was executed.

**N6a2a — source-reviewed**

merge_sort_mod::sort overwrites default-integer vectors or reorders integer matrix columns according to a selected reference row, with optional caller-supplied history. Recursive halves are combined by merge_1i/merge_1ih using a temporary copy and a left-first <= comparison. This is active internal integer sorting (N6a2a); the history option is not a rank-only interface. The descending wrapper reverses arr without reversing history, so the ascending-history correspondence must not be assumed to survive reverse=.true. The implementation moves whole columns for 2-D input; it is not independent sorting of every row. No stability guarantee, descending-history check or author example was executed.

**N6a2b — source-reviewed**

The real(sp), real(dp) and real(qp) generic bindings overwrite a vector or permute complete matrix columns using one selected real reference row. The inspected double-precision wrappers and shared merge bodies support active internal real sorting (N6a2b). The optional history is moved during ascending merges; reverse=.true. reverses only the data in the inspected wrappers, so descending history correspondence is not verified and appears inconsistent. Real128 support, NaNs, signed-zero ordering, stability after reversal and extreme sizes were not checked. No passive-rank, character or complex-key mapping is inferred.

The public rearrange generic applies reference_history as a gather permutation. The included 1-D body copies arr(reference_history(i)); the 2-D body copies complete arr(:,reference_history(i)) columns. Default integer and real sp/dp/qp variants are exposed. This supports the N8 permuting leaf, independently of how the permutation was obtained. The caller must supply valid indices with the correct direction; the inspected bodies do not validate a bijection or compute its inverse. The separate descending-sort history discrepancy is retained in the sorting mappings. No bounds, permutation-cycle or round-trip checks were executed.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `792c088d60db7b8f1b9eaf28602b71f1498d69d0cab547ab45e13c29c21f9977`.

**L — documentation-reviewed**

The README lists scalar/vector error metrics and automatic missing-data skipping. These routines assess predictions; they do not themselves produce forecasts. Missing-value and zero-denominator behavior need more detailed review.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `e432d745265027e45ade8197710ba1bb4402e5d2`.

[README.md](https://github.com/tkdhss111/fortran-metrics/blob/e432d745265027e45ade8197710ba1bb4402e5d2/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `0b1bf8f7ee6de4a4cc3ebff4261c6807beb84a415398cbc852d213d00e1b06a4`.

**L1 — source-reviewed**

The vector calc binding forms prediction-minus-observation errors after removing pairs matching the -999 sentinel, then returns N, mean bias, mean absolute error, root mean squared error and a percentage summary. L1 records data/error summarization; these are not confidence intervals or distribution tests. The implemented vector MAPE is SUM(ABS(error)/observation*100)/N, with a signed observation denominator: negative observations can give negative contributions and zero observations divide by zero. Scalar APE instead takes ABS of the percentage error. Arrays must conform, default REAL precision is used, and sentinel matching is not IEEE NaN handling. No outputs were checked by execution.


Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use equal-length finite arrays and positive nonzero observations if using percentage summaries. Legitimate values near the NA sentinel are treated as missing. Vector MAPE uses signed y, not ABS(y). Read components for the active overload only; the object does not reset every component on every call. Allocatable assignment/reallocation is used internally.

**H — documentation-reviewed**

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `f4a61fad769d0d63bbd53a7666fcaf5fc255bd45`.

[README.md](https://github.com/cerea-daml/fnn/blob/f4a61fad769d0d63bbd53a7666fcaf5fc255bd45/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `40062feaaccb7556ffaf3ca9a511b187360a6d6fc84cc499697a3b9434322229`.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The public SequentialNeuralNetwork tangent-linear and adjoint bindings propagate perturbations/cotangents through sequential layers. Unlike an input-only Jacobian API, DP includes packed parameter perturbations and the adjoint returns both parameter and input cotangents. Dense layers pack biases first, followed by the reshaped weight matrix. Call APPLY_FORWARD for the same MEMBER and unchanged parameters/base input first: layer forward_input and activation state supply the linearization trajectory. APPLY_ADJOINT may overwrite the supplied DY; keep a copy for dot-product comparisons. Batch-member storage is mutable, and no automatic shape/member/status checks should be inferred. The inspected dense/tanh path supports a smooth derivative example; dropout modes and ReLU at zero need separate interpretation. Review covers sequential dispatch, dense chain-rule products and tanh derivative implementation, not the complete layer catalogue or executed consistency tests.

**H2a1a2 — source-reviewed**

The selected numerical_integration paths evaluate a user procedure on a finite interval using composite trapezoids or a fixed-depth Romberg tableau. Trapezoids use N panels; Romberg uses N extrapolation levels with nested trapezoid refinement and powers-of-four Richardson extrapolation. H2a1a2 records nonautomatic quadrature: neither routine accepts an accuracy target or returns an error estimate/status. The trapezoid path uses ABS(B-A) and samples upward from A, so require A<B; it does not implement signed reversed-interval integration. Require positive N and keep Romberg depth modest because sample counts grow exponentially and default-integer powers can overflow. Simpson paths in the same module are not included: notably the one-third loop gives the last endpoint an extra interior weight. No integral or educational example was executed.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected public fixed-step solver implements the classical four-stage explicit RK4 formula. The adaptive solver compares one full RK4 step with two half steps and accepts using an unscaled absolute maximum component difference, then adjusts the step with a fifth-root rule. Both solve a callback-defined first-order initial-value system. The fixed interface stores time/state by rows, whereas the adaptive output stores time/state by columns. The fixed routine does not guard a one-column solution buffer before dividing by n_steps-1; the adaptive routine requires a forward interval and a positive meaningful tolerance. Its discrepancy test is not a certified global error bound. I1a1a records one-step nonstiff scope. The separate VSS routine and stiff-system claims are not included in this review.

**N6a1b — source-reviewed**

The inspected REAL(8) overload initializes an index permutation, ranks OpenMP chunks through the bundled REAL64 ORDERPACK-derived merge-ranker, offsets local indices, and repeatedly merges adjacent ranked chunks. A is INTENT(IN); A(order) is the intended ascending sequence. N6a1b records passive internal real sorting, not in-place value mutation. Review covers the REAL(8) wrapper, REAL64 ranker and outer merge, not the other overloads or a parallel scaling/stability proof. Kind 8 must match REAL64 on the compiler. Chunking uses omp_get_max_threads rather than an actual-team-size query, and tiny/empty inputs, large index arithmetic and oversubscribed chunk layouts have not been checked. No OpenMP build, permutation or timing was run.

**L5a1p — source-reviewed**

poisson_log_pmf evaluates k*LOG(lambda)-lambda-LOG(k!) using the log_factorial helper, and poisson_pmf exponentiates that result and converts it to DP. L5a1p records Poisson probability masses/log masses, not cumulative/inverse probabilities or random draws. K is an INTEGER(C_INT), lambda a REAL(C_DOUBLE); log results use REAL(C_LONG_DOUBLE). C_LONG_DOUBLE is platform-dependent and must not be assumed to be IEEE binary128 despite QP comments. This implementation rejects K<0 and lambda<=0 with error -1, including the valid degenerate lambda=0 distribution, rather than returning its mathematical mass. Check ERR_CODE before interpreting sentinel -1 log values. Log-factorial uses a sum for N<35 and LOG_GAMMA(N+1) otherwise; the integer N+1 can overflow at the representable limit. NaNs and every nonfinite case are not explicitly validated. No probability or overflow test was run.

**L5a1n — source-reviewed**

normal_log_pdf computes -LOG(sigma)-LOG(SQRT(2*pi))-0.5*((x-mu)/sigma)**2 in the configured C_LONG_DOUBLE kind; normal_pdf exponentiates and converts to C_DOUBLE. L5a1n records univariate normal densities/log densities, not a CDF, tail probability, inverse or random generator. SIGMA is a positive standard deviation, not variance; nonpositive values return ERR_CODE=-1. The source does not explicitly reject NaNs/nonfinite X/MU/SIGMA. QP is a C_LONG_DOUBLE alias with platform-dependent precision. A log-density sentinel of -1 on failure is not distinguishable from a valid value without checking ERR_CODE. Density conversion can underflow or overflow independently of the log representation. No density values or tail behavior were run.

**N6a1b — source-reviewed**

The public indexx real generic initializes indices, returns that identity permutation if ANY(ISNAN(xx)), and otherwise recursively quick-partitions indices with a small interchange-sort fallback. Values remain INTENT(IN); xx(order) is the intended ascending sequence. This supports passive internal real sorting N6a1b. The low-level public quick_sort instead expects caller-initialized valid indices and has no NaN guard. Equal-key stability is not promised. The integer overload converts to double-precision-valued keys and is outside this mapping; wide integer representability should not be inferred from it. No sort, compiler portability or million-element author example was executed.

quick_sort_in_place initializes an ordering vector, invokes the same internal index quicksort, then assigns list=list(order). This is an active real-array sort N6a2b, but uses O(N) automatic permutation storage rather than constant-extra-space in-place partitioning. Unlike indexx, this wrapper has no NaN check: NaN pivots can prevent scan termination before bounds are crossed. A finite-input precondition is necessary for the reviewed usage. Recursion, worst-case depth and equal-key stability were not tested. No output was generated for this catalog.

[README.md](https://github.com/willklausler/fortran_rationals/blob/ce260c0bb3131d8eab635f116f7815c13f12f874/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `a648a9650a2f8fc9bb8d19246d0f8006778cc5f38ea46f06ee6587eb7cbb0690`.

**A2 — source-reviewed**

The rational type stores reduced INT64 numerator/denominator pairs with positive denominator. The selected integer constructors simplify with Euclidean GCF, reject zero denominators and the most-negative integer, and normalize signs. Rational addition cancels denominator common factors before checked integer products/sums; multiplication cancels cross factors before multiplying. These are exact finite-width rational operations, not arbitrary precision. Error paths use ERROR STOP and some representable final results can still encounter finite intermediate limits; this review does not prove completeness of overflow handling across every operator. Other intrinsic overloads, matrices, random rational generation and formatted I/O are outside this selected arithmetic review.

**A6a — source-reviewed**

The REAL64 rational constructor iterates continued-fraction convergents until conversion back to REAL64 equals the original absolute input, the fractional remainder vanishes, or the next convergent/reciprocal exceeds the finite INT64 bounds. It then restores the sign. Consequently this is a real-to-fraction conversion/approximation, not a promise of representing the exact binary rational or the originally intended decimal. If no round-tripping convergent fits, the last fitting convergent is retained. Nonfinite/out-of-range input reaches ERROR STOP. The reverse REAL overload divides the stored integer components in REAL64 and rounds normally. No round-trip or best-approximation experiment was performed.

**B — source-reviewed**

The public integer gcf and lcm generics expose Euclidean greatest-common-factor calculation and divide-before-checked-multiply least-common-multiple calculation. GCF normalizes with ABS and defines zero cases, including gcf(0,0)=0; LCM returns zero if either input is zero. INT32 overloads compute via INT64 and reject results exceeding INT32. The direct INT64 GCF/LCM path applies ABS without guarding the most-negative representable INT64 input, which is excluded from this mapping usage. B is the available GAMS number-theory leaf; this is not primality or factorization software. No integer-result or boundary tests were run.

**E1b — source-reviewed**

For the explicitly selected finite line element, SHAPEFUNC constructs nodal Lagrange polynomial basis functions and EVAL evaluates them at a requested reference coordinate. An interpolated value is the dot product of nodal data with returned basis values. This E1b mapping is restricted to the univariate polynomial case; it does not conflate reference-element shape functions with scattered-data mesh generation or global spline fitting. Node ordering can be permuted through NODES, so the sketch forms data from the returned COORDS instead of assuming a particular edge/interior order. SET requires a cubature object from the separate fortran_cubatures dependency; invalid setup can ERROR STOP. Review covers finite Lagrange line construction/evaluation, not every simplex/serendipity/infinite-element variant or an executed interpolation result.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use cubatures, only: cubature,CUB_LIN
use shapefuncs, only: shapefunc
type(cubature) :: q
type(shapefunc) :: sf
real(real64),allocatable :: nodal(:),basis(:),derv(:,:),curv(:,:,:)
real(real64) :: value,first,second
q=cubature(CUB_LIN,4)
sf=shapefunc(q,2)
allocate(nodal(sf%nnodes),basis(sf%nnodes),derv(1,sf%nnodes),curv(1,1,sf%nnodes))
nodal=sf%coords(1,:)**2
call sf%eval([0.25_real64],basis,derv,curv)
value=dot_product(nodal,basis)
first=dot_product(nodal,derv(1,:))
second=dot_product(nodal,curv(1,1,:))
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Finite line/polynomial example using the separate cubatures dependency and REAL64. Derivatives are with respect to reference XI, not automatically physical coordinates. No interpolation, node-order or partition-of-unity check was run.

Implementation helper `lagrange`: [src/shapefuncs.f90:687–706](https://github.com/willklausler/fortran_shapefuncs/blob/724caede81540a0b171d2586f94b4da2fe0a4d15/src/shapefuncs.f90#L687-L706).

**H1 — source-reviewed**

SHAPEFUNC%EVAL also returns analytic first and second derivatives of each basis function in reference coordinates. LAGRANGE propagates value/first/second derivatives through product factors; EVAL_PRODUCTS assembles mixed derivatives and applies the constant factor-coordinate chain rule, symmetrizing curvature. This is numerical evaluation of analytic basis derivatives, not finite-difference differentiation of an arbitrary callback. Physical-space gradients/Hessians require the appropriate geometric mapping, including extra terms for nonaffine maps; returning reference curvature does not perform that transformation. Infinite directions have singularities at XI=1. The selected sketch uses a finite line and differentiates an interpolated nodal polynomial. Review covers product/chain-rule formulas, not verified high-order conditioning, geometric Jacobians or all special element families.

**N5c — source-reviewed**

FINDI performs a binary search for an exactly equal default-REAL key in an ascending array, returning the matching one-based index or -1. N5c records searching on a key, not insertion position, an interpolation bracket or approximate floating-point comparison. Empty N=0 and one-element cases follow the same outer-bound loop; N must be nonnegative and agree with the actual array capacity. Duplicates can yield any encountered match. NaN keys/comparands are not a meaningful ordering and are not rejected. Computing R=N+1 can still overflow even though the midpoint uses a difference formula. The README makes no guarantee of compiler-independent speed; none was benchmarked. No search cases were run.

**L10a2a1 — source-reviewed**

The public ARMA_ACVF function forms theoretical autocovariances for a supplied causal ARMA model using a state transition/loading representation and fixed-point iteration of the stationary state covariance. It then propagates lag vectors to extract covariance at lags zero through MAX_LAG. These are model-implied covariances, not estimates from a sample. The sketch uses a stable AR(1), positive innovation variance and explicitly allocated empty MA coefficients. Invalid lag/variance returns an empty array; covariance iteration is capped and a failure returns HUGE-valued entries rather than a general status. A finite-value test alone does not reject that finite sentinel, and this routine does not independently prove model stability. Review covers state representation, iterative covariance and lag extraction, not the many unrelated translated time-series packages in the repository.

**L10a2d3 — source-reviewed**

ARMA_FORECAST uses a supplied ARMA model, theoretical covariance and the innovations recursion to recover sample innovations and extend the centered AR/MA recurrence. It adds the sample mean back and builds normal prediction intervals from accumulated squared infinite-MA weights times innovation variance. This is ARMA forecasting L10a2d3, not model selection, parameter fitting or a parameter-uncertainty interval. Even for a supplied model, centering uses the current sample mean rather than a stored model intercept. Require allocated AR and MA arrays, stable valid parameters, positive variance/horizon and a confidence level strictly inside (0,1). The returned INFO distinguishes input/innovation errors, but the covariance helper finite-HUGE sentinel warrants additional model/diagnostic validation. Review covers forecast recursion, innovations dispatch and interval construction, not empirical coverage or all transformed/nonlinear variants.

**L10a2c2 — source-reviewed**

The public BURG_FIT helper estimates univariate autoregressive coefficients by forward/backward prediction-error recursion. It demeans the series, computes reflection coefficients from paired errors, updates AR coefficients and innovation variance, then forms an approximate covariance matrix using an empirical Toeplitz matrix inverse. This supports AR parameter estimation, not automatic order selection or a global likelihood optimum. Input order must be positive and smaller than sample size; zero variance, degenerate error denominators, vanished innovation variance and failed covariance inversion have INFO returns. Reflections are clipped to [-1,1], and equality at a boundary can drive the variance failure path, so the header stable claim is not used as an unconditional guarantee. Review covers the native shared Burg implementation rather than only the ITSMR wrapper; covariance outputs are approximations, not verified inferential coverage.

**N6a2a — source-reviewed**

The committed generated INTEGER(INT32) no-history overload dispatches small arrays to binary insertion sort, detects ascending/descending runs, extends short runs, maintains a run stack and merges it. The default OPTMLVL=1 merge copies the shorter run and merges forwards/backwards; OPTMLVL=0 is the simple merge. This supports active internal integer sorting N6a2a. Private tsort_int32 is reached through public sort. Source findings qualify the implementation: run discovery reads array(start_+1) without guarding a final singleton run; descending runs admit equal keys before reversal, so stable tie ordering is not established. Module-wide gallop variables are reset on calls, so do not assume reentrancy. History, real overloads, optimization-level 2 and asymptotic/performance claims were not verified, and no sort was executed.

**F1b — source-reviewed**

toolkit::brent accepts a real scalar callback, checks a specifically oriented sign bracket, and uses inverse quadratic interpolation or a secant formula to generate trials and replace bracket endpoints. F1b records its general scalar-equation interface, not minimization despite copied maximizing/minimizing comments. This scoped source finding does not certify equivalence to a fully safeguarded Brent-Dekker method: there is no inspected trial-acceptance test forcing a fallback bisection when interpolation leaves the interval. The implementation requires F(x0)<=0 and F(x1)>=0 even though it later contains a bracket-reordering branch. IND=10/11 are endpoint-root returns; 20/21 reject the sign orientation. X and IY can be unassigned on early failures and IY counts only selected trial evaluations, excluding endpoints and repeated F(xc). TOL is used for both residual and interval tests. No root or safeguard test was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `7eb273a73fdcd596a6fa5f3c2660c38e8213f30b`.

**L4a1a5 — source-reviewed**

The module provides fixed-lambda Yeo-Johnson and Box-Cox transformations plus lambda selectors using golden-section maximization on [-3,3] with tolerance 0.001. This supports transformation selection, but it is not a validated maximum-likelihood estimator: both internal objectives compute sqrt(sample variance) into var_z. In the Yeo-Johnson objective, -0.5*n*log(var_z) therefore weights log standard deviation by half the usual coefficient relative to the unchanged Jacobian term, changing the optimization criterion. In the Box-Cox selector the geometric-mean scaling absorbs the Jacobian and the same factor is an overall positive likelihood scaling, which by itself leaves the maximizing lambda unchanged. The Box-Cox selector also computes log(x) before any positivity shift, unlike box_cox_lambda which shifts a nonpositive dataset by 1-min(x). Constant/short data, nonpositive selector inputs, overflow, near-zero cancellation and convergence/global optimality are not guarded. The sketch deliberately uses fixed lambdas and does not recommend the Yeo-Johnson selector without objective correction and validation; the Box-Cox selector still requires strictly positive data.

**L6a14 — source-reviewed**

rnorm generates default-REAL normal variates by the Box-Muller sine/cosine transform of intrinsic RANDOM_NUMBER uniforms, then applies mean and sd (defaults zero and one). It handles odd lengths by discarding the second member of the last pair. RANDOM_NUMBER can return zero, but the code does not reject/resample u1=0 before log(u1); negative n, sd<0, exceptional values and seed reproducibility are not validated. This mapping records the implemented generator, not a distributional test or a portable reproducibility guarantee.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The two-dimensional square-stencil path constructs tensor-polynomial reconstruction matrices from cell integrals, solves for ideal sub-stencil coefficients and blends reconstructed point values with WENO-Z smoothness weights and positive/negative coefficient splitting. E2a records reconstruction on a gridded bivariate stencil, scoped to cell-average inputs rather than scattered point interpolation or a complete PDE solver. Initialize the stencil, add evaluation points and compute ideal coefficients before rank-two reconstruct. The inspected inversion helper has INTENT(OUT) IERR but assigns it only on failure; its success return is undefined and is then checked by setup. This must be resolved/validated before relying on the setup status. REAL(16) setup arithmetic and preprocessing limit portability. NDEBUG removes size checks; reconstruction does not return an accuracy estimate or enforce positivity. Other widths/masks, rhombus and one-dimensional paths are excluded. No reconstruction or formal-order test was run.

[README.md](https://github.com/suzuyuyuyu/fortran-approx/blob/23e6a461c6e6db03f01e31cf8ea135f17f5de95a/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `0572aaee52242bafbf922bbf1b5add23812d2a2fded47276532675ffc4f7095a`.

**A3a — source-reviewed**

The public elemental aeq and haeq generics implement absolute tolerance abs(a-b)<=tol and hybrid tolerance abs(a-b)<=atol+rtol*max(abs(a),abs(b)). Defaults are 1e-10 in each supported real kind. Array calls return elementwise logical masks, unlike the scalar array-reduction behavior of tcanich/compare. Explicit tolerances must match the argument kind; haeq exposes two-argument default or four-argument explicit forms. Negative tolerances, NaNs/infinities and subtraction/scaled-threshold overflow are not specially handled, so the mapping/sketch is limited to finite ordinary-range values and nonnegative tolerances. REAL128 overload declarations affect compiler support even for a REAL64-only user. No accuracy/equivalence test was performed.

Modified first-kind Bessel I0/I1 for real X, with even/odd parity respectively. These unscaled functions may overflow for large ABS(X). Elemental scalar interface: real argument and result use public kind BK=REAL64; arrays may be evaluated elementwise. No status/error estimate is returned. These four routines take X alone, not an order argument, and are distinct from the general-order or exponentially scaled entry points.

Usage:

```fortran
VALUE = besseli0(X)
```

**E3 — source-reviewed**

The inspected rbf_type%build constructs a local RBF interpolation matrix for each caller-supplied neighbor stencil, obtains its inverse and forms derivative matrices from kernel evaluations. This is an interpolation service (E3), not a complete value-evaluation API: optional y is not referenced, and the routine neither fits data values nor returns values at arbitrary queries. The Gaussian unaugmented matrix path is identifiable in source; the derivative and polynomial branches need correction/checking. In particular, the Gaussian second derivative expression differs from the analytic derivative; polynomial-augmented B entries are not fully initialized before whole-matrix multiplication, and an active debug print indexes node ten without checking node count. Compile with USE_LAPACK: inverse_matrix has an empty alternative branch. Select a distance function first, validate indices and stencil nonsingularity, and use poly_order=-1 to avoid augmentation. No interpolant, derivative matrix or failure was checked by execution; no PDE-solver or general scattered-interpolator mapping is inferred.

The public fun_zero implementation combines secant proposals with bisection for a scalar function supplied by procedure pointer. The inspected body does not implement inverse quadratic interpolation, despite the Brent wording in its header. It requires strictly opposite endpoint signs: endpoint zeros are rejected by the initial product >= 0 test. Optional controls set absolute tolerance, iteration budget and printing. Initial NaNs have a status path, but the interior NaN check is inside the show_iterations branch. This is a nonpolynomial single-equation mapping, not an all-roots guarantee or a numerical validation.

**F1a — source-reviewed**

poly_roots builds a real companion matrix from descending-power coefficients, dividing by the leading coefficient, balances it and obtains real or complex-conjugate roots through its private real Hessenberg double-QR iteration. Degree <= 0 and zero leading coefficients have explicit error statuses; QR exhaustion also returns failure. The optional accuracy_hint is a machine-epsilon/degree/iteration/norm heuristic, not a certified root error bound. The source path establishes polynomial-root scope; repeated roots, conditioning and accuracy were not checked by execution.

**D1b4 — source-reviewed**

The public CSRcomplex%MATMUL binding checks the input-vector size and dispatches a complex CSR row sum, or MKL_ZCSRGEMV under the MKL preprocessor branch. The inspected fallback uses one-based ROW/COL arrays and sums VAL*X without conjugation. The type owns private storage and has public constructors/setters. Output Y is assumed-size and its capacity cannot be checked by the routine; dimension errors STOP the process. The separate NONZERO binding returns the terminal row pointer (NNZ+1), not NNZ, and setter allocation/search contracts are not fully verified. This review covers a valid constructed matrix and the non-MKL product path, not sparse solves, all insert/update behavior or MKL correctness/performance.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The inspected xoshiro256star2 output rotates state(2)*5 and multiplies by 9, then performs the four-word XOR/shift/rotate recurrence. The inherited real-valued random_number converts the high 52 output bits into an IEEE binary64 mantissa and subtracts one, targeting a uniform grid in [0,1). L6a21 records uniform generation with explicit state, not normal sampling or a statistical-quality certificate. set_state assigns an allocatable array without validating its length or rejecting the all-zero state. random_seed with no options only allocates uninitialized state; it does not seed it. The integer multiplications require intended modulo-2**64 behavior, which signed Fortran overflow does not guarantee. Other generators, seed-from-generator and the INT32 converter are outside this review. No sequence or reference comparison was executed.

**E1a — documentation-reviewed**

The README documents value, first/second derivative and extremum interfaces, plus linear behavior outside the data range. Endpoint and extrapolation behavior have not been independently checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `88f138a0a8ad8e71c89237df5fc236097ab695cc`.

[README.md](https://github.com/ja72/FortranConsoleSpline/blob/88f138a0a8ad8e71c89237df5fc236097ab695cc/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `e0e73f70d5f53e49d7792e489b66b948502b36c7b6b9c7459cb1735b716528cf`.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The module constructs and evaluates a real64 univariate piecewise-cubic interpolant from ordered samples, with optional endpoint first derivatives and natural endpoint conditions when slopes are absent. The type-bound value, slope and slope2 methods evaluate the interpolant and its derivatives; outside the data range the implementation suppresses the cubic terms, giving linear value/slope extrapolation and zero second derivative. E1a is the supported polynomial-spline classification; this is not smoothing, multidimensional fitting or a generic global-extremum solver. Source inspection found a material construction discrepancy: the interior coefficient sig uses x(i)-(i-1), mixing an abscissa with an index, instead of the adjacent abscissa difference expected for the documented arbitrary-grid cubic-spline recurrence. Ordered, distinct abscissae and compatible lengths are not comprehensively validated. The extrema helper continues bisection even after its same-sign endpoint branch, so no root/extremum enumeration claim is added. Neither the author example nor interpolation accuracy was tested.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `88f138a0a8ad8e71c89237df5fc236097ab695cc`.

**J — source-reviewed**

The inspected rA19CWT_zerobc constructs scale levels, cubic B-spline approximation coefficients and fourth cumulative sums, evaluates seventh-degree B-spline kernels with wavelet coefficient differences, and scales the resulting CWT. It supplies a real continuous wavelet transform of a uniformly spaced signal under zero boundary conditions. J is retained because this taxonomy has no wavelet-specific child; it is not classified as an ordinary Fourier transform. The card selects the cubic B-spline wavelet CBSW path, not all real/complex or periodic variants. Input is signal(0:Nmesh-1); allocated outputs are scales(0:Nscales-1) and CWT(0:Nscales-1,0:Nmesh-1). Positive Lbox/Nsubs and compatible mesh/level bounds are caller obligations; there is no status return. Wavelet selection uses substring matching and STOP on an unknown name. No coefficient, boundary error, transform accuracy or timing was checked by execution.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The public random generic dispatches to intrinsic RANDOM_NUMBER for REAL(dp) scalar values and builds interval/list/integer variants from repeated scalar calls. L6a21 records intended uniform output. Every scalar draw first calls RANDOM_INIT(.false.,.false.), reinitializing the intrinsic generator rather than advancing an explicitly seeded local stream. This can defeat caller seeding, adds reseeding work and provides no guarantee of independent repeated values. Integer sampling scales a real draw with FLOOR; b<=a is rejected including a singleton interval, and b+1-a can overflow. No randomness, endpoint, stream-independence or compiler comparison was executed.

**L6a14 — source-reviewed**

normal_dist dispatches to Box-Muller, Marsaglia-Bray polar rejection, or a Bernoulli-sum CLT approximation. The inspected BMA path transforms pairs of uniform values using sqrt(-2*log(u1)) and trigonometric components, then returns only the first component of each pair. L6a14 records normal-variate generation, not a verified distribution or an exact-normal claim for CLT. Despite its documentation comment naming MBA default, actual code defaults to BMA. Box-Muller does not guard u1=0. All paths inherit fr_random per-draw intrinsic reseeding; the sketch selects MBA, which rejects q<=0 and q>=1, but does not repair reseeding. No samples, moments or distribution tests were run.

**L10a2e — source-reviewed**

KALMAN_FILTER evaluates per-observation Gaussian log-likelihood contributions for a linear state-space model. It initializes zero state mean and a stationary covariance using DLYAP, then forms innovations/covariances, performs the Kalman prediction update and accumulates contributions only for t>T0. The selected one-observation-channel use fits the univariate state-space class; the implementation also accepts multivariate observations, but this map does not infer a smoother or returned state trajectory from a likelihood-only function. Require stable transition dynamics and positive-definite innovation covariances. The basic path does not handle missing observations; separate missing-data functions exist. DLYAP and Cholesky/inversion status values are not propagated by this API, so finite likelihood output alone is not a convergence or factorization certificate. The reviewed non-SLICOT DLYAP branch uses covariance doubling; the SLICOT conditional branch has its solver call commented out and must not be assumed equivalent. Review covers the basic filter and initializer, not every alternate recursion or particle-filter method.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `7fffbcfb037163295f12071d318455fa5651a2a1`.

**D2a4 — source-reviewed**

Initialize the configured Trilinos/MPI execution environment and communicator, construct valid compatible Tpetra objects, check FORTRILINOS_IERR/exception text after wrapper calls, and release owned handles before finalizing MPI. Match the generated bindings to the installed C++ Trilinos build; these are dispatch interfaces, not standalone numerical kernels. TrilinosSolver%setup_matrix retains a sparse Tpetra matrix and %setup_solver builds a Stratimikos/Thyra solve strategy from a ParameterList. %solve applies NOTRANS to one or more right-hand sides using compatible domain/range-map TpetraMultiVectors. The optional third Fortran argument is a LOGICAL convergence result: this is a subroutine call, not a logical function. Backend errors still require the separate wrapper error check. The selected algorithm and optional Ifpack2/MueLu preconditioner depend on the parameter list and build; no specific iteration, sparse direct method or accuracy follows from the wrapper name. Preserve original A/B and check residuals independently.

**D4a2 — source-reviewed**

Initialize the configured Trilinos/MPI execution environment and communicator, construct valid compatible Tpetra objects, check FORTRILINOS_IERR/exception text after wrapper calls, and release owned handles before finalizing MPI. Match the generated bindings to the installed C++ Trilinos build; these are dispatch interfaces, not standalone numerical kernels. TrilinosEigenSolver exposes A*x=lambda*x without an M operator through Anasazi::BasicEigenproblem. Setup requires NumEV, Solver Type and a matching named solver sublist; initial vectors are randomized. The selected general real interface does not set a Hermitian flag, so no symmetric specialization is inferred. Eigenvalues are written as alternating real/imaginary C_DOUBLE entries, with C_INT eigenindex encoding and a TpetraMultiVector for vectors. The integer function result is the returned value count; use %converged() separately and check independent residuals. Critical source finding: the C++ buffer guard tests 2*capacity<count rather than capacity<2*count and compares the requested/clipped count, while copy loops use the full returned Evals/index sizes. Requested NumEV alone therefore does not ensure adequate buffers, especially around conjugate pairs. Repair guards/copy bounds against actual returned sizes before treating the sketch as an executable driver. This review records the implemented dispatch and interface, not a verified or memory-safe eigensolve.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

Initialize the configured Trilinos/MPI execution environment and communicator, construct valid compatible Tpetra objects, check FORTRILINOS_IERR/exception text after wrapper calls, and release owned handles before finalizing MPI. Match the generated bindings to the installed C++ Trilinos build; these are dispatch interfaces, not standalone numerical kernels. NOXSolver binds NOX/Thyra nonlinear system solving to a model evaluator supplying residuals, an initial guess and linear-solver factory, plus analytic Jacobian operators or the configured Matrix Free Newton path. For a Fortran subclass, construct the base ForModelEvaluator and call init_ForModelEvaluator before setup, as documented in the binding and author test; keep the model alive during solver use. %setup consumes Jacobian Settings and Nonlinear Solver Settings; unknown Jacobian types throw. This wrapper hardcodes a 20-iteration limit and a combined NormF(1e-8)/NormWRMS(1e-2,1e-8) convergence test with finite-value termination. Those thresholds are not exposed by the selected wrapper parameter path. %solve is a function returning the named NOX status enum, not a logical success or a solution vector. NOXConverged still warrants an independent model residual check. Review covers nonlinear-system dispatch rather than all NOX algorithms or the application-specific demonstration PDE.
