**D1b4 — source-reviewed**

The public CSR_MATVEC loops over one-based CSR row-pointer ranges and accumulates real64 VAL(k)*X(COL(k)), optionally with OpenMP row parallelism/SIMD. CSR_VALID separately checks positive dimensions, allocated lengths, one-based endpoints, monotonic row pointers, finite values and strictly increasing in-range column indices. CSR_MATVEC itself assumes setup/shape validation and returns no status. This is sparse multiplication by a vector only; the large direct-solver, AMG, backend and mixed-precision features are not promoted to source-reviewed from this service review. Numeric summation order and empty rows follow the row loop; no accuracy/performance or external-backend run was measured.

**C3a2 — source-reviewed**

The public LEGENDRE generic selects a private double-precision routine that returns P0=1, P1=x, and otherwise applies the standard three-term Legendre-polynomial recurrence. C3a2 records ordinary Legendre polynomial evaluation, not all associated functions, normalized harmonics or coupling coefficients in the module. The routine documents nonnegative degree and -1<=x<=1 but does not validate either or return a status. Negative degrees fall through to the initialized P0=x instead of signalling invalid input. High-degree recurrence accuracy and overflow were not tested. No polynomial or harmonic was evaluated for this catalog.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

SHGLQ uses LMAX+1 nodes for Gauss-Legendre quadrature on [-1,1]. The inspected implementation initializes symmetric root guesses, evaluates Legendre recurrences and derivatives, performs up to 100 Newton updates, mirrors the nodes and computes reciprocal-derivative weights. H2c records a rule-generation service; callers still evaluate their integrand and form the weighted sum. LMAX must be nonnegative and outputs have LMAX+1 entries. The absolute Newton-step tolerance is fixed at 1e-15 and no status is returned if the iteration cap is reached. Exactness statements describe the mathematical rule, not verified floating-point output. No node/weight, moment-exactness or convergence test was executed.

**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

These external entries use shared geometry, sparse-matrix, parameter and title modules: FI(NUMTOTAL) alone does not supply the problem. Initialize NUMCELLS/NUMTOTAL, allocated one-based CSR IOFFSET/JA/A, diagonal positions, RHS SU, RES, reporting labels and per-field NSW/SOR/RESOR consistently. DIAG/triangular traversal assumes the row ordering supplied by this code. They print reports rather than return a separate convergence/error code; iteration exhaustion is not a successful solve certificate. Require a positive iteration budget and recompute the true residual independently. The reviewed source is serial SRC, not SRC-PARALLEL. DPCG uses diagonal-preconditioned conjugate gradients for a symmetric positive-definite sparse operator. It forms the initial residual, adds optional O-C grid-cut coupling terms, divides by the matrix diagonal and updates the solution/search directions with dot products. Nonzero usable diagonals and SPD of the complete operator/preconditioner are caller assumptions, not validated. The initial absolute L1 residual threshold is 1e-13, with subsequent stopping on a relative L1 residual against SOR(IFI). No zero/near-breakdown guards protect all PCG denominators. Positive definiteness is not implied by the file comment saying symmetric.

**D2a4 — source-reviewed**

These external entries use shared geometry, sparse-matrix, parameter and title modules: FI(NUMTOTAL) alone does not supply the problem. Initialize NUMCELLS/NUMTOTAL, allocated one-based CSR IOFFSET/JA/A, diagonal positions, RHS SU, RES, reporting labels and per-field NSW/SOR/RESOR consistently. DIAG/triangular traversal assumes the row ordering supplied by this code. They print reports rather than return a separate convergence/error code; iteration exhaustion is not a successful solve certificate. Require a positive iteration budget and recompute the true residual independently. The reviewed source is serial SRC, not SRC-PARALLEL. BICGSTAB performs preconditioned nonsymmetric Krylov iteration using forward/back substitutions with an incomplete diagonal factor, while GAUSSSEIDEL updates entries sequentially from CSR row residuals. The BiCGStab routine reports ILU(0), but its structural searches assume matching transpose entries and valid pivots; an absent counterpart can leave a search beyond the row. Restrict the selected sketches to ordinary CSR systems with NOC=0: initial BiCGStab residual includes cut-coupling AL/AR but the two iteration matrix products omit it; Gauss-Seidel has those extra terms commented out entirely. BiCGStab divides by shadow-product and factor quantities without a complete breakdown-status policy. Gauss-Seidel stopping uses residual values collected during sequential updates rather than a freshly evaluated simultaneous residual of the final iterate. Matrices must satisfy conditions for the chosen iteration to converge; this is not an arbitrary sparse direct solver. The generic LINEAR_SOLVER file has repeated placeholder selectors, so these cards identify the actual external routines rather than endorse that dispatcher.

**L8e — source-reviewed**

The reviewed Fortran type-bound PREDICT_ONE entries evaluate previously trained nonlinear regression models: a neural network uses dense affine layers and activation callbacks, a decision tree follows feature-threshold comparisons, and a random forest averages tree outputs. The implementation is prediction, not native Fortran training or a particular least-squares/regularization optimizer; Python/scikit-learn training and serialization remain external. Require initialized model dimensions, allocated consistent coefficients/nodes, live activation pointers and positive tree_count. Neural predictions overwrite stored activation arrays, so sharing one object across simultaneous calls is not assumed safe. Precision is selected by preprocessing to numeric kind 4 or 8, single by default; PS is private, so caller data must match the build. Export helpers shift scikit-learn child/feature indices to one-based Fortran (leaf sentinel becomes -1), depend on historical scikit-learn attributes and write values with limited decimal formatting. Tree traversal is bounded by recorded maximum depth and does not validate malformed node links. Softmax is defective in this pin: it reads SUM(TMP) before TMP is assigned and returns a logistic expression instead of softmax. Restrict regression sketches to compatible validated models/activations (e.g. identity output); do not infer classification probabilities or current scikit-learn compatibility. Source review does not establish prediction accuracy or equivalence with training-library output.

f_sts_mean checks for at least two values then calls the pure mean core, which divides SUM(X) by SIZE(X). L1a1a records arithmetic location of raw univariate data, not a median, weighted estimator or missing-data mean. The wrapper prints an error and returns a NaN for size<=1, including a mathematically defined singleton mean. The public core has fewer checks and is not a drop-in validated wrapper. Working kind WP is REAL64; accumulation is a direct intrinsic SUM, not an explicitly compensated algorithm. Nonfinite/missing-data handling is not supplied by this selected path. No sample summaries or error paths were run.

**L1b — source-reviewed**

f_sts_pcc validates equal-length vectors with more than one entry, then computes centered covariance divided by the square root of the product of centered population variances. L1b records descriptive two-variable Pearson correlation, not a correlation hypothesis test or a fitted regression model. The covariance/variance cores use direct centered dot products and divide by N in this selected call. The wrapper does not guard zero variance, near-overflow products or nonfinite inputs; constant series can divide by zero. Private error/NaN utilities are dependencies, and core calls bypass wrapper validation. No correlation result, significance or numerical stability test was run.

The source expresses an active REAL(8) sort with insertion sort for lengths <=8, recursive quick partitioning for intermediate sizes, and heap sorting for lengths >=8192. N6a2b records that real-array sorting intent, with repair required rather than a successfully compilable API claim. Both heap-branch IF statements at lines 65 and 88 are missing a closing parenthesis. The heap indices are relative to array element 1 instead of beg; insertion uses a compound .AND. guard that does not guarantee short-circuit protection for arr(j) after j falls below beg. Values/order should not be relied upon until these findings are resolved and checked. No compiler or sort was run.

**J — source-reviewed**

cfst1f Fourier-transforms the input, doubles positive frequencies and clears negative bins through cht1f, then inverse-transforms Gaussian-weighted circularly shifted spectra into frequency voices. cfst1b sums the voices, restores conjugate negative-frequency content and transforms back. J records the one-dimensional Stockwell integral-transform service because this taxonomy has no Stockwell leaf; it is not classified as a plain Fourier transform merely because FFTs implement it. Default-kind COMPLEX input/output, allocated forward bounds (0:N/2,0:N-1), DC voice SUM(H)/N, and inverse voice/time layout are source-visible. Intended round trips assume real-valued data represented as complex; independent negative-frequency information is discarded. Require nonempty input and a correctly shaped inverse array; failures use ERROR STOP, not returned status. The 2D DOST and voice-extraction paths are outside the selected usage review. No transform/round trip was executed.

**J1a2 — source-reviewed**

The separately public FFTPACK::cfft1_ wrapper allocates save/work arrays, initializes FFTPACK 5.1 tables and dispatches CFFT1F or CFFT1B on an in-place default-COMPLEX vector. Backend drivers dispatch mixed-radix passes. J1a2 covers this callable one-dimensional complex Fourier-transform interface, distinct from the Stockwell construction. DIR is exactly lowercase f or b; invalid direction returns ERR=1. Empty input reaches ILOG2(0) and is unsupported. Workspace/tables are rebuilt each call. Wrapper backend interfaces declare WORK INTENT(IN) although the linked FFT uses it as scratch, an interface-contract inconsistency needing correction. Review covers wrapper and dispatch, not all butterfly kernels, normalization proofs or compiler purity checks; no FFT was run.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected array overload accumulates 0.5*(x(i+1)-x(i))*(f(i)+f(i+1)), a composite trapezoidal integral of sampled data. H2a1b2 records nonautomatic grid-data quadrature, including nonuniform spacing, not a tolerance-driven callback integrator. Caller must provide ordered nodes and matching arrays; empty/singleton arrays produce zero. The parent declares a separate callback trapezoidal_rule_f but this submodule only supplies the array body. Plain FUNCTION headers in these submodules differ from the parent MODULE FUNCTION declarations and build compatibility was not checked. Mismatch handling delegates to an unreviewed print_error_message policy. No integral or build was executed.

**H2a1a2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected 1D Gaussian path obtains tabulated Gauss-Legendre nodes/weights for N=1..5, maps them affinely from [-1,1] to the first two endpoint entries, evaluates a procedure pointer and scales the weighted sum by half the interval length. H2a1a2 records nonautomatic finite-interval callback quadrature; no tolerance/error estimator is present. Unsupported N has no SELECT CASE default and leaves rule data undefined. The callback pointer must be associated, endpoints must have at least two entries, and its optional parameter-array convention must match. Plain submodule FUNCTION versus parent MODULE FUNCTION consistency needs build checking; multidimensional behavior is unreviewed. No quadrature result was executed.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The benchmark::solve driver evolves a box-domain population using tournament selection, covariance-aware Gaussian crossover/mutation, reflective constraints, elitism/temperature acceptance and restart-like covariance changes. Fitness is ABS(target_value-objective), so it targets a known objective value rather than generically minimizing the supplied function; target zero on nonnegative benchmark functions is the selected interpretation. It prints target error/evaluation count but returns no optimum or status, and budget accounting includes the initial population outside generation counts. Initialization uses the global minimum lower bound and maximum upper bound, not each dimension bound separately; first evaluations can therefore be outside heterogeneous bounds. Some counters are updated inside DO CONCURRENT and need a concurrency semantics audit; no parallel-safety or global-optimality claim is made. The callable sketch uses the standalone tournament service only. The solve module shares a file with a demonstration program and needs separation for another main.

**K1b1a1 — source-reviewed**

GADF_FIT performs modified Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least squares on model functions defined with ADVAR arithmetic. It forms weighted residuals/Jacobians, sums normal-equation contributions across images, solves a damped system and optionally applies a directional second-derivative/geodesic correction. With USE_AD true, the user supplies the model expression rather than analytic derivative routines. Global fitting here means simultaneous datasets with shared parameters, not global optimization. The selected sketch follows the author single-dataset Gaussian setup with error mode NONE; other weighting modes change the objective. Call GADF_INIT, add datasets, mark active parameters and then fit. Data arrays are pointer-associated on input and need valid lifetime/targets. Coarray and preprocessing support plus compatible numerical libraries are required. The code repeatedly combines PRESENT with optional-argument access in logical expressions; strict evaluation/absent-option safety needs separate audit. No complete numerical fit or termination/covariance validation was run.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The AD module overloads arithmetic on ADVAR, carrying primal VAL, directional derivative D and second directional derivative DD in forward mode, and recording a tape in reverse mode. The selected multiplication path explicitly applies first/second product rules and uses INDEX/=0 to mark active operands. Setting derivative seeds without a nonzero INDEX leaves an operand inactive. The sketch selects forward mode and direct multiplication rather than the integer-power path, whose derivative formula divides by X and Y and needs care at zero even for mathematically regular powers. This is automatic differentiation of the executed operations, not finite differences or symbolic differentiation, and does not make discontinuous branch choices differentiable. Shared module tape/mode state requires coordinated lifetime/thread use; reverse-mode tape capacity and all transcendental branches were not audited.

**G2e1 — source-reviewed**

EQP solves equality-constrained quadratic subproblems through projected/preconditioned iterative work with dependency removal and sparse block factorizations. The concrete sketch has positive-definite H=2I, so its mapping is the convex quadratic-program class G2e1; this does not assert that all library EQP problems require positive-definite H on the full space. Public QPT data stores the constraint constant C in A*x+C=0, as the native example and feasibility RHS=-C show, despite the solve prologue shorthand A*x=c. H uses its lower triangle in coordinate storage. The sketch sets Hessian_kind=-1 to select the supplied Hessian explicitly. The source module name is precision-preprocessed; GALAHAD_EQP_double is the author-example public double-precision facade. Match its integer ABI and configured sparse/dense factorization backends. INITIALIZE/SOLVE/TERMINATE form the lifecycle; TERMINATE overwrites INFORM, so retain solve diagnostics first. Review covers the public solver, author data layout and selected native dispatch/stopping paths, not every linear algebra backend or a numerical verification.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
program quadratic_sketch
use GALAHAD_EQP_double
implicit none
integer,parameter :: wp=kind(1d0)
integer :: status
type(QPT_problem_type) :: p
type(EQP_data_type) :: data
type(EQP_control_type) :: control
type(EQP_inform_type) :: inform
p%n=2; p%m=1; p%f=0._wp; p%new_problem_structure=.true.
allocate(p%G(2),p%C(1),p%X(2),p%Y(1))
p%X=0._wp; p%Y=0._wp
p%Hessian_kind=-1; p%G=[-2._wp,-4._wp]; p%C=[-1._wp]
! EQP interprets the equality as A*X + C = 0.
call SMT_put(p%H%type,'COORDINATE',status)
if(status/=0) error stop "H storage allocation failed"
call SMT_put(p%A%type,'COORDINATE',status)
if(status/=0) error stop "A storage allocation failed"
allocate(p%H%val(2),p%H%row(2),p%H%col(2))
allocate(p%A%val(2),p%A%row(2),p%A%col(2))
p%H%ne=2; p%H%row=[1,2]; p%H%col=[1,2]
p%H%val=[2._wp,2._wp]
p%A%ne=2; p%A%row=[1,1]; p%A%col=[1,2]; p%A%val=1._wp
call EQP_initialize(data,control,inform)
control%SBLS_control%symmetric_linear_solver="sytr"
control%FDC_control%symmetric_linear_solver="sytr"
call EQP_solve(p,data,control,inform)
if(inform%status/=0) then
 print *,"solver status",inform%status
else
 print *,inform%obj,p%X
end if
! Preserve solve status before termination, which overwrites INFORM.
call EQP_terminate(data,control,inform)
end program
```

**G2e2 — source-reviewed**

QPB solves quadratic programs with simple variable bounds and two-sided linear constraints using a primal-dual interior/trust-region approach. The implementation supports indefinite Hessians and explicitly handles negative-curvature information in the GLTR subproblem/convergence paths; the selected sketch H=diag(-1,2) is indefinite and maps to G2e2. Status zero is the package stopping condition and does not certify the global optimum of a nonconvex QP. A is the constraint matrix with C_l<=A*x<=C_u, distinct from the EQP constant-vector convention. H uses lower-triangular coordinate storage. The source module name is precision-preprocessed; GALAHAD_QPB_double is the author-example public double-precision facade. Match its integer ABI and configured sparse/dense factorization backends. INITIALIZE/SOLVE/TERMINATE form the lifecycle; TERMINATE overwrites INFORM, so retain solve diagnostics first. Review covers the public solver, author data layout and selected native dispatch/stopping paths, not every linear algebra backend or a numerical verification.

```fortran
implicit none
integer,parameter :: wp=kind(1d0)
integer :: status
type(QPT_problem_type) :: p
type(QPB_data_type) :: data
type(QPB_control_type) :: control
type(QPB_inform_type) :: inform
p%n=2; p%m=1; p%f=0._wp; p%new_problem_structure=.true.
allocate(p%G(2),p%C(1),p%X(2),p%Y(1))
p%X=0._wp; p%Y=0._wp
allocate(p%X_l(2),p%X_u(2),p%C_l(1),p%C_u(1),p%Z(2))
p%G=0._wp; p%C=0._wp; p%Z=0._wp
p%X_l=-1._wp; p%X_u=1._wp; p%C_l=-0.5_wp; p%C_u=0.5_wp
p%X=[0.1_wp,-0.1_wp]
call SMT_put(p%H%type,'COORDINATE',status)
if(status/=0) error stop "H storage allocation failed"
call SMT_put(p%A%type,'COORDINATE',status)
if(status/=0) error stop "A storage allocation failed"
allocate(p%H%val(2),p%H%row(2),p%H%col(2))
allocate(p%A%val(2),p%A%row(2),p%A%col(2))
p%H%ne=2; p%H%row=[1,2]; p%H%col=[1,2]
p%H%val=[-1._wp,2._wp]
p%A%ne=2; p%A%row=[1,1]; p%A%col=[1,2]; p%A%val=1._wp
call QPB_initialize(data,control,inform)
control%infinity=1e20_wp
call QPB_solve(p,data,control,inform)
if(inform%status/=0) then
 print *,"solver status",inform%status
else
 print *,inform%obj,p%X
end if
! Preserve solve status before termination, which overwrites INFORM.
call QPB_terminate(data,control,inform)
end program
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build the complete GALAHAD double-precision modules and dependencies, with integer kinds matching this author-style default-integer sketch. Validate feasibility and optimality independently; a successful status is not a global guarantee for an indefinite problem. No QP, factorization or termination case was run.

[README.md](https://github.com/ckormanyos/gamma_f77/blob/56568aa9257f587c4c09f033954c3cadd5ef4666/README.md)

**C7a — source-reviewed**

The inspected GAMMA_MOD::TGAMMA evaluates real Gamma by a 48-coefficient reciprocal-Gamma expansion in Horner form, recurrence products after reducing |X|, and reflection for negative noninteger arguments of magnitude above one. Positive integer arguments take a factorial-product branch. C7a records Gamma evaluation; no log-Gamma, reciprocal-Gamma output API, incomplete Gamma or complex extension is inferred. QP=selected_real_kind(32) requires compiler support for at least 32 decimal digits and sufficient range for the source literal 1e4000. At zero/negative integer poles the routine returns that finite sentinel rather than an IEEE infinity or status. Default-INTEGER conversions of X are not range-guarded; NaN, infinities, overflow and large recurrence products are not handled robustly. The last DATA coefficient lacks the _QP suffix used by the others, so coefficient rounding deserves checking before asserting a full precision guarantee. gamma.f also contains a main test program after the module; extract/build the module separately when linking a different main. No accuracy or pole/overflow case was executed.

**L6a20 — source-reviewed**

garch_mod::simulate_garch generates a GARCH(1,1) return path using Gaussian innovations, starting conditional variance at omega/(1-alpha-beta), emitting optional conditional STANDARD DEVIATIONS and updating variance with alpha*noise**2+beta*sigma2+omega. Supply preallocated caller arrays; despite a source comment, the dummy is assumed-shape and not allocated inside. Require finite mu, omega>0, alpha/beta>=0 and alpha+beta<1 for this initialization. No parameter guard enforces those constraints. The normal helper caches a Box-Muller draw and replaces a zero uniform by 1e-10, so random state is not simply reset by reseeding the intrinsic stream after cached draws. This mapping is stochastic time-series generation, not estimation accuracy or a financial recommendation. No stochastic/variance test was run.

The public obj_fun_mod::garch_sigma filters an observed return vector with supplied parameters [mu,omega,alpha,beta], initializing variance from the sample variance (floored if nonpositive) and applying the GARCH(1,1) lagged-residual/variance recurrence. It returns conditional STANDARD DEVIATIONS, with -1 sentinels where the computed variance is negative. Nonempty/nondegenerate finite data and admissible parameters remain caller requirements; it writes the first variance entry without an empty-input guard. This time-domain volatility calculation does not fit parameters, validate the model or forecast a full stochastic path. It is distinct from the simulator, whose initialization uses unconditional rather than sample variance. No filtered path or estimator comparison was run.

**L8c1a1 — source-reviewed**

FSTEPWISE selects raw covariates by minimum residual sum-of-squares, transforms that improvement through incomplete-beta Gaussian-covariate probabilities and orthogonalizes remaining columns after accepting a variable. IA marks excluded/used columns; IA(K)=1 is the special intercept convention used by the R wrapper, so a last-column exclusion must not be mistaken for an intercept flag. X is overwritten; PP stores selected indices as doubles and probabilities, KMX is also output. Require finite nondegenerate data, valid exclusion indices, enough residual degrees of freedom and safe output extents (the source declares MINSS(N) while using selection-count indices). The no-candidate-improvement path can leave IC undefined, and the intercept probability branch caps its ratio with DMIN1(...,1e-10); these need separate validation rather than interpreting all outputs as calibrated probabilities. This review covers the forward path and its dispatch, not every robust/all-subsets postprocessing wrapper.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `ecb48f9d64502780a36347bce46554988c43c583`.

**L8c1b1 — source-reviewed**

The selected QRDECOM -> LSQQR pipeline fits a full-column-rank unweighted raw design matrix using scaled Householder transformations and triangular back substitution through QRSOLV. X and Y are overwritten, intercepts must be explicit columns, and QRDECOM only flags an exactly zero column scale rather than providing pivoted numerical rank revelation. The INV=.FALSE. branch is selected: the optional inverse-related path calls RSOLV, which immediately RETURNs before its triangular solve, so inverse-related outputs cannot be trusted from this revision. No residual, conditioning or covariance guarantee follows from SING=.FALSE. This mapping is the selected fit pipeline, separate from forward-selection probability calibration.

**L10a2 — source-reviewed**

The public ARMA residuals and GARCH variances bindings evaluate supplied-parameter time-domain recursions for each mixture component. ARMA_RESIDUALS subtracts lagged observations and, once enough residual history exists, lagged residuals; it also records in-sample fitted values. GARCH_VARIANCES adds an intercept, lagged squared residuals and lagged conditional variances. The input is squared by the supplied caller, not inside the variance routine. This is time-domain analysis L10a2, not evidence of successful parameter estimation, out-of-sample forecasting, a complete EM fit or a leaf specifically for GARCH. Require positive consistent lag orders, enough observations, initialized datetime/value arrays and allocated model parameter/prediction containers; setters alone do not initialize the lag metadata. Early recursions omit unavailable history instead of stationary/backcast initialization. No output status, missing-value handling, positivity test or numerical validation is provided. The public STABILITY function only tests row sums below one and does not check coefficient nonnegativity or ARMA root stability.

The public ARMA%RESIDUALS binding evaluates the conditional ARMA residual recurrence for supplied coefficient rows, subtracting lagged observations and, after a finite startup interval, lagged residuals. It stores in-sample fitted observations in MODEL%Y_HAT. This specific supplied-model operation supports the ARMA/ARIMA model family L10a2d, without claiming a parameter-estimation, identification or forecasting leaf: coefficients are not fitted by this routine, no differencing is performed and the generated predictions remain in sample. Positive compatible orders, allocated parameter/prediction containers and sufficiently long initialized datetime/value sequences are required. Startup omits unavailable MA history; no error status, root-based stationarity/invertibility check or uncertainty estimate is returned. The separate L10a2 entry records associated conditional-variance recursions, for which this taxonomy offers no dedicated GARCH leaf.

**K5 — source-reviewed**

GCVSPL constructs B-spline design/penalty bands, then calls SPLC to obtain coefficients for a fixed smoothing parameter or searches the selected GCV/MSE/degrees-of-freedom criterion by bracketing and golden-section steps. K5 records smoothing by natural splines of degree 2*M-1, not proof of a global GCV optimum or a validated noise model. X must increase strictly; weights are positive; N>=2*M, K>=1 and leading dimensions/capacities must match. Positive MD initializes saved setup, while negative MD reuses saved scalar state and WK and must not be interleaved with another fit. IER=0 reports normal exit, not a numerical accuracy certificate; not every shape/capacity is checked. The selected sketch uses a fixed smoothing parameter (MD=1), avoiding claims about an unrun automatic parameter choice. No smoothing or noise/statistical validation was performed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `00e57d093252d10a98d71513060b5625d52efe89`.

This sketch supplies a fixed penalty rather than trusting a GCV optimum from six points. Evaluate the returned coefficients using SPLDER, not as fitted sample values. For negative-MD reuse, retain the corresponding WK/setup and avoid interleaving different fits.

**K6a2 — source-reviewed**

SPLDER locates an interval in the supplied knot sequence, differences B-spline coefficients for positive IDER, evaluates the reduced-order tableau and applies the derivative factorial scale. K6a2 is derivative evaluation of an already fitted function, not fresh numerical differentiation of arbitrary raw data or an ODE solver. Require coefficients from compatible GCVSPL settings, N>=2*M, in-range T, nonnegative IDER, mutable interval L and Q(2*M) scratch. IDER>=2*M returns zero, matching the degree limit; there is no error/status output or negative-order guard. Accuracy as an estimate of an underlying signal derivative depends on the smoothing/model and is not established by the algebraic spline derivative. No derivative or comparison was run.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The active rk_wrapper path selects the explicit seven-stage Dormand-Prince embedded tableau, then uses two weighted stage estimates for adaptive one-step integration of a callback-defined initial-value system. Tolerances are hard-coded to sqrt(machine epsilon), the estimator uses an L2 difference and a global maximum component scale, and accepted states use the bstar estimate. This records intended one-step nonstiff scope, not verified order or accuracy. A material source finding is that calc_k initializes dummy_y only once before the stage loop and accumulates all successive stage sums into it, instead of rebuilding each stage from y; the implemented stages therefore need correction/checking before relying on the named method. The first adaptive trial is not clipped to the interval endpoint; clipping occurs after a step. Rejection exhaustion STOPs; there is no status output. The routine writes to unit 22. Implicit/nonlinear-solver branches and their stiff suitability are not reviewed or mapped.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

The array overload of INTEGRATE_TRAP sums adjacent trapezoids using caller-supplied nonuniform abscissae and sampled values. It provides a nonadaptive finite-interval grid quadrature with no error estimate or automatic refinement; N<2 returns zero. Ordered, finite samples and matching dimensions are caller responsibilities. The callback overload is deliberately not covered: its loop begins at I=2 after evaluating XMIN and omits the first intermediate sample. The selected array path avoids that discrepancy. The repository Makefile promotes default REAL to 8 bytes while preserving double at 8 bytes; use consistent kinds/flags across producer and caller. No quadrature accuracy was verified.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

The module FSOLVE wrapper seeks a zero of N nonlinear equations in N variables through its HYBRD implementation: finite-difference Jacobian, QR model, dogleg trust-region step and rank-one updates. Callback FCN(N,X,FVEC) uses explicit-shape double-kind arrays and has no IFLAG dummy in this adaptation. FSOLVE fixes unit scaling, dense bandwidth and MAXFEV=200*(N+1), remapping HYBRD status 5 to 4. INFO=1 is a relative-step convergence estimate; check FVEC independently. This is a local root search, not a certified enumeration of roots or a successful moment-reconstruction result. The parent reconstruction source uses X**(K/3.) despite the introductory integer-moment formula, and mixes default REAL with the explicit double callback kind; its Makefile default-real promotion aligns those kinds. Those model/build details must not be mistaken for a verified reconstruction algorithm.

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The public real32 scalar solvers hybridD and hybridSA implement Newton/bisection and accelerated-secant/quadratic-candidate/bisection branches respectively. Their callbacks are pure scalar functions; hybridD also requires a derivative. Source findings prevent treating these as checked solvers: hybridD updates the bracket using fx0*fx1 rather than the newly evaluated midpoint value; hybridSA tests f0*f2 when accepting x3 rather than f0*f3. Both use relative step tests that divide by the candidate root, print on bracket failure without returning a status, and expose no explicit convergence flag. The separate range-scan routine root_searchD skips the first scanning segment and refers to optional max_iters without consistently using its local default. No all-roots or correctness guarantee is recorded, and no program was run.

**N5b — source-reviewed**

sub_int_node locates grid indices for subsequent interpolation on ascending ordered arrays; it does not compute interpolated values. The scalar overload finds a nearest node by MINLOC, adjusts rightward when needed and clamps the result to an endpoint interval. The vector overload exploits ascending queries using a moving search window and returns endpoint indices outside the grid. N5b records insertion/bracketing-position search, with this interpolation-specific clamping convention rather than a general upper_bound API. Require SIZE(x)>=2, nonempty sorted xp for the vector overload, and finite, distinct ascending grid values. Exact-knot conventions differ: the vector path can return 1 at the first knot, whereas the scalar path starts at 2. The EGM variant intentionally uses a left-of-grid sentinel 1 and differs again at knots; it is not substituted silently. No search result, speed comparison or interpolation was run.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `b6e0fbf261e47ba87fd213d044ea5b8a7859acc5d5a231f887cc2533ea522c13`.

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The inspected module solves a scalar real equation through function-value and first-derivative subroutine callbacks; the dummy vectors have length one. sub_newton takes Newton steps and attempts a sign-changing bracket after its Newton iteration limit, then calls sub_hybrid_nb, which bisects when a Newton trial leaves its current interval. F1b describes general nonpolynomial scalar root finding; this is not polynomial root enumeration, a derivative-free interface or a square-system solver. The hybrid code updates the first endpoint when f(x)<0, so its input pair must have the matching sign orientation; it does not validate a bracket on entry. Failure paths print and STOP rather than returning a status, and the Newton path divides by df before testing for a small derivative. The optional fnorm on direct Newton success stores the residual computed before the final x update. The fallback call does not forward the optional tolerance or iteration controls, so the hybrid defaults apply there. Convergence, singular-derivative behavior and all bracket assumptions were not checked by execution.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

chebyshev_quad::chebquad constructs a generalized Chebyshev quadrature rule from a Legendre piecewise discretization and sampled basis values already multiplied by square roots of discretization weights. It forms moments, uses interpolative decomposition to select nodes and a least-squares solve for weights, then sorts node/weight pairs. Raw unweighted function samples do not satisfy this interface. This is rule construction, not the nonlinear Gaussian-rule stage or a guaranteed positive-weight formula. Internal rank tolerance is machine epsilon; no status output, positivity proof, independent exactness check or execution result is supplied.

**L8c — source-reviewed**

The external ELNET entry computes an elastic-net penalized Gaussian multiple-linear-regression path. PARM interpolates ridge and lasso penalties; the covariance-update path standardizes data and uses coordinate updates with soft thresholding and coefficient bounds, then rescales compressed coefficients/intercepts to the original predictor scale. This is penalized regression, not ordinary least squares or robust-loss estimation. X, Y, W and CL may be overwritten. FLMIN>=1 selects the user-supplied lambda sequence; LMU, IA and NIN describe the returned compressed paths and should be used rather than treating CA as a full coefficient matrix. Positive JERR denotes fatal error and negative JERR can retain earlier partial solutions. The source declares default REAL, so standalone callers must match that kind or a deliberately promoted whole build; MATLAB double arrays do not change the raw Fortran declarations. Review covers the dense covariance-update path and penalty iteration, not sparse/multivariate families or cross-validation selection.

**L8 — source-reviewed**

The external LOGNET NC=1 path computes elastic-net penalized binomial logistic regression by iterated weighted/quadratic approximation and coordinate-descent updates. Y has two nonnegative count/weight columns even for NC=1, with column one defining the modeled event probability; rows are normalized internally and their totals become observation weights. G supplies offsets and is mutable working/output state. The routine dispatches the native LOGNET2N branch and rescales compressed coefficients after fitting. Positive row totals and both outcome classes are required; degenerate class probabilities, allocation, iteration and active-set limits have JERR conventions. The adopted GAMS regression tree has no dedicated penalized logistic/GLM leaf, so broad L8 is retained rather than labeling this nonlinear least squares or Gaussian regression. Review covers the dense binomial selection, normalization and penalized update paths, not multinomial/Cox/Poisson families, inferential coverage or predictive validation.

**G1a1a — source-reviewed**

The public GSS generic implements derivative-free golden-section interval reduction for a scalar objective, with optional CLASS(*) data forwarded to OBJ(X,FUNC_DATA). This selected smooth-unimodal problem class requires an ordered finite interval, positive tolerance and suitable iteration budget. FINDMAX defaults true, so a minimization caller must explicitly pass FINDMAX=.FALSE. Width-based termination and max-iteration exits have no separate status output, and the ITER<=MAXITER condition can permit an extra iteration. The returned point is the most recently generated trial, not a certified optimum or a reported final bracket. With a skipped loop Z/FVAL can remain undefined, so pathological tolerance/budget inputs require guards. This educational routine does not establish global optimality for multimodal objectives or convergence at a chosen test function.

**L4c1b — source-reviewed**

GridProjectedKDEType%ComputeDensity bins point coordinates, constructs active-cell lists and dispatches adaptive Gaussian-kernel reconstruction through ComputeDensityOptimization. Kernel cell weights use products of erf differences, reflection/unfolding and normalization over truncated support. The optimization combines density/roughness estimates and local bandwidth/shape updates. This mapping covers the multidimensional nonparametric density coordinator and inspected accumulation/kernel paths, not all histogram, boundary, sliced or weighted variants. DATAPOINTS stores observations in rows with three coordinate columns even for compressed lower dimensions. Module-owned density/roughness arrays and dimension state are shared across objects, so pointers are not independent persistent snapshots and concurrent estimators need state isolation. Output scaling can mean counts, mass or density depending options: no automatic probability-normalization claim is made.

**G1a1a — source-reviewed**

GOLDENSECTION performs derivative-free univariate interval reduction using golden-ratio interior points, evaluating a named external EVALFUNC1 rather than accepting a procedure argument. The user supplies ordered distinct endpoints and a fixed NITER; the routine returns four bracket/interior coordinates and function values, not a scalar minimizer or a status/accuracy estimate. GOLDENINT is a separate interactive file-writing wrapper that derives NITER from a requested relative interval contraction and chooses the smallest returned value. A unimodal finite objective over the supplied interval is required for usual interval-search interpretation; no multimodal global search guarantee is inferred. The kernel writes progress to Fortran unit 11 and does not reject zero-width/reversed bounds or invalid counts. Review covers the complete golden-section kernel/interface and the pinned sample objective, not all optimizers in GPopt.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The public BILINEAR routine interpolates values from a regular rectangular input grid to query points using four tensor-product weights. It estimates uniform spacing from axis endpoints; it does not search nonuniform coordinates. DATA_IN is laid out (NY,NX) and POINTS is (NQUERY,2). The out-of-range branches contain CONTINUE rather than CYCLE, so they fall through to invalid indexing and overwrite the sentinel; upper endpoints are also unsafe. This mapping records implemented gridded interpolation, not correctness at boundaries or source review of the separate scattered-data/triangle methods.

**L4b3 — source-reviewed**

CALC_CORR computes descriptive statistics for paired observations: both means/sample standard deviations, signed bias Ymean-Xmean, RMSE, centered population-scale difference spread and Pearson correlation. This supports elementary analysis of paired data; it does not compute a significance test, confidence interval or distribution model. The native routine uses default-real one-pass sums, so cancellation can affect nearly constant/large-offset data. Require NOBS>1 and finite prefiltered pairs because no missing-value or small-sample checks are performed. Constant-series correlation remains the initialized zero rather than returning a distinct undefined-correlation status. ABS under square roots masks negative roundoff terms, and the standard-deviation and centered-error denominators are not the same. Review covers the complete short calculation, not forecast-verification inference or numerical stability by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-06 at `a9bef907e570e4b18e0eca412aeba3f1e51b6cc3`.

**L2b — source-reviewed**

INI_CONT configures thresholds and ACC_CONT tallies observation/forecast category pairs for each experiment. The native loops use strict greater-than threshold comparisons, with categories numbered zero through NCLASS, so an observation equal to a threshold remains in the lower category. The input scatter layout stores observations in row one and forecast-minus-observation differences in later rows; ACC_CONT adds the observation back before classifying each forecast. It resets the count table on each call rather than accumulating successive batches. Supply initialized pointer-backed SCATTER_TYPE arrays, increasing thresholds, valid parameter indices and compatible experiment/table dimensions. The shared module state is not independent per caller. This is contingency-table construction L2b, not a score calculation, categorical hypothesis test or probability estimate.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The hyperdual type stores value, two first-direction components and a mixed component. The selected hdual constructor copies all four seeds. hdexp and hdsin propagate first derivatives and the mixed second derivative by chain-rule formulas, including the incoming mixed seed. For a univariate x seeded as (x,1,1,0), dx1 and dx2 represent the first derivative and dx1x2 the second derivative of the selected smooth expression. This is operator/function-based automatic differentiation, not a finite-difference step-size method or a full Hessian driver. Only the scalar constructor, exponential and sine paths were inspected; thousands of other overloads, branch logic and nonsmooth/domain behavior are outside this review. Floating-point errors/overflow remain and no derivative check was run.

**N6a2b — source-reviewed**

heap_sort builds a maximum heap by downward sifting, repeatedly swaps the root with the shrinking last element and sifts again. Data values are overwritten in ascending order, supporting active real sorting N6a2b. Optional permutation labels start as 1:N and follow the same swaps, so sorted(i)=original(perm(i)); this is also the relation tested in the author driver and is the inverse convention to the header formula sorted(perm(n))=unsorted(n). The size argument and permutation must match storage, C_SIZE_T/C_DOUBLE kinds must be respected, and index/size overflow and NaN ordering are not checked. No stability, performance or executed correctness claim is made.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `d77f88fb063944bade22b3f24ae297787434d8fc`.

**D2a2a — source-reviewed**

THOMAS performs the no-pivot forward elimination and back substitution for one real tridiagonal system. It copies the diagonal and right-hand side, so the input arrays are preserved. All four arrays use length N, with AS(1) and CS(N) unused; they are not packed N-1 off-diagonals. N must be positive and all intermediate pivots nonzero. There is no dimension check, singularity status, pivoting, condition estimate or iterative refinement. D2a2a records general real tridiagonal systems, not an SPD-only solver. Review covers the complete short native implementation; numerical stability on arbitrary inputs is not established.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The public compact differentiator constructs first- or second-derivative stencils and solves a tridiagonal or cyclic tridiagonal system. The periodic path uses two Thomas solves plus a Sherman-Morrison correction. Its padding treats the first and last samples as a duplicated periodic endpoint; it is not the usual N distinct periodic samples layout. The second argument is the divisor used directly: pass h for the first derivative and h squared for the second, as the CPU heat kernel does. The sixth-order label describes the intended smooth uniform-grid stencil, not a checked observed convergence rate. Nonperiodic constructors take boundary schemes and use the same solver, but their boundary formulas have not been numerically verified. Require enough nodes, positive spacing divisor and nonsingular solves/correction denominator; no status is returned.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The public Euler and RK3 integrator bindings advance objects implementing the abstract field RHS. Euler uses one forward step; RK3 uses three explicitly weighted stages. These are fixed-step one-step methods for the semi-discrete initial-value problem, not adaptive ODE solvers. Both compute FLOOR((ENDTIME-STARTTIME)/DT) and omit any fractional final step. Positive DT and an interval giving the intended number of steps are caller responsibilities, as are stability restrictions of the spatial operator. No error estimate, rejection, status or automatic step choice is implemented. Review deliberately does not endorse the separate AB2 path: its history update assigns F1 after overwriting F2, and its startup advances even when the computed step count is zero.

**I2a1b — source-reviewed**

The CPU field RHS applies compact second derivatives along all three axes of a uniform 3D tensor grid and sums them to approximate the Laplacian for unit-diffusivity heat flow. The native implementation constructs the periodic second-derivative operator and supplies h squared as its divisor. Paired with the reviewed explicit field integrators this is a parabolic initial-boundary-value prototype in two or more spatial dimensions. All axes share one spacing; boundary conditions are periodic with duplicated endpoints on each axis. It is not an arbitrary-domain, mixed-boundary, variable-coefficient or unconditionally stable PDE solver. Stored field values are default REAL, and the RHS allocates several full-size arrays. No status, spatial error estimate, conservation check or CFL enforcement is provided. CUDA variants and the separate AB2 integration history are outside this mapping.

**M — source-reviewed**

PREDICT_K_STEPS propagates an initial probability row vector through a finite-state transition matrix by repeated vector-matrix products. PREDICT_NEXT_STEP applies MATMUL(state_vector,transition_matrix), establishing the row-stochastic orientation. This is exact finite-step probability propagation up to floating-point arithmetic, not random path simulation or a continuous-time Markov solver. Broad stochastic-modeling class M is retained because the adopted taxonomy has no explicit finite-state discrete-time probability-propagation leaf; M1b is not inferred from the word Markov alone. The routines do not validate dimensions, nonnegativity, row sums, state-vector normalization or step counts. Negative K_STEPS simply leaves the original state under the loop semantics, so the sketch restricts K>=0. Review covers these pure first-order routines, not ergodicity, stationary distributions or the separate greedy higher-order trajectory routine.

Implementation helper `predict_next_step`: [src/markov_core.f90:18–25](https://github.com/barisbarisgithub/markov_fortran-/blob/38371cf44c5a221b53cbd5023be9fae2c4040f78/src/markov_core.f90#L18-L25).

**L10a2 — source-reviewed**

FIT_TRANSITION_MATRIX estimates a higher-order categorical transition table from an ordered state sequence. It encodes each length-ORDER history in base N_STATES, counts the following state and normalizes each observed-history row. An entirely unseen history receives a uniform row; this is a fallback, not Laplace smoothing of all observed counts. The result has N_STATES**ORDER rows and N_STATES columns, so storage and integer exponent/index overflow grow rapidly with order. Require state labels in 1..N_STATES, positive state count/order and enough sequence entries. There is no input-validation or statistical-status output. This is categorical time-domain model estimation, not linear autoregression, and broad L10a2 is kept rather than forcing an AR estimation leaf. The separate higher-order k-step routine chooses successive MAXLOC states and is not a full probability forecast; that routine is not used by this sketch.

The public DIVDIFF builds the triangular table of Newton divided differences; NEWTONPOLYVAL evaluates supplied Newton coefficients by nested multiplication. These are univariate polynomial interpolation components, separate from adaptive positivity/boundedness selection. Require distinct finite abscissae, 0<=D<N and initialized coefficient entries: trailing unused triangular cells in TABLE are not assigned. No duplicate-node guard, condition estimate or numerical error bound is supplied. The sketch uses the fully defined first row of a degree-two divided-difference table.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

ADAPTIVEINTERPOLATION1D constructs per-interval Newton polynomials using divided differences, expanding the stencil while the selected boundedness/positivity inequalities admit points, and evaluates at ordered output locations. INTERPOLATION_TYPE=1 selects data-bounded and 2 positivity-oriented constraints; DEG reports selected degrees. Require increasing distinct input/output coordinates, N>=3 (endpoint slopes read Y(3)), 1<=DEGREE<N and in-range queries for preservation claims. A header comment reverses input ordering, but source checks and interval comparisons require ascending order. Extrapolation explicitly loses the advertised preservation. The code may STOP on invalid coordinate ordering and does not return a success/status flag. This review covers stencil selection, interface and evaluation structure, not a proof that all bound conditions or floating-point corner cases preserve the advertised property.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

ADAPTIVEINTERPOLATION2D first interpolates each grid column along x and then each intermediate row along y through the selected scalar 1D adaptive routine. V has shape (NX,NY), VOUT (MX,MY). It is tensor-product gridded interpolation, not scattered data, conservative remapping or a proof of multidimensional positivity. Default ST here is 3, unlike the scalar routine default 1; EPS0/EPS1 are forwarded. The 1D minimum-size/order requirements and invalid-order STOP behavior propagate to both passes. No status argument is available and this tensor dispatcher was not executed or numerically validated.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

HOMPACK90::FIXPNF initializes a homotopy path and controls dense normal-flow continuation with STEPNF, switching tolerances on curvature and dispatching ROOTNF when lambda reaches 1. With IFLAG=-1 it targets F(X)=0, using externally linked F and Jacobian-column FJAC callbacks specified by HOMOTOPY; IFLAG=0 instead solves a fixed-point problem and -2 selects a supplied homotopy. F2 is the nonlinear-system leaf in this taxonomy, not a newly invented homotopy child. Source-visible input checks, adaptive tolerance updates, 1000-step continuation returns and cleanup are reviewed at driver level. IFLAG=1 is normal termination; 2/3 are resumable with saved state, and 4..8 record failures. Saved path arrays/scalars make interleaved solves unsafe without separate contexts. POLY_SWITCH is tested by presence, not logical value, so omit it for ordinary zero finding. No global-convergence guarantee, complete STEPNF/ROOTNF/kernel audit or numerical solve was established.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `c9701c43fdd4c5c2d8a7c1ea743ec74dd7d2c6e1`.

**L4a1b1 — source-reviewed**

The public SAFE-mode HPCS_MEDIAN/MAD/QUANTILE entries provide nonparametric location, dispersion and quantile summaries. They copy inputs, select order statistics by quickselect, average middle values for even-size medians, and interpolate quantiles with h=1+(n-1)*q. MAD is the raw median absolute deviation without a Gaussian consistency multiplier. SAFE mode propagates NaN with HPCS_SUCCESS rather than omitting it; callers must check both status and finiteness. Invalid n/q/mode returns do not promise an initialized numeric output, and NaN q is not rejected by ordinary range comparisons. Very large finite values can overflow middle-value averaging or interpolation differences. Explicit SAFE selection avoids the thread-local global mode; FAST/deterministic branches are not numerically validated here. Review covers public dispatch and SAFE calculations, not performance or rounding-error certification.

**L10a1c4 — source-reviewed**

HPCS_ROLLING_MEDIAN applies a trailing nonlinear median filter to a one-dimensional sequence. The SAFE path fills the first WINDOW-1 outputs with quiet NaN, then copies each complete window and calls the SAFE scalar median. This is a nonlinear filter, not a symmetric linear moving average or a centered window. NaN within a window propagates into its output, and no missing-value omission or boundary padding is performed. Require 1<=WINDOW<=N and an N-element output. Inner status is not propagated after each median call; the valid-window path finally returns HPCS_SUCCESS. The implementation allocates/copies window buffers and is not an O(n) sliding-order-statistic method. Review covers SAFE dispatch/window semantics, not all rolling anomaly/MAD algorithms or performance.

**D2b1b — source-reviewed**

HSSCHOLSOLVER solves a real dense symmetric positive-definite system through an approximate hierarchical semiseparable Cholesky representation, optionally refined by preconditioned CG. The caller supplies a dense matrix, block/rank/compression controls and one RHS vector, despite comments mentioning multiple RHSs. RS=S selects deterministic SVD compression and RS=R randomized compression; WPCG=N uses the approximate direct solve, Y the iterative refinement path. Selected construction code compresses tree blocks and applies local Cholesky/orthogonal transformations; SOLVECHOLSVD traverses the factor tree and applies triangular solves. INFO validates option flags but is not propagated from lower-level factorization/convergence/allocation failures (some allocation exits retain INFO=0). Thus INFO=0 is not a numerical solve certificate. Input A is copied internally and B overwritten; preserve original RHS and check a residual. Review covers the driver and selected construction/solve tree paths, not all low-rank kernels or an accuracy/scaling guarantee.

**D1b6 — source-reviewed**

DHSSMM compresses a dense square real A into a hierarchical semiseparable representation, then traverses its low-rank factor tree to overwrite dense B with approximate A*B in column panels. FASTHSSMM applies upward/downward tree products with dense block multiplications. The wrapper assumes LDA=M=N and needs valid block/rank and panel sizes; this is not a general rectangular matrix product. The selected wrapper has concrete limitations: INFO is never assigned, the remainder-panel branch slices B rows instead of columns, and multiplication TIME(2) subtracts clocks in reverse order. The sketch therefore restricts K to a positive multiple of NCOL and does not interpret INFO or timing as validation. Compression tolerance controls internal approximations, not an independently measured product error. Review covers construction/product dispatch and selected tree multiply paths; it does not certify every compression kernel or OpenMP variant.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `61a222115c41b83cad8deee501cb3f93818961a9`.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

DOPRI5 provides an explicit embedded Dormand-Prince 5(4) method for nonstiff initial-value systems. The inspected entry checks options/workspace, configures error tolerances and dispatches the stage/acceptance/step-control core in the same file. Stiffness detection can stop integration; it is not a stiff solver. This fork adds a LOGICAL DEBUG argument between IOUT and WORK, so an unmodified upstream DOPRI5 call is incompatible. Dense output requires selected component storage and SOLOUT configuration. Only this method, not all HWODE solvers, is source reviewed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `784b80fe5ed02670bd9f17a73489de42652c38b3`.

[examples/dopri5_eq1.f](https://github.com/cpmech/hwode/blob/784b80fe5ed02670bd9f17a73489de42652c38b3/examples/dopri5_eq1.f)

External double-precision nonstiff ODE driver. FCN(N,X,Y,F,RPAR,IPAR) supplies derivatives. ITOL=0 uses scalar tolerances and ITOL=1 vectors. Y and X are advanced. With NRDENS dense components, the author allocates LWORK=8*N+5*NRDENS+21 and LIWORK=NRDENS+21.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DOPRI5(N, FCN, X, Y, XEND, RTOL, ATOL, ITOL, &
     SOLOUT, IOUT, DEBUG, WORK, LWORK, IWORK, LIWORK, RPAR, IPAR, IDID)
```

```fortran
work = 0.0d0
iwork = 0
debug = .false.
iout = 0  ! no step-output callback; no dense components
call dopri5(n,fcn,x,y,xend,rtol,atol,0,solout,iout,debug, &
     work,size(work),iwork,size(iwork),rpar,ipar,idid)

```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use positive compatible tolerances and initialized callback parameters. IDID=1 reaches the endpoint; 2 means interrupted by SOLOUT. Negative codes describe input, step-budget, step-size and stiffness failures. The pinned example enables dense output; the fragment above disables it.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

HYPERBOB launches one bound-constrained BOBYQA local search per MPI rank from a common-seed random Latin hypercube, collects objective values, and broadcasts the best computed point. This is heuristic multistart global minimization, not certified coverage or a proof of global optimality. MPI_INIT and collective HYPERBOB_INITIALIZE precede use; HYPERBOB_CLEANUP releases module arrays. Every rank must use matching dimensions, seed and bounds. RHOBMIN/RHOEMAX and SEED are mutable. MAXTIME is explicitly not implemented; ERR only checks allocated row capacity and is not BOBYQA convergence or an MPI success report. The MPI_GATHER receive section can be noncontiguous when NROWS>NX; use NROWS=NX in the sketch pending validation of compiler packing and MPI-buffer behavior. Review covers wrapper selection/communication and callback contracts, not every BOBYQA or Latin-sampling kernel.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `c8460193927f74e93703e0c270e2533a08de8dbc`.

**R2 — source-reviewed**

The public pure elemental IS_IEEE_QUIET_NAN generic accepts IEEE_CLASS_TYPE or supported real kinds, classifies real values through intrinsic IEEE_CLASS, and compares the class with IEEE_QUIET_NAN. The same source provides separate signaling-NaN, signed-zero and infinity predicates. R2 records floating-point class checking, not arithmetic, a sanitizer for all numerical errors or a portable trap handler. SET_IEEE_QUIET_NAN is a companion IEEE_VALUE setter. Actual support for real kinds and exceptional values depends on the compiler/platform; the generated module includes REAL128, while the Fypp template can configure kinds. IEEE exception behavior, including signaling values, must be checked on the target compiler. Source review covers the dispatch and selected real64/class implementations.

**D4a2 — source-reviewed**

The public EIG generic computes ordinary eigenvalues of a real nonsymmetric square matrix by Householder Hessenberg reduction followed by implicit double-shift QR steps and recursive deflation. Its complex-output overload preserves complex-conjugate pairs; the real-output overload explicitly discards imaginary parts, so it is not a reliable representation of a general nonsymmetric spectrum. Error reporting is through an optional callback, whose default silently ignores both rectangular-input and nonconvergence events. The calling sketch installs a callback and uses complex output. This is an experimental eigenvalue-only implementation, not a complete Schur/eigenvector interface. Exceptional shifts are marked TODO, exact subdiagonal-zero splitting follows a numerical truncation heuristic and exhausted iterations can leave initialized placeholder results. Review covers the native reduction/QR/deflation paths and callback contract, not the separate bundled LAPACK comparison routine or numerical convergence guarantees.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `247c3d8cad2892fab419854c71ee04c2b2e715c6`.

**D4c1b2 — source-reviewed**

The public EIG_HESSENBERG_MATRIX function reduces a real square matrix to upper Hessenberg form using two-sided Householder similarity transformations. EIG_REFLECT forms the reflector from each active column and applies it from the left and right; the driver zeros entries below the first subdiagonal after reduction. This is the associated Hessenberg-reduction operation rather than an eigensolve or an orthogonal-factor-returning API. The function returns H only, not the accumulated similarity matrix Q. It assumes square nonempty input and does not expose a numerical status; unlike the eigenvalue callback path, it has no explicit rectangular-input check. The sketch therefore supplies a small finite square matrix. Review covers the actual reflector construction/application rather than inferring a reduction from a wrapper name.

**D1b3 — source-reviewed**

insitu_Array%init remaps contiguous REAL(4) target storage into a two-dimensional pointer with the supplied shape. %t then calls mipt to permute the underlying one-dimensional elements in place and remaps the two-dimensional view with reversed extents. This is a data-rearranging transpose, not merely a stride-only view. The implementation allocates a LOGICAL(KIND=1) flag array of m*n elements but never uses it, so no constant-workspace claim is made. Positive compatible extents, associated contiguous storage, sufficient capacity and nonoverflowing integer index products are caller preconditions, with no validation/status. REAL(4)/C interoperability and rectangular permutation edge cases need independent build/runtime checks.

**L8c — source-reviewed**

The selected ISLASSO entry estimates a weighted Gaussian multiple-linear regression with induced-smoothed lasso/elastic-net-style penalty terms. It precomputes X-transpose W X and X-transpose W(y-offset), alternates damped penalized coefficient solves and covariance/standard-error updates, and optionally adapts penalties/mixture parameters. This is penalized regression, not ordinary unpenalized least squares or a robust-loss mapping inferred from the lasso name. Starting coefficient/SE/covariance inputs and positive observation weights are part of the workflow. X, lambda, limits/tolerance and output arrays can be overwritten; STAND=0 avoids standardization in the sketch. CONV reports outer limit or numerical failure, but the initial DPOTRF status is overwritten by DPOTRS before inspection, so a failed factorization can be obscured; additional factorization validation is required. R interrupt/normal-density/CDF and trace helpers mean this is R-hosted code, not a standalone Fortran library. Review covers the Gaussian entry and penalty derivative routines, not the separate generalized-linear family/link paths or inferential coverage.

**H2b1a1 — source-reviewed**

The redistributed DCUHRE driver automatically integrates a vector of user-provided functions over a hyperrectangle. It validates dimension/rule/workspace controls, then DADHRE repeatedly bisects a region with greatest estimated error, evaluates embedded cubature rules and maintains a heap of regions until componentwise absolute/relative criteria or the evaluation budget is reached. The selected default two-dimensional rule has 65 samples per region and the driver supports dimensions 2..15, not a general one-dimensional quadrature entry. IFAIL=0 means the internal estimated-error criterion; IFAIL=1 returns an approximation after budget exhaustion and larger codes report invalid controls. Estimated error is not a rigorous bound. Restart requires preserved compatible workspace and controls; the sketch starts fresh. Review covers driver validation, subdivision/error aggregation and termination paths, not every cubature weight generator or high-dimensional reliability claim.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

NINFOL estimates an observed-information matrix, namely minus the Hessian of a user log-density/log-likelihood at a supplied mode. It evaluates central second differences with successively smaller steps, extrapolates using RID_EX and uses estimated diagonal curvature to scale mixed differences. It does not exponentiate the log function or divide the final log-Hessian by its exponential, despite ambiguous prose in the historical comments. MU must be a genuine stationary maximum with positive diagonal information; otherwise square-root scaling can be invalid. DP must contain nonzero meaningful steps and ITER must be positive. IERR is a real matrix of extrapolation-error estimates, not an integer success flag; ITER=1 sets these estimates to zero without estimating error. MU is temporarily perturbed and restored on normal paths. Review covers diagonal/mixed differencing and extrapolation dispatch, not a general-purpose Hessian routine valid at arbitrary points or a covariance/inference guarantee.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `fedde4bfd3bb9882640d303238188dbb73016598`.

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

adaptive_integrator%integrate wraps a procedure-pointer integrand, allocates work storage, obtains tolerances and subdivision limits, and dispatches the no-breakpoint finite-interval path to DQAGS. DQAGS partitions workspace for DQAGSE, whose inspected controller bisects high-error subintervals, calls DQK21 and uses DQELG extrapolation/error ordering. H2a1a1 records automatic finite-interval callback quadrature, scoped to dispatch and adaptive controller rather than an audit of every numerical kernel. Defaults are absolute/relative tolerance 1e-8 and ten subdivisions. Source concerns remain: ai_init can read an unassigned local flag when reusing adequate existing workspace; the separate breakpoint call passes bare iwork/work names instead of the declared object components. That breakpoint path is not validated here. Output info contains estimated error/evaluation/subinterval counts, while failures are reported through FERROR. No upstream library, example or numerical accuracy check was built/run.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `6ee15e29d77cc6789e55df4ba452fa2addcd4ec5780ba73f1267a12776745258`.

**E2b — source-reviewed**

The inspected quadratic_shepard_2d wrapper creates local quadratic models for scattered planar points through alg660::qshep2. The reviewed core builds weighted least-squares systems, applies Givens rotations and solves for nodal quadratic coefficients. qs2val blends those local polynomials with compact-support modified Shepard weights, returning the stored value exactly at a node; qs2grd differentiates that weighted quotient. E2b is scattered multivariate interpolation, not gridded tensor-product interpolation. Only this 2D path is reviewed: the spherical, triangulation and 3D variants are not certified here. The wrapper fixes neighbor counts, uses default REAL and requires at least six equal-length samples. Duplicate/collinear configurations and unsupported query locations have status paths. Query methods assume successful construction and do not guard against unallocated data. No interpolation or gradient check was run.

**D5 — source-reviewed**

iddr_qrpiv selects columns by trailing norms, builds Householder transformations and updates/recomputes pivot norms for a fixed-rank real QR. iddr_id then composes the pivot swaps into selected-column indices and backsolves R11*proj=R12, packing interpolation coefficients into the start of overwritten A. D5 records the QR-based decomposition path; ID is not an SVD, and selected original columns must be retained from a copy. Require 1<=krank<=MIN(m,n): the QR helper clips loop count but the ID wrapper subsequently accesses the requested rank. rnorms receives signed diagonal entries despite absolute-value wording in its header. Large interpolation coefficients are zeroed at a fixed 2**20 comparison, not reported as a numerical-error status. No matrix approximation, reference QR or error bound was checked by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `4de32e3d455b9e5c11bdb65aa37dc85e640f57d0`.

```fortran
external :: iddr_id

a(:,1)=[1.0d0,0.0d0,1.0d0,2.0d0]

a(:,3)=a(:,1)+a(:,2); original=a
```

[README.md](https://github.com/fremling/jacobi-theta-function-fortran/blob/ea49a80f47de5fde413d426521a2e970f8c682c1/README.md)

**C13 — source-reviewed**

THETA3 dispatches to a logarithmic implementation that shifts/inverts tau, reduces z, sums paired exponential terms and finally exponentiates the result. Source uses exp(i*pi*n*(tau*n+2*z)), so z has real period one, unlike conventions with period pi. Require Im(tau)>0. Invalid tau, excessive transformation/shift recursion and detected NaNs call EXIT(-1), terminating the process rather than returning status. MAXITER limits transformations/shifts, not the final series loop, whose stopping test uses floating-point stagnation. Only THETA3 and the inspected shared helper path are mapped here; the other advertised theta/log/generalized interfaces are not independently certified.

**D6 — source-reviewed**

The public JACV0_EXECUTE generic performs the one-sided Jacobi column-orthogonalization core of an SVD through a Fortran interface to AVX2/FMA or AVX-512 native kernels. It initializes V to identity, applies column rotations/swaps to G and V and returns packed transformation/sweep counters. It does not itself return a normalized U and singular-value vector, so a complete validated SVD needs postprocessing and residual/orthogonality checks. The inspected parameter/preparation predicates require M=N and vector-multiple dimensions; they must not be generalized to arbitrary rectangular matrices. Matrices and integer strategy workspace require matching alignment, prepared pivot offsets and supported CPU instructions. The reviewed C bridge expects 64-bit pointer-offset workspace and packed integer storage, so select a matching 64-bit-integer build rather than assuming default INTEGER works. QUERY/PREPARE use positive strategy counts on successful paths and EXECUTE INFO holds counters, not an INFO=0 success convention. Review covers the concrete Fortran bridge and AVX2 rotation/sweep paths, not the unrelated full LAPACK comparison executables or all platforms.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `5bfbbe74443636d30e5645e4902220a7a694f3eb76e6e89ac8ccd0470f43f228`.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected external newtonhook routine solves a square residual system using a matrix-vector callback, right-preconditioned GMRES and SVD-regularized hooksteps. It compares actual residual-norm reduction with the predicted reduction and retries trust-region radii. The author example approximates J*v by directional residual differences around module state new_x/new_fx; the core itself accepts a supplied operator and does not automatically differentiate an arbitrary callback. This is F2 root finding, not a general constrained optimizer or ODE integrator. Source limitations remain: newtonhook overwrites the GMRES return flag ginfo with the input print flag info immediately after the solve, so the advertised GMRES-failure propagation is not established; GMRES normalizes residual/Arnoldi vectors without explicit zero-norm guards. Some linear-algebra failures STOP. Reusing the saved Krylov state and module-wide solution arrays requires coordinated calls. No failure, periodic orbit or nonlinear accuracy result was reproduced.

External routine using the separate module newton for saved state. Allocate new_x(n), new_fx(n), set new_x to the initial guess, then provide f(n,x,y), df(n,v,jv), in-place preconditioner dfp(n,v), parameterless monitor sub(), and double-precision dp(n,a,b). df must apply the Jacobian at the current shared iterate. info is both print-control input and termination output. Tolerances and trust-radius parameters are double precision; del=0 disables hooksteps.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL newtonhook(f, df, dfp, sub, dp, m, n, gtol, tol, del, mndl, mxdl, nits, info)
```

**D — source-reviewed**

The public DHSVD2 module procedure performs a two-by-two real hyperbolic singular-value transformation, using a signature J with entries +/-1. It scales the input, triangularizes/pivots it, dispatches the specialized KHSVD2 transformation if needed, accumulates left/right transforms and handles signature-dependent sorting. This is a small signature-metric decomposition building block, not an ordinary Euclidean SVD for arbitrary matrix dimensions; broad D is retained. A is overwritten, U/Z are outputs, and positive INFO values encode transformation/exceptional-case bits rather than failure under a simple INFO/=0 rule. Negative INFO reports invalid signature/nonfinite/error paths; signature checks can be compiled out with NDEBUG. TH1 controls an exceptional near-unit-hyperbolic-parameter path that may retain off-diagonals. Preserve original A and use author transformation conventions for reconstruction and signature checks. Review covers the small dispatcher/triangularization/sorting and selected hyperbolic recurrence, not the complete parallel J-Kogbetliantz sweep driver.

**K4 — source-reviewed**

EIGEN_RANKN_PARAMS forms sqrt(Wx)*K*sqrt(Wy), computes a dense SVD and constructs Nystrom coefficients for separated singular-function kernel approximation, with X_FUNC_WTS sized (NY,RANK) and Y_FUNC_WTS (NX,RANK). This is a quadrature-discretized approximation for a supplied concrete two-variable kernel; it is not a uniform/global minimax error certificate. Although input guards allow nonnegative weights, later code divides by their square roots, so supply strictly positive finite weights; retained singular values must be nonzero before reciprocal scaling. Rank must be positive and no larger than either point count. No extra guard handles zero retained singular values, numerical rank deficiency or ill-conditioned kernels. The review covers this selected approximation path, not every numerically-optimal/rank-reduction algorithm in the larger library.

**F1b — source-reviewed**

BRENTZERO finds a scalar bracketed zero using bisection, secant and inverse-quadratic steps with finite iteration and function-evaluation tracking. The function is a concrete object extending SINGLEVAR_FUNC with a pure EVAL binding, not a bare external callback. Endpoint roots return immediately; same-sign endpoints produce ERRCode=2 and quiet NaNs, and iteration exhaustion returns code 1 and NaNs. Require a continuous finite-valued function on the bracket, a valid tolerance and positive iteration budget; the sign check multiplies endpoint values, so extreme scaling/overflow needs attention. The convenience ZEROIN function discards status, so the sketch selects the explicit-status service. No multiple-root enumeration, discontinuity handling or independent residual certificate is claimed.

**L10a2e — source-reviewed**

KFILTER performs sequential-observation Kalman filtering for a linear Gaussian state-space model, including optional exact diffuse initialization via P1INF/RANKP. The inspected ordinary branch updates innovations, gain, mean/covariance and log likelihood, then propagates the state with T and R*Q*R^T. TIMEVAR has five 0/1 selectors controlling third-dimension lengths of Z,H,T,R,Q. YMISS=0 means observed; positive missing flags skip measurement updates. The scalar-observation sketch avoids the requirement to transform correlated multivariate measurement errors before sequential filtering: the core uses diagonal H entries. AT(:,t) and PT(:,:,t) are prediction states before observation t; the optional THETA output uses those predictions and is not a smoothed estimate. Likelihood accumulation and tolerance-based zero-innovation handling do not certify covariance positivity or model fit. Review covers driver and ordinary/diffuse one-step recurrences, not every R-facing data transformation or non-Gaussian smoother.

Dense conjugate gradients for a real symmetric positive-definite A(N,N), B(N), and input/output initial guess X(N). Import WP from KISS (double precision). Optional RTOL/ATOL set the residual threshold MAX(ATOL,RTOL*NORM2(B)); MAXITER defaults to 10*N. Optional CALLBACK(X) observes iterates and must match the linked interface. Request optional INFO: 0 signals the internal residual stopping test, positive values the iteration count on exhaustion; this does not certify a separately recomputed residual or validate positive definiteness. B=0 returns X=0. All controls after X are independently optional and may be passed by keyword.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL cg_dense(A,B,X[,RTOL,ATOL,MAXITER,CALLBACK,INFO])
```

Argument declarations: [src/kiss@cg.F90:53–59](https://github.com/ivan-pi/kiss/blob/55f0f7ccb1601a0628a17928b5b6b79f61da2892/src/kiss@cg.F90#L53-L59).

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The F77 double-precision RNFARR copies a 100-value state, extends it by lag-100/37 modular floating-point additions and updates saved COMMON /RSTATE/. RNFSTR expands an integer seed, mixes its state and warms up the generator. L6a21 records floating-point uniform generation; the integer and Fortran-IV variants are not covered. RNFARR always writes its first 100 outputs regardless of N, so require N>=100 and seed explicitly first. Shared COMMON state is not independent per caller/thread. The separate scalar RNDNXD/RNDCYD convenience path reseeds to 314159 whenever its buffer refills, repeating blocks rather than continuously advancing; the sketch avoids it. No reference sequence, period, distribution or wrapper failure was run.
