SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `2f23b71ac36346fdf987a5cac81ae761aff5a285363465b863edf3b60d681974`.

**D6 — source-reviewed**

The real64 DKSVD0 interface and its included gksvd0 body implement a two-sided Kogbetliantz SVD of a square N-by-N matrix. The body generates index pairs, extracts 2-by-2 pivots, applies left/right rotations, optionally accumulates U and V, and extracts singular values from the transformed diagonal. D6 is already a GAMS leaf, with no separate cyclic or precision subclass. This review follows the cyclic/quasi-cyclic real64 path, not every blocked, dynamic, complex or higher-precision variant. Some strategies require even N. DKSVD2 is a Fortran wrapper around the external libpvn PVN_DLJSV2 kernel; it is not an independent local implementation of that 2-by-2 algorithm. INFO carries an input step budget/accuracy mode and an output sweep count or limit, rather than a universal zero-success convention. Scaling, rounding assumptions, reconstruction, orthogonality and parallel performance were not tested; no rectangular-matrix claim is inferred from the repository title.

Public entry point `DKSVD0`: [src/blksvd/dksvd0.F90:1–113](https://github.com/venovako/KogAcc/blob/c852e6d85355b5e7f3efb58b86cbe0c043cecd7d/src/blksvd/dksvd0.F90#L1-L113).

External REAL64 square-matrix SVD subroutine. G is overwritten; SV holds the singular values and JOB controls the pivot strategy and initialization/accumulation of U and V. All leading dimensions, schedule/work arrays and INFO must be prepared explicitly. INFO is an input step budget (with sign-dependent mode) and an output status/sweep count, not solely a LAPACK-style output error code.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DKSVD0(JOB, N, G, LDG, U, LDU, V, LDV, SV, W, O, R, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [src/blksvd/dksvd0.F90:78–89](https://github.com/venovako/KogAcc/blob/c852e6d85355b5e7f3efb58b86cbe0c043cecd7d/src/blksvd/dksvd0.F90#L78-L89).

The driver allocates W(MAX(6,3*M)), generates the schedule with JSWEEP, and prepares O and R for its padded matrix size M; these requirements depend on the chosen strategy. Do not pass uninitialized INFO. **L14a1b — source-reviewed**

The public EXTERNAL_TRAIN_MAP entry constructs a normal self-organizing map, trains through repeated best-matching-unit searches and neighborhood-weighted prototype updates, and returns nonhierarchical prototype assignments and map diagnostics. This is non-nested prototype clustering, not supervised classification or a dendrogram. The C-binding arrays use observations by variables; the wrapper fixes the random seed to 12345 and Euclidean distance even though DISTANCE_TYPE is accepted. GRID_TYPE=0/1 selects rectangular/hexagonal layout and NEIGH_TYPE=0/1 bubble/Gaussian neighborhoods. Invalid selectors are not comprehensively rejected. The training best-match search initializes its distance threshold to 100000, so scale inputs and investigate large-distance cases before trusting indices. Allocation/status and distortion diagnostics do not provide a convergence certificate. Review covers the normal-SOM wrapper, training update and prediction dispatch, not robust/ViSOM variants or cluster validity.

**L14a1b — source-reviewed**

The public SELF_ORGANIZING_MAP%TRAIN binding fits a fixed-grid Kohonen prototype map through online best-match selection and neighborhood-weighted prototype updates. The reviewed normal_som path uses a decreasing learning rate/radius and Gaussian or bubble neighborhoods, then assigns patterns to final best-matching nodes. This is non-nested prototype clustering, not hierarchical clustering or a supervised predictor. Training needs a created map, compatible initialized KOHONEN_PATTERN objects and validated layer parameters; create randomizes prototype values using the configured generator. The implementation visits patterns in supplied order, has radius/learning-rate floors and writes progress/distortion information. The OpenMP best-match loop updates a shared argmin without a visible reduction/protection; use a serial build or one OpenMP thread for this scoped sketch. Empty/invalid dimensions, unsuitable scaling and all nonfinite distances are not certified. Review covers the public binding and normal_som best-match/update paths, not all ViSOM or two-level variants.

**E1b — source-reviewed**

Interpolation::lagrange directly evaluates the global Lagrange interpolation polynomial by multiplying all nodal factors for each datum and summing the weighted ordinates. lagrangep applies that scalar function to query points, allocating yEval only if not already allocated. Require nonempty equal-length data with distinct abscissae; no duplicate-node, conditioning or overflow check exists. An already allocated yEval must match the query length because the routine does not resize it. This is global polynomial interpolation, not piecewise splines: the naturalcubicspline routines are unimplemented ERROR STOP placeholders, and are not mapped. No interpolation check was run.

**C3b — source-reviewed**

Polynomials::horner evaluates a polynomial stored in increasing-power coefficient order by starting from the last coefficient and descending with y=y*x+p(i). It checks for a nonempty coefficient array using ERROR STOP. This is ordinary nonorthogonal power-basis polynomial evaluation, not root finding or an orthogonal basis algorithm. No compensation, overflow detection or error estimate is provided. The empty Broyden stub and the root-finding module callback precision mismatch are not promoted as additional supported methods.

**L4c1a — source-reviewed**

The selected shared-memory Fortran pipeline computes the posterior mean of a linear Gaussian inverse problem with three-factor Kronecker-separable forward/covariance structure. CALCFACTORS solves component systems, constructs generalized symmetric eigenvectors and diagonal 1/(1+lambda1*lambda2*lambda3) factors; POSTERIORMEAN contracts the observed-minus-prior-predicted data through these factors and adds the correction to MPRIOR. This is conditional multivariate Gaussian analysis, not general non-Gaussian Bayesian sampling, arbitrary covariance structure or a new inverse-problem validation. Caller arrays must have consistent tensor-product dimensions/order and positive-definite covariance factors. The mean routine uses integer progress divisors EVERYNIT/NTHR: small models or many threads can make this zero, and initial ETA calculations divide by a zero count. Repair/validate that reporting path before relying on it. OpenMP runtime symbols are used even outside directives. The README marks the non-Julia implementations unmaintained.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The selected RngStream_RandU01 path dispatches to a six-state combined multiple-recursive MRG32k3a recurrence, or a two-draw increased-precision variant. The basic recurrence combines two modular components and optionally reflects the result for antithetic sampling. Stream objects hold mutable current/start states; these are pseudorandom uniforms, not cryptographic randomness. The rng module defines the type/constants, while the callable functions are EXTERNAL procedures after END MODULE, so USE rng alone does not import their interfaces. Literal real/integer kind 8 assumptions, valid nondegenerate seeds and serialized shared package initialization matter. No period, distribution, independence or reproducibility claim was tested.

**L6c — source-reviewed**

The selected reset methods restore the current state from the initial-stream or current-substream seed, or advance the substream seed with the hardcoded A1p76/A2p76 modular matrices. Creation uses A1p127/A2p127 to advance the package state. This records implemented seed/stream services, not independently verified jump lengths or independence. The inspected CheckSeed routine is incomplete: it rejects values greater than the moduli rather than greater than or equal, does not reject negatives, and prints but fails to set ierror for an all-zero first component. Supply six positive interior seeds and do not rely on this validation for arbitrary inputs. Reset/creation/package state are mutable and not automatically thread-safe.

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The inspected LBFGS path constructs a limited-memory inverse-Hessian action from stored step/gradient-difference pairs, uses a More-Thuente-style MCSRCH line search and requests function/gradient values through reverse communication. The user supplies first derivatives, not a Hessian; G1b1b records smooth multivariate unconstrained minimization. DIAGCO optionally requests a positive diagonal scaling through IFLAG=2. The normal stopping test is ||G||/max(1,||X||)<=EPS after a completed line search; no global-optimality or local-minimum certificate is implied. The initial step is 1/||G|| before that test, so an exactly stationary starting point is not safely handled by this path. LBFGS and MCSRCH retain SAVE state and shared LB3 parameters; do not interleave independent solves as though this interface were reentrant. Preserve workspace and re-enter with the returned IFLAG. No minimization, gradient comparison or full audit of MCSTEP/BLAS dependencies was executed.

External double-precision reverse-communication minimizer. N/M are positive default INTEGER; W needs N*(2*M+1)+2*M elements. Initially evaluate F/G and set IFLAG=0. Return 1 requests fresh F/G at X, 2 requests positive DIAG when DIAGCO is true, 0 reports normal completion and negative values report errors. Link the LB2 block-data defaults and keep the state/workspace intact between calls.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL LBFGS(N, M, X, F, G, DIAGCO, DIAG, IPRINT, EPS, XTOL, W, IFLAG)
```

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: lbfgs, lb2
integer, parameter :: n=2, m=3
integer :: iprint(2), iflag, calls
double precision :: x(n), g(n), diag(n), w(n*(2*m+1)+2*m)
double precision :: f, eps, xtol
logical :: diagco
x=[2.0d0,-1.0d0]
diagco=.false.
iprint=[-1,0]
eps=1.0d-8
xtol=epsilon(1.0d0)
iflag=0
do calls=1,1000
  f=0.5d0*sum(x*x)
  g=x
  call lbfgs(n,m,x,f,g,diagco,diag,iprint,eps,xtol,w,iflag)
  if (iflag <= 0) exit
  if (iflag /= 1) error stop "unexpected reverse-communication request"
end do
if (iflag /= 0) error stop "L-BFGS did not finish normally"
```

Uncompiled fragment minimizing a quadratic from an explicitly nonstationary initial point. It uses DIAGCO=false, so no diagonal-request branch is needed. The 1000-call guard is a caller limit, not a library convergence claim. Check an initially stationary point before entering this implementation. Link the complete lbfgs.f object, including LB2 and bundled support routines, with compatible default INTEGER/double precision; archive/block-data retention may require toolchain-specific handling. Saved/shared state prevents safe interleaving of solves.

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The wrapper allocates limited-memory/work arrays and translates SETULB reverse-communication requests into objective/gradient callbacks, with an observation callback after each SETULB call. **G2h1a2 — source-reviewed**

SETULB exposes an extended reverse-communication limited-memory BFGS bound-constrained optimizer. TASK requests F and G at X, returns accepted iterates and eventually reports convergence, stop or error strings. NBD selects no/lower/both/upper bounds; The inherited FACTR/PGTOL documentation does not match this fork: both projected-gradient stopping checks are commented out and the relative-objective test is guarded by IF(.FALSE.). Callers must supply their own convergence and work-budget logic. The actual interface adds TAUX,NFG,JMAX,TAUD,NBISECT, uses ISAVE(47), DSAVE(30) and WA length 2*M*N+5*N+11*M*M+8*M+2*JMAX*N: the inherited shorter workspace comments are obsolete. The selected smooth path keeps NFG=0 to bypass the added stored-gradient convex-hull test; it still uses this fork's modified line search. Enabling that extension requires caller-managed gradient/point history as in the supplied driver and separate investigation: FREEX=1/INDCLOSE uses integer division before real assignment. This mapping does not establish nonsmooth convergence, global optimality or correctness of that extension. Driver/workspace partition, Cauchy/subspace and line-search dispatch were inspected, not every BLAS/LINPACK kernel.

```fortran
 else

enddo
```

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected 1D method selects a neighboring interval and evaluates a two-point affine formula, so the supported mapping is univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation (E1a), not arbitrary-degree global Lagrange interpolation inferred from the repository name. The public method creates/destroys private stored data per call and supports none/constant/linear extrapolation selectors. Important source findings remain: constant extrapolation returns endpoint x values rather than y values; early exits do not assign the optional success output; an unsorted-input create failure is not checked before using internal arrays; and normal cleanup resets the public object success property even after a successful optional status has been assigned. The naive method also uses adjacent-point linear interpolation. Author tests query supplied nodes rather than establishing between-node accuracy. No interpolation result or failure was reproduced by execution.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The 2D method applies the 1D adjacent-point interpolation along grid rows and then along the other axis. E2a records gridded bivariate interpolation, not scattered-data fitting, an arbitrary-degree polynomial or a mesh generator. The data layout read by source is fxy_data(size(x_data),size(y_data)). The final along-x interpolation is inside the row-filling loop, so early iterations read not-yet-filled x_estimate elements; although the final iteration has all entries filled, invalid-value traps or intermediate results were not investigated. There is no 2D status output and the 1D failure/extrapolation limitations propagate. Tests use an equal-sized grid and node queries; nonsquare grids and between-node behavior were not verified by execution.

[README.md](https://github.com/lanczos-iterator/Lanczos_Iterator/blob/8779d64f2cd4479f9108c998e3eff44049a5d9be/README.md)

**D4a1 — source-reviewed**

rs_lanczos creates real vector views over output columns and invokes the iterator sequentially for the lowest requested eigenpairs of a matrix supplied by callback. The inspected core performs a three-term Lanczos update with orthogonalization, reduces to a tridiagonal problem and dispatches Ritz extraction/polishing. D4a1 records real-symmetric ordinary eigenproblems, not nonsymmetric/generalized solvers. Callback ADD controls overwrite versus accumulation and must be honored. The output named variance is filled by residual using vector_norm, so it is a residual norm rather than a squared variance. There is no public success flag; maxstep does not bound all later polishing work. Saved RNG/recurrence state prevents assuming reentrancy. The wrapper seed packing is normalized to a valid odd final seed by vector_random_fill before LAPACK use. Restart/range mode and complex variants are outside the usage sketch. No eigenpair or independent residual was computed.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected DGESV driver solves a general real dense square system with one or more right-hand sides. It checks dimensions, dispatches LU factorization with partial pivoting to DGETRF and solves through DGETRS only if factorization reports success. A is overwritten by LU factors and B by the solution; positive INFO reports an exactly zero pivot. D2a1 is the general-system class. This source review covers the driver interface and dispatch, not an audit of every BLAS/LAPACK kernel or vendor implementation. It does not establish conditioning, error bounds, inverse formation, sparse support or numerical accuracy by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce`.

External double-precision dense linear-system driver. A(LDA,N) is overwritten by factors, B(LDB,NRHS) by solutions, and IPIV(N) records row pivots. Check INFO before using the solution. Link a compatible LAPACK/BLAS library; this source file alone is insufficient.

```fortran
CALL DGESV(N, NRHS, A, LDA, IPIV, B, LDB, INFO)
```

**D9a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected real DGELS driver chooses QR or LQ factorization by matrix shape and applies orthogonal transformations and triangular solves for unconstrained least squares or minimum-norm underdetermined solves. For TRANS=N and M>=N, the reviewed path forms Q-transpose B and solves with R. The interface assumes full rank; positive INFO detects exactly zero triangular diagonals, not reliable numerical rank or near-singularity. D9a1 records the unconstrained L2 solution scope. Workspace queries and scaling are visible in the driver. This review does not certify all dependency kernels, rank-deficient methods, constrained least squares or runtime accuracy.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce`.

[SRC/dgels.f](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dgels.f)

Public entry point `DGELS`: [SRC/dgels.f:189–525](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dgels.f#L189-L525).

External full-rank real least-squares/minimum-norm driver. TRANS selects A or its transpose. A and B are overwritten; B needs at least MAX(1,M,N) rows even when the input right-hand side is shorter. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 before allocating the working buffer, then check INFO after the solve.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DGELS(TRANS, M, N, NRHS, A, LDA, B, LDB, WORK, LWORK, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [SRC/dgels.f:189–203](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dgels.f#L189-L203).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dgels
integer :: info, lwork
double precision :: a(3,2), b(3,1), query(1)
double precision, allocatable :: work(:)
a(:,1) = 1.0d0
a(:,2) = [0.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0]
b(:,1) = [1.0d0, 2.0d0, 2.0d0]
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, query, -1, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS query failed"
lwork = max(1, ceiling(query(1)))
allocate(work(lwork))
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, work, lwork, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS failed"
! For this M>=N case, b(1:2,1) holds the fitted coefficients.
```

Calling sketch only. Link compatible LAPACK and BLAS and match the integer/real ABI. The example uses the full-rank overdetermined TRANS=N branch; it is not a rank-revealing solver demonstration. Preserve original A/B for an independent residual check. Neither the fit nor any underdetermined branch was run for this catalog.

**D4a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected DSYEV driver computes ordinary eigenvalues of a real symmetric dense matrix, optionally eigenvectors. It reads the selected triangle, reduces through DSYTRD and dispatches eigenvalues-only work to DSTERF or the vector path through DORGTR and DSTEQR; optional scaling is undone on the eigenvalues. D4a1 is the real-symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem scope. This is not a generalized, complex, nonsymmetric or subset-eigensolver mapping. The driver exposes workspace-query and convergence status, but no eigenpair residual, orthogonality check or audit of all lower-level kernels was performed.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce`.

**I2b1a1a — source-reviewed**

LAPLACE_SOLVE dispatches five-point successive over-relaxation for a rectangular 2D Laplace/Poisson grid, in lexicographic or red-black ordering. Native interior sweeps leave boundary cells unchanged; boundary values and source must already be populated. The grid weights depend on both spacings and the relaxation formula uses their geometric mean. The nonzero source enters the particular stored-source normalization in the update, so callers must derive its scaling rather than pass an arbitrary physical RHS unchanged. The sketch uses zero source to avoid claiming a generic Poisson normalization. The stopping test is maximum iterate change, not a residual norm. The setup local counter K has declaration initialization and therefore SAVE semantics: repeated wrapper calls retain its previous count. Return NSTEPS is not a fresh per-call convergence flag. The separately named SOR9 routine repeats the five-point formula and is not treated as a nine-point method.

Public entry point `lbfgsb_module::setulb`: [src/lbfgsb.f90:88–286](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/lbfgsb/blob/ce1a9322016d6f31b652393e000a914b63af6fef/src/lbfgsb.f90#L88-L286).

Reverse-communication bound-constrained minimization. Set TASK=START, preserve WA(2*M*N+5*N+11*M*M+8*M), IWA(3*N), CSAVE(60 characters), LSAVE(4), ISAVE(44), DSAVE(29), and all state across calls. When TASK begins FG, compute scalar F and gradient G(N) at returned X; NEW_X permits monitoring/continuation. CONV denotes a termination test, ABNO abnormal termination and ERROR invalid input; inspect the full TASK message and independently check the result. NBD values 0/1/2/3 mean unbounded/lower-only/both/upper-only; X/L/U/G are real arrays of length N, M is correction-history size. FACTR scales a relative objective-reduction tolerance by machine epsilon; PGTOL controls projected-gradient stopping. IPRINT<0 suppresses printing. The last ITERATION_FILE string is optional. No objective callback is passed to SETULB. Import lbfgsb_kinds_module::lbfgsb_wp to match the preprocessed library real kind (REAL64 by default); do not assume another fork has this optional argument or the same task representation.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL setulb(N,M,X,L,U,NBD,F,G,FACTR,PGTOL,WA,IWA,TASK,IPRINT,CSAVE,LSAVE,ISAVE,DSAVE[,ITERATION_FILE])
```

Argument declarations: [src/lbfgsb.f90:92–244](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/lbfgsb/blob/ce1a9322016d6f31b652393e000a914b63af6fef/src/lbfgsb.f90#L92-L244).

**G2h2a3 — source-reviewed**

The current lcmin module exposes typed setup and lcmin_optimize. It copies sparse linear equalities/bounds, installs objective/gradient/Hessian callbacks into global procedure pointers, preprocesses fixed/dependent constraints and dispatches a primal-dual interior-point barrier solver. The inspected barrier driver updates the barrier parameter and calls Newton/KKT, line-search and objective-derivative routines. G2h2a3 records smooth optimization with linear constraints and supplied first/second derivatives, scoped to A*x=b plus simple bounds; generic linear inequalities need a suitable reformulation rather than an invented inequality-row API. Coordinate A arrays and sparse Hessian callbacks are caller-supplied. Globals, unconditional output files and external HSL/ALGENCAN dependencies prevent treating this as a standalone or reentrant routine. The old f90wrapper calls an obsolete external lcmin signature; use the reviewed module API. Several multiplier-copy blocks are commented out, so do not assume every vars dual field is populated. No KKT, feasibility, dependency build or optimization test was run.

**L8c1b1 — source-reviewed**

The selected AS274 pipeline CLEAR -> repeated INCLUD -> TOLSET -> REGCF accumulates weighted raw design rows into an orthogonal reduction and back-substitutes regression coefficients for the first NREQ variables. Intercepts must be supplied as a design column. INCLUD overwrites XROW; REGCF may zero D entries judged below tolerance. TOLSET uses a fixed 5e-10 threshold in this revision. IER checks dimensions but does not certify rank, finite inputs or fit quality. This is parameter estimation from raw rows, not a review of every exhaustive/forward/backward subset-selection path in the R package, inference or residual validation. Use nonnegative finite weights and adequate rank; preserve raw data for independent checks.

External double-precision coefficient extraction from the AS274 orthogonal state. Initialize and update state first; inspect IER after every stage.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL REGCF(NP,NRBAR,D,RBAR,THETAB,TOL,BETA,NREQ,IER)
```

Argument declarations: [src/leaps.f:1061–1072](https://github.com/cran/leaps/blob/64e219d7bfb29c0b5232182707d822c6ef825f45/src/leaps.f#L1061-L1072).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
integer :: ier,i
double precision :: d(2),rbar(1),theta(2),sse,tol(2),work(2),beta(2),row(2)
external :: clear,includ,tolset,regcf
call clear(2,1,d,rbar,theta,sse,ier)
if(ier/=0) error stop "CLEAR"
do i=1,4
  row=[1.0d0,dble(i)]
  call includ(2,1,1.0d0,row,1.0d0+2.0d0*i,d,rbar,theta,sse,ier)
  if(ier/=0) error stop "INCLUD"
enddo
call tolset(2,1,d,rbar,tol,work,ier)
if(ier/=0) error stop "TOLSET"
call regcf(2,1,d,rbar,theta,tol,beta,2,ier)
if(ier/=0) error stop "REGCF"
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This is a full-rank coefficient pipeline fragment, not a checked regression driver. NRBAR needs NP*(NP-1)/2 entries. No subset search, residual or rank-deficient case was run. Link/build the relevant AS274 routine set; package-wide R entry points require their runtime.

[README.md](https://github.com/SpirosZafeiris/Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto-Quadrature/blob/8ff674ed77eff6ed7e0c1b58755a182c4a5e1260/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `177498effaa9724b33e8f4fd3e925e889e610873e25b4ff168f37061e896c919`.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

LGL_nodes_weights constructs a requested-size Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto rule on [-1,1], using endpoint nodes and Jacobi-root iterations for the interior. LGL_quadrature combines a caller-provided vector of values at those nodes with the weights and scales by (b-a)/2. H2a1b2 describes this nonautomatic sampled-data finite-interval quadrature: the caller chooses N and supplies values; there is no integrand callback, adaptive subdivision, requested-accuracy controller or estimated-error return. The values must correspond to the mapped LGL nodes, not arbitrary or uniformly spaced samples. Jacobi-root iterations stop after at most ten steps with no convergence status, and small-N and high-order behavior were not verified. The pinned source also uses triplet-style array constructors such as [size_r:1:-1], requiring compiler support or source adaptation; no portable-build claim is made. General Jacobi/Gauss routines, polynomial exactness claims and author example results remain unverified by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `8ff674ed77eff6ed7e0c1b58755a182c4a5e1260`.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use legendre_gauss_lobatto, only: wp, LGL_nodes_weights, LGL_quadrature
integer, parameter :: n = 6
real(wp) :: rule(n,2), x(n), values(n), a, b, integral
a = -1.0_wp
b = 2.0_wp
rule = LGL_nodes_weights(n)
x = a + 0.5_wp*(b-a)*(rule(:,1)+1.0_wp)
values = exp(x)
integral = LGL_quadrature(n, values, a, b)
```

N is an explicit rule size, not an error tolerance, and there is no accuracy/status result. The integrand must be sampled at the rule nodes in the returned order.

The supplied LHSDRV program initializes shared modules, reads an LHS keyword file, dispatches marginal sampling and pairs ranks through MIX to produce Latin-hypercube or random-sample designs. In the inspected uniform marginal, IRS=0 selects one random point per equal-probability stratum; IRS!=0 removes that stratum offset. The driver reads command-line filename or prompts, writes named sample/report files, and leaves LHS.ERR on its flagged failure path. It is not an isolated subroutine taking a user array: LHS/UNIFRM/MIX consume shared state and Fortran units. Rank-correlation matching and stratification do not certify a requested Pearson correlation, independence or quality for every marginal. Source review covers the supplied program, uniform stratification and pairing dispatch, not every inverse-CDF distribution or a generated design.

**C12 — source-reviewed**

The public COUL90 module procedure is defined in a submodule, despite introductory wrapper prose calling it complex. The inspected KFN=0 path uses real64 X/ETA/order inputs, computes continued fractions with a 20000-iteration cap, recurs across integer-spaced real orders and normalizes regular/irregular Coulomb functions and x derivatives. JWKB is dispatched near the turning region; that helper is not independently audited. Arrays are written beginning at MINL=MAX(INT(XLMIN+ACCUR),0), ending MINL+LRANGE, so size depends on the base order rather than LRANGE alone. Require X>1e-7 (the square root of fixed ACCUR=1e-14), XLMIN>-1 and LRANGE>=0. Check IFAIL; fixed target accuracy and module diagnostic state do not establish a numerical error guarantee or reentrancy. Bessel/wrapper APIs are outside this mapping.

**C12 — source-reviewed**

The public lower-level COULCC interface takes complex argument, Coulomb parameter and starting order, with integer-spaced order output arrays and explicit MODE/KFN/IFAIL controls. Inspected implementation paths select Coulomb versus Bessel families, form gamma-based phase/normalization, choose real/complex continued-fraction routines and begin order recurrence. C12 records Coulomb-wave driver/dispatch scope, not a complete audit of the large Steed algorithm or its special-function helpers. IFAIL must be initialized because its input controls diagnostics; nonzero output indicates failure or incomplete order coverage. Convenience coulcc_wrapper passes an uninitialized IFAIL and terminates on errors; coulg requests MODE=4, which does not fill GC, before returning GC. Use the lower-level interface in the calling sketch. The README itself labels this repackaging untested; no values or complex-domain accuracy were checked here.

**E3a2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected SPLDER routine differences B-spline coefficients recursively to obtain derivative coefficients, then evaluates the lower-degree basis with FPBSPL; the highest derivative has a piecewise-constant branch. This is derivative evaluation of a supplied spline, not numerical differentiation of an arbitrary callback or recovery of derivatives of an unknown sampled function. The caller supplies knots, coefficients and spline degree. The fixed work arrays support the FITPACK degree range through five. The input checks cover derivative order and sorted queries, not complete knot validity or coefficient construction. The nonconstant branch clamps out-of-range queries to endpoints, while the highest-derivative branch differs; keep queries in the documented spline interval. No spline value, derivative or author example was executed.

**E3a3 — source-reviewed**

SPLINT obtains integrals of the normalized B-spline basis from FPINTB and contracts them with the supplied spline coefficients. The helper uses the Gaffney recurrence, reverses sign for reversed integration limits and clips limits to the spline support. E3a3 records quadrature of an already-fitted function, rather than an adaptive integrator for arbitrary functions. The spline is treated as zero outside its base interval according to the public header. The routine has no status or error estimate and assumes valid knots, degree and storage. The helper contains six-element local arrays, consistent with degree at most five; it is not a general arbitrary-degree API. No integral or author example was checked by execution.

**G — documentation-reviewed**

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The external DLF_LBFGS_STEP procedure supplies a limited-memory BFGS search step for smooth unconstrained multivariate optimization using caller positions and first derivatives. DLF_LBFGS_INIT allocates a selected shared instance/history; the step routine forms position/gradient differences and applies the two-loop inverse-Hessian recursion. The first step is normalized to length 0.02 and divides by the gradient norm without a zero-gradient guard. Later updates divide by y-transpose-s and y-transpose-y without safeguarding zero/invalid curvature, and a positive gradient-dot-step triggers direction inversion. This is a direction/update component, not a complete minimizer: the caller must evaluate energy/gradient, test convergence before the first/each call, choose acceptable new points and manage line/step control. Module LBFGS_MODULE stores history but the callable procedures are external, after END MODULE, so do not label the step as a module binding. Review covers step/init/destroy lifecycle and selected-instance state, not all DL-FIND coordinates, transition-state or chemistry workflows.

```fortran
use dlf_parameter_module, only: rk
use dlf_global, only: printl
external :: dlf_lbfgs_init,dlf_lbfgs_step,dlf_lbfgs_destroy
real(rk) :: x(2),g(2),step(2)
printl=0; x=[1._rk,2._rk]; g=2._rk*x
! Initialize the author DL-FIND allocation/runtime support before this fragment.
call dlf_lbfgs_init(2,5)
if(sqrt(sum(g*g))>1.e-8_rk) call dlf_lbfgs_step(x,g,step)

call dlf_lbfgs_destroy()
```

**G — documentation-reviewed**

The Evolution source header and interfaces identify genetic optimization, generations and a user fitness callback, with companion module dependencies. The documentation section files inspected were empty; numerical behavior and build setup remain unverified.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `1fbd3cc8922d16bd6cf408f5f4f345f70fda20c9`.

[src/evolution.f90](https://github.com/ramos/libga/blob/1fbd3cc8922d16bd6cf408f5f4f345f70fda20c9/src/evolution.f90)

**G2i — source-reviewed**

Evolution::Next_Generation sorts fitness values for minimization, transforms them into selection weights, retains elites, permutes selected organisms, crosses pairs and mutates non-elites. Changed organisms alone have fitness recomputed through the externally linked Feval callback. G2i records genetic global-search generation steps, scoped to the inspected real-valued genotype path rather than a complete stopping-controlled optimizer or all complex/integer/string variants. Caller must initialize/evaluate every member and drive the generations. Equal fitness gives FSUM=0 before MOD-based selection and needs caller/source handling. Real mutation multiplies genes by 1+normal, so an exactly zero real gene is unchanged by that mutation; no box-bound enforcement is present. Crossover lengths use the first organism twice in MIN, so use compatible genotype lengths. Public mutation/elite/crossover parameters are module-global. Required NumTypes/Statistics/etc. come from an external f90 utility library. No generations or fitness/selection properties were tested by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `1fbd3cc8922d16bd6cf408f5f4f345f70fda20c9`.

```fortran
use NumTypes, only: dp
use Genetics
use Evolution
type(Generation) :: current,next
integer :: i
call Init_Generation(current,20)
do i=1,20
  call Init_Organism(current%Member(i),[0,2,0,0],.true.)
  call Feval(current%Member(i))
end do
! Guard equal/invalid fitness and ensure a suitable initialized population.
next=Next_Generation(current)
```

Bounds, reproducible seeding, stopping budgets and final-best extraction belong to the caller. Only the real-gene path is selected.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

The real inverse overload copies the input, dispatches DGETRF, queries DGETRI workspace and calls DGETRI to form an explicit inverse. D2a1 records general real nonsymmetric matrix inversion, which is included under GAMS linear-system classes. Input is preserved and an allocated result is returned. Nonsquare or LAPACK failures call MATRIX_ERROR, which prints and STOPs, rather than returning INFO to the caller. Empty matrices are not handled as a separate valid case; use a nonempty square matrix. No condition estimate, residual, near-singularity test or complete backend kernel audit was performed. The containing module unconditionally imports f95_pfapack even though this inverse path uses LAPACK. No inverse or author program was run.

**D2a4 — source-reviewed**

The public GMRES routine solves a general real linear system represented by a matrix-action callback, stored as an N by S block-shaped vector. The native restarted Arnoldi process uses modified Gram-Schmidt, Givens rotations and right preconditioning. S is part of one flattened system, not a collection of independent right-hand sides. D2a4 records use with sparse/operator-defined general systems; no sparse matrix format is required by the callback. Restart length 30, absolute tolerance 1e-15 and iteration cap 100000 are hardcoded. The module preconditioner must be selected before calling, otherwise it terminates through the error handler. There is no returned convergence flag or residual history; estimated residual exits, breakdown divisions and restart behavior need independent validation. Review covers this implementation, not a guarantee of robustness or the whole parabolic solver.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `d071a7646872c1d106aa2dda63a7c2e0c784c2e2`.

**I2a1a — source-reviewed**

RUNGE_KUTTA_STEP advances a spatially discretized one-dimensional linear parabolic problem on the current mesh. It forms stage right-hand sides with source/boundary adjustments, dispatches explicit, diagonally implicit or fully implicit stage solves, and updates the solution with a carried roundoff-correction array. The fully implicit route forms an operator-defined coupled stage system and calls native right-preconditioned GMRES. The selected G2 tableau is two-stage Gauss; the source header mentioning only Crank-Nicolson understates the actual method dispatch. Users supply the complete parameter, boundary and spatial operator interfaces. Mesh state and RK tableau must be initialized, U and ROUNDOFF must match the interior mesh size, and ROUNDOFF initially must be zero. There is no adaptive time-step control or returned convergence status; GMRES estimated-residual and preconditioner limitations propagate.

```fortran
use RUNGE_KUTTA, only: set_runge_kutta,runge_kutta_step
real(RNP),allocatable :: u(:),roundoff(:)

roundoff=0._RNP
call runge_kutta_step(u,roundoff,0.001_RNP,0._RNP)
! Preserve ROUNDOFF between subsequent steps; T is the step starting time.
```

**E1b — source-reviewed**

LAGRANGE_INTERPOLATION evaluates a global degree-at-most-N-1 polynomial through explicit products of cardinal basis factors and a weighted sum. It is not piecewise interpolation, a spline or an adaptive stencil. Require N>=1, finite data and distinct abscissae; no denominator/duplicate-node or conditioning checks protect the O(N**2) product formula. Module-global error control can return early with Y unassigned when an earlier error is pending. This mapping is the scalar interpolation component, not orbital/ephemeris modeling or a numerical stability guarantee for high-degree/equispaced grids.

**E1c — source-reviewed**

TRIGONOMETRIC_INTERPOLATION sums cardinal products sin((x-xk)/2)/sin((xi-xk)/2). For an odd number N of distinct nodes modulo 2*pi, these products lie in an integer-frequency trigonometric polynomial space. The comments advertise arbitrary N, but even N gives N-1 odd half-angle factors and anti-periodic rather than generally 2*pi-periodic basis functions; this review does not certify that path as a conventional periodic interpolant. Duplicate nodes modulo 2*pi cause zero denominators. The sketch selects three radian nodes. Shared controlled-error state can return without assigning Y; there is no local error/status or accuracy estimate.

**D1b4 — source-reviewed**

The public native csrmv helper scales y by beta, then accumulates alpha times CSR row products for normal operation or scatters them for transpose operation. Symmetric storage additionally reflects off-diagonal contributions. D1b4 records this matrix-vector product, scoped to normal general one-based CSR in the sketch. Row pointers are supplied as separate begin/end arrays with exclusive ends; indices and vector extents are not validated. The helper uses y INTENT(INOUT) and reads it even when beta=0, so initialize y. The object crssparse mult wrapper inspected in parallel declares y INTENT(OUT) before passing it to an accumulating routine: that wrapper needs an intent repair and is not the recommended entry shown here. MKL/PARDISO, factorization and iterative-solver paths remain outside this review. No matrix product was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `3d93e03a0e7e7b66cc791c054dc45eb5d0a9d70a`.

**P — source-reviewed**

The public INTERSECT_TRIS generic clips one planar triangle against the three oriented half-planes of another with Sutherland-Hodgman-style clipping, then fan-triangulates the resulting convex polygon and drops tiny triangles by an area-spacing tolerance. It accepts real coordinate arrays (2,3) or TRI_TYPE values and returns up to TRI_BUF_SIZE=22 triangles with an explicit count. GET_LINES adjusts normals for vertex orientation. This is planar triangle intersection, not arbitrary nonconvex polygon clipping, a complete parallel supermesh build or certified exact predicates. Zero-area/near-degenerate inputs and floating-point tolerance effects require independent testing. The selected overloads and clip buffer use saved shared scratch and cannot be assumed thread-safe. Precision is configured through LIBSUPERMESH_PRECISION and the build/MPI setup, so callers must import REAL_KIND rather than assume double precision.

**G2a — source-reviewed**

The public LINEAR_PROGRAM constructor assembles a dense tableau for maximizing C-transpose*X with nonnegative variables and supplied <=, >= or equality blocks; RHS vectors must be nonnegative within epsilon. SOLVE with PRIMALSIMPLEX dispatches auxiliary-function feasibility initialization and tableau pivots with Dantzig selection. It updates status on the PROBLEM object, then allocates primal X/slacks/objective only on an optimal status. The declared solution Y/T fields are not populated by this path. MAXITER bounds the phase-two loop, not a reviewed total phase-one evaluation budget. The inspected scope is the LP constructor/high-level dispatch and tableau iteration, not the advertised QP/KKT features or all phase-one edge cases. No feasibility/duality or numerical accuracy was verified by execution.

**D2b1b — source-reviewed**

CHOLESKY forms a real lower-triangular Cholesky factor by diagonal square roots and column updates, supporting the positive-definite real-symmetric decomposition part of D2b1b. This routine does not solve for a right-hand side. Only the lower triangle of output L is assigned; the upper triangle remains undefined and the optional internal CHECK path nevertheless reads the full array through multiplication. The sketch sets CHECK=false and zeroes the upper triangle after return. Pivots <=1e-15 trigger file output and STOP, which can reject a small but positive-definite scaled problem; dimensions/symmetry are not validated. It reads upper-triangle input entries as lower-factor data and assumes symmetry. No factorization or residual was executed.

**D5 — source-reviewed**

GS normalizes the first column, subtracts projections of each original input column onto previous normalized columns, and normalizes the remainder. D5 records classical Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization, not modified Gram-Schmidt, pivoted QR or least-squares solving. NORMVECMAT divides by the Euclidean norm without zero/rank-deficiency protection. An internal CHECK compares Q*Q-transpose with an identity and prints file diagnostics using an absolute tolerance, but provides no returned rank/error status. The sketch uses independent columns and leaves numerical verification to the caller; no orthogonality or conditioning experiment was run.

```fortran
a=reshape([1.0d0,1.0d0,1.0d0,-1.0d0],[2,2])
```

**D6 — source-reviewed**

The public DSINGULARVALUEDECOMPOSITION type wraps real DGESVD after copying the input DMat into a temporary. INIT allocates thin U(M,MIN(M,N)), Sigma(MIN(M,N)) and V(MIN(M,N),N); despite its name V stores LAPACK V-transpose, as confirmed by the author reconstruction U*Sigma*V. Both query and compute calls use JOBU=JOBVT=S. LAPACK INFO is local and never returned or acted on, so a completed method call is not a convergence certificate. Match type bookkeeping N_ROW/N_COL to allocated M storage and initialize before use. This mapping covers the wrapper and author call pattern, not additional review of LAPACK kernels or validated singular values.

**D4b1 — source-reviewed**

GENEIGENSOLSYMD wraps DSYGVD for real symmetric generalized eigenproblems with positive-definite B. ITYPE selects A*z=lambda*B*z (1), A*B*z=lambda*z (2), or B*A*z=lambda*z (3). The method reads the upper triangles, queries workspace and copies final vectors to THIS%VEC. Although A/B are declared INTENT(IN), their allocatable matrix components are passed to the destructive external LAPACK routine; preserve inputs and resolve that contract before use. Both query/compute INFO values are ignored and not exposed, including non-positive-definite-B failures. Review covers wrapper setup and dispatch, not an assertion that arbitrary B is definite or that all type/ABI configurations compile correctly.

**K — source-reviewed**

nn_lrma_svd forms A=U*VT, applies an entrywise nonnegativity transformation and takes a truncated SVD, returning factors with singular values absorbed into U. METHOD=1 clips at zero; other methods reflect, clip at a positive shift or add a shift derived from the largest negative entry. K records the selected constrained low-rank approximation step. This routine performs one projection/truncation step, not an internally converged optimizer or a least-squares fit against a preserved original target; no narrower global-best approximation claim is inferred. METHOD=1 may regain negative entries after rank truncation, so repeat/control convergence at application level. Both real/integer workspace queries are supported via either length=-1, but zero-size/rank early returns precede query outputs. DGESDD error is not checked before copying factors and a following DDGMM call can overwrite IERR. Flat column-major buffers and actual capacities are caller obligations. No approximation, singular values or convergence test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `dc0c54ea975370bd7f54b259d931ef54bc03a9f8`.

Iterative real least squares with optional Tikhonov damping through mandatory DAMP (set zero for undamped). Aprod1(M,N,X,Y) must accumulate Y += A*X without altering X; Aprod2 must accumulate X += TRANSPOSE(A)*Y without altering Y. These callbacks add to, rather than replace, the output buffers. B(M) is input and X(N) output, not an initial guess. Match LSMR_WP and LSMR_IP from lsmrDataModule. ATOL/BTOL set matrix/RHS error tolerances; CONLIM controls the condition estimate, ITNLIM the budget, LOCALSIZE local reorthogonalization and NOUT<=0 suppresses logging. Inspect ISTOP and estimates NORMA/CONDA/NORMR/NORMAR/NORMX with ITN. The executable code uses 0 for zero solution, 1/2 residual/least-squares tests, 3 conditioning limit, 4/5 machine-precision tests, 6 machine conditioning and 7 iteration limit: some older declaration comments have different codes, so the linked executable termination tests are authoritative.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL lsmr(M,N,APROD1,APROD2,B,DAMP,ATOL,BTOL,CONLIM,ITNLIM,LOCALSIZE,NOUT,X,ISTOP,ITN,NORMA,CONDA,NORMR,NORMAR,NORMX)
```

**D2a3 — source-reviewed**

The public M_blas DTRSV module procedure solves real triangular systems by forward/back substitution, overwriting the RHS vector. UPLO selects the stored triangle, TRANS selects A or A-transpose, DIAG selects explicit or unit diagonal, and INCX supports strided/reverse storage. Invalid flags/dimensions/zero stride call XERBLA. Nonunit diagonals are divided directly without singularity or conditioning checks. This is a real triangular solve, not factorization of a general matrix, an SPD-only solve or an error-bounded solver. Review covers dispatch and substitution/stride loops, not every BLAS routine.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The public Mersenne-Twister real adapters turn a masked 32-bit pseudorandom word stored in INT64 into a REAL(SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,307)) uniform variate. REAL2 scales by 2^-32 for [0,1), while REAL3 adds one half before scaling for (0,1). MT state is explicit and advances on each draw. The core twist/temper recurrence was inspected, but the name RAND64 refers to storage kind, not 64 independent random bits. Initialize state explicitly with an INT32 seed. This is pseudorandom sampling, not a cryptographic generator, a statistical test result or a guarantee of independent streams.

**L6a16 — source-reviewed**

SCRAMBLE allocates integers 1 through N and permutes them by two full sweeps of random swaps, choosing each partner over the entire array using intrinsic RANDOM_NUMBER. The result preserves a permutation structurally, but this is not a Fisher-Yates shuffle and does not generally give every permutation equal probability. L6a16 records the permutations subset, not Poisson/Pareto/Pascal generation. Its RNG is the Fortran intrinsic state, separate from explicit Mersenne-Twister state. Use nonnegative N and validate allocation/large-size behavior independently. The mapping records the implemented permutation generator with an explicit distribution limitation.

**D6 — source-reviewed**

dgersvd1 orthogonalizes a caller-provided column sketch, optionally alternates matrix/transpose products and QR/LQ power steps, forms Q-transpose*A through a callback, computes its small SVD, and lifts left singular vectors by GEMM. D6 records approximate real SVD with kc sketch columns, not automatic rank selection or exact full SVD. The caller generates csk=A*Omega; the routine does not sample Omega internally. Arrays are contiguous rank-one buffers with explicit leading dimensions. Query both workspaces before execution. The checks bound kc by n but the QR path also needs kc<=m; require kc<=MIN(m,n). Several callback/LAPACK statuses can be overwritten by subsequent calls without an immediate return. No randomized approximation, singular values, error or author test was run.

**D1a11 — source-reviewed**

The Fypp-generated public moa_take/moa_drop generics select vector sections by signed counts and return POINTER views, not allocated copies. Take with a positive count selects the prefix and negative count the suffix; take zero yields an empty section. Positive drop selects the remainder after removing a prefix. The inspected nonpositive drop branch uses vec(:(n+sigma-1)), an off-by-one discrepancy: drop zero removes one element and negative drop removes one extra trailing element. The sketch therefore uses only positive drop. Counts with abs(sigma)>SIZE(vec) print a diagnostic and return a disassociated pointer; minimum-integer ABS overflow is unchecked. Actual vectors must be persistent TARGET objects if the returned pointer is retained. This is vector section service (D1a11), not a mathematical gamma function or general array algebra audit.

**D6 — source-reviewed**

The public SVD generic wraps precision-selected LAPACK GESVD for real RMAT values, offering full/economy left/right vectors and returning a decomposition with D,U,V (the wrapper transposes LAPACK's V^T). The source copies A into TEMP(NROW,NCOL) but uses LDA=A%NAROW, so padded row storage can give an invalid leading dimension; TEMP=A%A can also encounter nonmatching backing extents. Require exact unpadded storage or repair that path. Optional INFO is assigned only on failure, not zeroed on success, and an early query failure reaches cleanup before USEMYWORK is initialized. Request both vector sides explicitly to avoid passing unassociated unused pointer components in the legacy interface. This is a source-inspected wrapper, not an audit or new implementation of LAPACK itself. No singular values, reconstruction or memory-safety case was checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `3467ac0b6c62ab914e4a85dfd871e6b28e571b32`.

**D5 — source-reviewed**

The public QR generic wraps LAPACK GEQRF and explicitly constructs real Q/R through stored Householder vectors and BLAS products. FULLQ chooses full or thin Q; no column pivoting is performed in this generic. A is logically input, with copies used for the actual factorization; Matran temporary/pointer lifecycle still applies. The sliced GEMV/GER actual arrays are paired with adjusted leading dimensions, whose compiler temporary/contiguity behavior needs validation; the wrapper does not provide an INFO output or consistently act on LAPACK INFO. R is tagged upper triangular, so unused backing entries should not be interpreted as dense zeros. This source mapping is QR decomposition, not rank revelation or a least-squares solve. Review covers shape branches and Householder reconstruction dispatch, not a new LAPACK kernel audit or an orthogonality guarantee.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `3467ac0b6c62ab914e4a85dfd871e6b28e571b32`.

**L14a1b — source-reviewed**

ME1E alternates Gaussian-mixture M and E steps for one-dimensional observations with a variance shared by all G components. It begins from caller membership weights Z, computes means/variance/proportions, forms log densities, normalizes posterior weights with a log-sum-exp style shift and stops on relative log-likelihood change or iteration budget. VINv<=0 selects no uniform noise component; EQPRO=.FALSE. estimates component proportions. Z, MAXI, TOL and EPS are input/output: normal return writes iterations, achieved change and log likelihood; exceptional EPS sentinels represent insufficient membership or collapsed variance. This is one fixed-component mixture fit, not automated model-number/covariance-model selection, supervised classification or a guarantee of global likelihood maximum. BLAS is required and default LOGICAL/integer/double ABI must match.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `7eb32e4d370b270ef699ba5db81903b2bd3ae697`.

**L5b1n — source-reviewed**

DMVNORM evaluates multivariate Gaussian LOG densities by upper Cholesky factorization of Sigma, triangular solves of centered data and a squared-norm/log-determinant formula. Sigma is overwritten by its factor. The interface name does not imply exponentiated density or CDF output. W(P) is scratch; W(1) receives factorization INFO on failure, but range-rejection sets W(1)=0 and HOOD=FLMAX too, so W(1)=0 alone is insufficient. HOOD is not assigned on successful completion and is not a joint log likelihood: initialize it to a nonsentinel before calling and check the failure sentinel before reading LOGDENS. This source review covers the driver and selected helper, not all linked BLAS/LAPACK kernels or an independent distribution test.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `7eb32e4d370b270ef699ba5db81903b2bd3ae697`.

**L6a14 — source-reviewed**

Polar Box-Muller normal generation rejects radius outside (0,1), returns one deviate and caches the other. MU defaults to zero and SIGMA2 to one; the latter is variance and is square-rooted. Require nonnegative finite variance. Cached state is not cleared by a plain intrinsic RANDOM_SEED call and is shared across calls/threads. Distribution routines do not automatically call random_initialize. No normality, reproducibility or MCMC convergence test was performed.

**L6a7 — source-reviewed**

Gamma generation uses Marsaglia-Tsang acceptance/rejection for shape>=1, multiplying the result by B: B is SCALE, not rate. For shape<1 the public routine samples shape+1 and multiplies by U**(1/A), so the private helper warning about its own shape<1 branch does not describe the selected public path. A and B default to one; require positive finite shape/scale and nonnegative N. No parameter checks, finite-time acceptance bound or distributional test is provided. This is random-variate generation, not a complete MCMC posterior sampler.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The inspected MELG19937-64 variant supplies masks/lags to an explicit-state XOR/shift recurrence with a lung word and four index-selector phases. Scalar initialize expands a seed into 311 INT64 words and lung state. Inherited genrand64_real2 takes the upper 53 output bits and scales by 2^-53 for an intended [0,1) grid. L6a21 records this variant and conversion, not a proof of maximal equidistribution or every parameter set. Initialize before use: public index/selector/lung and allocated state must remain consistent. Seed expansion uses signed multiplication/addition assuming modular wrapping. Other interval variants, array seeds, jump polynomials and statistical/reference tests are outside this review; no sequence was executed.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `a4183e93dab04416471b54f384447f93960439e4eeeeb1b642c6b27465f2fb36`.

**D8 — source-reviewed**

DLA_GELYAP reduces a real coefficient matrix to Schur form when needed, transforms a symmetric right-hand side, dispatches a triangular Lyapunov solver and transforms the solution back. DLA_GESYLV performs the two-matrix Schur/transformation analogue for op(A)*X +/- X*op(B)=SCALE*Y. D8 is the GAMS matrix-equation leaf, covering these standard Lyapunov/Sylvester drivers, not generalized/Stein/refinement variants. FACT selectors distinguish general, Hessenberg and already-factored matrices; Schur factors overwrite A/B. Workspace query uses LDWORK=-1 and returns the required integer length in LDWORK itself, not WORK(1). Initialize INFO before calling because it is read on entry. Preserve and interpret SCALE and inspect INFO before treating X as a solution; internal failure can return before the back transformation. Library-global solver/blocksize options are consulted; lower-level kernels and all solver modes are not fully audited. No matrix equation or residual was run.

**P — source-reviewed**

BOWYER_WATSON2 implements an incremental planar triangulation path: initialize a first triangle plus dummy exterior triangles, locate conflicts, recursively remove cavity triangles, insert new triangles and remove exterior cells. Conflict tests use orientation and circumcircle predicates evaluated in a requested quad-precision kind after converting default-real input coordinates. This is broad computational geometry P because the GAMS taxonomy provides no finer general Delaunay leaf; it is not constrained Delaunay, refinement, 3D meshing or an elliptic-solver-specific domain triangulation claim. The README labels the project as development-stage. INITIALISE_MESH loops until the first three points are positively oriented, but its permutation calls are commented and the loop does not change them: clockwise or collinear initial triples can hang. Require at least three distinct points, a positive first-triangle orientation, initialized mesh counters and sufficient precision-kind support. Fixed absolute predicate tolerance is not exact arithmetic or a scale-invariant degeneracy guarantee.

**L8c — source-reviewed**

SPARSE_FOUR implements a dense Gaussian sparse-group-lasso path using block updates, separate group/L1 penalties, strong-rule screening and subsequent KKT rechecks. Groups are contiguous intervals described by BS/IX/IY; GAM supplies positive group curvature/step controls and LB/UB bound group coefficients. ALSPARSE splits lambda into L1 and group parts. Unlike a compressed scalar-coefficient path, BETA is dimensioned NVARS by NLAM but only active-group blocks are assigned, so inactive entries must not be interpreted as defined zeros. The native interface also declares JERR INTENT(OUT) and assigns it only on error paths, leaving the success status undefined; initializing a caller variable does not repair that contract. This needs a source fix before trustworthy success-status handling. NALAM/NBETA/ACTIVEGROUP delimit populated path blocks, and nonzero iteration/active-size errors can leave partial results. Review covers the concrete Gaussian update/screening implementation, not logistic/mixed-frequency preprocessing, inference or an assertion that the current native entry is production-ready.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

The public LINSOL generic dispatches to vector/matrix right-hand-side implementations. The inspected vector path checks squareness, calls an LU factorizer with partial row pivoting, permutes B and applies forward/back substitution in default REAL. The LU implementation swaps already computed L rows and updates a dense Schur complement. The singular check is exact-zero only, not conditioning/rank estimation. Error paths print and return without an allocated solution; assigning that function result is not a robust status protocol. This source review covers the vector solve and inspected LU/triangular helpers, not inverse/SOR or every module operation. No residual or numerical stability was checked by execution.

**D2a3 — source-reviewed**

The public functions prim::diag_sub, fwd_sub and bck_sub solve real diagonal, lower-triangular and upper-triangular linear systems. DIAG_SUB divides B by the extracted diagonal. Forward/backward substitution visit the solution components in dependency order and use dot products of the already computed segment, including zero-length segments at the first/last step. The checked contract uses N>=1, square A(N,N), a matching B(N), finite data, correct structure and nonzero diagonal entries. These low-level routines check squareness but do not verify triangularity or singular pivots; wrong structure is silently ignored in unused matrix regions, and division by zero is possible. Nonsquare input prints an error and leaves the function result undefined rather than returning a status. There is no condition estimate or error certificate. The APIs use default REAL, which is 32-bit in the recorded build; these are not double-precision generic interfaces. The complete main constructs known solutions for N=1..12, each of the three structures, and scales 1e-8, 1 and 1e8. Matrices have positive diagonals and small off-diagonal entries. All 108 function/system comparisons passed bounds checks and floating-point traps; maximum relative solution error was 1.726479e-7 and maximum scaled residual was 8.948365e-8, below tolerance 5e-6. The residual denominator is ||A||_infinity*||x||_infinity+||b||_infinity, and input matrices are checked unchanged. Only prim.f90 is compiled and executed for this driver; the existing LU/linear-solve review is separate. The STRANG automatic-dispatch wrapper, invalid/error cases, alternate real kinds, optimized builds, extreme scales and ill-conditioned data were not executed. Existing GPL-version-scope findings remain; no upstream numerical source is bundled.

Public entry point `prim::diag_sub`: [src/prim.f90:206–227](https://github.com/ghbrown/minila/blob/9f20969c68ce5b174d4a21cfc610c5ff276d183c/src/prim.f90#L206-L227).

Direct diagonal solve using componentwise division; caller must supply diagonal structure and nonzero pivots.

Usage:

```fortran
X = diag_sub(A,B)
```

Argument declarations: [src/prim.f90:214–217](https://github.com/ghbrown/minila/blob/9f20969c68ce5b174d4a21cfc610c5ff276d183c/src/prim.f90#L214-L217).

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
! GAMS D2a3: direct diagonal/triangular solvers in module prim.
program triangular
 use prim, only: diag_sub,fwd_sub,bck_sub
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 implicit none
 integer :: n,which,scale_case,i,j,count
 real,allocatable :: a(:,:),original(:,:),b(:),expected(:),got(:)
 real :: scale,solution_error,residual,maximum_error,maximum_residual,denom
 real,parameter :: tolerance=5.e-6
 count=0;maximum_error=0;maximum_residual=0
 do n=1,12
  allocate(a(n,n),original(n,n),b(n),expected(n))
  do i=1,n
   expected(i)=(-1.0)**i*(0.5+real(i)/7)
  end do
  do which=1,3
   do scale_case=1,3
    select case(scale_case)
    case(1);scale=1
    case(2);scale=1.e-8
    case(3);scale=1.e8
    end select
    a=0
    do i=1,n
     a(i,i)=scale*(4+real(i)/3)
     do j=1,n
      if(which==2 .and. j<i) a(i,j)=scale*0.02*real(mod(i+2*j,5)-2)
      if(which==3 .and. j>i) a(i,j)=scale*0.02*real(mod(2*i+j,5)-2)
     end do
    end do
    original=a;b=matmul(a,expected)
    select case(which)
    case(1);got=diag_sub(a,b)
    case(2);got=fwd_sub(a,b)
    case(3);got=bck_sub(a,b)
    end select
    if(size(got)/=n .or. .not.all(ieee_is_finite(got))) error stop 'invalid triangular result'
    if(any(a/=original)) error stop 'input matrix was modified'
    solution_error=maxval(abs(got-expected))/maxval(abs(expected))
    denom=maxval(sum(abs(a),dim=2))*maxval(abs(got))+maxval(abs(b))
    residual=maxval(abs(matmul(a,got)-b))/denom
    maximum_error=max(maximum_error,solution_error);maximum_residual=max(maximum_residual,residual)
    if(solution_error>tolerance .or. residual>tolerance) error stop 'triangular reference mismatch'
    count=count+1
   end do
  end do
  deallocate(a,original,b,expected,got)
 end do
 print '(a,i0)', 'Default REAL storage bits: ',storage_size(1.0)
 print '(a,i0)', 'Checked triangular systems: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum relative solution error: ',maximum_error
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum scaled residual: ',maximum_residual
 print '(a)', 'PASS triangular'
end program
```

**G1b — documentation-reviewed**

The README describes configurable test functions, finite-difference derivatives and optional gnuplot output. Its suggestion that ever-smaller derivative steps improve accuracy is not treated as a floating-point guarantee; convergence and default example behavior were not checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `e48bef3466dcf3e16eafffbdc0dbf8abb7fda44d`.

[README.md](https://github.com/BramvandePut/Minimization/blob/e48bef3466dcf3e16eafffbdc0dbf8abb7fda44d/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `c93fa408ab11b6051715857543b5351f6d86cbd97eebf6445eadaecc4cd3f9f8`.

**G1b1a — source-reviewed**

Steep repeatedly estimates a gradient by central differences of the selected source-defined objective and takes a negative-gradient step. A fixed config gamma is used when nonzero; zero selects a secant-based step update. G1b1a records smooth unconstrained minimization without user-supplied derivatives: the internal finite differences do not make it a derivative-supplied API. The objective is edited in MatFunction or RastriginFunction rather than passed as a callback. Source findings include copying uninitialized gradient into gradientOld on the first iteration, pointer targets repeatedly allocated without release in CalculateGradient, and an unguarded denominator in adaptive gamma. It stops on coordinate change/iteration limit but prints the same convergence message in either case, with no returned optimizer/status. The conjugate module freezes one Hessian and is outside this nonlinear-minimizer claim. No minimization was run.

Public module subroutine consuming ConfigType. Prints the final vector and overwrites Vectors.txt; no solution/status argument. The sketch uses the two-variable default objective and fixed positive gamma, but does not repair the recorded initialization/allocation findings.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL Steep(config)
```

Argument declarations: [SteepestDescent.f90:10–23](https://github.com/BramvandePut/Minimization/blob/e48bef3466dcf3e16eafffbdc0dbf8abb7fda44d/SteepestDescent.f90#L10-L23).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use ConfigHandler, only: ConfigType
use SteepestDescent, only: Steep
type(ConfigType) :: config
config%order=2; config%x1=[0.0d0,0.0d0]
config%mode="default"; config%direction="min"; config%list="off"
config%gamma=0.01d0; config%convergeLimit=1.0d-6; config%iterationmax=100

```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build ConfigHandler, objective modules and GradientCalculator before SteepestDescent. Resolve the first-iteration undefined gradient copy and pointer lifecycle before treating this as a checked driver. Fixed gamma avoids the adaptive-step division but does not certify descent/convergence. Output says convergence even at the limit; verify results independently.

Implementation helper `GradientCalculator::CalculateGradient`: [GradientCalculator.f90:18–53](https://github.com/BramvandePut/Minimization/blob/e48bef3466dcf3e16eafffbdc0dbf8abb7fda44d/GradientCalculator.f90#L18-L53).

Implementation helper `MatFunction::Formula`: [MatFunction.f90:14–21](https://github.com/BramvandePut/Minimization/blob/e48bef3466dcf3e16eafffbdc0dbf8abb7fda44d/MatFunction.f90#L14-L21).

**H1 — source-reviewed**

CalculateGradient perturbs each component by a fixed h=0.0000001 and forms (f(x+h e_i)-f(x-h e_i))/(2h), using a source-defined default or Rastrigin objective. H1 records first numerical derivatives, not automatic differentiation or user-provided gradients. The separate config h does not control this routine; it is used by the Hessian routine instead. Inputs and outputs are POINTER arrays, and the routine allocates a new gradient and scratch x without releasing their previous targets. The default objective accesses two components, so use two-dimensional input for the sketch. Unknown modes leave gradient unassigned. No truncation/roundoff error estimate or step-size study was executed.

Public module central-difference gradient routine. Input must be a REAL(8) pointer array; output gradient is also a pointer allocated by the routine. Use supported mode and correct objective dimension. It is not an assumed-shape allocatable-output API.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL CalculateGradient(config, input, gradient)
```

Argument declarations: [GradientCalculator.f90:9–24](https://github.com/BramvandePut/Minimization/blob/e48bef3466dcf3e16eafffbdc0dbf8abb7fda44d/GradientCalculator.f90#L9-L24).

Argument declarations: [ConfigHandler.f90:12–17](https://github.com/BramvandePut/Minimization/blob/e48bef3466dcf3e16eafffbdc0dbf8abb7fda44d/ConfigHandler.f90#L12-L17).

Argument declarations: [MatFunction.f90:14–18](https://github.com/BramvandePut/Minimization/blob/e48bef3466dcf3e16eafffbdc0dbf8abb7fda44d/MatFunction.f90#L14-L18).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use ConfigHandler, only: ConfigType
use GradientCalculator, only: CalculateGradient
type(ConfigType) :: config
real(8), pointer :: input(:), gradient(:) => null()
config%mode="default"
allocate(input(2)); input=[0.0d0,0.0d0]
call CalculateGradient(config, input, gradient)
deallocate(input,gradient)
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The internal scratch pointer x is not deallocated by the implementation; repeated calls leak storage. An already associated output gradient target can also be lost. No automatic error/optimal-step estimate is returned. The inspected STEEPEST_DESCENT entry uses a user objective and array-valued gradient, normalizes the descent direction, dispatches quadratic line interpolation with golden-section fallback, and tests mean squared gradient and relative cost change. **D — documentation-reviewed**

The README describes exact decomposition of a matrix into families and an approximate product of exponentials, using Misra-Gries edge coloring. Exactness of the split does not mean a finite-step product equals the full matrix exponential; timing and order claims remain untested.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `f8bced83bac281e80751c125b72253274a982a3a`.

[README.md](https://github.com/CaptainSifff/mscbdecomp/blob/f8bced83bac281e80751c125b72253274a982a3a/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `c4ad36b442e438ffede5b7d06baa926e500f0e264077bc2032286e9344e07cb0`.

**D1b6 — source-reviewed**

The public FULLEXP%LMULT binding applies a checkerboard splitting approximation of a Hermitian matrix exponential to a dense complex matrix. Graph conversion and Misra-van-Gries edge coloring partition off-diagonal couplings; the factory distributes diagonal terms and builds stage exponentials. The selected METHOD=2 constructs paired half-weight stages, and LMULT applies reversed/forward factor order through LMULT_T/LMULT for the Strang-style composition. This is an approximate exponential matrix action under matrix multiplication D1b6, not a matrix polynomial, exact dense exponential or arbitrary non-Hermitian routine. MAT2VERTS requires an exactly Hermitian zero-diagonal off-diagonal matrix; the diagonal is passed separately as a real allocatable vector. Method selectors outside the implemented set and invalid graph/data shapes are not certified, and several failures use STOP rather than a status return. Review covers the matrix-action path and factory/stage dispatch; the different vector-action loop is not inferred to have identical composition order.

```fortran
use MvG_mod, only: MvG_decomp

integer :: i
complex(wp) :: offdiag(n,n),mat(n,n)
real(wp),allocatable :: diagonal(:)

offdiag=cmplx(0d0,0d0,wp)

fe=createFullExponentialfromGraphData(gd,diagonal,2)
mat=cmplx(0d0,0d0,wp)
do i=1,n
 mat(i,i)=cmplx(1d0,0d0,wp)
end do
call fe%lmult(mat)
! MAT is a splitting approximation to the exponential, not a checked exact result.
call fe%dealloc()
call dealloc_graphdata(gd)
```

**G2h3 — source-reviewed**

The main program minimizes x(n), the common ball radius, through an external bmalgencan::algencan call. evalc computes the uncovered-area constraint as total polygon area minus covered area, while evalg, evalj and evalhl supply objective gradient, geometric constraint derivatives and sparse Lagrangian-Hessian entries. The objective Hessian is explicitly zero. This establishes a specialized nonlinear constrained optimization implementation (G2h3), not a generic optimizer implemented in this repository. A smoothness-specific leaf is withheld: the geometry includes tolerances, deterministic small center perturbations, topology changes and zero-derivative fallbacks for invalid configurations. Merely exposing derivative callbacks does not establish a global C2 contract; a later review must also resolve the external solver constraint convention before selecting the equality/inequality branch. The Makefile requires external ALGENCAN 4, HSL and BLAS; its single driver and restart/initialization heuristics do not certify a global minimum. No solve, derivative formula or asymptotic bound was verified.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `f97119df01ae48e396f881ad2d2e25085338282b`.

**G1b1a — source-reviewed**

LMDIF1 minimizes a sum of squared nonlinear residuals using values supplied by the caller and a finite-difference Jacobian. This derivative-free-user interface is a specialized least-squares optimizer, not a general arbitrary scalar-objective algorithm. Simplified Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least squares with M residuals, N variables and a forward-difference residual Jacobian. Require M>=N>0, TOL>=0, FVEC(M), IWA(N) and real WA(LWA) with LWA>=M*N+5*N+M. X(N) is input/output. FCN(M,N,X,FVEC,IFLAG) returns residual values for finite-difference calls, and may abort by setting IFLAG<0. INFO=0 signals invalid controls, negative values callback cancellation, 1..4 the documented reduction/step/orthogonality conditions, 5 evaluation exhaustion, 6..7 too-small tolerance; these are not a certificate of a zero residual or global minimum. The simplified wrapper fixes the budget to 200*(N+1), with no public counter output. All real arrays use REAL64 in this pinned module.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL lmdif1(FCN,M,N,X,FVEC,TOL,INFO,IWA,WA,LWA)
```

This independent review records the public interfaces, dispatch and caller contracts, not a new numerical execution check or audit of every dependency/kernel. INFO=1..4 records distinct stopping tests, 0 invalid input, negative callback cancellation, 5 exhaustion and 6..7 restrictive tolerance. Budget is fixed at 100*(N+1) residual calls. Check actual residuals/fit independently; this is not a general scalar-objective gradient interface. REAL64 is fixed by the module.

```fortran
CALL lmder1(FCN,M,N,X,FVEC,FJAC,LDFJAC,TOL,INFO,IPVT,WA,LWA)
```

Simplified Powell hybrid solver for N equations in N unknowns, using a forward-difference Jacobian. FCN(N,X,FVEC,IFLAG) computes FVEC(N); negative IFLAG cancels. Require N>0, TOL>=0, X/FVEC(N), WA(LWA) and LWA>=N*(3*N+13)/2. X is input/output. INFO=1 is the step/relative-error termination test, 0 invalid input, 2 budget exhaustion, 3 too-small tolerance, 4 lack of progress, or negative callback termination. The wrapper fixes the budget at 200*(N+1) and maps an internal stagnation status into INFO=4. Verify residuals independently; step termination alone is not a root certificate. REAL64 inputs/callback types must match the pinned module.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL hybrd1(FCN,N,X,FVEC,TOL,INFO,WA,LWA)
```

**K1b1a2 — source-reviewed**

LMDER1 configures LMDER for unconstrained nonlinear L2 least squares with supplied residual Jacobian, M>=N, relative cost/step tolerances and evaluation budget 100*(N+1). The inspected driver uses pivoted QR and Levenberg-Marquardt parameter/step dispatch. K1b1a2 records smooth unconstrained nonlinear least squares with user first derivatives, not arbitrary-objective optimization, bounds or rank-certified parameter identification. INFO=1..4 describe different normal stopping tests, not a zero-residual guarantee. The repository module callback interface declares IFLAG INTENT(IN) and both residual/Jacobian INTENT(OUT), conflicting with the classic preserve-the-unused-array/abort contract. The sketch uses the external routine and requires a correctly declared callback. No fit or Jacobian was checked and subordinate linear algebra is not audited.

Public entry point `minres::minres_solver`: [src/minres/minres_mod.f90:40–636](https://github.com/willdickson/minres/blob/c7bb4c7a0ddf13729d3556878ccc688a208a052a/src/minres/minres_mod.f90#L40-L636).

Solve a real symmetric (possibly indefinite) shifted system or its least-squares problem. Public module MINRES reexports MINRES_SOLVER from MINRES_MOD. APROD(N,X,Y) must replace Y by A*X (unlike LSMR accumulation callbacks). MSOLVE(N,X,Y) replaces Y by the solution of M*Y=X and is required as an actual procedure even when PRECON=.FALSE.; for PRECON=.TRUE., M must be symmetric positive definite. SHIFT implements A-SHIFT*I; CHECKA enables extra operator/preconditioner checks. B(N) input, X(N) output, REAL64 kind DP from MINRES_DATA_MOD. RTOL/ITNLIM control stopping and NOUT<=0 suppresses logging. ISTOP/ITN and norm/condition estimates must be inspected; termination is not a proof of small true residual or a minimum-length singular-system solution.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL minres_solver(N,APROD,MSOLVE,B,SHIFT,CHECKA,PRECON,X,ITNLIM,NOUT,RTOL,ISTOP,ITN,ANORM,ACOND,RNORM,ARNORM,YNORM)
```

**G1b1a — source-reviewed**

The selected unconstrained SIMPLEX command uses MINUIT reflection, expansion and contraction without user derivatives. Initialize shared state and define positive-step, unbounded parameters (limits both zero), then issue MNEXCM. Its IERFLG reports command outcome; MNSTAT ISTAT instead reports covariance quality and must not be mistaken for convergence. The simplex spread/call-budget stopping rules are not an optimality proof or strict per-call hard cap. Shared COMMON state and preprocessed precision conventions require a compatible build and callback ABI; this is not a reentrant interface or a review of MIGRAD/HESSE/MINOS.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: fcn, futil
integer :: ierr
double precision :: args(2)
call mninit(5,6,7)
call mnparm(1,"x",-1.2d0,0.1d0,0.0d0,0.0d0,ierr)
if (ierr /= 0) error stop "Parameter definition failed"
call mnparm(2,"y",1.0d0,0.1d0,0.0d0,0.0d0,ierr)
if (ierr /= 0) error stop "Parameter definition failed"
args = [1000.0d0,0.1d0]
call mnexcm(fcn,"SIMPLEX",args,2,ierr,futil)
if (ierr /= 0) error stop "MINUIT command failed"
! Retrieve parameter values with MNPOUT; MNSTAT ISTAT is covariance quality.
```
