**C19 — source-reviewed**

The public MLF_GARRAPPA generic maps scalar/rank-1/rank-2/rank-3 inputs to private bindings. The inspected scalar two-parameter binding sets gamma=1 and dispatches SUB_GENMLF_MULTISHOT: alpha=beta=1 returns EXP, tiny z uses reciprocal Gamma(beta), and other cases dispatch inverse-Laplace evaluation with contour-parameter selection and residue contributions. The source review covers scalar entry/dispatch and contour evaluation structure, not every parameter-optimization, Gamma or sorting helper. Alpha must be positive. Invalid parameters print diagnostics and return without reliably defined outputs or a status code. The saved epsilon and RNG initialization are shared side effects. This is not a review of the separate derivative generic or all generalized three-parameter domains.

**L1a1 — source-reviewed**

The external CTRSC routine centers and rescales each observed column while preserving entries exactly equal to MVCODE. It computes mean and standard deviation using sums and sums of squares and divisor COUNT, not COUNT-1; this can suffer cancellation. Zero-variance columns are centered and SDV is set to one. For all-missing columns SDV is one but XBAR is not assigned. No observation-mask tolerance, NaN handling, overflow protection or stable online recurrence is provided. This mapping covers the descriptive-statistics/standardization component, not EM, imputation or the entire mixed-data model.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `c58906e60fca3fb4d9185f9127f25eef89f1a0f5`.

External in-place double-precision column standardization, with exact missing-value sentinel matching. Avoid reading XBAR for an all-missing column.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL ctrsc(X,N,P,XBAR,SDV,MVCODE)
```

Argument declarations: [src/mix.f:2–9](https://github.com/cran/mix/blob/c58906e60fca3fb4d9185f9127f25eef89f1a0f5/src/mix.f#L2-L9).

```fortran
double precision :: x(3,1),average(1),scale(1)
external :: ctrsc
x(:,1)=[1.0d0,2.0d0,3.0d0]
call ctrsc(x,3,1,average,scale,-999.0d0)
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. X is overwritten. Scale uses divisor N for fully observed data and is not the unbiased sample standard deviation. Supply finite observed values and a distinct exact missing sentinel. Do not treat untouched all-missing means as defined results; no standardization check was run.

**G2c3 — source-reviewed**

The external MT1 routine solves a binary single-capacity profit-maximizing knapsack through greedy initialization, integer upper bounds, branching and backtracking. CHMT1 checks selected admissibility conditions when JCK=1: at least two items, positive integer profits/weights/capacity, every weight <= capacity, total weight > capacity and nonincreasing profit/weight ratios. It is not a wrapper that sorts arbitrary inputs or handles the all-items-fit case. All eight arrays need N+1 elements; sentinel slots P(N+1),W(N+1) are overwritten despite a blanket unchanged-input comment. Integer products/sums and default-REAL ratio/bound arithmetic can overflow or lose precision; no large-instance robustness or optimality experiment was run. This mapping is the selected MT1 path, not every MT2/generalized/multiple knapsack algorithm.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `c1cb90365881dbfa699c070d0d9953fad98591ed`.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran

external :: mt1
p=[6,5,4,0]; w=[2,3,4,0]
call mt1(3,p,w,5,z,x,4,1,xx,minwork,psign,wsign,zsign)
if(z<0) error stop "MT1 input condition rejected"
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The first three items are sorted by decreasing profit/weight and meet the nontrivial-capacity conditions. Only X(1:3) is a solution vector; extra slots are workspace/sentinels. No profit/capacity/optimality check or large-integer test was run.

Implementation helper `chmt1`: [mknapsack/_algos.f:151–207](https://github.com/jmyrberg/mknapsack/blob/c1cb90365881dbfa699c070d0d9953fad98591ed/mknapsack/_algos.f#L151-L207).

**G2c2 — source-reviewed**

MTP minimizes the number of equal-capacity bins through a packing heuristic, lower bounds, reduction and ENUMER branch-and-bound, then reconstructs original item assignments. Require positive integer weights <= C sorted nonincreasingly and N>=2; JCK=1 enables the source checker. BACK=-1 requests unrestricted enumeration while nonnegative values bound backtracking and may return a heuristic solution. Z is the achieved bin count, LB a lower bound, XSTAR the item-to-bin assignment; compare bounds before claiming optimality. BACK is overwritten by actual work despite the Python f2py input annotation. This review covers dispatcher, checks and reconstruction, not all fourteen subordinate packing/reduction kernels or a new exactness/timing experiment.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `c1cb90365881dbfa699c070d0d9953fad98591ed`.

**G2h3b1b — source-reviewed**

The double-precision MMA_Sub generic builds moving asymptotes from iterate history, bounds a move interval, splits objective/constraint derivatives into reciprocal approximation coefficients, and dispatches the resulting subproblem to a primal-dual barrier/Newton routine. G2h3b1b records smooth nonlinear inequality-constrained minimization with supplied first derivatives; no equality support is inferred from the class title. This call performs one MMA subproblem step, not a complete outer optimizer: callers update values, gradients, history and stopping checks. Inputs are allocatable rank-two column arrays plus an m-by-n Jacobian. Inner iterations and fixed epsimin have no returned convergence flag. SolverDP passes INTENT(IN) A/B to overwriting DGESV, an intent mismatch needing repair; helper/kernel correctness is not certified. The supplied main sets maxoutit=1 and is not evidence of a converged optimum. No MMA step or KKT residual was run.

**C1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected public BINOMIALCOEF returns individual binomial coefficients as REAL64, using a stored Pascal table through n=20 and BINOMIALCOEFSARRAY Pascal recurrence above that. The array routine reconstructs each row from the previous row with endpoint ones. This is the GAMS integer-valued combinatorial-function scope, although the representation is floating point rather than exact arbitrary-size integers. For n>=0, out-of-range j returns zero. Negative n is not a supported validated input and large coefficients lose exactness or overflow; the routines return no status. Other utility modules and the separate table-generating API are not promoted by this source review.

**J1a2 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed FFTpack type exposes public fft/ifft generics for in-place one-dimensional complex transforms. Each method determines N from the array, destroys/reallocates workspace, initializes factors/twiddle tables through CFFT1I, calls CFFT1F or CFFT1B and destroys workspace again. It is not a cached-plan interface. The low-level forward path reinterprets complex storage through ISO_C_BINDING and dispatches radix passes; the inspected terminal radix-four case scales by 1/(4*l1), consistent with the documented forward-normalized/inverse-unscaled convention. This differs from FFTE/FFTW-wrapper forward-unscaled conventions. J1a2 records complex 1D transforms, not all real, multidimensional or trigonometric variants. Supply a nonempty vector; workspace sizing uses log(N) and does not validate N>0 first. Errors may ERROR STOP instead of returning to the caller. Parent/submodule CFFT1F declarations differ in workspace INTENT attributes; compiler acceptance was not checked. Source review covers the wrapper, setup/dispatch and a normalization path, not all factorization/radix arithmetic, build portability or round-trip accuracy. No transform or author test was executed.

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected legacy DQAG entry checks workspace and dispatches DQAGE, which selects a Gauss-Kronrod rule, estimates integral/error, bisects the largest-error subinterval and maintains error ordering through DQPSRT. Termination compares summed estimated error with max(EPSABS,EPSREL*abs(result)); IER reports tolerance, subdivision, roundoff or integrand difficulties. H2a1a1 covers automatic finite-interval callback quadrature. An error estimate is not a rigorous bound and oscillatory/singular/discontinuous functions need appropriate handling. This is the bundled double-precision legacy entry, not the unfinished high-level quadrature API. Review covers control flow and rule dispatch, not every kernel or machine-constant/error-handler implementation. No integral was evaluated.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The multiobjective DIRECT path keeps vector objective values and nondominated-point sets, evaluates rectangle centers and selects/subdivides rectangles. G2i is used for this global nonconvex search, with the multiobjective/Pareto scope explicit; the taxonomy supplies no separate multiobjective child here. The wrapper can combine MODIRECT and DFMO through separately budgeted phases. Crucially, the pinned CODE/main.f90 sets maxnf_MODIR=0, so the supplied main skips the global phase unless edited; this mapping describes an implemented optional path, not the default execution. Bounds and inequality-value callbacks are documented; no equality interface or complete Pareto-front guarantee is claimed. No phase was executed.

External high-level driver wrapper for MODIR/DFMO. Its two default-integer arguments are separate function-evaluation budgets. It obtains problem dimensions, bounds, objectives and inequalities from linked routines, manages shared solver state, and writes nondominated solutions to out_nondom.txt rather than returning a solution array.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL wrapper(maxnf_MODIR, maxnf_DFMO)
```


**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

The public MONOLIS_SOLVE_R wrapper copies the RHS and initial guess into assembled matrix storage, dispatches preconditioned conjugate gradients for a real sparse symmetric positive-definite system through the configured method selector, then retrieves X and updates halo values. The inspected recurrence uses sparse products, preconditioner applications and communicator-aware inner products, with periodic explicit residual recomputation. The caller must prepare the sparse/block pattern, values, DOF layout, communication tables, preconditioner/control state and compatible vector extents. CG requires an SPD operator and appropriate SPD preconditioner; BiCGSTAB has possible recurrence breakdowns and is not a universal nonsymmetric convergence guarantee. Query the parameter error/convergence records rather than treating return of X as success. This review covers the selected real CPU algorithm path, not all accelerator, variable-block, distributed partition, factorization or complex branches.

[README.md](https://github.com/pjbartlein/mp-interp/blob/5c8efd24551083f6d64b5e882ff2961c0799ef4d/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `51a5a038af526c8a1d28792e72f2f5df6d263019b645c8cd33d84e7f171fe4d7`.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected public ainv_int path constructs a cyclic neighboring-interval mean matrix from interval lengths, explicitly inverts it with LAPACK DGETRF/DGETRI, adjusts the input means, then calls a midpoint-based piecewise-linear daily interpolator and computes discrete interval means. E1a records this adjusted-input piecewise-polynomial interpolation intent. Inputs are interval averages rather than ordinary point values; x_ctrl/x_targ are read for debug output, not used as a general arbitrary-coordinate grid. Require positive interval lengths summing to ntargs and at least three intervals. LAPACK INFO is not checked and no failure status is returned. The interpolator uses cyclic padding with a specific left-end offset; exact preservation of requested discrete means must be checked independently. Outer-series padding, clipping, missing-data and enforce_mean correction workflows remain outside this implementation review. No interpolation or residual check was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `5c8efd24551083f6d64b5e882ff2961c0799ef4d`.

Public module subroutine for one cyclic set of interval means. INTEGER(4) sizes/lengths and REAL(8) arrays are required. Outputs are y_int(ntargs) and its recomputed ym_int(nctrl). Link a compatible double-precision LAPACK library; the routine has no status argument.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL ainv_int(nctrl, ym, ymiss, x_ctrl, nsubint, ntargs, &
              x_targ, y_int, ym_int)
```

Argument declarations: [f90/modules/mp_interp_killworth_subs.f90:174–189](https://github.com/pjbartlein/mp-interp/blob/5c8efd24551083f6d64b5e882ff2961c0799ef4d/f90/modules/mp_interp_killworth_subs.f90#L174-L189).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use mp_interp_killworth_subs, only: ainv_int
integer(4) :: lengths(4), i
real(8) :: means(4), control_x(4), target_x(120), values(120), recovered(4)
lengths = 30
means = [1.0d0, 2.0d0, 3.0d0, 2.0d0]
control_x = [15.0d0, 45.0d0, 75.0d0, 105.0d0]
target_x = [(dble(i), i=1,120)]
call ainv_int(4, means, -999.0d0, control_x, lengths, 120, &
              target_x, values, recovered)
! Inspect recovered-means; no preservation check was executed here.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile pseudo_daily_interp_subs before this module and link LAPACK. Use finite nonmissing means, positive lengths and matching total target count. **A3c — source-reviewed**

The selected variant-1 MPMODULE interface reexports the MP_REAL datatype, mpreal string conversion and arithmetic generics while keeping implementation procedures private. MP_REAL contains fixed-capacity multiword integer storage determined by the compiled MPFUNF settings (2500 standard digits in the pinned variant). User working-precision arguments are WORD COUNTS, not decimal digits; mpdpw converts digits to approximate word count. The selected string constructor records capacity and dispatches decimal conversion, and addition uses the greater operand precision capped at the compiled maximum before calling MPADD. mpinit initializes FFT/random support at the requested word precision. This is adjustable working precision within a configured capacity, not unbounded automatic allocation. Mixed-mode variant 1 and variants 2 are distinct interfaces. Front-end dispatch and type/configuration were inspected; full carry/rounding/conversion kernels and numerical results were not audited by execution.

**C4b — source-reviewed**

The selected exp(MP_REAL) generic reads the operand precision, caps it to MPFUNF capacity and calls MPEXP. The inspected MPEXP path uses argument reduction around log(2), a scaled exponential series and repeated squaring; precomputed log(2) precision and adequately initialized/sized arrays are prerequisites. It diagnoses excessive positive arguments through MPABRT and can return zero for very negative arguments. This records the real exponential path in variant 1, not arbitrary-argument exactness, all transcendental functions, complex branch behavior or independent correct-digit verification.

**A3c — source-reviewed**

The public MP_REAL type and overloaded real addition use multiword mantissas with an active precision set by MPINIT. The real-plus-real specific dispatches MPADD, which aligns exponents, combines signed mantissa words and calls MPNORM. The fixed type capacity is derived from MPIPL=2005 decimal digits; MPINIT(N_MPIPL) selects an active precision no greater than that capacity and prepares constants/state. Use MPMODULE for the user-facing generics rather than private MP_ADDQQ. This selected addition mapping establishes extended real arithmetic support, not interval bounds, correct rounding of all operations or a complete arbitrary-precision API audit. Global precision/error state and legacy REAL*4/REAL*8 storage assumptions affect build compatibility; avoid default-kind promotion flags.

**C4b — source-reviewed**

The public EXP generic selects a TYPE(MP_REAL) adapter which calls MPEXP with precomputed log(2) and active precision. The inspected core reduces by log(2), evaluates a Taylor series at the scaled argument, repeatedly squares and restores the binary exponent. It checks shared error state, argument magnitude and iteration count; documentation warns that the last result word is unreliable. C4b records the extended-precision real exponential subset, not every logarithmic or complex branch. MPINIT is required before use and errors may invoke the configured abort policy. No correctly rounded result or high-precision reference comparison was run.

**D2a4 — source-reviewed**

SOLVE_SYST dispatches initialization, analysis, numerical factorization, solution and cleanup for real sparse general systems through MA48, SuperLU, MUMPS or UMFPACK wrappers. The selected UMFP path passes compressed-column pointers/row indices/values to symbolic and numeric factorization and solves A*x=b, with iterative refinement explicitly disabled. This is an orchestration layer, not an independent direct-solver implementation or proof of stability. MAT_SOLV contains backend storage, dimensions, sparse arrays, RHS and solution; the caller must use backend-compatible index base, kinds and allocation/ownership. CODE/MESS are marked unused, and several failures STOP instead of returning status. Cleanup unconditionally deallocates ELTPTR/ELTVAR even for assembled storage, so that allocation path needs review. The MUMPS branch initializes/finalizes MPI itself and fixes SYM=0. No symmetric-specialized or complex solver claim is inferred from the backends' wider capabilities. Source driver/UMFP dispatch were inspected; external backend kernels and dependent support modules were not audited.

**L1a1c — source-reviewed**

The external BS02R routine sums centered third and fourth powers, then normalizes them with the N-1 sample variance: SKEW=sum(delta**3)/(N*SDEV**3) and CURT=sum(delta**4)/(N*VAR**2)-3. These are the exact implemented sample-shape conventions, not claimed unbiased skewness/kurtosis estimators. Require N>=2 with N available finite values. The input-length check is commented out; for constant data the code leaves SKEW=CURT=0 rather than flagging undefined normalized moments. No hypothesis test, robustness or numerical accuracy was verified. Unlike the BS01R examples with internal routines, this reviewed file supplies a standalone external procedure.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The inspected stateful MT19937 path seeds 624 words, twists and tempers 32-bit outputs carried in INT64 storage, and scales them by 2^-32 in mtprng_rand_real2 for intended [0,1) uniform output. It is not a 64-bit-payload generator despite the rand64 function name. Explicit mtprng_init is essential: default mti=-1 bypasses the outer mti>=624 block that encloses the proposed lazy-seed test, then indexes mt(-1). The default-state path is therefore unsafe. This review covers explicit positive single-seed initialization and real2 dispatch, not array seeding, range conversion, normal sampling or statistical/bitwise validation. No generator was run.

**L — source-reviewed**

NESTRUN initializes state/randomness and dispatches Bayesian nested sampling with user log-likelihood/prior transformation and dumper callbacks. The likelihood overwrites unit-cube coordinates with physical and derived parameters; dumper receives posterior/live-point pointer arrays and estimated log-evidence/error. Selected iteration code partitions live points, uses ellipsoidal proposal machinery and estimated remaining-evidence stopping; a finite iteration cap and estimated evidence tolerance are not guarantees of posterior coverage or integration accuracy. The pinned fork identifies itself as MultiNest v2.17 (2012), so this is not a review of later MultiNest interfaces. Global module state, output-file naming, optional resume behavior and optional MPI initialization/finalization are part of the contract. Review covers public dispatch, callback declarations and selected stopping/proposal paths, not a full statistical algorithm audit. Broad L is retained rather than a deterministic quadrature or optimizer leaf.

**I2b1a1a — source-reviewed**

NDSM_POISSON::solve_poisson_bvp applies multigrid V cycles to finite-difference Poisson problems on Cartesian rectangular grids. This mapping and local check select two dimensions, uniform equal spacing in both directions and homogeneous Neumann conditions. NDSM_ROOT sets FP to double precision and IT=C_INT64_T; do not pass default-width integers where the interface requires IT. Create MG_HANDLE through new_mg_handle with coordinate vectors and valid hierarchy sizes, set smoothing count, coarse tolerance, boundary selectors and the module DEBUG flag. The constructor floors coarser sizes and can reach one point; choose levels so every active dimension retains at least two points, since setup divides by NQ-1 and stencils read adjacent coordinates. Select zero-mean compatible Neumann data; the generic smoother subtracts the arithmetic solution mean to fix its additive constant. SOLVE_POISSON_BVP returns IERR=0 on its chosen maximum/mean iterate-change tolerance, 1 when the outer cycle budget is exhausted, and DU_LAST is that change metric rather than a PDE residual. Coarse relaxation may print nonconvergence without propagating a distinct outer status; independently check residual and gauge. The selected generic 2-D path uses red/black relaxation, restriction/interpolation and coarse correction; optimized 3-D paths and OpenMP behavior were not checked. A complete serial main program adapted from the BSD-licensed author setup was compiled and run on 17x25 and 33x49 grids. Maximum solution errors were 8.78906e-4 and 2.19727e-4 (ratio 0.25), independently calculated interior residuals below 3.4e-12, and solution means below 1.5e-19. These are checks of one manufactured family, not every dimension, boundary configuration or convergence regime.

```fortran

!    this list of conditions and the following disclaimer in the documentation
!    and/or other materials provided with the distribution.

!    contributors may be used to endorse or promote products derived from
!    this software without specific prior written permission.
!

! AND ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, THE
! IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE ARE
! DISCLAIMED. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE COPYRIGHT HOLDER OR CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE
! FOR ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL
! DAMAGES (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR
! SERVICES; LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER
! CAUSED AND ON ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY,
! OR TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE
! OF THIS SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE.
! GAMS I2b1a1a. Manufactured Neumann problem, following the author test setup.
program check_poisson
  use ndsm_root
  use ndsm_poisson
  implicit none
  real(fp) :: errors(2),residuals(2),gauges(2)
  debug=.false.
  call solve_case(17_it,25_it,3_it,errors(1),residuals(1),gauges(1))
  call solve_case(33_it,49_it,4_it,errors(2),residuals(2),gauges(2))
  if(.not.(errors(2)<0.35_fp*errors(1)))error stop 'refinement did not reduce error by expected order'
  print '(a,es12.4)','Fine/coarse error ratio: ',errors(2)/errors(1)
  print '(a)','PASS Poisson: two grids, analytic error, interior residual and zero-mean gauge'
contains
  subroutine solve_case(nx,ny,ng,error,residual,gauge)
    integer(it),intent(in) :: nx,ny,ng
    real(fp),intent(out) :: error,residual,gauge
    type(mg_ptr) :: mesh(2)
    type(mg_handle) :: bvp
    real(fp),allocatable :: u(:,:),exact(:,:),rhs(:,:)
    real(fp) :: h,x,y,lx,ly,du,stencil
    real(fp),parameter :: a=0.75_fp,b=-0.4_fp
    integer(it) :: nshape(2),nsize,ierr
    integer :: i,j
    nshape=[nx,ny]; nsize=nx*ny; h=1.0_fp/real(nx-1,fp)
    lx=1.0_fp; ly=real(ny-1,fp)*h
    allocate(mesh(1)%val(nx),mesh(2)%val(ny),u(nx,ny),exact(nx,ny),rhs(nx,ny))
    mesh(1)%val=[(real(i-1,fp)*h,i=1,int(nx))]
    mesh(2)%val=[(real(j-1,fp)*h,j=1,int(ny))]
    do j=1,int(ny)
      y=mesh(2)%val(j)
      do i=1,int(nx)
        x=mesh(1)%val(i)
        rhs(i,j)=a*(2*x-lx)+b*(2*y-ly)
        exact(i,j)=a*x*x*(x/3-lx/2)+b*y*y*(y/3-ly/2)
      enddo
    enddo
    exact=exact-sum(exact)/real(nsize,fp)
    call new_mg_handle(bvp,2_it,nshape,ng,mesh,.true.,100000_it)
    bvp%ms=5_it; bvp%ex_tol=1e-13_fp; bvp%copt='N'
    u=0.0_fp
    call solve_poisson_bvp(bvp,nsize,1e-12_fp,256_it,u,rhs,du,ierr)
    if(ierr/=IERR_POISSON_SUCCESS)error stop 'Poisson solver did not report convergence'
    error=maxval(abs(u-exact)); gauge=abs(sum(u)/real(nsize,fp)); residual=0.0_fp
    do j=2,int(ny)-1
      do i=2,int(nx)-1
        stencil=(u(i-1,j)+u(i+1,j)+u(i,j-1)+u(i,j+1)-4*u(i,j))/(h*h)
        residual=max(residual,abs(stencil-rhs(i,j)))
      enddo
    enddo
    if(.not.(error<0.5_fp*h*h))error stop 'analytic solution error too large'
    if(.not.(residual<5e-8_fp))error stop 'independent interior residual too large'
    if(.not.(gauge<1e-11_fp))error stop 'Neumann solution gauge not removed'
    print '(a,2i5,a,3es13.5)','Grid ',nx,ny,' error/residual/mean: ',error,residual,gauge
    call delete_mg_handle(bvp)
  end subroutine
end program check_poisson
```

Complete main program compiled and run locally on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), 2026-11-06. FP=binary64; IT=C_INT64_T. All five module sources and the driver used -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow, with OpenMP disabled. Saved source, runner and report are under drivers/ndsm/. Checks require solver success, maximum analytic error<0.5*h**2, independent interior residual<5e-8, absolute solution mean<1e-11 and fine/coarse error ratio<0.35. Both grids passed; the observed ratio was 0.25. The main program retains the author copyright/license notice; the author benchmark is linked as inspected provenance, while this catalog driver provides the recorded checks.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

With NDIM=1 this is univariate piecewise-linear interpolation, a degree-one polynomial spline, not a single global high-degree polynomial fit. Seven independent known-value checks cover an affine function at endpoints, a node, an interior point and below the interval, plus a non-affine nodal table with explicitly calculated interpolation and extrapolation values. Maximum error was 1.655814e-16. NDSM_INTERP::ninterp uses adjacent nodes in each coordinate and successively reduces the 2**NDIM corner values with linear weights. Supply strictly increasing coordinates with at least two nodes and uniform spacing within each axis; different axes may have different spacing. FP is the module double-precision kind and IT=C_INT64_T, so all size/shape arguments must use IT. F contains PRODUCT(NSHAPE) samples flattened in Fortran order, with the first coordinate varying fastest. MG_PTR%VAL stores each coordinate vector and may have nondefault bounds. Set NDSM_ROOT DEBUG explicitly. The bracketing helper selects the first/last interval for endpoint or exterior queries; NINTERP discards its IERR and applies the weights without clipping or returning status. Exterior values therefore extrapolate the end cell rather than reporting failure. Assertions can stop on inconsistent dimensions or indexing; no accuracy estimate is returned. High dimension requires exponentially many corner samples. Nonuniform or decreasing coordinates, repeated nodes, and high-dimensional behavior are outside the checked contract. The complete catalog main program and both original module sources were compiled and run locally with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental) on Windows, with bounds checks and floating-point traps; tolerance was 5e-13. These finite known-value cases do not establish arbitrary-data accuracy or every extrapolation regime.

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
! Catalog-owned numerical checks; upstream numerical sources are downloaded separately.
program check_linear
  use ndsm_root, only: fp, it, mg_ptr, debug
  use ndsm_interp, only: ninterp
  use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
  implicit none
  integer(it) :: ndim, shape(3), nsize, k, j, index, rem, axis
  integer :: trial, checked
  type(mg_ptr) :: mesh(3)
  real(fp), allocatable :: f(:)
  real(fp) :: q(3), x(3), want, got, err, maximum
  real(fp), parameter :: tol=5.e-13_fp
  debug=.false.
  checked=0
  maximum=0
  do ndim=1_it,1_it
    shape=[4_it,5_it,3_it]
    nsize=product(shape(:ndim))
    do axis=1,ndim
      ! Different spacing per axis; nondefault mesh bounds exercise internal remapping.
      allocate(mesh(axis)%val(-2:shape(axis)-3))
      do j=0,shape(axis)-1
        mesh(axis)%val(j-2)=-0.5_fp*axis+0.25_fp*axis*j
      end do
    end do
    allocate(f(nsize))
    do k=1,nsize
      rem=k-1
      x=0
      do axis=1,ndim
        index=mod(rem,shape(axis)); rem=rem/shape(axis)
        x(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(index-2)
      end do
      f(k)=known(ndim,x)
    end do
    ! Tensor product of endpoint, node, interior and exterior coordinates.
    do trial=0,5**int(ndim)-1
      rem=trial
      q=0
      do axis=1,ndim
        j=mod(rem,5_it); rem=rem/5
        select case(j)
        case(0); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(-2)
        case(1); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(shape(axis)-3)
        case(2); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(-1)
        case(3); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(-2)+0.37_fp*axis
        case(4); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(-2)-0.1_fp*axis
        end select
      end do
      want=known(ndim,q)
      got=ninterp(ndim,nsize,shape(:ndim),mesh(:ndim),q(:ndim),f)
      if (.not.ieee_is_finite(got)) error stop 'nonfinite interpolation'
      err=abs(got-want)/max(1._fp,abs(want))
      maximum=max(maximum,err)
      if (err>tol) error stop 'interpolation mismatch'
      checked=checked+1
    end do
    ! A non-affine nodal table distinguishes piecewise-linear evaluation from a global fit.
    f=[0.25_fp,0.0625_fp,0._fp,0.0625_fp]
    do trial=1,2
      if(trial==1) then
        q(1)=-0.375_fp; want=0.15625_fp
      else
        q(1)=-0.6_fp; want=0.325_fp
      end if
      got=ninterp(ndim,nsize,shape(:ndim),mesh(:ndim),q(:ndim),f)
      if (.not.ieee_is_finite(got)) error stop 'nonfinite tabular interpolation'
      err=abs(got-want)
      maximum=max(maximum,err)
      if(err>tol) error stop 'piecewise tabular mismatch'
      checked=checked+1
    end do
    deallocate(f)
    do axis=1,ndim
      deallocate(mesh(axis)%val)
    end do
  end do
  print '(a,i0)', 'Known-value checks: ',checked
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
  print '(a)', 'PASS linear'
contains
  pure function known(n,x) result(y)
    integer(it), intent(in) :: n
    real(fp), intent(in) :: x(3)
    real(fp) :: y
    y=1.25_fp-0.7_fp*x(1)
    if(n>=2) y=y+0.4_fp*x(2)+0.6_fp*x(1)*x(2)
    if(n>=3) y=y-0.3_fp*x(3)+0.2_fp*x(1)*x(3)-0.5_fp*x(2)*x(3)+0.8_fp*x(1)*x(2)*x(3)
  end function
end program
```

**E2a — source-reviewed**

With NDIM=2 or 3 this is bilinear/trilinear interpolation on a Cartesian grid, not scattered-data interpolation. The complete driver evaluates a multi-affine polynomial with cross terms on nonsquare 4x5 and 4x5x3 grids and unequal coordinate spacings. A tensor product of endpoint, interior-node, between-node and lower-exterior positions gives 150 independent known-value checks; maximum normalized error was 6.692324e-16. NDSM_INTERP::ninterp uses adjacent nodes in each coordinate and successively reduces the 2**NDIM corner values with linear weights. Supply strictly increasing coordinates with at least two nodes and uniform spacing within each axis; different axes may have different spacing. FP is the module double-precision kind and IT=C_INT64_T, so all size/shape arguments must use IT. F contains PRODUCT(NSHAPE) samples flattened in Fortran order, with the first coordinate varying fastest. MG_PTR%VAL stores each coordinate vector and may have nondefault bounds. Set NDSM_ROOT DEBUG explicitly. The bracketing helper selects the first/last interval for endpoint or exterior queries; NINTERP discards its IERR and applies the weights without clipping or returning status. Exterior values therefore extrapolate the end cell rather than reporting failure. Assertions can stop on inconsistent dimensions or indexing; no accuracy estimate is returned. High dimension requires exponentially many corner samples. Nonuniform or decreasing coordinates, repeated nodes, and high-dimensional behavior are outside the checked contract. The complete catalog main program and both original module sources were compiled and run locally with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental) on Windows, with bounds checks and floating-point traps; tolerance was 5e-13. These finite known-value cases do not establish arbitrary-data accuracy or every extrapolation regime.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The inspected spline object constructs tensor-product B-spline coefficients on Cartesian-product axes by solving one-dimensional basis systems successively, then evaluates target grids via basis matrices and BLAS products. Cox-de Boor recursion implements the basis, and the author 2D example concatenates x/y axes and flattens f(i,j) in Fortran order. This establishes gridded multivariate interpolation E2a, not scattered-data fitting. The basis order k means degree k-1 (k=4 is cubic). Supply valid strictly increasing axes and compatible sizes/orders. DGESV info is ignored in set_coefs_1d, so singular/invalid interpolation systems are not reported to the caller. Extrapolation is a saved module-wide flag shared across objects, not an object-specific setting; omitted init arguments retain its previous value. Reinitialization requires cleanup, and fin assumes initialized allocations. This review excludes skip_solve-only workflows and does not establish interpolation accuracy, extrapolation safety or derivative APIs. No author test was run.

Public type-bound generic initializer for type(spline). ks(:) gives B-spline orders and ns(:) gives axis sizes; xs concatenates axes with length SUM(ns), and fs flattens the source grid with length PRODUCT(ns), first axis varying fastest. Use real64 arrays, at least two axes for this mapped scope, 1 <= ks <= ns, and valid distinct increasing axis coordinates. Set extrapolation explicitly; keep skip_solve false when evaluating data. Failures may STOP and no status is returned.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL sp%init(ks, ns, xs, fs, extrapolation, skip_solve)
```

Public type binding for a Cartesian-product query grid. ns(:) gives target axis sizes and xs concatenates target axes. Results are stored as the flat allocatable component sp%fs, not returned as an argument; reshape to the target shape in Fortran order. Read/copy sp%fs before fin. Use an initialized, fully solved object and queries inside the source domain; shape mismatches are not a recoverable status interface.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL sp%interpolate(ns, xs)
```

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use NdSpline, only: spline, dp
type(spline) :: sp
real(dp) :: axis(3), values(3,3), result(1,1)
integer :: i,j
axis = [0.0_dp,1.0_dp,2.0_dp]
do j=1,3
  do i=1,3
    values(i,j) = axis(i)+axis(j)
  end do
end do
call sp%init([2,2],[3,3],[axis,axis],reshape(values,[9]), &
             extrapolation=.false.)
call sp%interpolate([1,1],[0.5_dp,1.5_dp])
result = reshape(sp%fs,[1,1])
call sp%fin()
```

Uncompiled 2D calling sketch, using order-two (piecewise-linear) bases. The analytic reference at (0.5,1.5) is two, but this was not checked. Compile NdSpline.F90 with preprocessing and link compatible BLAS/LAPACK; the author build also enables OpenMP. Source and query values are Cartesian-product grids. The shared extrapolation flag and unchecked solve status remain limitations.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

NN_TL computes a Jacobian-vector product for the configured dense network while also returning the nonlinear output; NN_AD computes the transpose-Jacobian action on a supplied output seed. They apply analytic activation derivatives and ordinary/transposed BLAS GEMM through the layer sequence, recomputing nonlinear trajectories for the reverse path. Parameters are fixed module data; these interfaces differentiate inputs, not train weights or differentiate arbitrary Fortran source. Architecture constants in YONOGWDNN fix input/output sizes, width and hidden depth. Allocate/populate INPUT/HIDDEN/OUTPUT and batch-shaped bias arrays before any call; KLON must agree with storage. PARKIND1 selects NNP=DOUB in the inspected build. No argument-shape/status validation or derivative-accuracy certificate is exposed. Review covers the input tangent/adjoint paths and author setup contract, not execution of the supplied Taylor/dot-product tests.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `1c7ee0929555fae85f68de6e404eaa07d3e2b8cb`.

[README.md](https://github.com/ARVE-Research/newspline/blob/1cc98c9966641ea1fc6f111bfc2846e55d1cca2e/README.md)

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected unbounded newspline path constructs interval-wall control points, solves a linear system for mid-control adjustments using integrated Hermite basis formulas, then evaluates cubic Hermite pieces at subinterval sample locations. This supports univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation from interval means (E1a), not ordinary interpolation through point-valued samples. The construction targets continuous interval-mean constraints; exact equality of discrete output arithmetic means was not established. Boundary inputs act as adjacent buffer interval values in the wall/control formulas. Require at least two input intervals, matching positive subdivision counts and output storage of sum(nk). No size/status checks or recoverable solve flag are supplied. matsol substitutes a tiny value for a zero pivot and does not return conditioning information. Optional lower/upper/absolute/percentage adjustment branches are present but outside this unbounded-path review; their bounds and conservation are not certified. No mean-preservation or spline test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `1cc98c9966641ea1fc6f111bfc2846e55d1cca2e`.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed NITSOL path solves a square residual system with inexact Newton steps and residual-norm backtracking. The public driver validates option selections, partitions caller workspace and dispatches to nitdrv. The inspected GMRES path uses Jacobian-vector products, modified Gram-Schmidt and Krylov corrections; nitjv chooses supplied analytic products or directional finite differences and optional right preconditioning. nitbt evaluates trial residuals and reduces the step until its decrease condition holds. F2 is the system-of-equations leaf; the internal linear solves and residual norms do not make this a general nonlinear least-squares or optimization API. BiCGSTAB/TFQMR dispatch is present, but those implementations were not reviewed. Normal termination also permits a small-step criterion without the residual reaching ftol, so independently check the returned residual. Common blocks, saved initialization and the block-data defaults require coordinated builds and do not establish thread safety. No nonlinear solve or convergence test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569`.

Public entry point `nitsol`: [Nitsol/nitsol.f:1–604](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitsol.f#L1-L604).

External double-precision square-system solver. x(n) is the initial guess and returned iterate; f(n,xcur,fcur,rpar,ipar,itrmf) supplies the residual. jacv supplies selected J*v or right-preconditioner actions, or may be a dummy when both are disabled. Initialize the ten-element input array, provide info(6), parameter arrays and method-sized rwork, plus BLAS-compatible dot/norm callbacks. iterm=0 may mean small step rather than small residual; rwork(1:n) holds the final residual on the normal driver path.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL nitsol(n, x, f, jacv, ftol, stptol, input, info, rwork, rpar, ipar, iterm, dinpr, dnorm)
```

Argument declarations: [Nitsol/nitsol.f:4–9](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitsol.f#L4-L9).

Argument declarations: [Nitsol/nitsol.f:42–80](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitsol.f#L42-L80).

Argument declarations: [Nitsol/nitsol.f:92–106](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitsol.f#L92-L106).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: nitsol, residual, jacobian_action
double precision, external :: ddot, dnrm2
integer, parameter :: n=2, kd=2
integer :: options(10), info(6), ipar(1), iterm
double precision :: x(n), work(n*(kd+5)+kd*(kd+3)), rpar(1)
options = 0
options(4) = kd
x = [1.0d0,1.0d0]
rpar = 0.0d0
ipar = 0
call nitsol(n,x,residual,jacobian_action,1.0d-8,1.0d-10, &
            options,info,work,rpar,ipar,iterm,ddot,dnrm2)
! Check iterm and independently inspect work(1:n).
```

**F2 — source-reviewed**

NITSOL validates integer controls, initializes real algorithm parameters and slices caller workspace before dispatching NITDRV. The inspected driver evaluates the residual, chooses GMRES/BiCGSTAB/TFQMR/classical-GMRES, backtracks and updates the nonlinear iterate and forcing term. F2 records a nonlinear-system inexact Newton-Krylov interface, not verification of every Krylov/finite-difference kernel. Analytic Jacobian-vector and right-preconditioner callbacks are optional; finite differences are the default. INPUT(12), RINPT(9), INFO(6) and solver-specific RWORK sizes belong to this fork, not the original shorter interface. ITERM=0 can mean a small step rather than a small residual, so inspect RWORK(1:N) independently. NITDFLTS explicitly fills RINPT; do not assume an all-zero real vector selects all documented defaults. Illegal integer controls can branch to cleanup before IPUNIT is assigned, an uninitialized-variable finding on that error path. No nonlinear solve or failure case was executed.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The public NEURALNET%BACKPROP method differentiates the scalar network loss with respect to packed weights and optional biases by reverse propagation through activation derivatives and BLAS products. This is analytic chain-rule/backpropagation differentiation, not finite differences or a general source-transforming AD tool. WEIGHTS/BIAS are inout buffers: their entry values become model parameters and their returned contents become gradients. DATA uses predictor rows plus one target row and observation columns. The LOSS callback supplies derivative with respect to prediction, despite its name; the supplied MSE returns 2*(prediction-actual), with averaging performed inside BACKPROP. Activation callbacks distinguish forward value from derivative with FW. The method mutates network intermediate state and reports selected dimension failures via IERR. EVALUATE declares IERR INTENT(OUT) but does not set it on success; BACKPROP immediately tests that undefined value and likewise lacks an explicit final success assignment. Repair the success-status contract before relying on returned gradients. Review covers the scalar-output gradient path and interface, not arbitrary tensor AD, every activation at nondifferentiable points or verified gradient accuracy.

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The public OPT_MOD::ADAM module subroutine updates an unconstrained vector using a supplied gradient callback, exponential first/second moments and bias-corrected adaptive steps. The selected class describes smooth multivariate minimization with user-provided first derivatives; the method neither evaluates an objective nor supplies bounds/Hessians. IBUDGET limits gradient calls; an exactly zero gradient causes early return, but no norm-based convergence/error status is returned. Caller must choose valid decay/step/epsilon values and a suitable gradient. The SGD sibling uses geometric step decay; ADAGRAD is not promoted here because its inspected initial zero accumulator is tested for zero before the first accumulation, causing immediate return. Review covers the ADAM recurrence and callable contract, not optimizer convergence or network-training correctness.

**D9b1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected solve routine forms A-transpose A and A-transpose b, adds variables to a passive set according to the positive projected residual, solves passive normal equations through update_s/DSYSV, and moves toward feasible nonnegative coefficients before updating the residual. This supports constrained L2 least squares D9b1, specifically nonnegative coefficients, not general equality/inequality constraints or a rank-revealing QR method. The code overwrites X from zero and returns ||A X-b||. Material discrepancies: implementation sets MODE=1 and leaves it there on normal completion despite comments/README saying zero; -1 reports iteration exhaustion and returns infinite X/residual. The iteration counter advances only in the inner feasibility loop, so MAXITER is not a strict cap on all outer iterations or linear solves. update_s ignores INFO from both DSYSV workspace query and solve, so rank-deficient/singular normal equations have no safe reported fallback. Normal equations can amplify conditioning issues. No KKT, residual, rank-deficient case or execution was checked.

Public module subroutine, also BIND(C,name="solve"). Fortran callers use module nnls. A(m,n), b(m), x(n), tolerance/residual use C_DOUBLE; dimension/mode/MAXITER scalars use C_INT. The binding lacks VALUE, so C scalar arguments are pointers. There are no INTENT declarations; pass variables rather than relying on input-only dummy semantics. A/b are not assigned in the inspected body; x is overwritten. Actual normal MODE is 1, not the documented 0.

Usage:


**G1b2 — source-reviewed**

The external HOOKE function carries out derivative-free coordinate exploration, pattern extrapolation after improvements and geometric step shrinkage after failed exploration. It links a named external F(X,N) rather than taking the objective as a callback dummy. The supplied file includes PROTO__ explicit interfaces, Rosenbrock (or preprocessor-selected Woods) objective and a main program: separate these appropriately to reuse the optimizer with another main/objective. Require 1<=NVARS<=250, adequately sized arrays, 0<RHO<1 and a positive stopping tolerance/budget. The return is an iteration count, not a success flag; the algorithm also writes progress and uses shared FUNEVALS. Step-size termination is not proof of stationarity or a global minimum, especially for general/nonsmooth functions. This mapping records the selected direct-search mechanics without a new convergence/accuracy claim.

**K1b2a — source-reviewed**

factoring initializes W/H and alternates multiplicative updates involving W-transpose*A and A*H-transpose, with additive 1e-10 denominator offsets. K1b2a records its intended nonnegative bilinear least-squares matrix approximation: factor entries have linear nonnegativity constraints, unlike an SVD. Implementation findings limit use: w_update loops over H dimensions rather than W dimensions, causing incomplete/out-of-bounds updates for common reduced ranks; init_start_h declares width SIZE(A,1) but fills SIZE(A,2). The reported Error squares the sum of signed residuals, not the Frobenius residual norm. factoring runs a fixed iteration count and only prints reconstruction, returning a printing-helper integer rather than W/H or an optimizer status. No low-rank fit or convergence was verified.

**L10 — documentation-reviewed**

The README distinguishes extensions of Rouwenhorst and Tauchen discretizations. This is transition/state approximation of a stochastic process, not a parameter-estimation routine for arbitrary Markov models.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `761d3a4806175d3eba60b2e651cfb0c1de62a70c`.

[README.md](https://github.com/gfell/nsmarkov-fortran/blob/761d3a4806175d3eba60b2e651cfb0c1de62a70c/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `a06fa8ef529b4f5848b40e327415b1f487ad06aaa7ce3b54466209c24c28c11a`.

**M1a — source-reviewed**

lcrouwenhorst propagates unconditional standard deviations of a supplied time-varying AR(1), creates a finite symmetric state grid, and recursively constructs Rouwenhorst transition matrices. lctauchen instead forms time-varying grids and Gaussian bin probabilities using ERF. M1a records finite-state discrete stochastic-model construction for simulation, not random path generation or fitted AR parameters. Both assume y(0)=0; rho(1) does not set a stationary initial variance. Output trans(i,j,t) is row-oriented from period t-1 to t, with identical first-period rows. Caller must provide compatible T vectors, N>=2 states, nonzero innovations/variance and valid positive grid scales; no status, input validation or probability/moment check is returned. No chain or approximation-error test was run.

**L6 — documentation-reviewed**

**L6b14 — source-reviewed**

The public MultiNormalGenerator constructor builds 128 Ziggurat strips; get checks shapes/symmetry, factors the covariance in a private Cholesky helper, fills independent scalar normal proposals and applies mean + L*z to each sample row. This supports the multivariate normal generation intent (L6b14). Important implementation qualifications: strip indices use IAND(NINT(U*10000),127), which is not exactly uniform over 128 strips; the tail logs unguarded RANDOM_NUMBER results, which can be zero. Symmetry uses absolute tolerance 1e-6 and Cholesky rejects updated diagonal values below 1e-6, including some small positive-definite covariances. The intrinsic RNG is global rather than owned by each object. This source mapping does not certify exact distribution, randomness quality or empirical covariance; no samples were run.

**K5 — source-reviewed**

The selected Reg1D kernel computes local polynomial regression at one query using bandwidth H relative to RANGO and observation weights W. Kernel 1 is compact Epanechnikov, 2 triangular and 3 Gaussian; IFCV=1 removes observations at exactly the query value. It centers polynomial powers at X0, calls the local weighted regression helper and returns fitted level, first/second polynomial coefficients, standard errors, R-squared and helper status in PRED(1:8). The third polynomial coefficient is not multiplied by 2, so PRED(3) is not automatically the second derivative. At least seven positive-weight local observations are required even for lower degree. The fixed four-column local design and output accesses motivate restricting this sketch to degree 2. Invalid/insufficient fits set all PRED=-1, so failure cannot be detected from PRED(1) alone. This is a selected smoothing kernel, not the complete factor-by-curve/bootstrap R workflow.

**L8c1b1 — source-reviewed**

The bundled public LSQ module implements sequential weighted least-squares reduction using STARTUP, INCLUD and REGCF (AS75/AS274 lineage). With unit weights it estimates ordinary multiple-linear regression coefficients from raw rows, including a caller-supplied leading constant when fit_const is true. STARTUP allocates shared saved state; INCLUD overwrites XROW and deliberately omits dimension checks. REGCF back-substitutes the reduction, calling TOLSET if needed, and uses negative IFAULT values for detected deficient diagonals rather than proving numerical rank. The module is stateful and not a reentrant independent-fit object. Review covers initialization, row inclusion and coefficient recovery; variable-selection/inference routines in the same file are not promoted by this claim.

**L6b — source-reviewed**

SIMTHOM simulates a Thomas/Neyman-Scott clustered spatial point pattern: Poisson parent count, uniform parents in a width-one/height-TY rectangle, Poisson offspring counts, and Box-Muller Gaussian offspring offsets. Offspring coordinates are wrapped periodically into the rectangle. The class records joint spatial sampling rather than independent univariate draws or an unbounded-window model. AMU is overwritten by AMU*TY; use a fresh density value on each call. NPTS counts parents, and NCL(i) counts offspring of parent i. IER=-1 reports parent-capacity overflow; IER=-2 reports an offspring row exceeding NMAX, leaving only partial outputs. Only initialized rows/columns are meaningful. The external RNG INIT/RANDOM and POIS support are required. Review covers the simulation path, not parameter estimation, reproducibility across R builds or goodness of fit.

**J1a2 — source-reviewed**

The selected external nufft1d1f90 driver computes centered complex Fourier modes from nonuniform source locations using Gaussian spreading, an oversampled FFTPACK transform and modewise deconvolution. Type 1 includes a 1/NJ factor, visible in source strengths before spreading. Nonnegative IFLAG uses the positive exponential sign, negative IFLAG the negative sign. The centered output indices are -MS/2:(MS-1)/2. Source documentation restricts locations to [-pi,pi], requests EPS in [1e-33,1e-1], and returns IER=1 outside that tolerance interval; extremely small EPS is a request, not proof of matching double-precision accuracy. Positive dimensions, finite values, integer workspace bounds and allocation success are caller concerns. The selected type-1 driver is not a direct inverse, a type-2/3 audit or a new transform timing/error comparison.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `499cecd77eefd2255e3e52cc67413b4688b12916`.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

CSPLREP constructs piecewise-cubic coefficients by solving a tridiagonal system for second derivatives with user-supplied endpoint curvatures; CSPLEV selects an interval and evaluates its local polynomial. Zero endpoint curvatures give a natural cubic spline. Require at least four matching sorted, well-separated data nodes. Source findings: fewer nodes return uninitialized coefficients, CSPLREP uses ALLOCATED(CSP%X).AND.SIZE(CSP%X) without guaranteed short-circuit evaluation, and the interval lookup can return 0 or N for outside/upper-end queries although coefficients have N-1 columns. Those queries are not safe extrapolation. The mapping covers fitting and scalar value evaluation, not derivative/integral/root helpers or a full dependency audit.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected FDM path forms central first differences with step 1e-6, diagonal second differences with step 1e-3, and mixed Hessian entries from simultaneous positive/negative perturbations after subtracting diagonal contributions. LIBRARY_REAL8::DIFF selects this path when GLOBAL::GRAD_PAR=1 and initializes gradient/Hessian outputs. The objective is not a passed callback: OBJ_FUNC dispatches fixed selectors 1 (x cubed), 2 (sine plus cosine with degree-to-radian conversion), or 3 (von Mises stress with additional GLOBAL dimension setup). A new objective requires adapting the included source consistently across the typed modules. H1 is the differentiation leaf; the review establishes finite-difference implementation structure, not derivative accuracy. The supplied main selects a different hyper-dual path, which is not audited here, and complex/hyper-dual algorithm correctness is not inferred from the README. Unsupported method selection leaves zero outputs and unsupported objective selection leaves ANS unassigned. No error/status or user step-size parameter is exposed. No driver was compiled or run.

**D2b1b — source-reviewed**

The external CG routine forms the initial residual, then applies conjugate-gradient alpha/beta recurrences with dense MATMUL and dot products, updating X until the infinity norm of the recursively updated residual is small. D2b1b records real symmetric positive-definite dense systems, not arbitrary matrices or a sparse storage API. It has no iteration cap, SPD/breakdown checks or status return; an exact initial solution still enters the loop with ERR=1 and can divide 0/0. EPS>=1 can skip all work. Recompute the true residual independently and avoid treating the recurrence as an error certificate. The same source file contains a separate fixed 2-by-2 demonstration MAIN; extract the external CG procedure before linking to another main program. No system was solved for this catalog.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `96dac60273953c545d659e52024322c1a4a7207f`.

**F1a1 — source-reviewed**

The bisec_code program halves a sign-changing interval for its hardcoded real-coefficient cubic x**3-x-2 and prints one selected real root. F1a1 records that polynomial root demonstration, not a general all-roots algorithm or root isolation. The linked external function F supplies the fixed cubic; a and b are assigned in MAIN rather than user inputs. There is no initial-bracket validation for a modified problem, iteration limit, stagnation guard or returned status. Termination uses an absolute function residual of 1e-6 in default REAL, not a bound on root-location error. No program output was executed.

**A3a — source-reviewed**

The inspected REAL64 summation object implements compensated addition: subtract the stored compensation from the incoming addend, form the new sum and recover the lost low part. Public operator(+) and the add binding return a new object; they do not mutate the receiver. kahan_babushka_sum uses a magnitude-dependent correction accumulated alongside a scalar sum. A3a records compensated standard-precision arithmetic, not arbitrary precision or interval arithmetic. Compiler reassociation/unsafe floating-point optimizations can defeat these compensation steps. The separate Klein routine prints that its implementation may be incomplete and is excluded. No rounding-error experiment or compilation was performed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `d639dc5b06a323b8727eff24e405b5b13cd3a65d`.

The same online_variance object uses the Welford delta times updated-delta recurrence for M2. var() divides M2 by count, whereas sample_var() divides by count-1; both require at least two observations and otherwise ERROR STOP. This mapping covers only the univariate streaming dispersion routines. The separately inspected online_covariance module adds the product of two OLD-mean deltas to its cross accumulator instead of an old/new-mean product; that covariance implementation needs correction and is not promoted as a checked covariance algorithm. **E3c — source-reviewed**

Lagrange_polynomials returns all cardinal polynomial values and their derivatives at XP via a descending-order recurrence dividing by X(j)-X(r). E3c records manipulation/evaluation of interpolation basis functions, not a black-box fit or a verified interpolation-error bound. Row 0 holds basis values, positive rows derivatives, and row -1 a polynomial antiderivative difference whose lower limit is selected by the actual MINLOC-minus-two expression; it should not be assumed to integrate from X(0) or from the nearest node. Callers combine rows with their data to form an interpolant or its derivatives. Default REAL is used. Require nonempty finite distinct nodes; no duplicate-node, conditioning or overflow status is returned. This module is separate from the repository Numerical Recipes directory, whose routines are not reviewed here. No basis identities, interpolation or derivatives were executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `fbb90a3d2fa196fa982f1c458f1c2a8c34298e7b`.

```fortran
basis = Lagrange_polynomials(x, xp)
```

```fortran
use Lagrange_interpolation, only: Lagrange_polynomials
```

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The REAL64 root_brentq path evaluates two endpoints, accepts an endpoint zero, then alternates secant/inverse interpolation with bisection safeguards and a combined absolute/relative interval stopping rule. F1b records a derivative-free scalar root, not polynomial-specific roots or optimization. The callback is a subroutine f(x,fx), not a scalar function. Optional res carries status and counts; on a same-sign interval the early return leaves x0 undefined, so inspect res before using it. Sign checks multiply endpoint values and can overflow/underflow; finiteness, positive tolerances and valid iteration limits are not comprehensively checked. No root, failure or author example was run.

**J1a2 — source-reviewed**

numFort::fft is an in-place recursive radix-two complex transform: split odd/even-indexed subsequences, recurse and recombine with exp(-2*pi*i*k/N). It computes an unnormalized forward transform. Correct radix-two use requires a positive power-of-two length; the code does not enforce that precondition, and odd lengths leave unmatched entries. No inverse, normalization parameter, multidimensional transform or general mixed-radix support is claimed. The enclosing module imports QUADPACK, LAPACK95 and minFun, so this routine is not a standalone build merely because its arithmetic uses intrinsics. No transform accuracy or timing was tested.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

The sampled-data trapZZ overload, exposed through generic trapZ, applies the trapezoidal sum using ONE width abs(x(1)-x(2)) for every panel. It is therefore restricted to an equally spaced ascending grid in this mapping, with at least two x values and matching y length. Nonuniform-grid integration is not implemented by this overload. Descending grids do not produce signed reversal because the width is absolute; mismatched lengths and short arrays are unchecked. There is no error estimate or adaptive refinement. The callback-based trapZ and QUADPACK wrappers are outside this selected source review.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The scalar and vector rk4_explicit_step overloads evaluate the classical four Runge-Kutta stages at t, t+h/2, t+h/2 and t+h, then form the 1:2:2:1 weighted update. I1a1a records an explicit one-step ODE initial-value method. The parent module declares public generics and implementations live in a submodule; compile/link both rather than assuming the interface module supplies code. H is declared INOUT but is unchanged in these implementations, and T is input-only. Caller chooses H and advances time; there is no local error estimate, rejection loop, stiffness detection or returned status. Scalar and vector callbacks use rkp=ISO_FORTRAN_ENV real64 and have distinct explicit interfaces. No ODE, convergence-order or stiffness experiment was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `3d6a7d6c41b3be91ef3d75b39036eead77049627`.

**L1a1a — source-reviewed**

MCM returns the arithmetic mean of each column of a double-precision matrix by straightforward sequential summation and division by the number of rows. Calling with one column provides a univariate raw-data location summary; multiple columns are treated independently, not as a joint model. Require N>0, positive column count, matching storage and finite prefiltered data. There is no missing-value, overflow, compensated-summation or recoverable status policy. This records the implemented descriptive statistic, not an inferential estimate with uncertainty or a robustness guarantee.

**L1a1b — source-reviewed**

VARIAN computes sample variance as (SUM(X**2)-SUM(X)**2/N)/(N-1); VOLAT calls it and takes a square root except that variance below a fixed 1e-30 threshold is returned as zero. Both set INFO=-2 for fewer than two observations. The one-pass difference-of-squares formula is vulnerable to cancellation and can produce a negative computed variance for poorly scaled inputs; VOLAT then silently returns zero rather than reporting that loss of accuracy. Require finite data and inspect scale/conditioning independently. These routines are raw-data dispersion summaries, not confidence intervals, robust scale estimators or an accurate two-pass variance implementation.

**L1a1c — source-reviewed**

SKEWN and KURTOS accept a raw sample plus a caller-supplied mean and variance, accumulate third/fourth central powers and apply explicit finite-sample formulas. SKEWN requires N>=3 and variance>=1e-15; KURTOS requires N>=4 and variance>1e-15. The mean/variance must describe the same sample and use a compatible convention; these are not independently estimated inside the routines. SKEWN initializes INFO=0, but KURTOS assigns INFO only on failure and leaves it unchanged on success: initialize it before calling. The header labels the kurtosis unbiased excess kurtosis, but the hand-coded expression is retained as implementation evidence rather than certifying equivalence to the usual bias-corrected estimator. Neither formula, overflow behavior nor sample distribution was numerically validated. These are descriptive shape calculations, not normality tests or confidence intervals.

**L1c1b — source-reviewed**

COVM computes column means, centers N by P observations through EMPCOV and forms the sample covariance; CORM normalizes it to a correlation matrix. Require N>=2, P>=1 and finite complete data. COVM needs DWORK(P*(N+1)); CORM actually needs P*(N+P+2), as its header states, despite a shorter conflicting workspace comment. CORM returns INFO=-5 when a variance is <=1e-30. The underlying COVR scales by 1./FLOAT(N-1), evaluated in default real before assignment, so this factor can have lower precision than the double arrays. COVCOR and CORCOV convert a supplied covariance/correlation matrix and standard deviations; COVCOR rejects diagonals <=1e-30, while CORCOV does not validate a correlation matrix or standard deviations. These are descriptive/representation operations, not hypothesis tests, missing-data estimation or certification of positive definiteness. Although some headers mention a mean vector, COVM has no separate named mean output; its first P workspace entries contain the means.

**L1c1 — source-reviewed**

TENSORK and TENSORKK calculate selected slices of third- and fourth-order empirical central co-moments from multivariate raw data. They compute column means, multiply centered coordinates with a fixed K (and L), average by N and fill a symmetric P by P output slice. These are unstandardized central moments, not dimensionless skewness/excess kurtosis, cumulants or unbiased corrected estimators. Require N>0, P>=1, valid fixed indices in 1..P, X(N,P), DWORK(P) and H(P,P). Invalid K/L returns INFO=-1000; N/P and input finiteness are not generally validated. The parent raw-data multivariate class is retained because its covariance/correlation child does not describe higher moments. Review covers these directly callable slice routines, not all higher-tensor wrappers or their differing workspace comments.

**L5a1n — source-reviewed**

GETNORMALPDF evaluates the standard normal probability density as the stored approximation to 1/SQRT(2*PI) times EXP(-X*X/2). It is a density at a real argument, not a cumulative distribution, inverse quantile, sampling routine or nonstandard-mean/variance normal PDF. Match the DOUBLE PRECISION external function declaration in the caller. There is no status, scaled/log-density alternative or tail-accuracy guarantee; extreme X can underflow or overflow the intermediate square even when the true density is tiny.

**L6a14 — source-reviewed**

GENNOR implements location/scale transformation AV+SD*SNORM() of an Ahrens-Dieter/Forsythe-style normal generator. The inspected SNORM uses stored tables and acceptance/rejection paths supplied by RANF. This is an intended normal-sampling implementation, but the ordinary default-real call chain is defective: SNORM declares RANF as DOUBLE PRECISION while the provided RANF function returns default REAL. A compatible return ABI must be repaired or established explicitly before use. RANF also depends on preprocessing: INTELFOR invokes INIT_RANDOM_SEED on every draw before RANDOM_NUMBER; the other path uses the compiler-specific RAND intrinsic. Seed policy, endpoint behavior and parallel independent streams are not established here. Require positive finite SD and a validated uniform source strictly suitable for the rejection algorithm. The contract sketch is deliberately commented until these issues are resolved; no sample distribution, reproducibility or randomness quality was tested.

**I2b1a1a — source-reviewed**

The public FAS full-multigrid/V-cycle entries solve discretized elliptic problems on an initialized MPI tree/grid. The selected Cartesian constant-Laplacian path installs native centered box operators and Gauss-Seidel or red-black smoothers; the supplied uniform-grid driver creates a rectangular domain and a manufactured Poisson problem. A cycle restricts data/coarse RHS, relaxes the coarse grid, prolongs corrections and smooths upward. One call performs a cycle, not an automatic globally tolerance-driven solve. MAX_RES optionally reduces maximum residual magnitudes across ranks; callers must repeat/check cycles and assess discretization error separately. Fully periodic constant-Laplacian setup removes mean RHS/solution to address compatibility/gauge. The coarse level must reside on one rank in the reviewed cycle implementation; unsupported geometries/smoothers/configurations can ERROR STOP. Review covers selected native dispatch, cycles and constant operator, not every AMR refinement or boundary case.

**I2b1a3 — source-reviewed**

The native variable-Laplacian methods implement a Cartesian divergence-form elliptic operator with a smoothly varying cell-centered coefficient. Neighbor coupling uses harmonic face coefficients 2*a0*a_neighbor/(a0+a_neighbor) divided by squared grid spacings, supporting a nonseparable second-order linear elliptic mapping. VLAPLACIAN_SET_METHODS reserves coefficient storage, configures coefficient ghost boundaries and installs the native box operator/smoother for FAS cycles. Supply finite positive coefficients and valid initialized ghost values; zero/opposite-sign neighboring coefficients can make harmonic denominators singular and ellipticity is not checked. The method explicitly disables the constant-Laplacian mean-subtraction flag, so periodic/nullspace compatibility must not be assumed to be handled identically. Geometry/smoother restrictions and collective cycle prerequisites remain. This review records the selected smooth variable-coefficient implementation, not discontinuous-material accuracy, a general anisotropic tensor operator or automatic convergence.

[README.md](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/odepack/blob/94bbe0d5a9dd007dc9e07788ec9c8316417619c8/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `f56477f023a05337e138efa3fb79f30be3ce86af87a97b46be0b28b2203a07a9`.

**I1a1b — source-reviewed**

The selected M_odepack::DLSODE method flag 10 selects Adams multistep with functional iteration for nonstiff ODEs. The driver checks task/state/tolerances and workspace, constructs method/iteration flags and dispatches DSTODE for predictor/corrector steps, weighted error control and optional chord-system solves. This is the selected explicit RHS ODE path, not a mass-matrix/DAE capability inferred from the broader class. NEQ is an integer assumed-size array in this modernization; RTOL/ATOL are also array dummies. ISTATE=1 starts and ISTATE=2 reports normal return/continuation; negative states need diagnosis before reuse. Module and saved integration state make independent concurrent solves unsafe without appropriate state management. This review covers driver dispatch/interface and inspected core iteration paths, not every Jacobian, coefficient or linear-algebra kernel or a new numerical accuracy check.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `94bbe0d5a9dd007dc9e07788ec9c8316417619c8`.

Public module ODE driver; selected MF=10 path. Supply F(NEQ,T,Y,YDOT) and a compatible JAC dummy procedure even when this method does not call the user Jacobian. Preserve work arrays/state across continuation calls.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DLSODE(F,NEQ,Y,T,TOUT,ITOL,RTOL,ATOL,ITASK,ISTATE,IOPT, &
     RWORK,LRW,IWORK,LIW,JAC,MF)
```

Argument declarations: [src/M_main/dlsode.inc:1351–1366](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/odepack/blob/94bbe0d5a9dd007dc9e07788ec9c8316417619c8/src/M_main/dlsode.inc#L1351-L1366).

Author example (not run): [example/lsode.f90:13–38](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/odepack/blob/94bbe0d5a9dd007dc9e07788ec9c8316417619c8/example/lsode.f90#L13-L38).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use M_odepack, only: DLSODE
integer :: neq(1),istate,iwork(32)
double precision :: y(2),t,tout,rtol(1),atol(1),rwork(128)
external :: rhs,jac_dummy
! Provide matching RHS and JAC procedures; this is a setup fragment.
neq=[2]; y=[1.0d0,1.0d0]; t=0.0d0; tout=1.0d0
rtol=1.0d-6; atol=1.0d-9; rwork=0.0d0; iwork=0; istate=1
call DLSODE(rhs,neq,y,t,tout,1,rtol,atol,1,istate,0, &
     rwork,128,iwork,32,jac_dummy,10)
if (istate /= 2) error stop "DLSODE status requires attention"
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Callback definitions and problem equations are not supplied here; see the pinned author demonstration. MF=10 is the selected Adams multistep with functional iteration for nonstiff ODEs path. Allocate workspace for the actual dimension/method and use the array NEQ/RTOL/ATOL interface, rather than copying legacy scalar calls blindly. No IVP or stiff/nonstiff comparison was run.

**I1a1b — source-reviewed**

The DLSODE MF=10 path integrates explicit first-order nonstiff ODE initial-value systems by variable-step/order Adams multistep methods with functional iteration. The driver initializes workspace/error weights, calls DSTODE for stepping and interpolates to TOUT for ITASK=1. DCFODE constructs the Adams coefficients up to order 12; adaptive order/step control and local error estimates are internal. RTOL/ATOL weight local error rather than bounding global solution error. ISTATE=1 initializes and ISTATE=2 continues a successful solve; preserve work arrays/state for continuation and inspect negative status codes before using output. COMMON-backed solver state is not an independent reentrant solver object. Review covers this nonstiff selection, driver/status dispatch and multistep coefficient/step paths; it does not classify MF=10 as a stiff or DAE method.

**I1a2 — source-reviewed**

The DLSODE MF=22 path solves stiff explicit first-order ODE IVPs using variable-order BDF and a full Jacobian estimated internally by finite differences. The driver partitions matrix workspace and dispatches through DSTODE/DPREPJ/DSOLSY; BDF coefficient generation is distinct from the Adams branch and supports order up to five. This selected entry is not a residual-form DAE solver, even though the broad GAMS I1a2 class also covers mixed algebraic-differential equations. MF=21 is the separate user-Jacobian variant and is not required by this sketch. Local tolerance control, convergence/error status, workspace preservation and shared COMMON-state limitations still apply. Review covers the stiff selection and driver/coefficient/step dispatch rather than every sparse/Krylov/rootfinding ODEPACK variant.

**J — source-reviewed**

The Fortran FBT driver chooses an Ogata mesh spacing from a golden-search peak estimate and a Newton solve, then sums tabulated Bessel-zero quadrature terms for order 0 or 1. J records its Bessel/Hankel-transform service; the available taxonomy has no dedicated Hankel leaf. The source uses f(knots*z/qT) with its explicit z/qT and one-half weights; use its normalization rather than assuming a conventional radial-transform definition. Require 1<=n<=98, qT>0, Q>0, z>0 and nu=0/1. get_ht accesses the nth tabulated zero before lower routines check n; unsupported nu leaves res undefined. Newton has a 20-step limit but no returned convergence status; no quadrature error estimate is supplied. Finite-node accuracy, Bessel approximation kernels and broader C++ variants were not certified. No transform or author example was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `19e1bfb2dcd6fc61c21aeea14b31b56623c30485`.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The continuous sa_cont_type path initializes energies/state, clips uniform neighbor perturbations to one shared scalar bound interval, accepts moves using a Boltzmann probability, cools and returns the best state found. G2i records simulated-annealing global search, scoped to the continuous path with linear-additive cooling and monotonic temperature. It does not establish global optimality, a stationary sampling distribution or the discrete/combinatorial paths. state_curr is a pointer to caller-owned writable target storage and energy is a required associated type-bound callback. Bounds/damping defaults depend on the initial state and can collapse exploration; set them explicitly. max_step counts accepted moves plus a 1 percent random increment for rejected moves, while total_steps counts trials, so max_step is not an evaluation budget. prog_bar uses a MOD divisor rounded from max_step/91, which can be zero for small limits; the sketch disables it. No optimization or acceptance/cooling test was run.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The public OPT_RUNSA routine performs bounded real-vector simulated annealing with a user scalar objective, sparse Gaussian coordinate perturbations clipped to shared scalar bounds, Metropolis acceptance, geometric cooling and optional reheating. It returns the best visited vector, not a convergence or global-optimality status. A sampled objective-difference scale determines initial temperature; constant sampled objectives can make this zero and subsequent temperature formulas unsafe. NPRINT must be positive because MOD(ITERNUM,NPRINT) is unguarded; initialization bounds must lie inside the search bounds. The routine reseeds the intrinsic RNG from SYSTEM_CLOCK on every call, so a caller seed alone does not control reproducibility. The mapping is heuristic global/nonconvex optimization rather than a deterministic smooth constrained leaf. Review covers the annealing entry, proposal helper, callback and seed setup, not all genetic/evolutionary methods in this repo.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

The inspected DGAUSS routine constructs an n-point Gaussian rule from the monic orthogonal-polynomial recurrence coefficients. It builds the symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix implicitly, iterates eigenvalues and first eigenvector components, sorts nodes and scales squared components by dbeta(1), the measure mass. It returns nodes and weights rather than invoking an integrand or returning an integral. H2c is therefore the precise quadrature-service mapping; an internal eigensolver does not make this a general eigensystem API. The caller must supply a valid positive integration measure and consistent recurrence coefficients. Negative beta entries and iteration exhaustion have error returns; eps is an eigensolver convergence parameter, not a requested integration-error bound. Other ORTHPOL recurrence-generation and Gauss-Radau/Lobatto routines are outside this source review. No moment or quadrature test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `07aee9bd398887c0f47ae5406b3be865aa692d40`.
