External double-precision Gaussian-rule constructor. dalpha(n), dbeta(n), dzero(n), dweigh(n), and workspace de(n) are required. dbeta(1) is the total mass; later entries are recurrence coefficients. Supply n >= 1 and positive deps. ierr=0 indicates normal return; -1/-2 flag size/negative beta and a positive value flags iteration exhaustion. Form the weighted sum yourself.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dgauss(n, dalpha, dbeta, deps, dzero, dweigh, ierr, de)
```

Argument declarations: [legacy/dgauss.f:3–9](https://github.com/ivan-pi/orthpol/blob/07aee9bd398887c0f47ae5406b3be865aa692d40/legacy/dgauss.f#L3-L9).

Argument declarations: [legacy/gauss.f:24–44](https://github.com/ivan-pi/orthpol/blob/07aee9bd398887c0f47ae5406b3be865aa692d40/legacy/gauss.f#L24-L44).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dgauss
integer, parameter :: n=4
integer :: i, ierr
double precision :: alpha(n), beta(n), nodes(n), weights(n), work(n), q
alpha = 0.0d0
beta(1) = 2.0d0
do i=2,n
  beta(i) = dble(i-1)**2/(4.0d0*dble(i-1)**2-1.0d0)
end do
call dgauss(n,alpha,beta,epsilon(1.0d0),nodes,weights,ierr,work)
if (ierr /= 0) error stop "Gaussian rule failed"
q = sum(weights*nodes**6)
```

Uncompiled calling sketch using the monic Legendre recurrence on [-1,1]. The analytic integral of x**6 is 2/7, but no moment comparison was run. The measure weight is already represented by the recurrence and quadrature weights: do not multiply it into the sampled integrand again. Rule-generation convergence does not bound integration error for a general function.

**G2e1 — source-reviewed**

OSQP_solve passes one-based CSC P/A arrays and l<=A*x<=u data through a C bridge to OSQP setup/solve, then copies primal/dual values and solver information back. G2e1 is scoped to the positive-definite convex-QP subset, as in the pinned two-variable demo; the README also advertises broader semidefinite problems. This is an interface/dispatch review, not an audit of the external OSQP iteration or factorization. Supply upper-triangular P and matching integer/real build modes. C temporarily decrements and restores pointer/row arrays despite Fortran INTENT(IN); storage must be writable. If setup fails, osqp_status is uninitialized and solution pointers can still be dereferenced; a nonzero solve return invokes process exit. status=0 alone does not establish optimality: inspect info%status_val and residuals. Optional resolve paths are outside this review. No QP or mixed-language ABI test was run.

**K4 — source-reviewed**

The public ACPADE path (SOLVER=0) forms a Beach rational-approximation matrix with N=2*r coefficients, solves it in a least-squares sense and evaluates numerator degree r-1 over a monic degree-r denominator. This is rational/Padé approximation from sampled complex values, not a verified recovery of analytic continuation or guaranteed pole accuracy. The inspected scope uses NPRECISION=64 and MTR=0, dispatching standard ZGELS through double conversion; quad and SVD branches are not numerically audited. SOLVER=1 (Thiele) is explicitly unimplemented and STOPs. Even positive N, matched shapes, enough samples and a nonzero denominator are caller requirements. The low-level entry avoids reading pade.par but writes diagnostics to unit 90; the module also needs a generated gitversion include. Backend positive INFO can produce a log message and still return coefficients without a caller status.

**D1b6 — source-reviewed**

PSMMA_TOEPLITZ computes a distributed dense-by-Toeplitz product Q=alpha*A*H+beta*Q from replicated Toeplitz generators and block-cyclic matrix data. The native core circulates local panels with BLACS, constructs needed Toeplitz blocks and uses dense products or RRQR-compressed block products. Despite an older wrapper comment saying low-rank work is not implemented, the inspected core does call ConstToeplitzlowrank and Compress_RRQR. This can therefore be an approximate product, not an exact-structure FFT convolution or an eigensolver. The sketch restricts N=K, full generators LDB=2*K-1, equal descriptor row/column block sizes, origin submatrices and REDIST=false. These avoid extrapolating from unverified symmetric-short-generator, submatrix-offset or redistribution layouts. No INFO is returned; allocation/backend failures can print and return, and internal compression tolerance is not a user-requested product error bound. Review covers wrapper, panel multiplication and low-rank construction/compression dispatch, not parallel scaling or all descriptor combinations.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `87e84e00fd32300eb9945b429f5d794c30abd236`.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The source initializes a swarm uniformly in a box, updates velocities from inertia, personal best and global best, clips velocities and evaluates only particles currently inside the box. Best-so-far values are updated for minimization; positions themselves are not clamped or reflected. G2i records a stochastic global-search heuristic, not guaranteed global optimization or smoothness-specific local convergence. The compiled program always completes max_iter iterations: VTR only records the first qualifying iteration, not termination. If that never occurs NIR=0, yet reports index gbest_val_store(0), outside the one-based array. NFE counting stops after the target is recorded even though work continues. No swarm, benchmark or repeatability test was run.

**License: MIT**

[LICENSE](https://github.com/MPMC-Lab/PaScaL_TDMA/blob/7d118e3a2253ed1332ae3bdd37801387560ae17b/LICENSE)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `b2fc15567fdfe4fa756fc44d394b30b5c7e7fb6f9eaba18472fc76b01d2a3996`.

**D2 — documentation-reviewed**

The README documents rank-local reduction, reduced-system exchange/solve and reconstruction, with a single-rank Thomas path. It distinguishes the published Fortran implementation from later C++ extensions; performance is hardware/problem dependent and was not measured here.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `7d118e3a2253ed1332ae3bdd37801387560ae17b`.

[README.md](https://github.com/MPMC-Lab/PaScaL_TDMA/blob/7d118e3a2253ed1332ae3bdd37801387560ae17b/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `50206ba4a23cc26c34238323850ceba6fc25736a38991d935b03f709b0beec6f`.

**D2a2a — source-reviewed**

PASCAL_SOLVER solves batches of real tridiagonal systems using CUDA Fortran device arrays, with one system per GPU thread in the single-rank Thomas path. The multi-rank dispatcher reduces each local row segment to two interface rows, redistributes and solves reduced systems using CUDA-aware MPI, then reconstructs each local solution. A/B/C are lower/main/upper diagonals and D is overwritten by solutions; C is destroyed even on the single-rank path, and A is also changed on the distributed path. No pivoting or caller-visible numerical INFO is supplied, so matrices must avoid zero/unstable elimination pivots. Public plan creation and cleanup bracket repeated solves. Distributed calls require compatible system counts/decomposition and at least two local rows, with CUDA-aware MPI rather than a host-staging fallback. The sketch uses only one rank, while the evidence records distributed dispatch without claiming a tested parallel solve. This is a general real tridiagonal mapping, not an SPD-only or cyclic solver claim.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `7d118e3a2253ed1332ae3bdd37801387560ae17b`.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use mpi
use cudafor
use PaScaL_TDMA_cuda, only: ptdma_plan_cuda,pascal_plan_create,pascal_solver,pascal_plan_clean
type(ptdma_plan_cuda) :: plan
integer :: rank,nranks,ierr,istat
real(8),device :: a(0:1,0:3),b(0:1,0:3),c(0:1,0:3),d(0:1,0:3)
real(8) :: solution(0:1,0:3)
call MPI_Init(ierr)
call MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD,rank,ierr)
call MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD,nranks,ierr)
! Launch this sketch with one MPI rank and a visible GPU.
if(nranks/=1) error stop "single-rank sketch"
istat=cudaSetDevice(0)
if(istat/=0) error stop "device selection failed"
a=-1d0; b=4d0; c=-1d0; d=2d0
a(:,0)=0d0; c(:,3)=0d0; d(:,0)=3d0; d(:,3)=3d0
call pascal_plan_create(plan,2,MPI_COMM_WORLD,rank,nranks,32,32)
call pascal_solver(plan,a,b,c,d,2,4)
istat=cudaDeviceSynchronize()
if(istat/=0) error stop "GPU solve failed"
solution=d
call pascal_plan_clean(plan)
call MPI_Finalize(ierr)
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Requires NVIDIA CUDA Fortran, compatible GPU/runtime and MPI modules. A/B/C/D follow the exact zero-based system-first layout. Preserve coefficients/RHS and check a residual independently; the solver has no pivot/status guarantee. Restore destroyed coefficients before reusing a plan. No serial or distributed solve, pivot case or timing was tested.

**D2b1b — source-reviewed**

The cg binding computes a real conjugate-gradient recurrence with distributed row products, global dot-product reductions and gathered search directions for an assumed symmetric positive-definite operator. D2b1b records that ordinary CG system-solve scope; no nonsymmetric or indefinite support is inferred. Matrix input can be a compatible crssparse object or gen_coeff extension. x is a replicated global-length coarray; only owned rows are updated and the full solution is assembled on image 1 at the end. Initial x is required zero, but the source tests SUM(x)==0 rather than every entry. RHS is read from a binary stream file with integer header. Stopping adds image-local Euclidean norms, not the square root of globally summed squares; zero RHS and curvature breakdown are unguarded. getlargeeigenvalue receives MINVAL, and last-image scratch is O(maxit**2). No coarray solve, speed or convergence check was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `36408df93ae5d6515d3bf7d27008aca16780e77e`.

**L6 — documentation-reviewed**

[README.md](https://github.com/DSCF-1224/pcg-fortran/blob/b07ffaa552c2da4d3e2c8b361d5c860478b4f7ad/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `36f34de60c05c99d570156e89ecc5f530060fe04aff58d985d66e172e9ac7f02`.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The inspected oneseq 64-state/32-output XSH-RR branch initializes a fixed state, saves the old state, advances an LCG using multiplier 6364136223846793005 and increment 1442695040888963407, then xor-shifts/narrows/rotates the old state to an INT32 bit word. L6a21 records uniform pseudorandom word generation. Signed negative INT32 results are bit patterns, not failed draws; there is no real scaling or unbiased bounded-integer conversion in this binding. The arithmetic relies on compiler behavior for signed integer overflow and out-of-range narrowing, which Fortran does not portably define as unsigned modular arithmetic. Other PCG widths, stream families, output permutations, seeding and jump-ahead methods are outside this implementation review. The author C-comparison test was inspected but not run; no sequence or statistical quality claim is validated.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

DPCHIM constructs monotone piecewise cubic Hermite derivatives and DPCHFE evaluates that interpolant. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

Reviewed 2026-11-07 at `8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10`.

[src/pchip_module.f90](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/PCHIP/blob/8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10/src/pchip_module.f90)

Public entry point `pchip_module::dpchim`: [src/pchip_module.f90:2216–2365](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/PCHIP/blob/8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10/src/pchip_module.f90#L2216-L2365).

Construct shape-preserving Hermite nodal derivatives D from X and F. Require N>=2, strictly increasing X(N), INCFD>=1 and F/D storage with leading dimension INCFD and N columns; ordinary scalar data use INCFD=1. Only the first row of D is written. IERR=0 is normal, positive values count monotonicity direction switches rather than failure, and negative values report invalid N/stride/abscissae. All real arguments are REAL64. Call DPCHFE next to evaluate the constructed interpolant.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dpchim(N,X,F,D,INCFD,IERR)
```

Argument declarations: [src/pchip_module.f90:2218–2254](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/PCHIP/blob/8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10/src/pchip_module.f90#L2218-L2254).

Argument declarations: [src/pchip_module.f90:10–32](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/PCHIP/blob/8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10/src/pchip_module.f90#L10-L32).

Public entry point `pchip_module::dpchfe`: [src/pchip_module.f90:1446–1635](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/PCHIP/blob/8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10/src/pchip_module.f90#L1446-L1635).

Evaluate a previously defined Hermite interpolant at XE(NE), returning FE(NE). Supply N/X/F/D/INCFD consistently with DPCHIM (or supplied Hermite derivatives), NE>=1, and REAL64 arrays. Initialize SKIP=.FALSE. for validation; it becomes .TRUE. on normal return. Reset it if the data/controls change. IERR>0 counts extrapolated evaluation points; negative values indicate invalid input. Extrapolation uses the nearest endpoint cubic and is not a bound on approximation error.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dpchfe(N,X,F,D,INCFD,SKIP,NE,XE,FE,IERR)
```

Argument declarations: [src/pchip_module.f90:1448–1494](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/PCHIP/blob/8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10/src/pchip_module.f90#L1448-L1494).

Public entry point `pchip_module::dpchia`: [src/pchip_module.f90:1652–1806](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/PCHIP/blob/8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10/src/pchip_module.f90#L1652-L1806).

Return the signed integral of the stored REAL64 cubic Hermite interpolant from A to B, using the same N/X/F/D/INCFD convention as DPCHIM/DPCHFE. Initialize SKIP=.FALSE. unless data have already been validated. IERR=0 is normal, 1/2/3 flag A/B/both endpoints outside the interpolation interval, and negative values signal input/internal errors. Extrapolated integrals may be unreliable. This integrates the fitted piecewise cubic, not an arbitrary function callback.

Usage:

```fortran
VALUE = dpchia(N,X,F,D,INCFD,SKIP,A,B,IERR)
```

Argument declarations: [src/pchip_module.f90:1654–1698](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/PCHIP/blob/8f5350565072622a2344dd0ec75193832b31eb10/src/pchip_module.f90#L1654-L1698).

**L10c — source-reviewed**

The public PDAF_ASSIMILATE_ETKF entry schedules ensemble-transform Kalman analysis within an initialized multivariate state-space forecast workflow. It invokes forecast operations at each call, passes collected state/observation/error callbacks through PUT_STATE_ETKF when the forecast interval ends and redistributes the next ensemble forecast. The reviewed SUBTYPE=1 analysis path forms ensemble-space observation-error-weighted covariance/information, combines distributed contributions with MPI and uses symmetric eigendecomposition to construct weights and an ensemble transform. An ensemble larger than one, consistent MPI/decomposition state, valid error covariance application and matching callback precision are required. Different filter subtypes select other analysis variants not reviewed here. OUTFLAG=0 can mean an ordinary forecast step with no analysis due, not proof that every call assimilated data; nonzero status must be handled. This is multivariate time-series/state-space analysis L10c, not a physical-domain PDE mapping or an independently validated forecast system. Review covers public scheduling/dispatch and selected native ETKF algebra, not the complete model/callback ecosystem.

**I2a1a — source-reviewed**

PDECHEB semidiscretizes mixed one-space-dimensional parabolic PDE/ODE systems by C0 Chebyshev generalized collocation. INICHB initializes element/grid/workspace COMMON state and initial values through CSET/UVINIT. PDECHB builds the implicit ODE residual by element differentiation, flux/boundary assembly through CRES/DRES and optional coupling through SODEFN. Time integration is delegated to DASSL; PDECHB alone does not advance time. User routines SPDEFN, SBNDR, UVINIT and compatible optional coupled-ODE definitions are required. NPTS=NEL*NPOLY+1 and NEQN=NPDE*NPTS+NV; workspace lengths depend on polynomial degree/elements/coupling. ITIME=-1 signals setup failure and IRES communicates residual rejection/termination to DASSL. Shared saved COMMON blocks preclude assuming independent concurrent contexts. Review covers initialization, residual assembly and an author call sequence, not spatial convergence, temporal integration or every supported coordinate/coupling variant.

**G2h1a1 — source-reviewed**

The selected modified BOBYQA entry minimizes a real smooth objective with bound constraints through interpolation-based quadratic trust-region models, without user derivatives. It partitions workspace, adjusts an initial point/radii against bounds and dispatches BOBYQB, which evaluates named external CALFUN and computes constrained model steps through TRSBOX. Unlike the original Powell interface, this variant adds F, INFO and FTARGET; callers must use the pinned signature and matching modified dependency set. N>=2, N+2<=NPT<=(N+1)*(N+2)/2, adequate workspace and positive ordered radii are required; RHOBEG/RHOEND can be overwritten. INFO distinguishes radius/target termination, evaluation cap, invalid inputs and numerical failures. Radius/target success does not establish a global optimum or objective error bound. Review covers public workspace/adjustment dispatch and selected evaluation/trust-step/status paths, not a complete trust-region proof or every PDFO front end.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `76e12cbf798c4ed583c37e547513da4396db928f`.

**G2h3b1a — source-reviewed**

The selected modified COBYLA entry minimizes an objective under nonlinear inequality constraints CON(i)>=0 using simplex interpolation and local linear trust-region approximations, without derivatives. The wrapper partitions real/integer workspace and returns F, INFO, RESMAX and constraint values in addition to overwriting X and the MAXFUN evaluation-count argument. Named external CALCFC must compute objective and every constraint at each trial. Equality constraints are not a separate exact interface; no equality support is inferred from this mapping. The implementation computes violation as max(0,-CON), tracks simplex geometry/model steps and distinguishes target/radius/cap/numerical termination. A small final radius alone does not imply feasible or globally optimal output; inspect RESMAX and original constraints. The signature differs from original Powell/classical COBYLA and must match this source set. Review covers wrapper, callback/violation handling and selected trust-region/status paths, not all PDFO preprocessing or the complete LP kernel.

**D4b2 — source-reviewed**

PDHGEQZ computes generalized eigenvalue pairs of a distributed real nonsymmetric Hessenberg/upper-triangular pencil, optionally overwriting it with generalized real Schur form and accumulating left/right orthogonal Schur factors. The native driver dispatches small/large QZ kernels, with shift/deflation work in the distributed implementation. This entry assumes H already upper Hessenberg and T upper triangular; it is not a complete arbitrary dense-pencil reduction in one call. Eigenvalues are represented by (ALPHAR+i*ALPHAI,BETA); retain that representation for zero/tiny BETA instead of blindly dividing. Schur vectors are not individual generalized eigenvectors. MPI/BLACS context, block-cyclic descriptors and local storage must match on all ranks. Query both real and integer workspace after setup; nonzero INFO can mean invalid input or algorithmic failure and no residual/conditioning guarantee follows from zero alone. Review covers public dispatch, workspace contract and selected QZ/deflation paths, not every tuning variant or backend.

PDGGHRD reduces a distributed real matrix pair with general A and already upper-triangular B to Hessenberg-triangular form using accumulated left/right Givens rotations and blocked sliver updates. The workspace-query branch returns a debugging workspace size before assigning INFO, so the sketch does not interpret INFO from that query as validation. **D4c2b — source-reviewed**

PDHSEQR computes the ordinary eigenvalues of a distributed real upper Hessenberg matrix and optionally its real Schur form/factors. The native multishift QR path invokes aggressive early deflation and bulge-chasing kernels, with alternative/recovery paths for small or unconverged blocks. This is specifically the compact Hessenberg eigenvalue leaf D4c2b; a general dense matrix must first be reduced, and Schur vectors must not be labeled individual eigenvectors. WR/WI contain replicated real/imaginary eigenvalue components. The query requires valid distributed descriptors and returns real/integer workspace sizes; H is overwritten on computation. Nonzero INFO needs interpretation for invalid controls or incomplete convergence, and balancing/reduction transforms must be retained if original-matrix factors are desired. Review covers public driver, workspace/dispatch and selected AED/multishift calls, not every tuning/kernel or numerical accuracy claim.

**D4c1a — source-reviewed**

PDGEBAL balances a distributed general real matrix by optional permutation and diagonal similarity scaling. It isolates rows/columns, communicates norms and applies power-of-two scaling with underflow/overflow guards. JOB=B performs both stages; JOB=P or S selects one, and SCALE combines permutation records outside the active interval with scale factors inside it. This is an associated eigenproblem transformation, not an eigenvalue computation or a promise that balancing improves every problem. A is overwritten and ILO/IHI identify the remaining active block. The caller must retain SCALE/permutation information and apply matching backtransformation conventions when using original-matrix vectors. NaN/invalid inputs can invoke PXERBLA. Review covers the native distributed permutation/scaling path and public contract, not the original LAPACK implementation or arbitrary exceptional floating-point behavior.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

DSKTRF computes a pivoted Parlett-Reid congruence factorization of a real skew-symmetric matrix, P*A*P^T=L*T*L^T or U*T*U^T. D2a1 is used only for this related factorization in the real nonsymmetric general-storage branch; it does not assert a solver for every nonsymmetric matrix. MODE=N fully tridiagonalizes, while MODE=P performs the partial even-order reduction used for Pfaffians. The driver chooses blocked DLASKTRF or unblocked DSKTF2 panels, propagates zero-pivot INFO and adjusts permutations. It overwrites the selected triangle with tridiagonal entries and multipliers. DSKPFA is also annotated as the public Pfaffian consumer of this reduction; it returns a Pfaffian, not a determinant, and reports zero for odd order. No new QR/SVD classification is inferred from this congruence reduction. BLAS/LAPACK-compatible support and the remaining PFAPACK kernels are required; this review inspects dispatch and Pfaffian accumulation, not all panel arithmetic.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dsktrf
double precision :: a(4,4),query(1)
double precision,allocatable :: work(:)
integer :: piv(4),info,lwork
a=0d0; a(2,1)=-1d0; a(3,1)=-2d0; a(4,1)=-3d0
a(3,2)=-4d0; a(4,2)=-5d0; a(4,3)=-6d0
call dsktrf("L","N",4,a,4,piv,query,-1,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "workspace query failed"
lwork=max(1,ceiling(query(1))); allocate(work(lwork))
call dsktrf("L","N",4,a,4,piv,work,lwork,info)
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Only the lower triangle is supplied; the full mathematical matrix is skew-symmetric. Interpret INFO and the documented packed multipliers/pivots before further operations. Preserve the original matrix to check the congruence residual. Match BLAS/LAPACK real/integer ABI. No factorization residual or Pfaffian was tested.

**D2a4 — source-reviewed**

PFLARE supplies approximate-ideal-restriction multigrid and related preconditioners for PETSc sparse-system solves; it is not a complete replacement for the outer PETSc KSP solver. The public Fortran PCRegister_PFLARE entry registers air and pflareinv types. Selecting air on a PETSc KSP PC constructs a Fortran shell, builds the hierarchy through setup_air_pcmg and applies its underlying PETSc PCMG object. The selected usage assumes an initialized compatible real-scalar PETSc/MPI build, an assembled square host AIJ nonsymmetric A, compatible distributed vectors and a separately chosen outer Krylov method. Call registration before selecting the type when using this explicit path, check each PETSc ierr and KSP converged reason, then independently evaluate the unpreconditioned residual. Registration has no ierr dummy. Options choose strength splitting, transfer operators, approximate inverses, smoothers and coarse solves; this review traces registration/setup/application dispatch and does not certify every numerical method, GPU path, convergence rate, complex-scalar build or preconditioner reuse policy.

**D2e — source-reviewed**

CF_SPLITTING::compute_cf_splitting selects fine/coarse point sets for algebraic multigrid and returns PETSc IS objects containing global zero-based row indices. This is a linear-system associated partitioning operation, not a system solve or geometric mesh generator. The selected real host-AIJ usage chooses CF_PMISR_DDC: a strength-graph first pass dispatches PMISR, followed by a fixed number of diagonal-dominance cleanup passes and index-set rebuilding. Other modes include PMIS/aggregation/compatible relaxation with distinct threshold semantics; their full numerical kernels and device state are not certified here. Initialize PETSc/MPI, use a square assembled matrix with compatible row ownership, fresh output IS handles and valid mode/control values. Returned sets must be destroyed before replacing them. The native module routine has optional CR controls but no ierr/status output; internal PETSc errors are not uniformly forwarded, and unknown first-pass modes abort MPI. Review covers mode dispatch, ownership-index conversion and IS lifecycle; it does not establish optimal coarsening, deterministic random choices or solver convergence.

**D9a1 — source-reviewed**

SVDFIT forms a weighted linear least-squares design from the built-in FUNCS1 ENTRY, divides each row and response by SIG(i), factors it through local SVDCMP, zeros singular values below 1e-14 of the maximum, and applies SVBKSB. It is linear in fitted coefficients of a permutationally invariant polynomial basis in exp(-distance), not nonlinear parameter fitting or a generic callback-based fitter. PREPOT must previously initialize saved basis tables, MPI state and COMMON model/training distances as in the application driver; FUNCS1 is an ENTRY in that initialized routine. Require positive finite weights/scales, 1<=MA<=NDATA<=MAXDATA, MA<=MAXTERM and MA<=MAXDATA for local SVD buffers, MP>=NDATA and NP>=MA, matching includes/COMMON layout and sufficient memory for U(MP,NP), V(NP,NP) and large static model arrays. The safest selected dimensions are MP=NDATA, NP=MA, matching the author call and avoiding the oversized NP dummy contract in SVBKSB. Only coefficients A are returned: CHISQ, U/V/W are local despite stale comments suggesting outputs. There is no exposed convergence/rank/error status; SVDCMP has a finite iteration loop but its nonconvergence PAUSE diagnostic is commented out. Recompute weighted residuals and assess rank independently; this is not a certified robust or converged fit.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

newton_raphson calls supplied residual/Jacobian functions, solves J(x)*dx=-F(x) using the companion unpivoted LU path, adds the step and stops on the sum of absolute coordinate changes. fixPoint repeatedly assigns G(x) and uses the same step-change test. F2 records real nonlinear systems/fixed-point iteration, not guaranteed global convergence or a singular-Jacobian-safe Newton solver. Callbacks return allocatable default-REAL vectors/matrices. ITE is both maximum iterations and successful iteration count; ITE<=0 leaves OK unassigned. EPS must be positive and meaningful for default REAL. There is no residual, contractivity, pivot or finite-value validation. The companion LU does not pivot or report breakdown, and the whole module depends on it even when only fixPoint is used. No nonlinear solve or convergence test was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `adec2977efac83c3a5297d01cbeaac4ac50e3d11`.

[README.rst](https://github.com/PolyChord/PolyChordLite/blob/370f6af5d59a4d3af2ed3333acfba152fdb7a4cf/README.rst)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `90851316c7cc9274d55c7e031b77ee436b32de50f475b03b12ee7eb949cc51d0`.

**L — source-reviewed**

RUN_POLYCHORD exposes nested sampling for Bayesian evidence/posterior exploration using user log-likelihood and unit-hypercube-to-prior transformations. The full wrapper copies/initializes settings, initializes randomness, and dispatches NESTEDSAMPLING; constrained slice sampling supplies replacement live points. A custom DUMPER receives live/dead points, logweights and log-evidence/error estimates; the public wrapper does not return those as scalar output dummies. Prior normalization, finite log-likelihoods and derived-output dimensions are caller responsibilities. Stopping combines maximum dead points and a live-evidence precision criterion, which is an estimate rather than a correctness certificate. Output files and MPI/random-state lifecycle are part of the configured workflow. Broad statistics L is retained instead of treating Bayesian sampling as deterministic quadrature or optimization. Review covers interface, selected iteration/stopping and slice dispatch, not multimodal completeness or uncertainty calibration.

**K1a1a2 — source-reviewed**

The PROGRAM contains its fitting helpers; they are not externally callable public library routines. In the independent-coefficient path, the code builds sums of weighted powers of shifted abscissae, factors and inverts the symmetric normal matrix via DSYTRF/DSYTRI, multiplies by the weighted data vector, and accumulates weighted squared residuals. Ordinary polynomial powers support K1a1a2 (unconstrained univariate polynomial least squares). More general exponents are accepted, but this mapping does not certify those domains or shared-coefficient, resampling or intersection branches. Fewer-than-coefficient point sets are skipped with zero-initialized coefficient storage; near-singularity and normal-equation conditioning remain user concerns. No upstream code or author example was compiled or run.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `9c4372d6079eeec5c9f867a233940b8de558ca35`.

[README.md](https://github.com/EVADEVacStab/polyhomocont/blob/9c4372d6079eeec5c9f867a233940b8de558ca35/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `5588ae6af881df6a3b99d19d2c8bab77219c84fe746b6eebd3165cffeaed1e84`.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

SOLVE builds a randomized total-degree homotopy with product(degrees) start paths, tracks in projective coordinates using an RK4 predictor and Newton corrector with adaptive step rejection, and optionally applies a Cauchy end game. The driver classifies finite/infinite and regular/singular endpoints, refines regular solutions and clusters duplicates. STATUS reports setup errors separately from RES%NFAILED, path statuses and end-game status: STATUS_OK alone does not mean all roots were obtained. Numerical residuals, condition estimates, winding/multiplicity counts and real-root tolerances are diagnostic approximations, not certified algebraic counts or proof of completeness. A custom POLY_SYSTEM must supply exact total degrees, evaluations and Jacobians; the default homogeneous evaluator loses accuracy near infinity, so sparse/direct homogeneous evaluation is preferable there. Source review covers construction/driver dispatch, selected tracker and endpoint classification, not every continuation/end-game kernel or a numerical root test.

**D2 — source-reviewed**

polynomial_arnoldi::gmres builds a Krylov basis using twice-applied modified Gram-Schmidt, applies Givens rotations to a Hessenberg least-squares problem and updates X through a triangular solve, restarting when the subspace fills. D2 records this linear-system solver implementation. The public API is hardwired to external SpecialMatrices::Poisson2D, not a general dense/sparse matrix or arbitrary operator callback, so no unrestricted matrix-storage subclass is inferred without a dependency implementation review. The tolerance is internal ATOL+RTOL*NORM(B), with no caller tolerance/status dummy. A zero RHS is normalized before an early-exit check, and the total iteration cap is tested only at outer-cycle boundaries using <=; a full cycle can exceed it. Happy-breakdown/zero rotations and triangular pivots need independent validation. It prints a final true residual but returns X even if the budget is exhausted. Polynomial-preconditioned variants/root extraction and dependency kernels are outside this review. No solve or convergence experiment was run.

[README.md](https://github.com/jlm785/polynomial_interpolation/blob/5147f4797ce8f7278bcc34e8b1147f45e5283357/README.md)

**E1b — source-reviewed**

poly_interp implements a Neville-style Lagrange correction recurrence for the polynomial through n+1 distinct samples, also propagating derivative corrections. It evaluates at zero, so callers shift their abscissae by the desired query. This is a single polynomial (E1b), distinct from the local moving-stencil grid wrapper. Output y(0) is the value and y(k) is derivative k, not divided Taylor coefficients. dy is the last signed interpolation correction, not a certified error bound. There is no input-validation/status interface; duplicate nodes divide by zero. Restrict this reviewed use to n >= 1 and 0 <= nd <= n: for n=0 or derivative orders beyond n, some dy entries need not be assigned. Accuracy, conditioning and behavior on closely spaced nodes were not checked by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `5147f4797ce8f7278bcc34e8b1147f45e5283357`.

Pass xin(0:n), yin(0:n), output y(0:nd), dy(0:nd), degree n >= 1 and derivative limit 0 <= nd <= n. xin must contain distinct offsets from the target point, not absolute nodes unless querying zero. No error status is returned. dy entries are signed corrections, not guaranteed absolute errors.

Usage:


```fortran
nodes = [0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk]
```

Uncompiled calling sketch. The analytic value/first derivative at 0.5 are 0.25 and 1, but no comparison was run. Match selected_real_kind(12) consistently with the external routine. A small final correction does not certify interpolation error, and duplicate or nearly coincident input abscissae need independent validation.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected ordered-grid branch of grid_interp selects a local n+1-point stencil for each target, shifts its abscissae to that target and calls poly_interp. Stencil changes produce a piecewise-polynomial interpolation scheme (E1a), without an established spline smoothness condition at transitions. Both values and requested derivatives are copied into the target matrix. The wrapper checks some sizes and rejects extrapolation outside a scale-dependent tolerance. The unordered-grid sorting path is present but outside this source review. Its reported dymax is updated as a maximum of signed dy values starting from zero, rather than absolute corrections, so negative corrections can be hidden; it is not an absolute error estimate. Use distinct strictly ordered samples, in-range ordered targets and 0 <= nd <= n. No grid interpolation or derivative error check was executed.

Jenkins-Traub roots of a real polynomial. Supply DEGREE>=1, real OP(DEGREE+1) in descending-power order with nonzero leading coefficient, and real output ZEROR/ZEROI(DEGREE). ISTAT=0 is full success, -1 zero leading coefficient, -2 no roots found and positive values the count found on partial failure; do not use all output slots after partial failure. Use POLYROOTS_MODULE_RK (REAL64 default). Coefficients are not overwritten. Check polynomial residuals independently.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL rpoly(OP,DEGREE,ZEROR,ZEROI,ISTAT)
```

Argument declarations: [src/polyroots_module.F90:97–106](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/polyroots-fortran/blob/165ed6fbec98cc23d9ed4784fbc4708adb5e0bcf/src/polyroots_module.F90#L97-L106).

Real-coefficient companion-matrix roots through LAPACK SGEEV/DGEEV. N>=1, P(N+1) in descending-power order with nonzero leading term, WR/WI(N) real output. INFO=0 is eigensolver convergence, -999 a zero leading coefficient; remaining diagnostics are LAPACK INFO. Use POLYROOTS_MODULE_RK. The REAL128 branch ERROR STOPs because no quad LAPACK solver is provided; matching real32/real64 LAPACK must be linked. Root order is not specified, and small eigenvalue residuals are not certified here.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL polyroots(N,P,WR,WI,INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [src/polyroots_module.F90:2680–2687](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/polyroots-fortran/blob/165ed6fbec98cc23d9ed4784fbc4708adb5e0bcf/src/polyroots_module.F90#L2680-L2687).

Complex-coefficient companion-matrix roots through LAPACK CGEEV/ZGEEV. N>=1, COMPLEX(kind=POLYROOTS_MODULE_RK) P(N+1) in descending-power order and W(N) output. INFO=0 converged, -999 zero leading coefficient; other diagnostics come from LAPACK. REAL128 ERROR STOPs; real32/real64 requires matching LAPACK. Work arrays are internal. Results are unsorted and should be checked by residuals, particularly for ill-conditioned/multiple roots.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL cpolyroots(N,P,W,INFO)
```

**G2h1a1 — source-reviewed**

BOBYQA performs local derivative-free minimization of a smooth objective subject to simple bounds, using interpolating quadratic models and bounded trust-region subproblems. The reviewed wrapper partitions workspace, checks interpolation-count/bound-spacing restrictions and adjusts the starting point near bounds; BOBYQB dispatches model steps and objective evaluations. The model gradient is internal and does not mean the caller supplies derivatives. Require N>=2, N+2<=NPT<=(N+1)(N+2)/2, positive ordered radii and each bound interval at least twice RHOBEG. This original interface returns the best sampled variables but no explicit convergence flag or objective output argument. Printed termination reasons, independent objective/feasibility checks and evaluation-budget exhaustion must be distinguished; RHOEND is a radius target, not a solution-error certificate. This is a local constrained method, not global optimization.

**G2h3b1a — source-reviewed**

COBYLA minimizes an objective subject to nonlinear inequalities using simplex interpolation of objective/constraint values and native linearized trust-region subproblems. The caller supplies CALCFC values with feasible constraints CON>=0; it supplies neither objective nor constraint derivatives. G2h3b1a records the smooth general nonlinear-constraint/no-derivative scope, with zero equality constraints in this selected interface. Equalities are not separate inputs and tight paired inequalities need independent care. Unlike the other reviewed Powell folders, this copy has no IMPLICIT REAL*8 declaration and its Makefile does not promote REAL, so the reviewed default build uses default-real arrays and radii. MAXFUN is an input evaluation limit overwritten with evaluations used. There is no returned convergence code, and small final simplex radius does not guarantee feasibility or an accurate optimum.

**G2h2a1 — source-reviewed**

LINCOA performs local derivative-free minimization of a smooth objective with linear inequalities, building quadratic interpolation models and solving linearly constrained model trust subproblems. Columns A(:,J) are constraint normals for A(:,J) dot X<=B(J). The wrapper normalizes constraints and, if the initial point violates one, increases its internal normalized right-hand side to admit that point; the input B array itself is not overwritten by this adjustment. A feasible initial point is therefore important if the original feasible region must be preserved. Model-improvement objective calls may be infeasible; the incoming sign of F is a feasibility indicator before CALFUN overwrites it. Require nonzero constraint normals, valid N/NPT/radii and sufficient budget/workspace. W(1) and W(2) return objective and evaluation-count information after the normal algorithm; invalid-input early returns need separate handling and there is no explicit status code. It is neither linear programming nor a global optimum certificate.

**G1b1a — source-reviewed**

NEWUOA minimizes a smooth unconstrained multivariate function from a supplied initial point without user derivatives. It forms quadratic interpolation models with least-change Hessian updates and calls a truncated-CG trust-region model solver. N must be at least two, NPT must lie in the documented interpolation range, and both radii must be positive with RHOEND<=RHOBEG. This original entry uses a globally linked CALFUN symbol and a caller-sized double-precision workspace, changes X and reports progress through printing rather than a returned convergence status. The callback must be defined on trial points outside any intended box because no bounds are enforced. This mapping records the native local search/dispatch and model step, not a guarantee that RHOEND measures actual solution error or that a global minimum is found.

**G2h2a2 — source-reviewed**

GETMIN is the documented TOLMIN entry for a differentiable objective with linear equalities/inequalities and simple bounds. The caller supplies FGCALC objective and first derivatives; the solver maintains active constraints, seeks feasibility, uses line searches and tests the projected first-order/KKT residual against ACC. Constraint normals occupy columns; the first MEQ constraints are equalities and subsequent constraints use A(:,J) dot X<=B(J). Fixed variables can use equal lower/upper bounds. INFO is an input evaluation limit (zero means no imposed limit) and an output reason: 1 is the normal feasibility/first-order stop, while 2/3 indicate stalled feasible progress and 4 through 8 report invalid/inconsistent constraints or budget exhaustion. Return is not a second-order or global optimality certificate. Review covers the public contract, feasibility/minimization dispatch and native first-order stopping path, not every degeneracy/line-search dependency.

**G2h1a1 — source-reviewed**

The public bobyqa_module::bobyqa minimizes a smooth real scalar function under lower/upper variable bounds without supplied derivatives. It builds quadratic interpolation models and uses a trust-region method, dispatching to private BOBYQB. The selected public interface has ten arguments: N,NPT,X,XL,XU,RHOBEG,RHOEND,IPRINT,MAXFUN,CALFUN; it allocates workspace internally. This differs from older external BOBYQA interfaces with a user workspace and from other forks with status/F outputs. N must be at least 2; N+2<=NPT<=(N+1)*(N+2)/2; NPT=2*N+1 is a suggested initial choice. Provide conforming REAL(wp) vectors X/XL/XU of length at least N. wp is REAL64 in the pinned kind_module. Require positive RHOEND<=RHOBEG and each bound interval at least 2*RHOBEG wide; scale variables appropriately. The wrapper can adjust the initial X away from bounds to construct its interpolation model. CALFUN(N,X,F) is a subroutine callback with default INTEGER N, assumed-shape REAL(wp) X(:) INTENT(IN), and scalar REAL(wp) F INTENT(OUT). X is overwritten by the best estimate; neither objective value nor convergence status is an output argument. Reevaluate the callback to obtain F and independently assess the result. Invalid NPT or insufficient bound spacing prints a diagnostic and returns; normal return alone is not a success certificate. IPRINT=0 suppresses ordinary iteration output but not those wrapper diagnostics. MAXFUN limits callback evaluations; there is no public counter/status result. This review inspects the public wrapper, callback declarations and precision selection, not every private interpolation/trust-region kernel. The illustrative calling program was not compiled or run for this independent review. The existing playground box-quadratic checked driver remains separately recorded and is not reclassified as a new independent numerical test.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
program bounded_minimum
  use kind_module, only: wp
  use bobyqa_module, only: bobyqa
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: n=2, npt=5
  real(wp) :: x(n), xl(n), xu(n), f
  x=[0.5_wp,0.5_wp]
  xl=[0.0_wp,0.0_wp]
  xu=[1.0_wp,1.0_wp]
  call bobyqa(n,npt,x,xl,xu,0.2_wp,1.0e-8_wp,0,1000,objective)
  call objective(n,x,f)
  print *, x, f
contains
  subroutine objective(n,x,f)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(wp), intent(in) :: x(:)
    real(wp), intent(out) :: f
    f=(x(1)-2.0_wp)**2+(x(2)+1.0_wp)**2
  end subroutine objective
end program bounded_minimum
```

See the pinned declaration links for all inputs and callback types. Bounds, interpolation geometry, scale, evaluation budget and absence of a returned success flag remain caller responsibilities.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The reviewed PCM path of ppr_1d reconstructs piecewise-constant cell profiles from cell means and remaps them by integrating profile/target-cell overlaps. rcon1d dispatches to pcm, which copies each cell mean as its constant coefficient; rmap1d/xmap1d selects that one-coefficient representation, and imap1d evaluates integral basis differences and divides the accumulated mass by target-cell width. A subsequent compensated-sum defect correction adjusts an extremal target mean. This establishes a degree-zero piecewise-polynomial reconstruction/remapping path in E1a; it is not point-sample interpolation or a standalone PDE integrator. Restrict this review to ndof=1, PCM, compatible monotone source/target edges over the same domain and positive cell widths. The higher-order PLM/PPM/PQM and limiter implementations were not fully reviewed. Workspaces and all option fields must be initialized; the init methods dereference opts even though declared optional. No conservation, positivity or remapping-accuracy test was run.

**G2h1a1 — source-reviewed**

The modern BOBYQA module driver minimizes a real objective under simple bounds without user derivatives, constructing quadratic interpolation models and bounded trust-region steps through BOBYQB. It preprocesses dimensions, bounds, radius/budget controls and optional histories before dispatch. X is both starting point and returned approximate minimizer; CALFUN has the modern assumed-shape (X,F) interface and must match configured RP. Bounds and interpolation geometry matter: this is local smooth-model optimization, not a global minimum certificate or a claim of nonsmooth convergence. INFO reports the specific termination reason, NF the evaluation count; radius and target/budget terminations have different meanings. This review covers driver/core trust-region dispatch, not all geometry/rescue/update kernels or fresh optimization results.

**G2h2a1 — source-reviewed**

LINCOA minimizes a smooth objective without user derivatives under linear equalities/inequalities and optional bounds. The modern driver assembles and scales constraints, prepares a quadratic interpolation model and dispatches feasible trust-region/geometry steps to LINCOB. AINEQ has one constraint per row with AINEQ*X<=BINEQ; AEQ*X=BEQ is the equality convention. This is local linearly constrained optimization, not nonlinear constraint handling or a global certificate. Returned CSTRV is the reported constraint violation and INFO/NF describe termination and work, which need inspection alongside an independent residual calculation. The review covers driver and selected trust-region dispatch, not all initialization/geometry/update routines.

**G2h3b1a — source-reviewed**

The modern COBYLA interface minimizes an objective with nonlinear INEQUALITY values NLCONSTR(X)<=0, alongside optional LINEAR equalities/inequalities and bounds, without user derivatives. The core maintains simplex-based linear models and solves trust-region linear subproblems. This sign convention differs from historical COBYLA interfaces using nonnegative constraint residuals. M_NLCON must exactly match the callback output count; CALCFC evaluates both objective and nonlinear values. The selected mixed-constraint sketch includes a linear equality plus one nonlinear inequality; it does not claim a separate native nonlinear-equality callback. Smooth-function classification records this local derivative-free approximation path, not a global convergence or exact-feasibility guarantee. INFO/CSTRV/CTOL and termination details need independent interpretation.

**D6 — source-reviewed**

The nonrestarted real DLANSVD driver dispatches Lanczos bidiagonalization with partial reorthogonalization, solves the projected bidiagonal SVD, refines Ritz error estimates and extends the Krylov space until requested singular triplets converge or the space is exhausted. APROD must supply both A*x and A-transpose*x. Singular-vector reconstruction is dispatched only on the driver completion conditions. K is overwritten with the number obtained, and INFO distinguishes ordinary completion, smaller invariant subspace and failed convergence. Caller workspace, callback correctness and options are essential; the few scalar guards are not a complete input validator. LAPINFO from the bidiagonal solver is not propagated as a checked caller status in the inspected path. No callback, singular triplet or numerical error bound was verified by execution; restarted/complex variants remain unreviewed.

**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

The public PSB_KRYLOV generic dispatches its distributed real-double CG selection to a native preconditioned conjugate-gradient iteration. The implementation forms b-A*x, applies the supplied preconditioner, computes global dot products and updates search directions, solution and recursive residual. This selection requires an SPD system and compatible fixed SPD preconditioning, not an arbitrary nonsymmetric matrix. The caller must initialize a PSBLAS/MPI context, assemble the distributed sparse matrix/vectors/descriptor and build the preconditioner. ISTOP=2 selects relative residual scaling and iteration/error outputs are explicit; zero denominators and breakdown exits have internal conventions, so INFO plus a fresh independently computed residual should be checked. Unknown method strings otherwise fall back to BiCGStab, making the exact CG selector significant. Review covers public dispatch, CG recurrence and convergence cleanup, not every backend/precision or Krylov variant.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The selected lfsr258 module updates five saved signed integer states with shift, mask and XOR recurrences, combines them with XOR and maps the result to REAL(dp) by multiplying by about 2**(-64) and adding 0.5. rand is a scalar wrapper and rand_arr repeats it N times. The source comment describes [0,1), but floating-point rounding can reach an endpoint; strict open/half-open endpoint guarantees were not established. Seeds are adjusted with masks rather than validated through a returned status. Correct bit behavior assumes the intended 64-bit integer model; shared saved state is not reentrant or thread-safe. This mapping concerns the selected LFSR path, not all generators in the file or cryptographic security. No statistical, period or reference-sequence test was performed.

This routine is a seed-support utility, not a primality/factorization algorithm, and was not executed.

**D — source-reviewed**

PSFUN_D_ARNOLDI approximates a distributed sparse matrix-function action y=f(alpha*A)*x by building an Arnoldi Krylov basis, evaluating the small Hessenberg matrix function through PSFUN_D_SERIAL, and projecting back. The default serial function object selects EXP/EXPOKIT. This is broader matrix-function linear algebra, not merely ordinary matrix-vector multiplication or an explicitly supplied matrix polynomial; the retained class D avoids an unsupported narrower leaf. EPS/ISTOP select estimated stopping behavior, not a certified normwise error bound. The implementation normalizes by the input norm and Arnoldi subdiagonal without a visible zero-input/happy-breakdown guard; projected dimensions and final accumulation require numerical validation. The routine temporarily changes FUN scaling and has a shared error-handler path. Review covers the Arnoldi path, public interface and serial dispatch, not every serial function or rational/Lanczos variant.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The public OPTIMIZER initializes random particles, evaluates a scalar callback, updates velocity from inertial/personal/social terms and clamps coordinates to bounds. It retains personal/global best costs and returns a parameter vector after a generation budget or desired-cost threshold. The inspected scope is the star topology (TOPO=1); adaptive-neighborhood logic is not independently reviewed. Source findings: the star social index is selected initially and not refreshed in the general generation loop, and the returned global-best parameters are copied from the particle current position rather than its saved personal-best position. They can therefore disagree with the stored best error. There is no returned objective/status; desired_error is an objective threshold rather than parameter accuracy. This is heuristic global search, not a global-optimum guarantee or a validated convergence result.

**K1b2a — source-reviewed**

The selected DQED path minimizes a sum of squared nonlinear residuals under simple bounds and linear equality/inequality constraints. DQEDEV supplies function/constraint values AND first derivatives in FJAC; numerical differentiation is not supplied by the driver. IND encodes lower/upper/two-sided/unbounded entries for variables and constraint values. DQED sizes workspace and dispatches DQEDMN for bounded linear/quadratic local models and iteration control. The source documents slightly nonlinear constraints but warns about strongly nonlinear ones; this mapping deliberately selects the linear-constraint class. WA/IWA storage and IOPT/ROPT/IGO protocols must follow the documented options. Saved driver/workspace state prevents arbitrary interleaved solves and some storage errors STOP. This is driver/interface and model-dispatch review, not a complete audit of every bounded least-squares kernel, convergence flag or a new optimization result.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

LININTERPOL searches for neighboring abscissae and evaluates an affine weighted pair, using a saved interval index for subsequent calls. The implemented interpolation is univariate piecewise linear. Despite header prose promising zero outside the table, those returns/assignments are commented out; search conditions may evaluate negative/out-of-range elements and the final formula extrapolates after clamping. The nold<1 check does not reject a one-point table. Even an in-range query on a two-point table can first read beyond the upper end because the saved-index clamp sets nold-1 then accesses ilastnum+1. Resetting ILASTVAL sets ILASTNUM=-1; a subsequent upward search can begin at -2 and read a negative index even for an in-range query. More table points do not repair this. The sketch records the interface only; the search requires repair and checked testing before use. This review does not establish flux conservation or review the spectral-resampling dispatcher.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `baa2789e0607b063737e4d52759fa21c3e1ef9a7`.

**L4c — source-reviewed**

The external GAMV kernel computes directional lag-binned spatial continuity statistics from irregular multidimensional coordinates and observed variables. It enumerates accepted data pairs, filters lag/direction/bandwidth and trimming conditions, accumulates products/differences and normalizes per-bin means. The selected IVTYPE=3 branch returns lag covariance after subtracting the head/tail means. The adopted GAMS tree has no dedicated spatial-variogram leaf, so this spatial statistical analysis remains in multidimensional elementary data analysis L4c rather than being called temporal autocovariance or kriging interpolation. NP reports floating-point pair counts; empty bins remain zero and need masking. The semivariogram cloud branch has an off-by-one capacity guard and stores cumulative bin values rather than a clearly isolated pair statistic; the sketch selects covariance, for which that cloud branch writes no points. No general success status is returned. Review covers covariance accumulation/normalization and related public declarations, not every variogram type or the separate kriging solver.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `c26c3bff20c7cc16583c94fb850e17600b9a610d`.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

The external GAUSSLEGENDREQUADRATURE routine generates successive n-point Gauss-Legendre rules with polynomial recurrence/Newton root refinement, linearly interpolates tabulated X/Y at those nodes and returns the last weighted sum. This is nonautomatic finite-interval quadrature of gridded data, not a callback integrator or accuracy-controlled algorithm. N_INT is the last quadrature order, not a tolerance. Source finding: an optional-argument fallback computes N_INTERATIONS, but the actual loop uses N_INT directly; omitting it references an absent optional argument. Orders below one leave Z undefined. LININTERPOL status is ignored and its indexing is unsafe even for in-range queries: resetting its saved index to -1 can start the upward search at -2. The calling sketch does not repair this. The rule generator caps Newton refinement at ten steps without reporting nonconvergence. This review does not promote the larger INTEGRALALL dispatcher or every branch to source-reviewed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `bab28287f29298c701e4c8bbc7d881f62c97fd4a`.

**L5a1n — source-reviewed**

NORMCDF overwrites a double-precision vector with standard-normal cumulative probabilities using one half times (1+DERF(x/sqrt(2))). This is a direct statistical function-evaluation kernel from historical PyMC2, not a current PyMC interface or a Bayesian sampler. It is a CDF, not a density or a normal random-number generator. The left-tail formula can lose relative accuracy by cancellation; there is no complementary-tail/log-CDF branch, finite-input check or returned status. A direct Fortran call includes NX, although f2py hides the length in Python. Review covers the complete short routine and its actual in-place behavior, not numerical tail accuracy or compiler support for the legacy DERF spelling.

**L5a1p — source-reviewed**

The external POISSON kernel sums log Poisson mass terms across independent integer counts, with either one shared rate or a rate per count. A call with N=1 evaluates one log probability mass; larger N returns the joint log likelihood rather than a vector of individual masses. It uses the native FACTLN/GAMMLN support for log factorials and returns a large finite negative sentinel for negative counts/rates. Require NMU=1 or N: the Fortran implementation does not validate every length accepted by its broadcast-like convention. The pair count=0/rate=0 is special-cased, but positive counts with zero rate reach LOG(0), which can trigger floating-point traps. No returned status or gradient is part of this entry. FACTLN has a lazily populated saved table, so concurrent-call safety is not established.

**L5a2w — source-reviewed**

EXPONWEIB_PPF computes exponentiated-Weibull quantiles directly from probability q and positive shape parameters a,c, with each parameter supplied as a singleton or length-N array. For a=1 this specializes to the ordinary Weibull inverse CDF, supporting the GAMS Weibull inverse-distribution leaf. The native formula uses ordinary power and LOG(1-q**(1/a)), not stabilized LOG1P/exponential-difference kernels, so endpoint and extreme-parameter accuracy is not established. Require 0<q<1, positive finite shapes and valid broadcast lengths. Invalid shape-array lengths return before assigning outputs, while invalid probabilities/shapes have no explicit validation or status. This is deterministic quantile evaluation, not a random sampler.

**License: MIT selected solver components; LGPL-3.0-or-later pyOpt framework**

The root explicitly distinguishes the LGPL-3.0-or-later framework from separately licensed optimizers. The selected SOLVOPT, SLSQP and COBYLA component notices grant MIT-style terms and name their original authors and pyOpt modifiers. This is scoped component evidence, not a claim that all optimizers, every bundled BLAS/helper, Python wrappers or linked binaries share one license.

**G1b2 — source-reviewed**

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. The unconstrained path minimizes or maximizes general locally Lipschitz objectives using a modified Shor r-algorithm with space dilation and supplied gradients/subgradients or finite differences. The selected fragment minimizes with an analytic subgradient; it does not establish smooth Newton convergence or global optimality. The patched interface adds explicit B(N,N), twelve real N-vectors and IDX(N) work storage, plus output unit/file controls. The executable calls FUN(N,X,F), GRAD(N,X,G), FUNC(N,X,FC) and GRADC(N,X,GC); the header synopsis omits N and must not be copied literally. N must be at least two. OPTIONS has thirteen DOUBLE PRECISION entries: call SOPTIONS then set entry 5 to -1 for quiet operation without opening a file. Entry 9 is an iteration count or negative abnormal-stop code; the N<2 branch actually sets -1 despite the header listing -2. Output is not an optimality certificate.

**G2h3b2 — source-reviewed**

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. The constrained path combines the objective with an adaptive penalty on a scalar maximal constraint residual, using a supplied active-constraint gradient/subgradient or finite differences. FUNC must aggregate violations consistently with g(x)<=0; encode equality residuals explicitly if needed. This is not an array-of-constraints callback, nor a global method. Reevaluate the original objective and every constraint at returned X; F can include a penalty. The patched interface adds explicit B(N,N), twelve real N-vectors and IDX(N) work storage, plus output unit/file controls. The executable calls FUN(N,X,F), GRAD(N,X,G), FUNC(N,X,FC) and GRADC(N,X,GC); the header synopsis omits N and must not be copied literally. N must be at least two. OPTIONS has thirteen DOUBLE PRECISION entries: call SOPTIONS then set entry 5 to -1 for quiet operation without opening a file. Entry 9 is an iteration count or negative abnormal-stop code; the N<2 branch actually sets -1 despite the header listing -2. Output is not an optimality certificate.

**G2h3b1b — source-reviewed**

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. SLSQP implements smooth nonlinear equality/inequality constrained minimization with bounds, BFGS Hessian updates and SQP subproblems. Unlike the inherited reverse-communication header, this patched top-level routine loops internally, calling SLFUNC(M,MEQ,LA,N,F,C,X) and SLGRAD(M,MEQ,LA,N,F,C,G,A,X); MODE starts at zero and returns final status. Supply equality constraints first and remaining constraints as C>=0, XL/XU bounds, C(LA), G(N+1), A(LA,N+1), LA=MAX(1,M) for the selected contract. The executable workspace check uses 4*N1 where the copied header uses 3*N1; use the actual check at lines 201-210. Nonzero MODE includes infeasibility, rank/line-search/iteration failures or encoded insufficient workspace; zero reports stopping criteria, not global optimality. Review covers interface, callback loop, workspace checks and SQP update dispatch, not all nested constrained-LS/BLAS kernels.

**G2h3b1a — source-reviewed**

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. COBYLA minimizes an objective under nonlinear inequalities CON>=0 by simplex interpolation and a decreasing trust-region radius without user derivatives. The mapping selects smooth objective/constraints without supplied derivatives; the routine does not enforce smoothness itself. Its pyOpt signature adds CALCFC first and status/count/unit/file/FF/GG arguments. CALCFC(N,M,X,F,CON) supplies values; encode bounds as constraints. Allocate W>=N*(3*N+2*M+11)+4*M+6 and IACT>=M+1, choose positive RHOBEG>=RHOEND and an evaluation budget. IFAIL=0 is normal radius termination, 1 evaluation limit and 2 damaging roundoff. FF/GG are set on each callback evaluation, but final selection can restore X from the best simplex vertex without refreshing those outputs; reevaluate F/CON at returned X. RHOEND does not guarantee accuracy or feasibility. This review covers the driver, interpolation/trust-region dispatch and output bookkeeping, not every TRSTLP numerical branch.

**D9b1 — source-reviewed**

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. NNLS solves nonnegative linear L2 least squares by an active/passive-set method, Householder updates and Givens rotations. A(MDA,N) and B(M) are overwritten, X(N)>=0 is the selected variable constraint, and W(N), Z(M), INDEX(N) are scratch. MODE=1 success, 2 invalid dimensions, 3 iteration count above 3*N. The same class also covers LSEI below, but NNLS has no equality/general inequality inputs. Preserve originals for residual and KKT checks; supplied legacy BLAS calls include zero-increment broadcasts. LSEI uses Householder null-space reduction for min ||E X-F|| with C X=D and G X>=H. Its selected contract requires 0<MC<N, ME>=N-MC, MG>=1, full row rank C and the reduced design assumptions; inputs are overwritten. Avoid the MC=N shortcut if inequalities need validation: it bypasses the inequality solve. The returned XNRM is combined with the equality-space solution norm in the constrained branch and should not be assumed to equal the original residual norm; compute that from saved E/F. MODE=1 is the native success code, with rank, compatibility and NNLS-limit failures otherwise. Workspace follows the source formula with L=N-MC; JW>=MAX(MG,L).

**D9a1 — source-reviewed**

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. HFTI handles rank-deficient unconstrained linear L2 least squares through column-pivoted Householder reduction and a retained-rank minimum-norm completion. TAU is an absolute diagonal threshold, not a relative singular-value tolerance; KRANK is a computed pseudorank. A and B are overwritten; B first N rows hold solutions and RNORM(NB) residual norms. Require positive M/N, MDA>=M, MDB>=MAX(M,N), H/G/IP length N. There is no MODE or conditioning estimate. The sketch gives B an extra row to keep zero-length tail references within storage; choose TAU based on problem scaling, preserve originals and independently assess numerical rank/residuals.

**G2e1 — source-reviewed**

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. LDP solves the minimum-distance problem min 0.5*X^T X subject to G X>=H by forming a dual NNLS problem. This is a strictly convex quadratic objective with identity Hessian, not an arbitrary quadratic-programming interface. G(MG,N), H(M) are preserved; X(N), XNORM and first M workspace entries return the solution, norm and multipliers on MODE=1. W length is at least (M+2)*(N+1)+2*M, INDEX at least M; require N>=1, M>=1, MG>=M. MODE=2 is invalid N, 3 NNLS iteration limit, 4 incompatible constraints. Near degeneracy and floating-point feasibility must be assessed independently; no original residual or KKT certificate is returned.

**D1b11 — source-reviewed**

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. H12 constructs (MODE=1) and/or applies (MODE=2) an elementary Householder reflection, represented by modified U and separate UP. LPIVOT<L1<=M with LPIVOT>=1 defines the pivot and tail. IUE strides U; ICE strides C elements; ICV strides vectors; NCV counts transformed vectors. No explicit dense Q is returned. Invalid/degenerate indices can return silently; a zero construction vector can leave UP undefined, so do not apply that undefined state. Selected sketch uses a nonzero vector and contiguous column-major C. Preserve U/UP when applying the same reflection again; there is no status output.

**G2h3b1b — source-reviewed**

OGEXEC coordinates feasibility correction and gradient-based objective improvement with active constraints, scaling and line searches through OGCORR/OGOPTI. Constraint types support >=, <= and equality against zero/reference conventions configured by setup; the last output is the objective/merit. The selected VARDER=1 path uses caller first derivatives, configured through OGDERI; finite-difference modes exist but are outside this mapping. CALVAL is actually called with (VALVAR,VALCON,IFLAG), while CALDER receives (VALVAR,VALCON,DERCON), with physical unscaled callback quantities. FINITE is an iteration-count output, not the derivative-mode selector. Call OGINIT and configure types, scales/tolerances and objective direction before OGEXEC, then release through OGCLOS. COMMON pointer/array state is shared and not reentrant. The algorithm targets near-linear constraints; FINOPT local optimality/feasibility labels are termination criteria, not mathematical certificates or a new trajectory/domain validation.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

The wrapper initializes complex polynomial term coefficients/exponents and a partitioned linear-product start system, then calls POLSYS_PLP to track homotopy paths, returning candidate roots, per-path statuses and evaluation counts in module arrays. This is a square complex polynomial-system solver, not a general nonpolynomial system API or a new proof that every path succeeds. INIT_POLY expects concatenated equation terms; INIT_PARTITION defines variable groups for each equation. Always pass DENSE explicitly: the omitted-optional branch in SOLVE attempts to assign the absent dummy. The wrapper also fixes SCALE_FACTORS length at 30, so do not exceed 30 variables without correcting that bound; COMPLEX(KIND=8) coefficients must match core R8. Shared polynomial/partition/output state is not reentrant. Inspect SOLVE_STATUS/PATH_STATUS before interpreting roots; the wrapper assumes core output pointers are associated when copying them, so abnormal-error paths need additional protection. This review covers setup/driver dispatch and inspected core path tracking, not every singular/multiple/infinite-root case.

**L10a3a2 — source-reviewed**

EEBLS scans a supplied frequency grid, folds mean-centered observations into phase bins, searches contiguous box windows including wrapped windows, and records the strongest box-least-squares statistic, period, depth, duty fraction and bin endpoints. This supports periodogram analysis for box-shaped periodic signals, not a Fourier power-spectral density estimate, sinusoidal Lomb-Scargle fit or false-alarm probability. The native arrays Y/IBI have length 2000: checking NB<=2000 alone is insufficient because wrapping writes through NB+FLOOR(QMA*NB)+1. Validate the extended bound, positive time span/frequencies and sorted finite times. Every considered window must avoid all-sample/empty denominators, and at least one eligible window must exist; otherwise best-window scalars can remain undefined. Invalid NB/frequency controls can STOP the process. There is no explicit returned convergence/error flag, weighting or missing-data handling. Review covers the actual frequency/phase/window loop and output extraction, not detection significance.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `f066acfbd9ab1dd238ec3b592db32c93fa183500`.

**G2b — source-reviewed**

QAPH4 searches permutations to minimize SUM(A(i,j)*B(perm(i),perm(j))) using random transpositions, a Metropolis acceptance probability and a decreasing temperature with increasing trials per stage. The O(N) swap delta explicitly assumes symmetric A and B; it is not a general asymmetric QAP implementation or a continuous quadratic-programming solver. The R wrapper validates symmetric nonnegative matrices and schedules independent restarts. The Fortran core has no equivalent validation and calls R RNG/interrupt services via a C wrapper; it is not standalone Fortran. Require N>=2, valid permutation, positive trial count, FITER>=1 and 0<FT<1, finite well-scaled data and representable iteration counts. OPE/OL are best-found heuristic output, not a proof of global optimality.

**A3c — source-reviewed**

The selected ddmodule interface stores each dd_real as two REAL*8 components. Defined string assignment calls DDINPC after copying into a fixed 80-character buffer; a REAL*8 assignment instead puts the already-rounded input in the high component and zero in the low component. Rational-style exactness and arbitrary runtime precision are not claimed. The selected addition overload passes the two-word arrays to a C++ wrapper and DD addition; the kernel selects sloppy_add or ieee_add at compile time and uses compensated two-sum/renormalization steps. Arithmetic range remains based on the component format and correct rounding/reassociation/build conventions matter. This source review covers construction/assignment and addition dispatch plus selected C++ addition branches, not the whole quad-double library, all transcendental functions or an independent precision/error bound.

**D7 — source-reviewed**

DQR1UP updates an existing real QR factorization after A -> A+u*v-transpose. It forms Q-transpose*u, applies Givens rotations to factors, updates the leading row and retriangularizes; the economy branch additionally handles the component orthogonal to the basis and dispatches a Cholesky update. This is decomposition updating, not a fresh QR factorizer or a linear solver. Inputs must already form a valid full/economy factorization. Q/R and V are overwritten, U can be destroyed in economy form, and WORK needs 2*K elements. Invalid scalar dimensions go through QRUPDATE_XERROR; no status dummy is returned. Review covers this driver/rotation dispatch, not every helper, downdate or complex variant.

Public entry point `quadpack::dqag`: [src/quadpack_generic.F90:96–220](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/quadpack/blob/ab42d50794280a8e7996f2ee4cda1f8753dfde5b/src/quadpack_generic.F90#L96-L220).

General finite-interval adaptive Gauss-Kronrod integration. KEY chooses a 15/21/31/41/51/61-point rule pair (out-of-range values are clamped to the endpoint choices). Require LIMIT>=1, IWORK(LIMIT), LENW>=4*LIMIT and WORK(LENW). Supply absolute/relative tolerances; invalid tolerance combinations give IER=6. The integrand callback supplies the full ordinary integrand. The public quadpack module reexports these REAL64 DQ routines from quadpack_double, which preprocesses quadpack_generic.F90. F(X) is a scalar REAL64 function with REAL64 INTENT(IN) X. RESULT is the integral estimate, ABSERR an estimated absolute error, NEVAL a call count and LAST the partition count. IER=0 is normal algorithmic termination; nonzero values need routine-specific interpretation (invalid controls, exhausted subdivision or numerical difficulty), not unconditional acceptance. Error estimates are not certified bounds. Match default INTEGER and REAL64 types and provide finite callback values on the sampling domain.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dqag(F,A,B,EPSABS,EPSREL,KEY,RESULT,ABSERR,NEVAL,IER,LIMIT,LENW,LAST,IWORK,WORK)
```

Improper integration: INF=1 selects (BOUND,+infinity), INF=-1 selects (-infinity,BOUND); the interface also supports INF=2 over the whole real line, with BOUND unused. The mapped checked configurations are the half-lines; no whole-line verification is imported here. Require LIMIT>=1, IWORK(LIMIT), LENW>=4*LIMIT and WORK(LENW). Supply the ordinary integrand and tolerances; convergent tails are a caller responsibility. The public quadpack module reexports these REAL64 DQ routines from quadpack_double, which preprocesses quadpack_generic.F90. F(X) is a scalar REAL64 function with REAL64 INTENT(IN) X. RESULT is the integral estimate, ABSERR an estimated absolute error, NEVAL a call count and LAST the partition count. IER=0 is normal algorithmic termination; nonzero values need routine-specific interpretation (invalid controls, exhausted subdivision or numerical difficulty), not unconditional acceptance. Error estimates are not certified bounds. Match default INTEGER and REAL64 types and provide finite callback values on the sampling domain.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dqagi(F,BOUND,INF,EPSABS,EPSREL,RESULT,ABSERR,NEVAL,IER,LIMIT,LENW,LAST,IWORK,WORK)
```

**G2e1 — source-reviewed**

The standard qp_problem constructor copies and Cholesky-factorizes a positive-definite quadratic matrix, stores its inverse triangular factor, and records linear equality/inequality rows. solve_standard_qp packs constraints and calls the private qpgen2 active-set implementation. The reviewed driver starts at the unconstrained quadratic minimizer, selects violated constraints, computes primal/dual steps, adds constraints with Givens rotations and removes constraints when a dual step requires it. G2e1 records positive-definite-Hessian quadratic programming; no indefinite or merely semidefinite extension is inferred. The objective is 0.5*x-transpose*P*x - x-transpose*q, with A*x=b and C*x>=d; sign and row orientation matter. The constructor checks dimensions but does not propagate TRTRI INFO, and its Cholesky call has no returned err argument. The unconstrained wrapper branch sets X and success but never assigns result%obj; the sketch therefore uses a constrained case. The boolean success loses detailed driver failure information, so validate returned feasibility/stationarity independently. Compact storage, least-squares/LASSO variants and external numerical kernels are not audited. No QP or author tests were executed. The linked inequality test transposes C despite the constructor row-storage interface; that example orientation needs checking and is not copied into the sketch.
