**G2e1 — source-reviewed**

The quadprog generic copies the Hessian, changes signs/transposes row-oriented constraints, appends bound inequalities when requested, allocates workspace, and dispatches to Goldfarb/Idnani qpgen2 with Cholesky-based positive-definite setup. G2e1 records strictly convex QP with linear equality/inequality constraints, not indefinite or general nonlinear optimization. H_check changes every near-zero diagonal to 1e-10; this is not a valid general positive-definiteness test and can change the problem. constrain_check misses some positive equality residuals because its two-sided test uses AND incorrectly. res is qpgen2 criterion/objective output, not an independently computed feasibility residual despite wrapper wording. The C adapter copies only qeq constraint rows and is outside the shown Fortran API. This review covers wrapper and core setup/dispatch rather than every active-set update. No QP or feasibility/KKT check was run.

**L8c3 — source-reviewed**

RQFNB solves the bounded linear-program form used for multiple quantile regression with a Frisch-Newton primal-dual interior-point iteration and weighted normal-equation solves. The selected TAU=0.5 case is multiple median/L1 regression and supports L8c3; other quantiles use asymmetric check loss rather than an ordinary Lp norm. The caller supplies A=X-transpose, cost=-response, RHS=(1-tau)*sum(X,rows), unit upper bounds and initial WN(:,1)=1-tau, as the Python wrapper establishes. Regression coefficients are minus WP(:,1), not the raw primal/dual vector in WN. Iterations are hard-capped at fifty; INFO primarily reports normal-equation factorization and may remain zero on iteration exhaustion, so NIT and independent optimality/residual checks are needed. Inputs/workspaces are overwritten and boundary quantiles or singular designs are not supported by this sketch. Review covers initialization, predictor/corrector loop, solve dispatch and wrapper sign conventions, not censored/constrained variants or statistical inference.

```fortran
x(:,1)=1d0; x(:,2)=[0d0,1d0,2d0,3d0,4d0,5d0]
response=[1d0,3d0,5d0,7d0,9d0,20d0]
a=transpose(x); cost=-response; rhs=0.5d0*sum(x,dim=1)
d=1d0; u=1d0; wn=0d0; wn(:,1)=0.5d0; wp=0d0
call rqfnb(n,p,a,cost,rhs,d,u,0.99995d0,1d-6,wn,wp,nit,info)
if(info/=0.or.nit(1)>=50) error stop "inspect LP factorization/iteration diagnostics"
coef=-wp(:,1)
print *,coef
! Check median-regression optimality independently; INFO alone is insufficient.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Default INTEGER/DOUBLE PRECISION fragment with transposed design, explicit dual initialization and compatible BLAS/LAPACK. The cap check conservatively requests inspection even if a fiftieth step met tolerance. No quantile fit, LP gap, singular case or Python wrapper was tested.

**K1b1a2 — source-reviewed**

nlls_solve drives repeated nlls_iterate calls for a local first-order critical point of 0.5*SUM(F(X)**2). The inspected unconstrained first-order model evaluates residuals and an analytic Jacobian, sets the residual-Hessian contribution to zero, dispatches a trust-region step and compares actual with predicted reduction before updating. K1b1a2 records smooth nonlinear least squares with supplied first derivatives, scoped to MODEL=1, no bounds/weights/regularization. The public solve still requires a Hessian-callback argument; the supplied dummy is suitable for this selected first-order model. The default MODEL=3 is hybrid, so explicitly select MODEL=1 for this usage. Status 0 reports the selected stopping tests, not a unique/global minimum or accuracy certificate. Convergence can be on residual, gradient or step size; inspect inform fields and recompute residuals. Optional weights multiply residuals, rather than being unsquared objective coefficients. Preprocessing creates separate single/double modules. No fit or trust-region kernel/dependency audit was executed.

**L6b14 — source-reviewed**

The selected SHINOZUKA branch prepares spectral wave vectors/density weights, draws random phases and assembles cosine sums over spatial points through matrix products, scaled by the spectral spacing. It is a finite spectral random-field approximation intended to model Gaussian covariance structure, not an exact multivariate-normal factorization or a proven covariance match. GEN_STD_GAUSS normalizes coordinates by correlation lengths, dispatches the method and attempts to restore geometry. Material findings: its restoration multiplies RDF%XRANGE twice; the Shinozuka chunk/sample loops repeatedly replace SKMAT by SQRT(SKMAT), changing spectral amplitudes after the first chunk/sample; very many wave vectors can make XSLAB zero before division. Resolve these before validating/reusing the field distribution, multiple samples or normalized-coordinate round trips. Objects require fully initialized mesh/grid, positive correlation lengths, spectra, seed, sample-selection flags and associated output pointers. MPI/logging/FFTW/HDF5 dependencies are part of the build stack; alternatives were not fully reviewed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `865ee27abad2d1cbdafb05b1e23fd02cf7b5dfc3`.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

rng_m provides object-owned MT19937 state with 624 INT32 words, single-seed expansion, a twist recurrence and bitwise tempering. The selected uint32 binding masks signed INT32 output into a nonnegative INT64 result, carrying a 32-bit integer payload rather than generating 64 random bits or a real-valued variate. L6a21 records intended discrete uniform pseudorandom output. An unseeded state falls back to seed 5489; explicitly seeding is shown. Seed multiplication and the lower-mask expression rely on signed wrap behavior not guaranteed by standard Fortran. C array-seeding code explicitly differs from reference initialization and is excluded. Source inspection does not establish period, bitwise agreement or statistical quality; no generator was run.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The selected rk54DormandEachStep forms seven explicit stages and two embedded endpoint estimates, scales their difference with global rtol/atol and proposes/rejects a step. The inspected stage calls all pass t unchanged rather than t+c_i*h, so this mapping is restricted to autonomous systems such as the bundled Pleiades RHS; general time-dependent ODEs require correction. DyDtMod::dev is a compiled dependency to replace, not a callback argument. Global atol has only 50 slots, controls/counters need initialization, and the IEEE_IS_NORMAL endpoint check rejects exact zero and subnormals as well as NaNs/infinities. Zero estimated error also enters err**(-1/6) without a separate guard. No claimed order, trajectory accuracy or success was verified by execution.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The reviewed Fortran 90 module provides setup plus range_integrate/step_integrate for a real first-order ODE vector. Setup validates shapes, tolerance/thresholds and direction, selects an explicit RK method and allocates state. The controller calls explicit stage combinations, estimates local error from an embedded pair with threshold-weighted max norm, rejects/shrinks or accepts/rescales steps, and returns requested output through interpolation when supported. I1a1a records one-step nonstiff IVP methods. Stiffness detection warns rather than turning this into an implicit stiff solver. This review covers the public stateful driver contract and selected stage/error-control paths, not all coefficient tables, interpolants or global-error assessment. Fatal errors stop by default and successful flag=1 is not a global-accuracy bound. Setup nullifies pointers, so collect_garbage before reinitializing allocated state; shallow copying communication objects is unsafe. No ODE or author template was run.

[README.md](https://github.com/eachonly/Robust-Gauss-Newton-Algorithm/blob/277ad1bab849f66a5c152a82aa99fd4c42514800/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `289828e2cbc8a47f3020b8c28bf205cc2d03925695f9f0730873d3586673a74e`.

**K1b2 — source-reviewed**

The public RGN module routine minimizes one-half the sum of squared user residuals subject to simple lower/upper parameter bounds. It estimates the Jacobian by bound-clipped finite differences, forms J-transpose*r and J-transpose*J, adjusts the active bounds and solves a reduced Gauss-Newton system with step/globalization logic. This is constrained nonlinear least squares; Robust in the project name does not establish an outlier-resistant loss function. Callers must supply consistent residuals and scalar objective, finite strictly separated bounds and the module-defined kinds. ERROR reports callback/interface failures, while INFO%TERMFLAG distinguishes iteration limit, small objective change, no reduction and small parameter change; ERROR=0 alone does not certify convergence. Some input/storage errors use STOP or console interaction rather than a clean status return. Review covers the native bounded iteration and concrete Rosenbrock callback convention, not convergence guarantees, rank-deficient behavior or a global optimum claim.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
program bounded_ls_sketch
use constantsMod, only: ik,rk
use rgnMod, only: rgn,rgnConvType,rgnInfoType,setDefaultRgnConvergeSettings
implicit none
type(rgnConvType) :: cnv
type(rgnInfoType) :: info
real(rk) :: x0(2),lo(2),hi(2),x(2)
integer(ik) :: error
character(100) :: message
x0=[-1._rk,0._rk]; lo=[-1.5_rk,-1._rk]; hi=[1.5_rk,3._rk]
call setDefaultRgnConvergeSettings(cnv)
cnv%iterMax=200_ik; cnv%dumpResults=0_ik
error=0_ik; message=""
call rgn(residual,2_ik,2_ik,x0,lo,hi,cnv,x,info,error,message)
if(error/=0_ik) error stop "RGN callback/interface failure"
print *,info%termFlag,info%f,x
contains
subroutine residual(nPar,nSim,x,r,f,timeFunc,error,message)
 integer(ik),intent(in) :: nPar,nSim
 real(rk),intent(in) :: x(:)
 real(rk),intent(out) :: r(:),f,timeFunc
 integer(ik),intent(inout) :: error
 character(100),intent(inout) :: message
 r(1)=1._rk-x(1); r(2)=10._rk*(x(2)-x(1)**2)
 f=0.5_rk*sum(r*r); timeFunc=0._rk; error=0_ik; message=""
end subroutine
end program
```

**L8c4 — source-reviewed**

The external rlRWAGm2 kernel implements the W-algorithm for robust/bounded-influence multiple-linear regression. The selected ITYPE=1, ISIGMA=0 branch performs a fixed-scale M-estimation update with residual-dependent weights, rank-revealing QR and coefficient increments. IPS=3 selects Huber psi; PSP0=1 is its derivative at zero. This scoped use does not include a high-breakdown initial fit or the complete MM regression workflow exposed by higher-level R wrappers. COV supplies the packed coefficient convergence metric and WGT is not an arbitrary precision-weight interface for all ITYPE branches. NIT is an iteration count, not a general numerical-success code; small-scale/rank exits can bypass final output assignment, so SIGMAF and coefficients need inspection. Source review covers the selected fixed-scale update and psi selector, not all scale estimators, leverage corrections or inferential covariance calculations. The full package includes R trace/error helpers.

**L5b1n — source-reviewed**

MVNPRD computes a standardized multivariate-normal rectangular probability for off-diagonal correlations rho(i,j)=BPD(i)*BPD(j), using independent-coordinate factors and one-dimensional adaptive Simpson integration of products of conditional normal probabilities. L5b1n records normal multivariate probabilities, restricted to this product-correlation family rather than arbitrary covariance matrices. N is limited to 1..50 and ABS(BPD)<1. A contains upper and B lower limits; INF=0/1/2 select lower-to-infinity, minus-infinity-to-upper and finite intervals. IERC selects derivative-based or interval-halving error control, and HINC<=0 is replaced by 0.24. IFAULT distinguishes input, integration/evaluation-limit and requested-bound failures; do not treat the header accuracy claim as a verified rigorous bound. The defining Fortran uses default REAL and the C++ wrapper converts to float, so R double inputs do not give a double-precision integration kernel. The Student-t path is excluded. No probability or error-bound test was run.

**C8a — source-reviewed**

The external ALNORM helper evaluates lower or upper standard-normal tail probabilities using symmetry and separate rational approximations, with an exponential factor in the larger-argument branch. C8a records normal-distribution/error-function evaluation, not an inverse distribution or random generator. UPPER=.TRUE. requests the right tail and .FALSE. the lower CDF. Default REAL arithmetic and hard-coded LTONE=7/UTZERO=18.66 determine clipping/complement behavior; extreme tails can become exactly zero/one and no log-tail output or status is returned. This is the bundled AS 66 approximation, not an intrinsic ERF wrapper. No tail accuracy or clipping boundary was tested.

**L4c1b — source-reviewed**

RLDS computes a nonparametric robust multivariate location/scatter estimate from projection outlyingness. RLWEIGHTS samples subsets defining projection directions, standardizes projected distances using medians and robust scale, retains maximal outlyingness and forms redescending weights. RLDONOSTAH then computes weighted location using W and scatter using W squared, normalized by their respective sums; this is not the ordinary sample covariance. The GAMS nonparametric multidimensional-data-analysis class is retained because the adopted taxonomy has no specific Stahel-Donoho leaf. Positive NRESAMP bounds requested valid random subsets and MAXRES bounds attempted subsets; NRESAMP=0 instead enumerates all subsets and is not bounded by MAXRES. NRESPER reports valid subsets, not a success or accuracy certificate. Degenerate data or vanishing weight sums need caller-side checks because the location/scatter divisions have no general error status. The routine brackets its own R RNG state and requires the package R/native helpers. Review covers the estimator paths, not breakdown guarantees, covariance calibration or exhaustive runtime complexity.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `cf03cf78676a871eedc1615a2dc4d6734e8afaf3`.

**G2d — source-reviewed**

RELAXALG builds network incidence lists and invokes the RELAX4 relaxation/auction algorithm for integer capacitated minimum-cost flow. The wrapper takes positive supplies in B1 and converts them to internal demands with B=-B1, despite a lower-level R comment calling them demands. It overwrites capacities with residual capacities, supplies with final internal deficits, flows X1 and reduced costs RC1. CRASH=1 selects auction initialization. Valid node indices, nonnegative capacities, balanced supplies and bounded integer arithmetic are caller responsibilities. The wrapper starts FEASIBLE=1 but some large-cost/capacity rejection paths return before copying that flag or output arrays, so FEASIBLE1 alone is not a universal validation status. COMMON blocks preclude concurrent independent calls. Review covers wrapper/list construction and selected price-flow/feasibility paths, not complexity bounds, sensitivity analysis or every augmentation case.

**J — source-reviewed**

The public S2HAT_ALM2MAP module wrapper synthesizes scalar or polarized real maps on supported iso-latitude spherical pixelizations from distributed complex spherical harmonic coefficients. The selected no-precomputation scalar path builds associated-Legendre recurrences, accumulates harmonic coefficients in latitude, redistributes m/ring work with MPI and performs Fourier ring synthesis through the configured FFT backend. Spherical harmonic transforms do not have a dedicated more-specific class in the adopted GAMS tree, so broad J is retained rather than claiming a plain Cartesian FFT leaf. The calling fragment is scalar NSTOKES=1, PRECOMPUTE_PLMS=0 and native LDA=LMAX storage; m ownership/ring ranges/map sizes and pointer arrays must come from the matching setup routines. Polarization/spin derivative variants, transform round-trip accuracy and quadrature conventions are not verified by this review. No numerical status is returned; a missing FFT compile flag only prints WRONG fft FLAG in the dispatcher, so backend configuration is essential. Review covers public dispatch and selected scalar Legendre/ring synthesis paths, not the full distributed analysis API.

**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

SKYSOLVE solves a symmetric skyline/profile-stored system by unpivoted LDL-transpose factorization, forward reduction and back substitution. MSKY locates each diagonal in the packed upper profile, and A/B are overwritten by factors/intermediate values/solutions. The selected full-system usage sets NEQ1=NEQ and IFLAG=3; other flags split phases, and NEQ1<NEQ supports reduction outside this selected sketch. The routine replaces zero or sufficiently small pivots and records corrections in DCOR, with IERR=-3 indicating singular/poor conditioning correction; positive IERR=3 flags negative factor diagonals. This is not an unrestricted pivoted indefinite solver, and a corrected system is not silently equivalent to the original. Initialize all DCOR entries before factorization: the preliminary loop resets only its first column while later negative-flag suppression can inspect other columns. Use positive EPS/SCALE and valid skyline bounds, compatible BLAS/default-integer ABI, full SAM dependencies and a valid log unit or LPU<0 to suppress diagnostics. Preserve originals and check IERR/NND plus an independently recomputed residual. Negative IFLAG suppression and reduced-system semantics are not certified by this source review.

Reviewed 2026-11-06 at `ed0b232ce8c31505fb2aa8555a8054e412387bbc`.

**L1a1b — source-reviewed**

Variance computes (SUM(X**2)-SUM(X)**2/N)/(N-1) over X(1:N); StdDev returns its square root. L1a1b records dispersion of univariate raw data, specifically sample variance with N-1 denominator. Require 2 <= N <= SIZE(X). The subtractive raw-moment formula can lose precision for small spread around large offsets and can yield a negative computed variance; there is no status or clamp. This review does not cover the Student-factor/confidence routines or verify distributional assumptions by execution.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

These are collective ScaLAPACK Fortran drivers, not serial LAPACK calls with larger arrays. Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. The selected real general square-system driver factors A with partial-pivoted LU, then calls the corresponding GETRS only after successful factorization. Local A stores factors, B is overwritten by the distributed solution, and local IPIV must accommodate LOCr(M_A)+MB_A entries and remain tied to A. Require block-aligned origin, square A blocks, matching A/B row block size and owning process row, and a common context. Positive INFO identifies an exactly zero U diagonal in the global submatrix, not a condition estimate or forward-error bound. The review covers driver checks and factor/solve dispatch rather than every distributed LU/communication kernel.

**D2b1b — source-reviewed**

These are collective ScaLAPACK Fortran drivers, not serial LAPACK calls with larger arrays. Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. This real symmetric positive-definite driver reads only the UPLO-selected triangle, factors it through POTRF and calls POTRS only on factorization success. A is overwritten by the selected Cholesky factor and B by X. The selected lower-triangle path requires block-aligned origins, square A blocks, compatible A/B row blocking/ownership and an initialized common grid. Positive INFO reports a nonpositive leading principal minor; no full symmetry/Hermitian validation, pivoted indefinite solve or conditioning estimate is performed here. The complex path uses conjugate-transpose Cholesky factors, not a complex-symmetric factorization. Review is of the driver and dispatch, not a numerical audit of all POTRF/POTRS kernels.

**D2a3 — source-reviewed**

These are collective ScaLAPACK Fortran drivers, not serial LAPACK calls with larger arrays. Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. PDTRTRS applies a distributed triangular solve through PDTRSM, selecting upper/lower, transpose and unit/nonunit diagonal conventions. The selected sketch uses lower, nontransposed, unit-diagonal input; diagonal entries are then implicit ones. A remains a triangular coefficient matrix and B is overwritten. Require matching block-aligned origins, square A blocks and compatible B row distribution. Important nonunit-path finding: the diagonal scan sets LL=IOFFA+LDA+1 repeatedly instead of advancing LL, so for blocks longer than two it can miss later zero diagonals. Do not rely on that scan as a complete nonsingularity check; repair it or validate diagonals independently before nonunit use. The unit-diagonal sketch bypasses the defective scan and does not establish numerical conditioning.

Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. PDGELS uses distributed QR for M>=N and LQ for M<N, applying orthogonal transformations and triangular solves for over/underdetermined systems. The selected TRANS=N, M>=N path is full-column-rank least squares. A and B are overwritten; B must have distributed global storage for MAX(M,N) rows even when the input RHS uses fewer rows. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 collectively and allocate each rank its returned local requirement. A/B need compatible row blocking/alignment/ownership for this selected tall case and a common context. Full rank is assumed: the driver uses PDTRSM without a rank-revealing step or explicit returned zero-pivot test, so INFO=0 does not certify rank, conditioning or a finite solution. Review covers driver scaling, QR/LQ and solve dispatch; no rank-deficient or minimum-norm accuracy is certified.

**D4a1 — source-reviewed**

These are collective ScaLAPACK Fortran drivers, not serial LAPACK calls with larger arrays. Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. PDSYEV computes the ordinary real-symmetric spectrum, optionally vectors, by distributed tridiagonal reduction followed by DSTEQR2 and back transformation. The selected JOBZ=V, UPLO=L path uses positive N, separate distributed Z with DESCZ=DESCA and all matrix origins (1,1); A is destroyed, W(N) is replicated and sorted ascending, and Z holds distributed eigenvector columns. Query local WORK collectively with LWORK=-1 before allocating it. The driver assumes homogeneous arithmetic and makes only limited interprocess eigenvalue comparisons; INFO=N+1 flags a detected mismatch, not a complete heterogeneity test. Positive INFO<=N reports tridiagonal nonconvergence. Review covers the driver and dispatch, not residual/orthogonality checks or all eigensolver kernels; arbitrary unequal A/Z offsets are outside the selected contract.

**D4a3 — source-reviewed**

These are collective ScaLAPACK Fortran drivers, not serial LAPACK calls with larger arrays. Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. PZHEEV handles the ordinary complex-Hermitian problem through PZHETRD, ZSTEQR2 and a unitary back transformation. Although the purpose header says selected eigenvalues, the interface has no index/value selection arguments and this inspected path produces the full spectrum. The selected positive-N JOBZ=V, UPLO=L path uses matching A/Z descriptors at origin (1,1). A is destroyed, W(N) is real and replicated, and Z contains distributed complex eigenvectors. It needs separate COMPLEX*16 WORK and DOUBLE PRECISION RWORK; query both with lengths -1, check INFO and allocate from the complex workspace real part and real workspace query. Homogeneous arithmetic is assumed; limited comparisons can report INFO=N+1, and positive INFO<=N denotes eigensolver nonconvergence. This review does not certify arbitrary offsets, heterogeneous grids or all tridiagonal/unitary kernels.

**D6 — source-reviewed**

These are collective ScaLAPACK Fortran drivers, not serial LAPACK calls with larger arrays. Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. PDGESVD reduces a distributed real rectangular matrix to bidiagonal form, calls DBDSQR and optionally back-transforms thin left/right singular vectors. JOBU/JOBVT accept V or N rather than serial DGESVD A/S conventions. A is destroyed; S(MIN(M,N)) is replicated in decreasing order, U has global shape (M,MIN(M,N)) and VT has (MIN(M,N),N), containing rows of V-transpose rather than columns of V. The selected sketch uses positive dimensions, matching block layouts and origins (1,1) for all arrays. Query local WORK collectively; even the query creates and releases temporary BLACS grids. Positive INFO can report bidiagonal nonconvergence or MIN(M,N)+1 for detected interprocess singular-value mismatch, so interpret the final status and check reconstruction/orthogonality independently. A further status-propagation limit is visible: DBDSQR failure is not checked before the optional back-transform calls reuse INFO, so a later successful call can overwrite that earlier failure status. Review covers driver workspace, reduction and dispatch, not every distributed/kernel path or arbitrary submatrix offset.

**D2a2 — source-reviewed**

PDGBSV is a distributed real general-banded solver using pivoted divide-and-conquer factorization through PDGBTRF and solve through PDGBTRS. Unlike the selected 2-D dense drivers, use its documented blocked one-dimensional matrix layout: A descriptor type 501 and B type 502 (or compatible documented type-1 descriptors). Initialize MPI/BLACS and compatible scalar/integer ABI; packed A needs LLD_A>=2*BWL+2*BWU+1, B needs its NB-based local row capacity, and IPIV at least NB entries. Require JA=IB and the noncyclic constraint P*NB>=MOD(JA-1,NB)+N; if spanning ranks, NB>=BWL+BWU+1. A factors differ from serial LAPACK band factors because of reordering; A/B are overwritten and pivot/work storage must follow this interface. Allocate the full documented WORK formula before entry: the driver forms WORK(1+WS_FACTOR) before lower-level calls and has no top-level LWORK=-1 query path. Positive INFO identifies a singular local/reduced partition, not necessarily the global diagonal-pivot convention used by GESV. Review covers driver layout, workspace slicing and factor/solve dispatch, not every banded kernel, arbitrary grid layout or condition estimate.

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed binding converts a C function pointer to a module callback adapter and forwards arrays/controls to the bundled modern QUADPACK implementation. Integrands return C_DOUBLE and accept x by value plus an args-array pointer. Workspaces, callback/args lifetimes, compatible C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real ABI and valid tolerances remain caller responsibilities. The implementation saves/restores callback slots around the call; OpenMP threadprivate directives only provide separate thread state when compiled with OpenMP. **F2 — source-reviewed**

HYBRD_WRAPPER exposes a MINPACK local nonlinear-system solve without user Jacobian entries, using a finite-difference Powell-hybrid driver and an explicitly supplied C callback address. It constructs the simplified driver workspace/scaling/control defaults while allowing MAXFEV to be passed through, then maps backend INFO=5 to 4. The callback fills N residuals from N parameters; dimensions are not passed in that callback ABI and must be known by its implementation. INFO=1 is a step-tolerance termination, not independent proof that all residuals are small; other codes need MINPACK interpretation. The module stores callback/args pointers, uses optional OpenMP threadprivate state and does not save/restore that state in this particular root wrapper, unlike the reviewed quadrature bindings. Nested calls on the same thread can overwrite context, and parallel calls without the appropriate OpenMP build share it. Review covers the wrapper and adapter, not every native MINPACK algorithm path or a global root guarantee.

**H2a2a1 — source-reviewed**

Review covers the named C binding, declarations, callback adaptation and native dispatch, not an independent verification of every bundled solver kernel. Match C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real kinds in the complete library build. All non-VALUE scalar arguments are passed by reference. Special finite-interval adaptive quadrature is exposed by DQAGP (caller-supplied interior breakpoints), DQAWO (cosine/sine weight), DQAWS (endpoint algebraic/logarithmic weights) and DQAWC (Cauchy principal value). DQAGP requires NPTS2=number of interior points+2, enough POINTS storage and valid LENIW/LENW. DQAWO requires LENIW>=2, MAXP1>=1 and LENW>=2*LENIW+25*MAXP1; INTEGR=1/2 selects cosine/sine. Its local native driver adds MOMCOM output, so link the matching vendored version. DQAWS requires ALFA,BETA>-1, INTEGR=1..4 selecting no log/left log/right log/both, LIMIT>=2 and LENW>=4*LIMIT. DQAWC integrates f(x)/(x-C), with C distinct from endpoints, LIMIT>=1 and LENW>=4*LIMIT. Supply f rather than multiplying the weight into the callback. IER/ABSERR remain diagnostics, not proof of convergence or a rigorous bound. This mapping does not imply generic singularities can be handled without compatible controls.

**K1b1a2 — source-reviewed**

Review covers the named C binding, declarations, callback adaptation and native dispatch, not an independent verification of every bundled solver kernel. Match C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real kinds in the complete library build. All non-VALUE scalar arguments are passed by reference. Callback dimensions are known by the callback rather than passed in its ABI. Module callback/args pointers are overwritten without save/restore; avoid nested calls through this interface. OpenMP threadprivate state is conditional on the build. The callback abstract interfaces here are not declared BIND(C); use the actual supported compiler/foreign-function ABI rather than assuming full standard interoperability from the exported wrapper alone. LMDER1_WRAPPER forwards residual and full user-Jacobian evaluation to LMDER1; LMSTR1_WRAPPER uses the row-wise Jacobian variant LMSTR1. In the full variant require LDFJAC>=M, FJAC(LDFJAC,N), IPVT(N) and LWA>=5*N+M. For the row variant require LDFJAC>=N (the returned factor is N by N), IPVT(N) and the same workspace lower bound. Both require M>=N>0. The callback receives X,FVEC,FJAC-or-row,IFLAG,ARGS, with IFLAG by reference but declared INTENT(IN); do not promise callback-requested early termination through that interface. LMDER uses IFLAG=1 for residuals, 2 for the full Jacobian; LMSTR uses IFLAG=1 for residuals and IFLAG>=2 for row IFLAG-1. Derivatives are of the residual vector, not the scalar squared norm. INFO and residual diagnostics must be checked; the factor returned in FJAC is not an untouched Jacobian or covariance matrix.

**D1a3b — source-reviewed**

Review covers the named C binding, declarations, callback adaptation and native dispatch, not an independent verification of every bundled solver kernel. Match C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real kinds in the complete library build. All non-VALUE scalar arguments are passed by reference. ENORM_WRAPPER returns the real Euclidean norm through an output argument. The inspected native ENORM splits small, intermediate and large magnitudes and uses scaled sums for extreme components, avoiding the naive unscaled sum-of-squares path for those ranges. N must be positive (the code divides by N); supply finite input. This is not an arbitrary-precision norm, a complex norm or a guarantee about NaN/infinity behavior.

**I1a1b — source-reviewed**

Review covers the named C binding, declarations, callback adaptation and native dispatch, not an independent verification of every bundled solver kernel. Match C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real kinds in the complete library build. All non-VALUE scalar arguments are passed by reference. The public LSODA/LSODAR bindings forward to the separately bundled state-object ODEPACK edition, with internal dense finite-difference Jacobian selection JT=2. Their C callbacks take T by VALUE and Y/derivative-or-event/ARGS by reference. Callback slots are saved/restored and per-thread only when OpenMP directives are active; solver COMMON replacement is a local derived object. This is inspection of interface/state handling and dispatch, not independent verification of the entire ODEPACK integration/event algorithm or thread reentrancy. The nonstiff branch is a variable-order Adams multistep method, not a Runge-Kutta method. LSODA initializes at T_EVAL(1), copies U0 to the first output column, and continues through later requested times. Require NEQ>0, NTIME>=2, monotone times and valid nonzero error weights from scalar RTOL/ATOL; MXSTEP controls each solver call. A negative ISTATE exits early, leaving later output columns unassigned. LSODAR instead returns at TOUT or a detected event; ISTATE=3 and JROOT distinguish a root from ordinary completion. Zero crossings/touching or closely spaced events need independent assessment. No direction-filter option is present in this particular event wrapper.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

Review covers the named C binding, declarations, callback adaptation and native dispatch, not an independent verification of every bundled solver kernel. Match C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real kinds in the complete library build. All non-VALUE scalar arguments are passed by reference. FITPACK stores knots and B-spline coefficients, not raw samples alone. Its wrapper does not infer array sizes, degrees, knot validity or workspace. The selected bundled sources are REAL*8/default INTEGER; preserve the matching C-sized ABI. CURFIT with IOPT=0 and S=0 constructs a univariate polynomial interpolating spline; SPLEV evaluates the representation. Require M>K, strictly increasing X, positive W, 1<=K<=5, bounds containing data, NEST>=M+K+1 for interpolation, LWRK>=M*(K+1)+NEST*(7+3*K), IWRK(NEST). The local fitter adds TOL and MAXIT trailing arguments, so historical unmodified interfaces are not interchangeable. Nonpositive CURFIT IER values can be normal returns; inspect FP/knots and preserve continuation work arrays if selecting IOPT=1. SPLEV E=0/1/2/3 controls extrapolation/zero/error/boundary value; E=2 can return after partial output. No claim of interpolation accuracy or suitability for noisy data is inferred from successful dispatch.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

Review covers the named C binding, declarations, callback adaptation and native dispatch, not an independent verification of every bundled solver kernel. Match C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real kinds in the complete library build. All non-VALUE scalar arguments are passed by reference. FITPACK stores knots and B-spline coefficients, not raw samples alone. Its wrapper does not infer array sizes, degrees, knot validity or workspace. The selected bundled sources are REAL*8/default INTEGER; preserve the matching C-sized ABI. SPLDER constructs differentiated B-spline coefficients in working storage and evaluates the selected derivative order NU. This is differentiation of an existing fitted spline, not arbitrary black-box finite differences, automatic differentiation or direct derivatives of unmodeled raw data. Require 0<=NU<=K, valid knots/coefficients, M>=1 and WRK(N); E controls the out-of-domain policy. Spline approximation error remains distinct from floating-point evaluation error; differentiation can amplify data/model error.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

Review covers the named C binding, declarations, callback adaptation and native dispatch, not an independent verification of every bundled solver kernel. Match C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real kinds in the complete library build. All non-VALUE scalar arguments are passed by reference. FITPACK stores knots and B-spline coefficients, not raw samples alone. Its wrapper does not infer array sizes, degrees, knot validity or workspace. The selected bundled sources are REAL*8/default INTEGER; preserve the matching C-sized ABI. REGRID with S=0 constructs a tensor-product spline interpolating rectangular-grid data; BISPEV evaluates such a representation. X/Y must be strictly increasing, MX>KX and MY>KY, degrees 1..5; interpolation storage requires NXEST>=MX+KX+1 and NYEST>=MY+KY+1. Input Z uses Z(MY*(I-1)+J), not an assumed Fortran Z(MX,MY) flattening. The modified fitter adds TOL/MAXIT. Its explicit workspace expressions and status are linked in implementation evidence. BISPEV requires sorted query axes, LWRK>=(KX+1)*MX+(KY+1)*MY and KWRK>=MX+MY, and returns flattened grid values. These are gridded tensor-product operations, not scattered-data triangulation or a general curved-domain interpolator.

Review covers the named C binding, declarations, callback adaptation and native dispatch, not an independent verification of every bundled solver kernel. Match C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real kinds in the complete library build. All non-VALUE scalar arguments are passed by reference. FITPACK stores knots and B-spline coefficients, not raw samples alone. Its wrapper does not infer array sizes, degrees, knot validity or workspace. DBLINT integrates a supplied bivariate tensor-product spline over a rectangle by forming products of one-dimensional integrated basis functions and contracting with the flattened coefficient array. H2b1 is retained at the rectangular-region level because the finer callback-versus-grid branches do not describe its coefficient representation precisely. WRK requires NX+NY-KX-KY-2 entries. **G2i — source-reviewed**

DIRECT normalizes finite box bounds, samples rectangle centers, chooses potentially optimal rectangles and divides their longest sides into thirds. ALGMETHOD selects the original or modified selection strategy. The inspected serial evaluation path rescales coordinates before invoking FCN(N,X,F,FLAG,IIDATA,IISIZE,DDATA,IDSIZE,CDATA,ICSIZE); FLAG=0 marks a defined objective and positive values mark hidden infeasibility. No derivative or explicit Lipschitz constant is required. Global search is an algorithmic scope, not a finite-budget certificate of the global optimum. Positive IERROR values include evaluation/iteration budget and rectangle size terminations. Fixed capacities include MaxDim=64 and Maxfunc=90000; MAXF is not necessarily a strict evaluation ceiling, especially while searching for a feasible point. The COMMON control state and fixed work storage require care for simultaneous calls. This review covers driver, selection and serial callback dispatch, not every rectangle bookkeeping routine.

**G1b2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected executable minimizes a finite maximum of component functions, a generally nonsmooth multivariate objective. functmu builds a log-sum-exp smoothing from value-only functs callbacks, and MAINBOX performs derivative-free line searches while adapting the smoothing parameter. This supports the G1b2 leaf. Despite the linearly constrained minimax paper cited in the header, the inspected interface exposes neither bounds nor a general linear-constraint callback or matrix; no G2h2 claim is inferred from the citation. Exponent clipping and a small-sum floor are implementation safeguards, not a checked stable log-sum-exp algorithm for every magnitude. The supplied Hald-Madsen rational-approximation problem can encounter denominator issues; its reported optimum was not reproduced. No convergence, minimax accuracy or example execution was checked.

**D1b6 — source-reviewed**

The selected utilclc routines compute a column Gram product S-transpose*S and its weighted analogue S-transpose*diag(w**2)*S using DOT_PRODUCT. Despite the names mkcov/mkcovweight, the routines neither subtract means nor divide by a sample-count denominator: raw input is not automatically converted to statistical covariance. Weights are applied to BOTH vectors and hence squared, not used once. Shapes are partly checked through printerror2; callers should supply full ncols-by-ncols outputs and matching row weights. Precision is the preprocessed SESAM BIGREAL/kr setting, with repository module/configuration and error-hook dependencies. This maps elementary matrix multiplication, not the full data-assimilation system or an automatic covariance estimator.

**E2b — source-reviewed**

QSHEP2 selects neighboring planar data, sets compact radii, forms local quadratic weighted least-squares models with Givens QR, enlarges neighborhoods/damps quadratic terms for conditioning, and returns cell-search/model data. QS2VAL blends those nodal polynomials by compact Shepard weights and returns exact nodal F on coincidence. E2b records bivariate scattered interpolation, not gridded-only or arbitrary-dimensional interpolation. N>=6, 5<=NQ<=MIN(40,N-1), 1<=NW<=MIN(40,N-1) and NR>=1 are required. Setup IER diagnoses ranges, duplicate nodes and degeneracy. QS2VAL returns zero both for some invalid input and for points outside all supports; use QS2GRD for a status-bearing evaluation. This review covers setup/evaluation control, not a complete audit of neighbor/rotation kernels or robustness in all geometries. No interpolant or author test was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `1aead0f26ca367514a658c6c509aa5bd33c0dfc6`.

**E3a2 — source-reviewed**

QS2GRD differentiates the compact Shepard quotient using nodal quadratic derivatives and derivatives of the weights. At a supplied node it returns F and the local linear coefficients A(4:5). E3a2 records derivatives of the fitted bivariate interpolant, not derivatives of an arbitrary callback or an automatic-differentiation service. Requires successful QSHEP2 data. IER=0 denotes supported evaluation, 1 invalid geometry and 2 no supporting node; the no-support path sets Q/QX/QY to zero while invalid-geometry early returns leave them unassigned. This is a source review of the derivative evaluator and status semantics, not a finite-difference/accuracy verification.

**D — documentation-reviewed**

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `0ba978e78727cb4c70e17d50153b09b4839d5c0a`.

[src/finterface_mod.f90](https://github.com/TREX-CoE/Sherman-Morrison/blob/0ba978e78727cb4c70e17d50153b09b4839d5c0a/src/finterface_mod.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `178b32a9b93faae4cd96cac2d2d89e85bb388b7d49d611745826c10b8b18489a`.

**D2e — source-reviewed**

The selected SM1 implementation updates an existing dense inverse after additive column updates A <- A + u*e_j^T, applying the Sherman-Morrison outer-product correction with denominator 1+(A^-1*u)(j). Updates_index is one-based, while C++ matrix storage is row-major. SM1_f is the exported pointer-to-pointer C wrapper. The checked-in Fortran SM1 declaration omits the required by-value BREAKDOWN argument and uses allocatable assumed-shape BIND(C) arrays, whose descriptor ABI is incompatible with these raw pointer-to-pointer parameters. The sketch therefore declares a separate C binding using C_PTR arguments, rather than calling that defective module interface. SM1 only logs a small denominator inside DEBUG1 and still divides by it; BREAKDOWN is not a protective error return. There is no status result or rollback. Review covers the naive update and C wrapper, not Maponi, recursive splitting, Woodbury variants or the independent determinant-scaled IRPF90 kernels.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `0ba978e78727cb4c70e17d50153b09b4839d5c0a`.

**C9 — source-reviewed**

The external C-binding POLYNOMIAL routine evaluates normalized real Legendre polynomials at colatitudes Y using a three-term recurrence. Its zeroth polynomial is 1/sqrt(2), so this is not the unnormalized P_l(cos(theta)) convention. UP advances degree with normalization factors; L_TARGET must be nonnegative and JX positive. The function accepts an array of angles, not arbitrary complex arguments or an associated order. The separate associated-function source supplies normalized recurrences for transform work but is not substituted for this public evaluation interface. Review covers the polynomial recurrence and output initialization, not high-degree stability, orthogonality or a quadrature error guarantee.

**J — source-reviewed**

The associated-function FORWARD/BACKWARD C-binding entries perform discrete associated-Legendre analysis/synthesis of longitude-Fourier coefficient columns. FORWARD applies sin(theta)*delta-theta weights on uniformly spaced colatitudes and accumulates normalized recurrence products; BACKWARD reconstructs from triangular degree/order coefficients. This is the Legendre integral-transform stage, not the Python FFT longitude stage or an exact Gauss-Legendre quadrature. N selects the order spacing via MOD(m,N); require N>=1, even positive KX and enough latitude points per OpenMP partition. INIT_GEOMETRY reads local Y(1), so fewer than two points in a thread partition is unsafe. Both this file and legendre_polynomial.f90 define C symbols FORWARD/BACKWARD, so link/load them separately as in the project rather than combining both implementations into one library. Review covers transform interfaces, recurrences and accumulation, not inversion accuracy or parallel scaling.

**L10a1d — source-reviewed**

The signal module exposes cosine-power and Kaiser taper generators and APPLY_WINDOW for interleaved real/imaginary sequence storage. The selected sketch uses the integer-order cosine window, whose code samples a periodic endpoint-excluded grid and multiplies by 2**ORDER*(ORDER!)**2/(2*ORDER)!; it does not normalize each sampled array to unit sum. APPLY_WINDOW multiplies the same real weights into both components. Positive LENGTH, small nonnegative integer ORDER and finite inputs are caller requirements; high orders can overflow intermediate factors. Generic fractional-order and Kaiser branches depend on GSL gamma/Bessel interfaces and were not audited as equivalent parameter conventions. This mapping is data tapering, not a spectrum estimate or a review of all decomposition/FFTW/ARPACK paths.

**L10a3a — source-reviewed**

The complex esprit_c path builds an uncentered delayed-sample Gram matrix, obtains its left singular subspace, solves normal equations for the shifted-subspace operator through LU/inversion, and estimates tone frequencies from eigenvalue angles. L10a3a records parametric spectral/frequency estimation, not a periodogram or the advertised but unreviewed RootMUSIC interface. Output folds frequency signs with ABS and does not sort tones. Source findings need repair: IPIV is declared COMPLEX rather than INTEGER for ZGETRF/ZGETRI, sigma(L) is assigned S(:L/2,1) with an incompatible extent, and the covariance builder omits a sliding window/divides by N. Error paths use ERROR STOP rather than returned status. No frequency, subspace or accuracy test was run.

**L10a2a1 — source-reviewed**

autocov_c builds outer products of reversed delayed complex sample windows with conjugate transpose and scales their sum by N. L10a2a1 records a lagged autocovariance-like matrix service, scoped to zero-mean input: no sample mean is removed. For N>M the loop uses N-M windows rather than all N-M+1 available windows and divides by N rather than its window count; this normalization/window convention is recorded rather than silently described as an unbiased estimate. N>=M>=1 and compatible storage are caller obligations. No covariance, PSD, normalization or sampling-distribution check was run.

**H2b2a1 — source-reviewed**

CADAPTRI adaptively integrates a complex-valued callback over a planar triangle. It compares a parent integral against the sum over four midpoint subtriangles, accepts the parent when the absolute difference is below EPS, otherwise recursively processes children through an explicit stack. The one-triangle kernel maps a hardcoded 82-node rule by an affine transformation and absolute Jacobian determinant. Header claims of a 60-point rule and approximately 30 digits are not accepted as precision evidence; the implementation uses double precision. EPS is a local parent/children comparison, not an apportioned bound on accumulated global error. NQUAD adds 79 per accepted parent and is inconsistent with the 82-node kernel and refinement evaluations, so it is not an actual function-evaluation counter. IER=4/16 report stack/depth exhaustion and partial VAL must not be treated as a complete integral. The source file begins with a debugging main; extract the documented library section to avoid duplicate main programs. Review covers this planar adaptive kernel, not the full singular surface-operator solver.

**G2h3b — source-reviewed**

sksolve relaxes nonlinear inequalities g(x)<=gamma, restores feasibility and reduces gamma while searching within variable bounds. Equalities require an appropriate inequality encoding; the inspected public interface has no separate equality count or equality flag. The pinned source selects SK_RESTTYPE=2, a function-value compass restoration; the ALGENCAN branch returns with instructions to uncomment code, so it is not active merely by changing that selector. Compass and SDS improvement paths are active; Nelder-Mead, BOBYQA and DFO branches return before commented implementations. G2h3b is the supported nonlinear-constraint scope. A smooth or fully general nonsmooth leaf is withheld because the reviewed material does not establish a matching regularity contract for all active paths; derivative-free alone does not imply nonsmooth convergence. The toy file describes HS6 as an equality but exposes one signed constraint value, so its encoding must be checked before reuse as an equality driver. No program was run.

Public module subroutine for constrained minimization with relaxed constraints. x is an in-place REAL(8) point, l/u are bounds and m is the constraint count. CALL sksolve(n, x, l, u, m, feas, opti, gammadec, reffort, delta, &
```fortran
             sfactor, verbose, uoptmtype, f, maxinfeas, fcnt, gcnt, flag)
```

**E1a — source-reviewed**

DLININT1 evaluates piecewise-linear interpolation on strictly monotone coordinates, with exact sentinel handling and optional removal of missing input values. The selected sketch uses ascending coordinates, ICYCX=0 and IOPT=0: no extrapolation is performed; out-of-range outputs and intervals touching missing data stay XMSG. Provide NXI>=2, NXO>=1 and separate work arrays, conservatively NXI2>=NXI+2; supported IOPT values are 0/1, with no rejection of other values. Independently validate coordinates and retained sample count: missing-value filtering can leave fewer than two nodes while the interpolation kernel accesses a pair. Single output coordinates are treated as ascending by the validator, so decreasing inputs with a single query can be rejected. DLINMSG separately fills interior missing runs on equally spaced sample indices in place. Its length threshold applies to interior and leading gaps, but the trailing MFLAG<0 continuation branch ignores MPTCRT. All-missing input remains missing. Missing values use exact sentinel equality, not NaN semantics. Cyclic extension and the internal short-gap optimization are outside the selected calling paths.

Reviewed 2026-11-06 at `a4eb5af00965b26e234c8bc25a565f7314a7b650`.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

DLININT2 performs separable linear interpolation on a rectilinear two-dimensional grid: X interpolation of each input row followed by Y interpolation of the intermediate field. FI is dimensioned (NXI,NYI), FO (NXO,NYO). Require at least two nodes on each input axis, nonempty output axes, strictly monotone coordinates with matching input/output direction, finite exact missing sentinel, and supported IOPT=0/1. The reviewed calling path uses ascending complete data, ICYCX=0, IOPT=0 and separate NXI+2 work arrays. IER=1 reports dimensions, 2 X-coordinate validation and 3 Y validation. Outputs outside the coordinate ranges or lacking valid bracketing values remain missing. Filtering IOPT=1 can leave fewer than two valid nodes and must be guarded by the caller; it is not a scattered-data method, conservative remapper or missing-data extrapolator. The same direction flag is reused after both coordinate checks and passed into both interpolation stages: use axes with the same direction, as in the sketch; independently increasing X and decreasing Y is not safely supported by that implementation.

**L10a1c2 — source-reviewed**

COMPUTE_LANCZOS_WEIGHTS constructs an odd-length symmetric windowed-sinc FIR filter. PASS_TYPE=1 normalizes low-pass weights to unit sum; 2 forms the high-pass delta complement. CUTOFF_FREQ is in cycles per sample and must lie strictly between 0 and 0.5; NWT must be odd and >=3. IERR=1/2/3/4/5 reports short/even window, invalid cutoff, near-zero normalization or unsupported pass type; do not apply weights after failure. APPLY_FILTER_1D reflects indices once at each boundary, requiring N>1 and half-window <=N-1; larger windows can access outside DATA. APPLY_FILTER_1D_PERIODIC wraps with MODULO and requires N>0. Use separate input/output arrays, generated symmetric weights and finite complete data: there is no missing/NaN policy or application status. The routines use REAL(8), which must be matched to the compiler build, rather than a portable named kind. This classification covers symmetric linear filtering, not a spectral estimator or certified frequency-response design.

**L4a1d — source-reviewed**

COMPUTE_S_VALUE sums pairwise signs in a clean ordered scalar series to obtain the Mann-Kendall S statistic. COMPUTE_BASE_VARIANCE copies and sorts the series, then computes the conventional independent-observation variance with equal-value tie correction. Both are public components of sequence analysis: these two entries do not return a p-value, significance decision, continuity-corrected Z or serial-correlation correction, and they do not establish general stationarity. Require finite, missing-free REAL64 data and a distinct sorted workspace with at least SIZE(Y) entries. Exact equality defines ties. S accumulation is quadratic in sample count; no missing filtering or time-coordinate vector is provided at these entry points. Preserve the original time ordering for S; sorting is only on the separate variance workspace.

**L8a3 — source-reviewed**

COMPUTE_SEN_SLOPE returns the median of all pairwise slopes (Y(j)-Y(i))/(j-i), a robust simple trend-slope estimate for unit-spaced observations. It constructs reciprocal index lags and dispatches to the public precomputed-lag variant, which materializes N*(N-1)/2 slopes and uses selection rather than a full sort; even counts average the two middle values. Require clean finite REAL64 data, a separate slope workspace of that size, and sample counts whose integer products/indices fit the compiler integer kind. N<2 returns quiet NaN. This is a slope per sample interval, not a full regression result: no intercept, confidence interval, p-value, time-coordinate array or missing-value removal is returned. Removing gaps before calling changes the time spacing and therefore the problem. Memory and pair construction are quadratic; no large-series performance claim was executed.

**C8c — source-reviewed**

Piecewise Chebyshev expansions and large-argument asymptotics implement the real Dawson integral. The routine returns zero beyond its large representable-argument threshold and has no user tolerance or recoverable status output. This is the modernized special_functions module implementation with service-module DP kinds and include files, not a numerical revalidation of the original SLATEC release. Invalid domains use ERROR STOP in the checked beta/gamma branches rather than a recoverable INFO argument. Review covers the selected function and visible dispatch; no complete dependency, rounding-error or cross-compiler audit was performed.

This is the unregularized lower integral from zero to X, not the regularized P(a,x) or upper complement. A must be positive and X nonnegative. Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `bc6621dea5be45fd1caa9822064be2c49e131213`.

[README.md](https://github.com/ericlindsey/slice/blob/bc6621dea5be45fd1caa9822064be2c49e131213/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `088c8224c7d4bf39e0a47258b8711eee4f0524ed967a8934f87cbe939f6f461e`.

**L6b — source-reviewed**

SLICE_WALKS generates bounded multivariate samples by coordinate-wise slice updates, drawing an exponential height above a negative log density, stepping out within parameter bounds and shrinking rejected intervals. The forward model is linked through FWD_MOD rather than a procedure dummy; the supplied FORWARD computes a weighted Gaussian line-fit negative log likelihood. Parameters, model data and RNG are shared module state and must be initialized. Independent walks start from random bounded points, with NBURN sweeps discarded. Samples are correlated and neither burn-in nor returned rows establish equilibrium or effective sample size; separated modes can mix poorly. The output assignment REAL(POINT(J)) rounds to default real before storing in kind=8 arrays. Use positive WIDTH, nonempty dimensions/counts and valid ordered bounds; the rejection loops have no explicit evaluation cap. The inspected source is serial, without an MPI convergence or statistical validation claim.

The SIDENT MATLAB-facing Fortran MEX gateway obtains a discrete-time multivariable state-space realization from a preprocessed block-Hankel R factor and a chosen model order. It translates MOESP/N4SID/combined method and job selectors, allocates workspaces and dispatches the external SLICOT IB01BD implementation. Optional sample-count inputs enable covariance/Kalman-gain output paths. This is multivariate time-series system identification, not direct identification from arbitrary raw data passed as R or a Kalman filtering run. The chosen order, input/output counts, preprocessing method and factor layout must match; requested output ordering depends on the job. Review covers gateway declarations/validation/dispatch/status and supplied MATLAB usage, not an audit of the separately linked numerical solver. MATLAB MEX pointer/integer ABI and the complete SLICOT/BLAS/LAPACK build must match; this gateway is not a direct Fortran numerical CALL interface.

**L15 — source-reviewed**

The external SURVWEIB entry fits a parametric Weibull proportional-hazards survival model by maximizing a likelihood with exact/right/interval-censored observations and optional left truncation. The likelihood contains exp(X*beta), Weibull baseline cumulative hazard and the selected censoring/truncation contributions; the baseline parameters are squared internally to keep them nonnegative. The baseline formula is S(t)=exp(-(b2*t)**b1), so B2 is an inverse-scale/rate rather than the usual direct Weibull scale. A baseline-only optimization precedes the covariate fit. For P>0, CONVERGED(1:2)=1 denotes success of both optimizer stages; zero is not the success convention. EPS holds integer accuracy exponents. Confidence-band arrays should only be used if requested and successfully computed. Saved module work arrays and unconditional R RNG enter/exit calls mean this is R-hosted shared-state code even with bands disabled. The interval branch subtracts survival terms and invalid likelihoods use a sentinel, so tail cancellation and invalid data need independent validation. Review covers the parametric likelihood/driver, not the separate spline model, confidence-band coverage or arbitrary survival workflows.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `a4179bf4656e4b17b72c6b6d3dfef49065ccc662`.

**M — documentation-reviewed**

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

The inspected module constructs 31 direction numbers from user-supplied primitive-polynomial parameters, updates a coordinate by Gray-code XOR and lowest-zero-bit position, and supports direct-index Gray-code skip-ahead. L6a21 is used for uniform-sequence generation, explicitly a deterministic low-discrepancy Sobol coordinate rather than independent pseudorandom draws. Users supply a state/direction set per coordinate; no multidimensional direction-number database is bundled in this API. Results use default REAL, so the 31-bit integer construction does not guarantee 31 bits of output precision and rounding may reach 1. Exhaustion, polynomial/seed validity and index bounds are not checked. Strided generation is outside the reviewed usage path. No sequence or discrepancy test was executed.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The public AKIMA_1D generic selects a vector path which extends data by two synthetic samples at each end, computes local Akima slopes and evaluates cubic Hermite polynomials between increasing source abscissae. Require matching array sizes, at least three distinct ordered valid source points and finite values; extension construction reads a third point. REAL(8) source/query arguments feed REAL(4) extended arrays, slopes and output. Without persistence flags, unlocated/out-of-range queries retain -6666.0. The optional missing sentinel is designed for contiguous missing boundaries, not arbitrary internal gaps; its boundary-index logic should be independently checked before use. L_SURF_PERSIST and L_BOTM_PERSIST are copied into initialized local logical variables that have implicit SAVE; omitting them after another call can retain previous settings. Set both explicitly to obtain predictable call behavior. Size mismatches STOP and no recoverable solver status is returned. The separate 3-D overload is not covered here.

Implementation helper `source extension, slope dispatch and cubic evaluation`: [src/mod_akima_1d.f90:90–220](https://github.com/brodeau/sosie/blob/f59113007c8d546249936d3b06cd7d70b248028d/src/mod_akima_1d.f90#L90-L220).

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The public AKIMA_2D routine constructs local bicubic interpolants on a regular source grid using Akima first/mixed slopes, analytically assembled 16-coefficient polynomials and a cached source-cell mapping for targets. Source coordinates must be regular and distinct; target coordinates may be irregular without turning the source into scattered data. REAL(8) coordinates and internal polynomial arithmetic accompany REAL(4) fields/output. K_EW_PER controls nonperiodic (-1) or overlapping east-west periodic boundaries. The routine depends on MOD_CONF initialization (including I_ORCA_SRC and L_FIRST_CALL_INTERP_ROUTINE), MOD_MANIP boundary extensions and IO_EZCDF shape helpers; it is not self-contained. Saved IXY_POS assumes the same grid across calls. ICALL=1 sets a saved always-first-call mode, rebuilding/deallocating the map thereafter; it is not a temporary per-call switch. Targets outside the extended source range return zero, not a missing sentinel. No conservative-remapping, positivity or overshoot guarantee is supplied.

**P — source-reviewed**

FIND_NEAREST_POINT maps each longitude/latitude target to source grid indices, with optional in/out target mask and dispatch by source regularity. The inspected regular-source FIND_NEAREST_EASY path estimates axis indices, scans a bounded +/-4-index neighborhood and minimizes the native spherical-distance calculation there. It is a grid-oriented nearest-point search, not an arbitrary-dimensional kd-tree or a certified global nearest neighbor for every folded or discontinuous longitude representation. Source extents must each be at least three because the regular path reads Xsrc(:,3) and Ysrc(3,:); use compatible finite degree-valued grids with overlapping latitude range and sensible target dimensions. Unprocessed points get -1 indices; inspect them before indexing fields. DISTANCE_2D uses a spherical radius from averaged Earth radii and clamps the acos dot product only above +1, not below -1. Dispatch/shape failures may STOP, the mask can change, and diagnostic output is printed. The alternate twisted-grid algorithm is outside this review.

**K5 — source-reviewed**

LOWESD initializes the packed LOESS workspace and LOWESF evaluates direct local polynomial fits through nearest-neighbor selection, distance weights, a local design matrix and QR/SVD-based least-squares work. XTDIST=1 selects Euclidean distances; XTDIST=0 selects the modified great-circle distance calculation with its assumed angular convention. The sketch restricts itself to Euclidean fits, finite data, positive span, valid degree 0..2 and initialized workspace. LOWESD version must be 106; IV/WV layout and per-coordinate degree controls must match the C workspace setup. LOWESF is an evaluation pass using supplied observation weights, not by itself the complete robust-reweighting workflow. Diagnostics call C/R EHG182/printing support rather than returning a general INFO dummy. Review covers setup/direct-fit dispatch and selected local weighting/design/solve paths, not the optional spatial distance model or validated smoothness/fit accuracy.

**L1a1a — source-reviewed**

ROWMEANS traverses compressed sparse rows and accumulates their stored values into the caller output. FLAG=1 divides by the number of stored entries in a nonempty row; other flags divide by NCL, including implicit zeros. RS MUST be initialized to zero by the caller. Stored explicit zeros count in the FLAG=1 denominator. Empty stored-only rows leave their initialized result unchanged; no size, column-count or pointer validation is performed. This is sparse-row arithmetic means, not covariance, missing-data handling or a numerically compensated reduction.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `93594ff359ffd4fd1caad6d55093e3ae3bf6be09`.

**D1b9 — source-reviewed**

CSRMSR converts a square 1-based CSR matrix to modified sparse-row storage with the diagonal in AO(1:N), AO(N+1) unused, and off-diagonal row pointers and columns sharing JAO. Missing diagonals become zero; duplicate diagonal entries are counted separately and the last value wins, so supply unique column indices per row rather than assuming duplicate summation. The code copies off-diagonal values backwards and then installs the pointers. There is no bounds/status checking. The sketch uses distinct input/output/work arrays and conservatively allocates N+NNZ+1 output entries. This is storage conversion, not a sparse solver or new factorization.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `93594ff359ffd4fd1caad6d55093e3ae3bf6be09`.

[Readme.MD](https://github.com/tueboesen/Sparse-iterative-parallel-linear-solver/blob/fe82bd08e2050716c2ed43996337d5e8f4723c44/Readme.MD)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `efd565ac71083e764250e5aed47d6075d4462bda0a3c1f328b64ac19c0984b28`.

**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

The selected mSolver SingleRHS path is real sparse preconditioned conjugate gradient, dispatching block SGS or BLUT preconditioning and sparse matrix-vector products. This supports a symmetric sparse linear-system mapping, with SPD matrix and suitable preconditioner required for ordinary CG guarantees; no general nonsymmetric solver is inferred. SetSolverSettings prepares ordering/scaling/preconditioners and SolverAxB dispatches the wrapper. Several implementation qualifications matter: setup reads optional iSolverType without PRESENT guards, uses integer truth tests, and the wrapper may change RHS and matrix normalization/order. Output%Success is private; public Output%Status is overwritten with a bounded iteration count even on exhaustion, and the iterate is restored to its starting value on unsuccessful termination. Therefore status is not a reliable convergence certificate. There is no initial zero-residual guard before CG quotients. Review covers the real iterative dispatch, setup and stopping paths, not the unimplemented Pardiso option or scalability.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `fe82bd08e2050716c2ed43996337d5e8f4723c44`.

**L8c — source-reviewed**

PENALIZED_L2_REGRESSION in the public Fortran SPARSEREG module performs cyclic coordinate updates for weighted multiple-linear regression with selected separable penalties. The reviewed ENET branch uses rho*((eta-1)*beta**2/2+(2-eta)*abs(beta)), with eta in [1,2], a different parameter convention from GLMnet PARM. SUM_X_SQUARES must be precomputed as sum(WT*X(:,i)**2); unpenalized columns use a direct coordinate minimizer and all required coordinate curvatures must be positive. ESTIMATE is updated in place and MAXITERS can be reset from a nonpositive value, but no actual iteration count or success code is returned. Shape mismatch, objective increase, convergence and exhaustion can all end without distinct diagnostics. Some invalid threshold inputs leave the function result unassigned, so validate sizes, weights and tuning values first. Although the file is under MATLAB private/, its module procedures are public by default and do not require a MEX entry for this direct call. Review covers the native weighted ENET path, not every nonconvex penalty, GLM family or MATLAB wrapper.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `59a6de001f95f6a59a0f7fb54e0c48fe00b90e3a`.

```fortran
use SPARSEREG, only: DBLE_PREC,PENALIZED_L2_REGRESSION
integer,parameter :: n=6,p=2
integer :: maxiters,j

logical :: penalized(p)
x(:,1)=1._DBLE_PREC; x(:,2)=[0._DBLE_PREC,1._DBLE_PREC,2._DBLE_PREC, &
 3._DBLE_PREC,4._DBLE_PREC,5._DBLE_PREC]
y=1._DBLE_PREC+2._DBLE_PREC*x(:,2); weights=1._DBLE_PREC; beta=0._DBLE_PREC
do j=1,p
 curvature(j)=sum(weights*x(:,j)**2)
end do
penalized=[.false.,.true.]; maxiters=1000
call PENALIZED_L2_REGRESSION(beta,x,y,weights,0.1_DBLE_PREC,curvature, &
 penalized,maxiters,"ENET",[1.5_DBLE_PREC])

```

**D1b9 — source-reviewed**

The inspected array_to_sparse_line converts a dense row/column vector into one-based index/value storage, dropping entries with ABS(value)<=tolerance; the reverse routine zeros a dense vector and sums contributions at stored indices. D1b9 records storage-mode conversion for sparse lines, which are the matrix assembly building blocks, not a sparse equation solver or completed CSR/CSC exporter. Default tolerance is 1e-8. sparse_line_to_array evaluates SIZE(array) before testing allocation, so the caller must supply an already allocated dense array. Public indices/counters are not validated. The separate assemble_sparse_line sets lcount=1 even for an empty line and its sorter has a fixed 50-integer stack; those assembly paths are outside the round-trip sketch. No conversion or assembled matrix was run.

```fortran
use sparseset, only: sparse_line, spdp, allocate_sparse_line, &
                     array_to_sparse_line, sparse_line_to_array, deallocate_sparse_line
type(sparse_line) :: line
real(spdp) :: values(4)
real(spdp), allocatable :: restored(:)
values = [1.0_spdp, 0.0_spdp, -2.0_spdp, 3.0_spdp]
call allocate_sparse_line(line, 4, 4)

call sparse_line_to_array(line, restored)
call deallocate_sparse_line(line)
```

With positive tolerance this conversion intentionally loses small entries, so round trips are not exact in general. Kind numbers are compiler dependent. Produce Bernoulli values in BN(0:N), using real kind SPECFUN_WP (REAL64 by default, preprocessor selectable). Require N>=2 because the implementation unconditionally writes BN(0), BN(1), BN(2). The routine writes B1=-1/2 and even-index values, but does not initialize odd entries greater than 1; do not read those output entries as zero without assigning them separately. There is no status, user tolerance or iteration-budget argument; the internal sum has a fixed tolerance/cap. This source review does not promote the untouched odd output elements into a checked sequence.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL bernob(N,BN)
```

Argument declarations: [src/specfun.F90:778–779](https://github.com/jacobwilliams/specfun/blob/e74d9c810d5c9248b5d8ffab4b766e7bb22ffd23/src/specfun.F90#L778-L779).

Evaluate digamma, the logarithmic derivative of gamma, through public generic DIGAMMA, backed by PSI. Scalar input/result are default REAL. Usage:

```fortran
VALUE = digamma(X)
```

**C10a4 — source-reviewed**

Computes J of complex argument and nonnegative real orders FNU through FNU+N-1. KODE=2 instead returns exp(-abs(Im(z)))*J. NZ counts the trailing underflowed sequence entries. The inspected AMOS driver validates arguments, applies range checks and dispatches to its dependent kernels. IERR=0 means normal completion; 1 invalid input, 2 overflow, 3 precision warning with a computed result, 4 excessive argument/order loss, and 5 algorithm failure. This is the underlying split-real Fortran API, not the Python interface. No kernel-wide audit or numerical test was performed.

**D5 — source-reviewed**

The external CARRQR routine computes a blocked column-pivoted QR representation: REDUCEQRCP selects/reduces candidate panels, the driver stores reflector coefficients and triangular factors, and UPDATEA applies the block update. JPVT maps the permuted columns; A is overwritten with factor/reflector storage, not an explicit Q. The current source hardcodes NTHD=1 and disables intended OpenMP paths, so no parallel communication-avoidance timing claim is made. Its LDA guard uses MIN(M,1) instead of MAX(1,M); callers must enforce LDA>=MAX(1,M) themselves. Require positive nonempty sizes and 1<=BLKMAX<=MIN(M,N); zero-sized cases are rejected by the block-size guard before the nominal quick return. This is the inspected Fortran QR component, not the full spectrum-revealing CUR workflow implemented elsewhere in the repository, a numerical rank certificate or an audit of all LUSOL/BLAS kernels.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `1d3499eb196203f7cc2751619d042bd247a6f5b9`.

**C9 — source-reviewed**

The selected ylgndr recurrence evaluates normalized associated Legendre functions for nonnegative degree/order, n<=nmax and 0<=m<=n, at finite x in [-1,1]. The normalization is sqrt(2*n+1)*sqrt((n-m)!/(n+m)!)*P_nm(x), with the negative diagonal square-root recurrence incorporating the Condon-Shortley sign. Only the lower triangle of y is assigned; other entries are undefined. There is no domain/status check or derivative output in this selected routine. This Fortran special-function mapping is separate from the MATLAB scattered-point fit and does not establish high-degree stability by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `1c2ba54dbcd19ff6d7d57f582f7ddb8b6809a320`.
