**K6a1 — source-reviewed**

The selected sheval3d/ sheval3d0 pair evaluates an already supplied spherical-harmonic expansion at one point using ylgndr and exp(i*m*phi) recurrence, combining both positive and negative orders. This is fitted-function evaluation (K6a1), not the scattered-point least-squares coefficient solve: the repository implements that solve in MATLAB. Coefficients use mpole(0:nterms,-nterms:nterms) and only abs(m)<=n is read. The basis omits the usual 1/sqrt(4*pi) factor. The helper comment about scaling by 1/sqrt(2*l+1) is not reflected in an extra scaling operation after ylgndr. No output status, coefficient fit or approximation-error check was performed.

**C10a3 — source-reviewed**

The inspected real SBESSJ evaluates spherical j_n(x), choosing a power series for |x|<=0.78*n and upward recurrence from sin(x)/x and (sin(x)/x-cos(x))/x otherwise. At x=0 the series returns j_0=1 and j_n=0 for n>0. C10a3 (real argument, real order) is used for the half-integer cylindrical-Bessel subset: j_n(x)=sqrt(pi/(2*x))*J_(n+1/2)(x) for positive x (NIST DLMF 10.47.3, https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.47.E3). The procedure exposes only nonnegative integer spherical n, not arbitrary real cylindrical orders, Y/Hankel or modified I/K functions. Negative order, a flagged low-accuracy positive-x region for n>50, and series nonconvergence print diagnostics and STOP. The low-accuracy guard uses x rather than abs(x), so negative-x reliability is not established by that guard. Series stopping uses an absolute term threshold and a finite 20+2*n budget; it supplies neither a returned error estimate nor a status code. Precision/accuracy claims in comments/README were not reproduced. Complex and quad variants and the comparison implementation remain outside this source review. No Bessel value or recurrence residual was executed.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

SPLIFT assembles/factors a tridiagonal system for nodal second derivatives with user endpoint relations, solves it and recovers first derivatives; SPLINT locates intervals by hunt/bisection and evaluates cubic values/first/second derivatives. E1a records interpolating piecewise cubics, not smoothing. Use at least four strictly increasing nodes for the reviewed fit path. ISX=1 reuses the factorization only when nodes, workspace and endpoint coefficients are unchanged; validation is skipped on that reuse path. Success is IERR/KERR=1, not zero. SPLINT extrapolates the end cubic and returns KERR=2; equal adjacent nodes can STOP. N<4 fitting returns zero derivatives and IERR=2 rather than the normal cubic result. No interpolation, derivative or extrapolation accuracy was run; integration through SPLIQ is outside this mapping.

```fortran
CALL splift(x,y,yp,ypp,n,w,ierr,isx,a1,b1,an,bn)
```

External evaluation of spline defined by X/Y/YPP. XI/YI/YPI/YPPI length NI; returns values and two derivatives. Queries may be unordered. KERR=1 normal, 2 extrapolation, 3 invalid NI. Preserve matching X/Y/YPP and check statuses before use.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL splint(x,y,ypp,n,xi,yi,ypi,yppi,ni,kerr)
```

Argument declarations: [splint.f90:29–43](https://github.com/jlm785/spline_interpolation_fortran/blob/f6068b941876e9df2930eeae60017a5e9491780b/splint.f90#L29-L43).

```fortran
external :: splift, splint

real(rk) :: xi(1), yi(1), d1(1), d2(1)
x=[0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk,3.0_rk]
y=x
call splift(x,y,yp,ypp,n,w,ierr,0,0.0_rk,0.0_rk,0.0_rk,0.0_rk)
if (ierr /= 1) error stop "spline fit failed"
xi=1.5_rk
call splint(x,y,ypp,n,xi,yi,d1,d2,1,kerr)
if (kerr /= 1) error stop "spline evaluation not in range"
```

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

splitmix64_next adds the fixed golden-ratio increment to a local copy of its INTENT(IN) seed, applies two XOR-shift/multiply mixers and a final XOR shift, returning an INT64 bit-pattern harvest. The caller seed is unchanged: calling repeatedly with the same seed repeats the same output. Assigning harvest back as the next seed instead iterates a different map from the usual SplitMix counter progression. L6a21 records the generator mixing step rather than claiming an automatically advancing stream or a real-valued uniform API. The BOZ constants are passed through TRANSFER, and signed integer addition/multiplication still assumes intended wrapping. No bitstream/reference or portability test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `08a181d9088daf4bf9b72856e705e0b0263bfe3b`.

[README.md](https://github.com/NLAFET/SpLLT/blob/08a181d9088daf4bf9b72856e705e0b0263bfe3b/README.md)

**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

SpLLT provides sparse real-SPD Cholesky factorization and triangular solves through analysis/factor/solve phases. The native factor wrapper selects task-based STF/PTG work; local diagonal kernels use Cholesky and block triangular updates, while solves traverse forward/backward work. Symbolic analysis uses SPRAL and requires the lower-triangular CSC pattern, consistent values and permutation storage. The selected usage is an initialized OpenMP/STF configuration after successful analysis. SOLVE JOB=0 or omission means both phases, JOB=1 forward and JOB=2 backward in the actual worker, despite a conflicting earlier prologue description. Task completion is explicit through SPLLT_WAIT where required. INFO%FLAG reports framework diagnostics, but the reviewed local diagonal kernel returns on nonzero DPOTRF status without exposing that status as a public argument; do not treat the wrapper flag as sufficient numerical certification. Review covers public phase dispatch, selected factor kernel and solve-job dispatch, not all runtimes, GPUs or indefinite systems.

```fortran
call spllt_factor(akeep,fkeep,options,val,info)
call spllt_wait()
if(info%flag/=0) error stop "inspect SpLLT factorization diagnostics"
call spllt_solve(fkeep,options,x,info=info)
if(info%flag/=0) error stop "inspect SpLLT solve diagnostics"
! Independently validate the residual, then release matrix data and finalize the runtime.
```

**D9a1 — source-reviewed**

spral_lsmr::lsmr_solve performs Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization through reverse-communication A and transpose-A products, applies plane rotations and updates the least-squares iterate and norm/conditioning estimates. D9a1 records unconstrained real L2 linear least squares, scoped to no preconditioner and no damping. The caller supplies matrix actions, so dense/sparse/matrix-free storage is a caller choice, not a mandatory stored matrix input. Initialize ACTION=0 and U=B. ACTION=1 requires V=V+TRANSPOSE(A)*U; ACTION=2 requires U=U+A*V, preserving the other vector. Overwriting with a bare product loses the recurrence contribution. ACTION=0 means termination, including errors; inspect INFORM%FLAG and independently verify residual/normal residual. Default CTEST=3 uses built-in stopping; custom tests/preconditioning/damping require their documented protocols. No solve, numerical monotonicity or dependency build was run.

```fortran
use spral_lsmr, only: lsmr_keep,lsmr_options,lsmr_inform,lsmr_solve,lsmr_free

type(lsmr_inform) :: inform
real(8) :: a(3,2),b(3),u(3),v(2),x(2)

action=0; u=b

  v=v+matmul(transpose(a),u)

  u=u+matmul(a,v)
 case default
  error stop "unexpected LSMR action"
 end select
end do
call lsmr_free(keep,stat)
! Inspect inform%flag, cleanup stat and independently check A*x-b.
```

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The inspected structured-grid path prepares four tensor-product bilinear weights from normalized x/y coordinates, caches them by a formatted coordinate key, and applies them to four supplied values. E2a records gridded bivariate interpolation; the type does not fetch a full field or perform three-/four-coordinate interpolation (higher-rank values carry extra fields). Important source defects prevent a general-use recommendation: REAL(8) regular-grid preparation uses FLOOR without the required one-based offset and leaves the fourth corner second index zero by writing corner 3 twice; REAL(4) uses CEILING but excludes the lower endpoint and accepts some cells past the final valid interval. apply calls prepare on a cache miss but computes its result only in the ELSE branch, leaving the first return undefined unless prepare is called explicitly. apply neither guards outside points nor checks value-array extents. Its corner order is (lower-left, lower-right, upper-right, upper-left) mapped to input positions (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,2), not the usual rectangular-field order. The sketch is a restricted REAL(4), strictly interior, explicitly prepared interface illustration. Curvilinear location/inversion and dependencies are not audited. No interpolation or defect was reproduced by execution.

Public generic, scoped to the REAL(4) scalar-field binding. Supply a two-by-two array in the source corner order: (1,1)=LL, (2,1)=LR, (1,2)=UR, (2,2)=UL, plus REAL(4) query coordinates. It mutates the cache; a prior prepare call is required for a defined return. Do not pass a conventional field slice without checking the swapped upper-corner ordering.

Usage:

```fortran
value = interp%apply(enclose_values, x, y)
```

REAL(8) regular grids have separate indexing defects. **L5a1e — source-reviewed**

The real exponential-distribution PDF specialization evaluates lambda*EXP(-x*lambda), and the CDF evaluates 1-EXP(-x*lambda). L5a1e records exponential densities/cumulative probabilities; lambda is a rate (mean 1/lambda), not a scale. The generic real32/64/128 input overloads are produced by Fypp templates, but these PDF/CDF implementations declare their result as default REAL for every input kind. Higher-kind inputs therefore do not imply a higher-kind returned value. X<0 or lambda<=0 calls stdlib error_stop rather than returning support-zero/status; provide finite X>=0 and rate>0. The subtractive CDF formula can lose relative accuracy for small x*lambda. Complex overloads, ziggurat random generation and distribution-tail accuracy are excluded. No template build or distribution values were run.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `afc812f2d1bc7e11ee09a5b8589a847b91117f60`.

**L5a2n — source-reviewed**

Algorithm AS241 PPND7 and PPND16 approximate the standard-normal quantile using central and tail rational branches. PPND7 uses default REAL, PPND16 DOUBLE PRECISION. Supply finite 0<P<1: endpoints/out-of-range probabilities return zero with IFAULT=1 rather than infinite quantiles. NaNs are not explicitly validated, and subtraction 1-P loses information near one. This mapping is inverse normal CDF evaluation, not a random-number generator or a new accuracy validation of the header precision claims.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The selected serial Evolutionary%optimize(solver="de",strategy="rand1") path performs stochastic bound-constrained global search with differential mutation, binomial crossover and greedy replacement. Explicitly request DE: the default solver is CPSO. DE/rand1 needs at least four population members. Bounds must have strictly positive widths to avoid normalization division by zero. The inspected boundary repair replaces offending normalized coordinates with uniform [0,1] draws rather than projection or uniform [-1,1]. Termination includes an absolute objective threshold and iteration budget; neither proves global optimality. MPI and other solvers are outside this mapping.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

simpson_integrator_vals integrates a vector of samples over a presumed uniformly spaced finite grid. Odd sample counts use composite Simpson 1/3; even counts use 1/3 up to the last four samples and a final 3/8 panel. H2a1b2 records nonautomatic quadrature from sampled data; no callback, adaptive error control or nonuniform-coordinate support is implied. At least three samples are needed for odd N and four for even N; the code does not validate these sizes, and N=1 divides by zero while small even counts address invalid elements. The routine returns only a scalar estimate and no error/status. Other integration, optimization and algebra routines remain outside this source review. No polynomial reference integral or upstream test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `5218aa8439405dd39fd9e1e2f7e3846850558a51`.

**P — source-reviewed**

The selected fixed-form TRIPACK TRMESH routine incrementally constructs an unconstrained planar Delaunay triangulation in linked adjacency storage. It initializes a noncollinear triangle, inserts nodes and swaps edges using orientation/circumcircle tests and nearest-node search starts. Require distinct coordinates and a noncollinear first triple. LIST/LPTR need 6*N-12 storage, LEND/NEAR/NEXT/DIST need N. IER distinguishes invalid size, initial collinearity, duplicate nodes and internal swap failure; partial adjacency is not a completed mesh on failure. This is planar triangulation rather than spherical geometry or a PDE discretization. The selected fixed-form source uses default REAL and is included by SRFPACK; the separate tripack.f90 variant uses REAL(8) and must not be mixed blindly with these call declarations. Review covers construction and storage contracts, not robust exact predicates or every constrained-edge operation.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `f87add7efe4db23165d820bfb5394c83596c18da`.

**E2b — source-reviewed**

The selected SRFPACK INTRC0 routine locates a triangle and evaluates a barycentric piecewise-linear interpolant of scattered planar nodal values. Outside the convex hull, it returns the value at the nearest boundary point rather than unconstrained linear extrapolation. IST is a mutable triangle-search start; NCC/LCC describe optional constraint curves, with a one-element dummy LCC for NCC=0. IER=0 denotes ordinary interpolation, 1 a constraint-region result, 2 extrapolation, and negatives invalid/degenerate cases. The sketch uses the matching default-REAL fixed-form TRIPACK included by SRFPACK, not the distinct REAL(8) mesh extension. Review covers triangle location/barycentric assembly and boundary behavior, not smooth cubic interpolation or gradient estimation.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

The reviewed HERMIT generator constructs Gauss-Hermite nodes and weights for the exp(-x*x) weight: initial root estimates, Newton corrections via HROOT/HRECUR, mirrored nodes/weights, and Gamma-based normalization. H2c records quadrature rule construction, not an adaptive integral evaluator. HROOT uses at most ten Newton iterations with no returned convergence flag; derivative/polynomial values used in weights are from the last pre-update evaluation. The initial-root expression differs from the formula in its comment, and 2**(N-1) uses default INTEGER arithmetic, which can overflow for higher orders. It prints node diagnostics and performs no order/overflow validation. Only modest positive orders are illustrated. Jacobi/Laguerre generators and numerical moment checks are outside this review.

**G1b2 — source-reviewed**

SUBPLX sorts step scales, partitions coordinates into subspaces and calls SIMPLX for derivative-free simplex minimization, repeating until its relative coordinate/step test is satisfied or a limit is returned. The nonsmooth unconstrained class records this local search, not global optimization. Unlike older comments, this fork has no MODE argument and always initializes default options through SUBOPT. COMMON and SAVE state make nested/concurrent use unsafe without isolation. This review does not establish noisy-objective performance or inspect the entire R bridge.

External objective-only minimizer with DOUBLE PRECISION F(N,X). X is overwritten, FX is the resulting cost, NFE the evaluation count. Allocate WORK >= 2*N+NSMAX*(NSMAX+4)+1 and IWORK >= N+INT(N/NSMIN), with default NSMAX=MIN(5,N), NSMIN=MIN(2,N).

Usage:

```fortran
CALL SUBPLX(F, N, TOL, MAXNFE, SCALE, X, FX, NFE, WORK, IWORK, IFLAG)
```

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The public RK4 routine implements one classical explicit four-stage Runge-Kutta step for a vector initial-value problem. It calls RHS at the standard starting, midpoint and endpoint stages and forms the weighted increment in a separate output vector. The actual callback signature is RHS(N,T,X,DXDT), including N, despite comments omitting that leading argument. DP is KIND(0D0) from TYPES. The caller owns the time loop, step choice, output scheduling and stability/error assessment; no adaptive control, embedded estimate, rejection, event location or convergence status is provided. This review selects the RK4 implementation rather than endorsing all other order-named routines or a particular dynamical-system model.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The public AKIMA generic computes regularized Akima slopes and evaluates piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation for scalar or vector queries. EVLAK locates an interval and evaluates the native Hermite formula; outside the data interval it continues the nearest interval polynomial. Supply matching arrays with at least three distinct strictly increasing abscissae: DAKIMA reads the third sample before its later N=2 return, so two-point input is unsafe. The slope rule includes an epsilon proportional to the abscissa span; it is not an unconditional monotonicity/shape-preserving guarantee. EVLAK saves its interval index between calls and clamps it to N rather than N-1, which can leave an invalid last interval when changing datasets/lengths. Concurrent calls and reuse with varying grids need review. This is univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation, not a global polynomial fit or quadrature.

**L1a1a — source-reviewed**

Location mapping: arithmetic and weighted means; AVEVAR also supplies a mean. The shared driver additionally checks sample variance under the separate L1a1b mapping. The public math::mean and avevar compute descriptive location/dispersion statistics. Unweighted mean uses SUM(A)/N; optional weights select DOT_PRODUCT(W,A)/SUM(W), despite a comment suggesting division by N. AVEVAR first computes the mean, accumulates squared deviations and their residual sum, and returns (SUM((A-AVE)**2)-SUM(A-AVE)**2/N)/(N-1), a corrected sample variance. DP=KIND(0D0). Empty input returns the module NaN; singleton AVEVAR divides by zero. Weight sizes, finite values and nonzero weight sum are not validated; signed weights are accepted mechanically. There is no missing-data policy, error estimate or negative-variance clamp. The checked contract is N>=2, ordinary finite arithmetic progressions and positive conforming weights. A complete main checks N=2..20, offsets 0 and 10, steps .25, 1 and 4 (114 cases), using closed-form mean, sample variance and weighted mean for W(I)=I. All outputs were finite and normalized errors <=2e-12; maximum 2.197555e-16. Huge offsets, cancellation, signed/zero-total weights, singleton/empty paths and overflow remain unchecked. Complete main compiled and run locally on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), 2026-11-06. Unmodified types/constants/utils/math modules use -fno-range-check -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow; main uses the same flags except -fno-range-check. The extra module flag accommodates constants.f90 zero-division NaN/infinity parameter initializers and is not a portability claim. Hashes, flags, warnings and successful results are under drivers/system-dynamics-math/. Only the named routines were executed; previous RK4/Akima source reviews are unchanged. Numerical Recipes notices in AVEVAR and eigen helpers leave component licensing unresolved; no upstream numerical source is bundled.

```fortran
      do is=0,2
        step=0.25_dp*4.0_dp**is
        x=offset+step*w
        expected_mean=offset+step*real(n+1,dp)/2
        expected_var=step**2*real(n*(n+1),dp)/12
        expected_weighted=offset+step*real(2*n+1,dp)/3
        m=mean(x);wmean=mean(x,w)
        call avevar(x,a,v)
        if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite([m,wmean,a,v])))error stop 'Nonfinite statistics'
        e=max(abs(m-expected_mean)/max(1.0_dp,abs(expected_mean)), &
          abs(a-expected_mean)/max(1.0_dp,abs(expected_mean)), &
          abs(wmean-expected_weighted)/max(1.0_dp,abs(expected_weighted)), &
          abs(v-expected_var)/expected_var)
        if(e>2e-12_dp)error stop 'Closed-form statistics mismatch'
        maximum=max(maximum,e);count=count+1
      end do
    end do
    deallocate(x,w)
  end do
  print '(a,i0)', 'Closed-form statistics cases: ',count
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized statistic error: ',maximum
  print '(a)', 'PASS statistics'
end program
```

**D4a1 — source-reviewed**

Public math::eigencov computes a real symmetric covariance eigensystem: copies P to U, applies private Householder TRED2 and implicit QL TQLI, clips all negative eigenvalues to zero, sorts values and eigenvector columns descending through EIGSORT, and sets RANK=COUNT(D/=0). This D4a1 mapping is limited to finite symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices; clipping invalidates a general indefinite eigensystem claim. TRED2 reads the lower triangle; there is no symmetry or positive-semidefiniteness test. RANK is exact-zero counting, not a tolerance-based numerical rank. VERBOSE prints trace diagnostics without a convergence guarantee. QL iteration exhaustion uses STOP rather than a returned error code. Require N>=1, compatible default INTEGER, DP=KIND(0D0), and P/U(N,N), D(N). The complete main checks 96 matrices: N=1..8, diagonal known spectra, rank-one outer products, positive-definite Toeplitz and dense Gram+.25I families, each at scales 1e-8, 1 and 1e8. Independently calculated eigenpair residuals and trace errors normalized by matrix infinity norm, and orthogonality errors, must be <=2e-11. Maxima were 7.993606e-16, 8.162378e-16 and 2.109424e-15 respectively. Sorted nonnegative values, unchanged input, exact-zero count convention and known diagonal eigenvalues also passed. The rank test does not certify numerical rank of nearly zero eigenvalues. Zero matrices, indefinite/asymmetric input, QL failure, large dimensions, extreme scales, optimized builds and other compilers were not executed. Public covariance eigensystem with descending eigenvalues. Negative eigenvalues are clipped and RANK uses exact-zero counting; no convergence status is returned. Intended for positive-semidefinite inputs only.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL eigencov(N,P,U,D,RANK,VERBOSE)
```

Argument declarations: [src/lib/math.f90:582–585](https://github.com/quimbp/system_dynamics/blob/366339d9f6fea2e4242f8a73b700f8ea0af07797/src/lib/math.f90#L582-L585).

Argument declarations: [src/lib/types.f90:12–15](https://github.com/quimbp/system_dynamics/blob/366339d9f6fea2e4242f8a73b700f8ea0af07797/src/lib/types.f90#L12-L15).

Locally checked main program:

```fortran
program covariance_eigen
  use types, only: dp
  use math, only: eigencov
  use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
  implicit none
  integer :: n,i,j,k,family,iscale,rank,cases
  real(dp) :: scale,norma,residual,orthogonality,trace_error,maxres,maxorth,maxtrace
  real(dp), allocatable :: a(:,:),p(:,:),u(:,:),d(:),gram(:,:),v(:)
  maxres=0;maxorth=0;maxtrace=0;cases=0
  do n=1,8
    allocate(a(n,n),p(n,n),u(n,n),d(n),gram(n,n),v(n))
    do family=1,4
      a=0
      select case(family)
      case(1)
        do i=1,n
          a(i,i)=real(i,dp)
        end do
      case(2)
        v=[(real(i,dp)/n,i=1,n)]
        do i=1,n
          a(:,i)=v*v(i)
        end do
      case(3)
        do i=1,n
          do j=1,n
            a(i,j)=0.5_dp**abs(i-j)
          end do
        end do
      case(4)
        do i=1,n
          do j=1,n
            gram(i,j)=sin(real(i+2*j,dp))
          end do
        end do
        a=matmul(transpose(gram),gram)
        do i=1,n
          a(i,i)=a(i,i)+0.25_dp
        end do
      end select
      do iscale=-1,1
        scale=10.0_dp**(8*iscale);p=scale*a
        call eigencov(n,p,u,d,rank,.false.)
        if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(u)).or..not.all(ieee_is_finite(d)))error stop 'Nonfinite eigensystem'
        if(any(p/=scale*a))error stop 'Input covariance changed'
        if(any(d<0).or.rank/=count(d/=0))error stop 'Rank/nonnegative convention mismatch'
        if(any(d(1:n-1)<d(2:n)))error stop 'Eigenvalues not descending'
        norma=maxval(sum(abs(scale*a),dim=2))
        residual=0
        do k=1,n
          residual=max(residual,maxval(abs(matmul(scale*a,u(:,k))-d(k)*u(:,k)))/norma)
        end do
        gram=matmul(transpose(u),u)
        do i=1,n
          gram(i,i)=gram(i,i)-1
        end do
        orthogonality=maxval(abs(gram))
        trace_error=abs(sum(d)-sum([(scale*a(i,i),i=1,n)]))/norma
        if(max(residual,orthogonality,trace_error)>2e-11_dp)error stop 'Eigensystem invariant failed'
        if(family==1)then
          if(maxval(abs(d-[(scale*real(n-i+1,dp),i=1,n)]))/norma>2e-11_dp)error stop 'Diagonal spectrum mismatch'
        end if
        maxres=max(maxres,residual);maxorth=max(maxorth,orthogonality);maxtrace=max(maxtrace,trace_error)
        cases=cases+1
      end do
    end do
    deallocate(a,p,u,d,gram,v)
  end do
  print '(a,i0)', 'Positive-semidefinite eigensystem cases: ',cases
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized eigenpair residual: ',maxres
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum orthogonality error: ',maxorth
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized trace error: ',maxtrace
  print '(a)', 'PASS covariance_eigen'
end program
```

**L1a1b — source-reviewed**

Dispersion mapping: corrected two-pass sample variance with N-1 denominator. Mean/weighted-mean functionality is separately classified L1a1a. The same 114 datasets support both mappings, not 228 distinct datasets. Location mapping: arithmetic and weighted means; AVEVAR also supplies a mean. The shared driver additionally checks sample variance under the separate L1a1b mapping. The public math::mean and avevar compute descriptive location/dispersion statistics. Unweighted mean uses SUM(A)/N; optional weights select DOT_PRODUCT(W,A)/SUM(W), despite a comment suggesting division by N. AVEVAR first computes the mean, accumulates squared deviations and their residual sum, and returns (SUM((A-AVE)**2)-SUM(A-AVE)**2/N)/(N-1), a corrected sample variance. DP=KIND(0D0). Empty input returns the module NaN; singleton AVEVAR divides by zero. Weight sizes, finite values and nonzero weight sum are not validated; signed weights are accepted mechanically. There is no missing-data policy, error estimate or negative-variance clamp. The checked contract is N>=2, ordinary finite arithmetic progressions and positive conforming weights. A complete main checks N=2..20, offsets 0 and 10, steps .25, 1 and 4 (114 cases), using closed-form mean, sample variance and weighted mean for W(I)=I. All outputs were finite and normalized errors <=2e-12; maximum 2.197555e-16. Huge offsets, cancellation, signed/zero-total weights, singleton/empty paths and overflow remain unchecked. The public in1 generic selects the rank-one/rank-one overload when passed a scalar result and two REAL(8) vectors of length iDm. The implementation zeroes the result and sums component products, supporting D1a4 (dot product). Explicit iDm determines the dummy extents; actual vector compatibility is not validated and no status or compensated summation is provided. Other rank combinations under the same generic do not inherit this source review. No dot product or continuum-mechanics example was run.

**D1b6 — source-reviewed**

The inspected vector/vector dyad overload assigns result(i,j)=a(i)*b(j), and the rank-two/rank-two overload assigns result(i,j,k,l)=A(i,j)*B(k,l). D1b6 records these outer-product forms of matrix/tensor multiplication, explicitly not an ordinary contracted matrix product. The overloads use a common square/cubic dimension iDm and fixed REAL(8) dummies, with no validation/status. Storage for rank-four output grows as iDm**4. Spectral decomposition, inverse and contractions remain outside this review. No outer product was executed.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

Tensor::inv for full Tensor2 uses explicit 3-by-3 cofactors divided by the determinant, assigning all nine inverse entries. D2a1 is scoped to fixed-size general real 3-by-3 inversion, not a pivoted factorization, a generic dimension solver or a rank-four tensor inverse. The selected Tensor2 is REAL(kind=8) storage AB(3,3); the symmetric compact overload exists but is not the selected sketch. There is no singularity, conditioning or overflow guard and no status result. det_2 performs the explicit cubic determinant formula. A zero/nearly-zero determinant can therefore yield invalid or inaccurate inverse entries. No inversion, identity residual or material-model example was run.

**D1a4 — source-reviewed**

Tensor::operator(.ddot.) for two full Tensor2 objects initializes a scalar to zero and sums the nine pairwise products AB(i,j)*AB(i,j). D1a4 records this real Frobenius inner product, viewed as a dot product on nine stored entries; it is not matrix multiplication or an arbitrary-rank complex contraction. The separately inspected Tensor2s pair weights off-diagonal compact entries by two. Only these scalar second-order contractions are covered, not every higher-order .ddot. overload. All values use fixed REAL(kind=8), direct unscaled accumulation and no overflow/cancellation status. No contractions or representation equivalence were run.

**D — documentation-reviewed**

The README documents complex block-sparse tfQMR solves, multiple right-hand sides and Fortran 90/77 entry points. CUDA implements the computational backend. Convergence, GPU availability and performance require individual testing and are not implied by this broad classification.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `a87bfcdcd75a127628f38053c16aa041f47464c6`.

[README.md](https://github.com/real-space/tfQMRgpu/blob/a87bfcdcd75a127628f38053c16aa041f47464c6/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `2be914674842b058aac9eaf8a4b285fd831707056977159e6dc1901de553fa05`.

**D2c4 — source-reviewed**

The public TFQMRGPU_BSRSV_COMPLETE wrapper solves complex non-Hermitian sparse A*X=B using block-sparse row patterns for A, B and the allowed solution X. It delegates to a private rectangular helper that creates a GPU handle/plan, uploads block data, calls the transpose-free QMR core, downloads X and frees resources. The core performs two TFQMR half-steps with sparse multiplications and per-RHS residual/breakdown tracking. Solution sparsity is prescribed by the caller, so a restricted X pattern is not equivalent to an unrestricted dense solve. Block sizes must have been compiled into the CUDA backend. Fortran patterns are one-based; block transposition flags are n/t, not an arbitrary conjugate-transpose operator. ITERATIONS/RESIDUAL are input limits and output reports. Helper CheckError uses STOP on many failures despite an IERR argument; core completion can include breakdown-stopped RHSs, so verify the reported and independently computed residual even after a successful status. Review covers the square-block convenience API and selected recurrence/stopping paths, not all precisions or block configurations.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `a87bfcdcd75a127628f38053c16aa041f47464c6`.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `30c5421cf3ce0cc5700dc64aa9d4154e588957b7`.

[README.md](https://github.com/sweichwald/tidybench/blob/30c5421cf3ce0cc5700dc64aa9d4154e588957b7/README.md)

**L10c — source-reviewed**

SLVAR performs selective multivariate autoregressive structure/lag search: each directed variable pair has one selected lag or no edge, candidate changes are scored in contiguous data batches and a greedy hill-climb retains improving changes. The final B matrix is batch-averaged absolute coefficients, not the full signed VAR lag tensor; A stores selected lags. BS, ML and MXITR can be rewritten, and MXITR=0 skips search so it requires an already initialized graph. The PRESS-like score helper calls DORGQR using workspace left by DGELS, which does not expose a reflector-TAU output contract; the validity of these leverage corrections is therefore not established and needs validation/repair. Too-small batches, singular designs and leverage denominators near zero also need checks. INFO is reused through candidate fits/final coefficient calculations and does not certify the global optimum or every intermediate fit. Review covers the native selection/control flow and concrete returned quantities, not a causal-identification guarantee or a validated scoring implementation.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `30c5421cf3ce0cc5700dc64aa9d4154e588957b7`.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The supplied TikTak program performs heuristic multistart global minimization: evaluate/rank Sobol starts, blend later starts with a best or rank-weighted lottery point, run a selected local method, and coordinate progress through filesystem state/checkpoints. It is a program/configuration-file workflow, not a public TIKTAK subroutine. The selected a mode uses scalar OBJFUNC with AMOEBA; the default b mode instead requires residual callback DFOVEC, and d uses a gradient-based local optimizer. The blending weight is clipped between 0.10 and 0.95. Cold and warm starts have different command-line layouts. Isolate working directories because state/control files coordinate workers; no MPI or OpenMP API is required by that orchestration. Neither finite multistart coverage nor a local convergence message proves a global minimum. Review covers program control, start modification and AMOEBA dispatch, not all local kernels or synchronization correctness.

**L10a3a2 — source-reviewed**

The external CalcAlphaBeta routine forms weighted sine/cosine normal-equation sums at a requested frequency and solves the two-by-two system for alpha and beta. The spec program uses alpha**2+beta**2 as its raw power before output transformations. t is in seconds and nu in microhertz; twopi_micro incorporates 1e-6. The routine reads timeseries::sumWeights rather than computing SUM(w), so callers bypassing ImportData must set that global consistently. Equal array lengths, positive effective weight sum, finite nonnegative weights and a nonsingular sine/cosine design are preconditions; determinant division has no check/status. There is no fitted floating mean/intercept in this routine and no automatic significance test. This is a source-reviewed least-squares periodogram path, not an FFT or a new spectral accuracy/timing check.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `92fc61c0a5b014363544c4ccd762077c9e1ba43e`.

**L10a2a1 — source-reviewed**

ARCV computes the theoretical autocovariance sequence of a stationary autoregressive model from its coefficients and innovation variance. It converts coefficients to partials to determine lag-zero variance, then rebuilds lower-order coefficient/covariance relations and extends the sequence recursively. These are model-implied covariances, not empirical estimates from observations or a fitted AR model. Timeslab uses X(t)+sum(ALPHA(j)*X(t-j))=innovation; consequently an AR(1) coefficient phi=0.5 is supplied as ALPHA=-0.5. ALPHA is overwritten by the intermediate conversion/reconstruction and should be copied if needed later. IER is nonzero when the partial-recursion stationarity check fails; unit-modulus partials are rejected in code as well as values beyond one. Require positive model order, nonnegative requested lag count, positive innovation variance and adequate output storage. Review covers the covariance recursion and its stationarity helper, not every interactive Timeslab command.

Implementation helper `arprt`: [ar.F:337–373](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Timeslab/blob/d77a2424d04be719fe1afa92abdd9b7023d2d478/ar.F#L337-L373).

**L10a2a2 — source-reviewed**

ARPRT implements the backward recursion converting stationary AR coefficients to signed reflection/partial-autocorrelation coefficients. It overwrites ALPHA and checks abs(c)>=1 at each stage before division by 1-c*c. The raw kernel returns Timeslab-signed partials; the public ARPART command negates its output before labeling it partial autocorrelations. The calling sketch includes that same negation and preserves no original coefficients. This computes partials implied by a supplied model, not sample PACF estimation or model-order selection. Near-unit partials can make the recursion ill-conditioned even without a nonzero IER, and invalid model orders are not checked in this kernel. Review covers the transformation and the caller-established sign convention.

**L10a2a1 — source-reviewed**

The supplied AUTOCOR executable estimates a univariate autocorrelation sequence using the squared Fourier amplitudes and an inverse transform. Its default path demeans/normalizes nonconstant data, zero-pads and divides lag values by the decreasing overlap count before normalizing lag zero. The -v path requests unnormalized autocovariance and bypasses the normalizing helper, so callers needing centered covariance should center input explicitly. The -p/-P periodic paths have different continuation/length conventions. The CLI reads files/columns and writes lag/value pairs; it is not a reusable Fortran module function. Constant-series normalization stops and the helper uses fixed one-million-point work arrays; default padding can make the helper limit smaller than the advertised input length. Review covers the command driver and Fourier-power/backtransform helper, not every file parser or a bias/uncertainty guarantee.

The supplied SPECTRUM executable forms a Fourier periodogram of a univariate sample sequence and prints frequency/power pairs. NLENGTH may be reduced to a supported transform length; the driver reports this truncation. The selected unsmoothed CLI use belongs to periodogram analysis L10a3a2, not an autoregressive spectrum or an arbitrary continuous Fourier transform. Review covers driver frequency/bin layout and the shared periodogram helper. Finite positive sampling rate, sufficiently long finite samples and interpretation of DC/Nyquist units remain caller responsibilities.

**L10a2e — source-reviewed**

SRCF forms a square-root covariance pre-array from R, C*S, A*S and B*Q (or a pre-multiplied B), triangularizes it with Householder helpers, and copies the updated lower factor S and optional combined-update gain K. SRIF constructs the corresponding information pre-array, triangularizes it and optionally solves for state X. L10a2e is scoped to scalar-observation (P=1) state-space filtering; the interfaces can also accept multiple observations, but no multivariate mapping is added here. SRCF updates covariance/gain only, not a complete observed-state trajectory. WITHK/WITHX are input requests that may be cleared by a condition estimate, leaving optional outputs unavailable. Inputs are triangular square-root/inverse-factor forms, not arbitrary covariance matrices; leading dimensions/workspace are caller responsibilities. No Kalman recursion, covariance identity or author driver was run.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

mod_numerical::linint uses locate to choose adjacent samples and forms their affine weighted combination. E1a records univariate piecewise-linear interpolation, not global high-degree polynomial fitting. The interval index is clamped so out-of-range queries linearly extrapolate using the first/last pair. It checks matching x/y lengths with PRINT, obsolete PAUSE and STOP; it does not validate ascending distinct x, minimum length, repeated knots or finite values. A zero interval divides by zero. Require equal lengths >=2 and strictly ascending finite abscissae. No interpolated result was compiled or run.

**N5b — source-reviewed**

locate performs a binary interval-position search on ascending REAL(8) xx. It starts with sentinel positions 0 and N+1, halves the interval until adjacent and returns the lower bracket. Exact first/last endpoints return 1 and N-1; below/above-grid queries return 0/N. N5b records insertion/interval-position search, not sorting or interpolation. It assumes nonempty ascending data and does not reject duplicates or NaNs. The linint caller clamps this position separately. No binary-search cases were executed.

**D2b1b — source-reviewed**

The public CHOLDC/CHOLSL pair factors and solves a real symmetric positive-definite dense system. CHOLDC reads the original upper triangle, stores strict lower factors in A and diagonal factors in P, leaving the upper input triangle in place. CHOLSL performs forward/back substitution using those factors. Require 1<=N<=NP, conforming REAL64 arrays and positive definiteness; there is no pivoting or symmetry test. Nonpositive computed pivots set INFO=1 and return incomplete factors; check before solving. CHOLSL treats INFO as input/output and returns immediately only when it equals 1, so pass the factorization status, not an uninitialized integer. Source comments credit Numerical Recipes; this mapping is source inspection, not a claim about complete third-party rights or numerical stability for arbitrary matrices.

MOINDRES_CARRES_LINEAIRE constructs JF-transpose JF and JF-transpose HIJ, then uses the local Cholesky pair to solve the normal equations. JF has NB_PTS rows and NB_VAR columns; require NB_PTS>=NB_VAR>0 and full column rank for the unregularized solve. This is unconstrained real linear least squares, not rank-revealing QR/SVD or a robust rank-deficient solver. Forming normal equations squares the design-matrix condition number. INFO from Cholesky is local and not returned; the routine still copies SCD to BETA after failure. It also passes the same SCD buffer as both solve B and X; strict aliasing/conformance behavior was not validated. Independently validate rank, residual and output before relying on the fit.

**K1b1a2 — source-reviewed**

MOINDRES_CARRES fits a scalar response at supplied two-coordinate sample locations using user model F and parameter-derivative DF callbacks. It periodically rebuilds the Jacobian (every ten iterations), forms normal equations, inflates each diagonal by 1.5, solves with Cholesky and applies a fixed RELAX-scaled correction to the first NB_VAR_DER parameters. This is a particular damped, periodically updated Gauss-Newton-like implementation, not a complete adaptive Levenberg-Marquardt/trust-region API. Require 0<NB_VAR_DER<=NB_VAR and compatible derivatives/design rank; callbacks must match the linked signatures and their parameter array is declared INTENT(INOUT). The relative correction stop divides by ABS(BETA) without zero guards, and there is no maximum-iteration limit or complete failed-factorization exit. INFO reports the local Cholesky state, not a convergence certificate; the same-buffer solve finding from the linear fitter applies. The commented calling contract is not recommended for unattended execution before adding termination/failure guards.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

INTERP1D refines an evenly spaced one-dimensional grid by a factor of two. It copies coarse values to even indices and evaluates fixed midpoint Lagrange stencils of order 1,3,5 or 7 at odd indices. Endpoint ghost samples use linear derivative continuation. This is index-grid prolongation rather than an arbitrary-coordinate interpolation routine. The body explicitly accesses indices 0..UB_GROS and writes 0..2*UB_GROS despite lower-bound arguments; use zero lower bounds and sufficient source extent (at least ORDRE) and output storage. Unsupported ORDRE stops. High-order interpolation can overshoot and is not conservative or monotonicity-preserving merely because it reproduces polynomials. The private coefficient-generation helper is not a public interpolator.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

INTERP2D applies the public one-dimensional factor-two interpolation along each axis of an evenly spaced Cartesian grid, first into an intermediate table and then into the final grid. Its TBORNE arguments carry declared array bounds, but the underlying operation assumes coarse axes 0..N and fine axes 0..2*N. Use matching zero lower bounds, fine upper bounds exactly twice coarse bounds and a supported order 1/3/5/7 with sufficient source extent on both axes. This is separable gridded polynomial prolongation, not scattered-data fitting, geographic remapping or general independent target coordinates. No error status, input-shape validation or conservation guarantee is provided.

**J1b — source-reviewed**

The selected TAB_INIT_FFTW3/TAB_CALC_FFTW3/TAB_END_FFTW3 path allocates independent two-dimensional complex FFTW buffers/plans indexed by OpenMP thread number. Initialize outside the work region with NB_THREADS_FFT at least the maximum participating thread count; keep dimensions and that count fixed until cleanup. The module has shared allocation state and is not an independent per-object context. Both transform directions divide by SQRT(LONG*LARG), giving symmetric/unitary normalization. Important sign convention: this module defines FORWARD=+1 and BACKWARD=-1 and passes those directly to FFTW, whose include defines FFTW_FORWARD=-1 and FFTW_BACKWARD=+1. Thus the module FORWARD uses the positive-exponent direction, opposite FFTW standard naming. Use the linked module constants with awareness of that convention. Build with OpenMP enabled and compatible FFTW double-complex interfaces/libraries. No direction validation, allocation-status return or general null-plan check is exposed here; initialize once, calculate as needed, then clean up before reinitializing. Review covers this selected multi-buffer wrapper path and planner dispatch, not FFTW kernels or all alternate real/single-buffer paths.

**N6a2a — source-reviewed**

SORT_ARRAY2 selects the integer(I4) in-place ascending quicksort branch and carries an order vector through swaps; optional companion arrays are rearranged using that vector. This is active sorting, not just returning a rank vector. Supported dynamic array types are INTEGER(I4) and REAL(R8), with no default unsupported-type error; avoid other kinds/types. Require N>=1 because pivot selection occurs before the recursive base-case return. Real NaNs do not have an explicit ordering policy. The quicksort is not stable. If TAB0 is supplied, initialize it to a valid 1..N permutation (normally with INIT_ORDER); the same vector is used to index companion arrays, so arbitrary labels in TAB0 can cause out-of-range indexing or unintended permutation. No status or stable tie convention is provided.

**C3a2 — source-reviewed**

TCHEBY evaluates the first-kind Chebyshev polynomial T_N(X) using an explicit finite power/combinatorial expansion, with T_0=1 handled separately. TAB_TCHEBY allocates a table of degrees 0..DEG by repeated calls. Require N/DEG>=0 and finite arguments; the routine does not reject negative degree or diagnose overflow/cancellation. This implementation is not the stable three-term recurrence or a Clenshaw evaluator for a polynomial series, and high degree or poorly scaled X can cause severe cancellation/overflow. TAB_TCHEBY returns an allocatable REAL64 table (NX,DEG+1); allocation ownership follows its INTENT(OUT) contract. Module-level dependencies include the local least-squares and utility modules even for this elementary evaluation.

Reviewed 2026-11-06 at `251579af492b05c3934f691698b2445c16e39266`.

**L10a3a — source-reviewed**

WAVELET removes the sample mean, optionally zero-pads, computes the series FFT, multiplies it by scale-dependent daughter spectra and inverse-transforms each scale. The inspected Morlet path uses a positive-frequency Gaussian; Paul and derivative-of-Gaussian branches are also visible. L10a3a records time-series spectral analysis using a continuous-wavelet transform, not a newly invented GAMS wavelet leaf or a significance-test certification. Returned WAVE holds complex coefficients, not powers; ABS(WAVE)**2 forms power. Require 1<=N<=NPAD<=65535, positive DT/S0, sensible DJ/JTOT and compatible storage. Only NPAD<N is explicitly rejected, with a printed message and unassigned outputs; MOTHER and negative PARAM can be modified to defaults. FFT/significance dependency kernels and edge-effect accuracy are not fully audited. No transform or author example was run.

**G2h3b — source-reviewed**

TRDF performs a constrained derivative-free objective trust-region iteration: it dispatches a feasibility solve, builds a quadratic interpolation model, solves a constrained model subproblem, evaluates the true objective and updates radius/model geometry. Constraints can mix equalities/inequalities and bound constraints; CCODED selects whether linked constraint Jacobian/Hessian routines are supplied. This review covers outer iteration/linked-problem dispatch, not all model algebra or ALGENCAN kernels. The interface requires linked CALOBJF/CALCON and optional derivative routines via functions.f, not procedure arguments. COMMON state and compile-time dimensions in tr_params.par limit reentrancy/size. An alternate model-build path calls CALFUN with three arguments although its wrapper takes four; this mismatch needs repair/checked validation. The routine returns F/FEAS/FCNT but no termination flag, and early failure can reach output code before a valid final model point exists. No feasibility or optimizer result was run.

**L4a1a6 — source-reviewed**

The program command dispatcher exposes tail-index assessment, anchor/order selection and evaluation of tail-regression estimates for samples with power-law tails. EVALUATE_TRE calls BOOTSTRAP_FIT, combines empirical central and analytically integrated fitted-tail moments and reports normalization/mean estimates and bootstrap uncertainties. INTEGRATE_FIT tests exponent/coefficient compatibility for moment existence/cancellation and analytically integrates fitted inverse-power contributions; it is not general numerical quadrature. This mapping is tail/outlier analysis and the inspected command/evaluation path, not proof of estimator bias/coverage, full automatic tail identification or a public library callback. Tail exponent assumptions, independence, fitting range/order and moment definition are material. The source is a standalone PROGRAM with internal procedures, plus MPI and LAPACK dependencies.

**D1b9 — source-reviewed**

pack_tri_indices maps a one-based symmetric index pair to columnwise upper-triangle packed position using triangular numbers; swapping I/J gives the same position. unpack_tri_indices estimates the inverse triangular number using SQRT and returns the upper-triangle representative. D1b9 records the indexing service for matrix storage-mode conversion, not a routine copying/converting full matrix data. The selected INT64 three-argument pack and inverse are PURE ELEMENTAL; other integer kinds and diagonal-shift overloads exist but are not certified here. There is no matrix dimension or status argument, positivity/range checks or overflow protection. Packing multiplies before dividing, and inversion forms 8*K-7 in integer arithmetic then converts to default REAL for SQRT; representable final indices do not guarantee safe intermediates or an accurate large-index inverse. No round-trip, boundary or overflow tests were executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `8f9037b16bcda22201dc491c3f6b47f8fd98a013`.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

The inspected triasymq entry retrieves tabulated reference-triangle nodes and weights, expands the D3 symmetry and maps them affinely to caller-supplied vertices. trianmap rescales weights to the absolute triangle area. This is a fixed-rule service returning nodes/weights, not an adaptive integrand-callback interface. The supported requested polynomial degree is 1..50, distinct from the returned node count (up to 453 according to the table). The wrapper ignores its internal ier, so validate degree before calling and supply a nondegenerate triangle and adequately sized arrays. The internal explicit-shape quaequad dummy uses the incoming nptsout value before overwriting it: initialize numnodes to the supplied capacity rather than relying on the author driver uninitialized variable. Tables and expansion/mapping paths were inspected, but all rule moments, degrees and claimed extended-precision construction accuracy were not independently verified. Other domains in the repository are outside this source review.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `332f5f4b2846bd7345400f5d25ad0650b884fa6f`.

**L10a2a1 — source-reviewed**

UNICORF dispatches univariate autocovariance, normalized autocorrelation and estimated error-bound calculations. The underlying AUTCOV centers using observations strictly between OUTMIN/OUTMAX and divides each lag sum by the total accepted-observation count, not the number of accepted pairs at that lag. Missing/out-of-bound pairs are skipped; zero accepted count or zero lag-zero variance causes unguarded divisions in mean/correlation calculations. Output COV(0:LAG,1:4) holds covariance, correlation and two error-bound arrays. Choose nonconstant finite accepted data and 0<=LAG<N. Review covers wrapper dispatch and mean/autocovariance/correlation calculations; error-bound coverage is not statistically validated.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `0490ac263bf000e7baa3573dd0fe75c5cfd88b2e`.

**L10b2a — source-reviewed**

CRSCORF computes lagged covariance/correlation between channels; the selected sketch uses two time series. Means are formed separately from values strictly within each channel bounds. C(L,I,J) pairs channel I at time t with channel J at t-L, dividing by sqrt(NSUM(I)*NSUM(J)); it is not recomputed with a pairwise-complete denominator per lag. R normalizes by lag-zero channel variances. Output includes both channel orders for nonnegative lags, so cross-lag orientation must be retained when comparing implementations. All-rejected/constant channels and large integer count products need validation because no error status guards their divisions. Review covers the two-channel wrapper and core normalization/lag loops, not every multivariate statistical model.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `0490ac263bf000e7baa3573dd0fe75c5cfd88b2e`.

**K4 — source-reviewed**

The selected real-valued SVD(N,A,TT,TOL,RMAX) overload converts a dense flattened tensor into tensor-train cores by successive right-to-left matricization SVDs, singular-value truncation and propagation of scaled left factors. The optional rank cap can force more truncation than the tolerance request. This is a separated tensor approximation, not proof of a best global TT approximation or a complete review of all matrix/DMRG/complex operations. Positive mode sizes, consistent Fortran-order input length, safe integer dimension/workspace products and compatible BLAS/LAPACK are caller requirements. The DTT type holds pointer-backed cores and has no active finalizer; release with DEALLOC and do not assume intrinsic pointer copying provides independent ownership. Zero-norm input has a special zero-rank/deallocation return.

**D1a4 — source-reviewed**

The real DOT(TT1,TT2) overload contracts compatible TT cores through successive DGEMM and transpose operations instead of expanding both tensors. Its result is a rank-one REAL(8) ARRAY, with length equal to the product of the four outer bond ranks; ordinary closed rank-one boundaries give a one-element array holding the scalar inner product. Matching core ranges, mode sizes, associated core storage and consistent bond dimensions are caller obligations; there is no comprehensive shape validation in the inspected routine. The selected real operation is not a review of conjugation conventions in the complex overload or a claim that arbitrary open-boundary contractions are scalars.

**K4 — source-reviewed**

DMRGG_LIB::DTT_DMRGG adaptively samples a tensor-valued function at selected multi-indices, updates TT cross pivots/cores and increases bond ranks. It uses MPI distribution/communication and optional OpenMP callback evaluation; the callback has the positional convention FUN(M,IND,N,PAR). MAXRANK bounds growth and ACCURACY tests sampled pivot magnitude relative to a reference for three consecutive strikes, not a rigorous global residual bound over every tensor entry. The routine wipes an incoming nonempty TT state to rank-one initialization. Require initialized MPI with number of ranks strictly less than tensor dimension M, positive mode sizes, valid callback parameters, consistent precision and safe indices. Some diagnostics read ME before MPI_COMM_RANK initialization. This review covers the adaptive driver and inspected pivot/termination paths, not all lower-level max-volume/inversion kernels, every process partition or the optional quadrature application.

**L10d — source-reviewed**

The selected legacy external twdtwf90gt routine aligns two multichannel time series by dynamic programming over Euclidean feature distances plus a logistic penalty on cyclic time differences. It takes the minimum cumulative cost from diagonal/horizontal/vertical predecessors, tracks start indices and reports best endpoint candidates. The first matrix column is accumulated separately without the LB exclusion used in later columns. XM is (M,D), YM is (N,D), with time in column 1. Callers must initialize CM first-row boundary costs and output buffers before the legacy call. JB is declared length N although as many as M endpoint groups may be written; this sketch restricts M<=N. Times must share a cycle representation with differences within CL. This is alignment/cost calculation, not automatic classification or an accuracy certificate. The separate callback BIND(C) routine marks CM INTENT(OUT) while reading boundary entries; that interface needs correction and is not the sketch path.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `d740a38151cc25b419683bb33c6234935ff34efc`.

The selected finite-interval quadrature services evaluate the built-in Tweedie Fourier-inversion integrand, using symmetric tabulated Gaussian-Legendre nodes/weights. They do not accept a user callback. GaussAdaptive compares a whole-interval rule with two half-interval rules and refines the interval with largest estimated error, capped at 40 intervals, only for CpSmall and Cp<4/3; other regimes return a single fixed-rule value with OK true. OK is therefore not a general error certificate. The caller/package must initialize allocated Cmu/Cphi/Cy arrays, current distribution state and Integrands_MOD error state. Module globals prevent independent concurrent calls without state isolation. This classification intentionally stops above user-provided-integrand leaves; the complete density/CDF inversion, tail/error propagation and R runtime build were not audited.

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The UCMINF core forms an inverse-Hessian search direction, limits its length, performs a soft line search and updates a packed inverse Hessian by BFGS when a curvature test permits it. This mapping is scoped to supplied first derivatives: the R frontend sets GRAD=0 when GR is provided; FDF dispatches objective/gradient through linked C routines evaluating an R environment. The fork removed the FDF callback argument from the Fortran entry. RHO is an opaque runtime handle, not an ordinary user integer work array. This is local smooth unconstrained optimization, not a standalone Fortran callback solver or a certified trust-region method.

**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

The public CONJUGATE_GRADIENT%SOLVE binding implements unpreconditioned CG for an attached real linear operator, including the sparse stencil operators used by this finite-volume framework. The native recurrence updates residual, search direction and the iterate using inherited matrix actions and scalar products. The operator must be symmetric positive definite in the actual pairing; the code does not verify symmetry/positivity, and its tiny-PAP guard checks magnitude rather than positive curvature. The stopping threshold is TOLERANCE*(1+NORM(RHS)); ACHIEVED reports a residual norm, but return can also follow a tiny denominator or exhausted iteration budget. There is no separate reason/status output. Affine constants from an attached operation must be moved to the RHS consistently. This mapping records sparse symmetric solver usage, not a sparse storage-format API or a guarantee for nonsymmetric/indefinite systems.

**D2a4 — source-reviewed**

The public GMRES%SOLVE binding implements restarted real GMRES for attached general linear actions, including sparse finite-volume stencils. It uses native Arnoldi orthogonalization, Givens rotations, triangular back substitution and correction updates. RESTART is the Krylov dimension, while MAX_ITERATIONS bounds outer restart cycles rather than the total number of matrix actions. On an estimated-tolerance exit the true residual norm is recomputed before returning, but an exhausted final cycle can leave an estimate as ACHIEVED. Zero MAX_ITERATIONS can leave that output undefined. The radius/breakdown branch can still reach division by a zero triangular diagonal; return has no dedicated failure/status code. Require positive tolerances, sensible dimensions, initialized attachment and explicit affine-RHS handling. This is a general sparse/operator solver mapping, not a rank-deficient least-squares solver or automatically preconditioned algorithm.

**I2b1a1a — source-reviewed**

DIFFUSION_STENCIL translates conductivity, tagged Robin/Dirichlet boundary relations and a chosen/default polynomial form into a compiled fitted-balance operator. The supplied POISSON program uses this factory for a unit-square Dirichlet Poisson problem with a manufactured sine solution, volume-scaled RHS, native GMRES and reported L2/max errors across supplied mesh sizes. The rectangular-domain leaf is supported by that concrete workflow; arbitrary domain/BC accuracy is not inferred. The native factory obtains face conductivities/areas, assembles boundary value/weight arrays and delegates to fitted-balance neighborhood fitting. The driver determines the assembled sign from its manufactured solution rather than enforcing a universal Laplacian sign convention, so copying its RHS to a new problem requires care. Mesh files and expected boundary labels are prerequisites. Review follows source assembly/dispatch and the supplied driver, not observed convergence or a checked PDE solution.

The external DDNOR routine evaluates the standard normal cumulative distribution via Cody-style piecewise rational error/complementary-error approximations. It uses symmetry and separate small/intermediate/large transformed-argument branches. The input is clipped internally to [-16,16], and positive-tail probabilities can round to one; this is not a survival-function API preserving arbitrary extreme-tail relative accuracy. No input argument is overwritten and no error/status output is supplied. Accuracy claims in inherited comments were not adopted as verified results. This selected distribution-function mapping does not imply every urca test or response-surface coefficient table was source reviewed.

**L5a2n — source-reviewed**

INNORZ estimates a standard normal quantile using an Abramowitz-Stegun-style initial approximation, a second approximation-based correction, then a CDF/density Newton correction through DDNOR. Use strictly interior probabilities: the input check rejects values outside [0,1] but permits endpoints whose later 1/PR**2 and logarithms are singular. Extreme interior probabilities can still overflow or lose accuracy through complementary-CDF cancellation and density division. Invalid input uses R REALPR/REXIT rather than a recoverable Fortran status. The result is a scalar quantile, not a random draw or normal order-statistic sample. Review covers approximation/correction flow and domain hazards, not validated tail accuracy.

**D9a4 — source-reviewed**

DTLS works on the augmented matrix [A B], optionally reduces it by LINPACK QR, calls DSVDC for its singular vectors, selects/lowers approximation rank according to tolerance and singular-value multiplicity, and transforms/solves the right-singular-vector partition for X. This is total least squares allowing perturbations in both A and B, not ordinary fixed-A residual least squares. D9a4 follows the Netlib vanhuffel index, which lists DTLS under D9a1 and D9a4; this claim uses its other-approximation leaf for the errors-in-variables contract. The driver checks dimensions and reports IERR/IWARN; it overwrites C, rank and tolerances. NUMEPS is fixed at 1e-16. Core QR/SVD and all HOUSH/TR2 kernels are dependencies, not fully audited here. Rank changes and scaling affect interpretation; no TLS fit or backward error was computed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `be5bb35b3a86052df986eadf4a540da5eeec362c`.

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The reusable Fortran SQNM_OPTIMIZER takes externally computed objective values/gradients, retains displacement/gradient histories, diagonalizes history and Hessian subspaces and returns a stabilized quasi-Newton displacement. The caller applies X<-X+STEP and reevaluates; SQNM_STEP does not call a user objective or overwrite X. Initialization configures history length, step scale/floor and subspace threshold; CLOSE_SQNM releases buffers. An internal max-gradient cutoff of 1e-11 returns a zero step, but application convergence/budgets are otherwise caller responsibilities. Degenerate history/eigenvalue divisions need valid inputs; LAPACK failures STOP, with no returned status. Only this fixed-coordinate unconstrained smooth supplied-gradient optimizer is mapped, not variable-cell/atomistic wrappers or a rigorous lower-bound guarantee.

```fortran
use iso_c_binding, only: c_int,c_double
use sqnm, only: sqnm_optimizer
type(sqnm_optimizer) :: opt
real(c_double) :: x(2),gradient(2),step(2),value
integer :: iteration
x=[2.0_c_double,-1.0_c_double]
call opt%initialize_sqnm(2_c_int,5_c_int,0.1_c_double, &
     0.001_c_double,1.0e-4_c_double)
do iteration=1,100
  value=sum(x*x); gradient=2.0_c_double*x
  if (maxval(abs(gradient)) < 1.0e-8_c_double) exit
  call opt%sqnm_step(x,value,gradient,step)
  x=x+step
end do
call opt%close_sqnm()
```

This ordinary path has no scaling or compensated-product correction; separate accurate variants are not covered. PENF defines the actual precision kind, and source preprocessing/dependency configuration must match. No product, floating-point range check, device kernel or author example was run.

**K1a1a3 — source-reviewed**

calculate_residues builds fixed-pole rational basis columns 1/(s-a), adds optional constant/linear terms, stacks real/imaginary sample equations and solves for real coefficients, coupling complex-conjugate poles so residues form conjugate pairs. K1a1a3 records this unconstrained linear least-squares fit in specified nonpolynomial basis functions with poles held fixed. It is not a mapping of the separate iterative pole-relocation optimization. The default morse_penrose_solve explicitly forms A-transpose*A and inverts it; the alternative pads the matrix and dispatches EISPACK SVD. Neither returns solver status to the caller. Adjacent complex conjugate poles are required and invalid pairing STOPs; sampling at poles is unguarded. NEW_A and C_HAT dummy arrays are not assigned by this routine, despite appearing in its signature. Require 2*NF>=number of real unknowns and adequate rank; normal equations worsen conditioning. No fit, conditioning or SVD/back-end accuracy was checked by execution.

**K6a1 — source-reviewed**

calculate_fit_function initializes each response as d+s*h and adds c(i)/(s-a(i)) for every supplied pole/residue. K6a1 records evaluation of an existing rational fit; it does not estimate coefficients, relocate poles, enforce passivity or validate stability. The external routine accepts explicit-size COMPLEX*16 vectors, REAL*8 d/h and no status. Caller must supply finite compatible arrays and avoid s=a denominators; no cancellation/overflow or singular-evaluation guard is present. No response values or checked driver were executed.

Review covers factor/substitution source paths, not a production solver API or validated residual.

**D2b4 — source-reviewed**

The public unpreconditioned CG demonstration forms a sparse grid-discretization system, computes residual/search-direction updates and stops when the absolute residual norm falls below RES or N_ITER is exhausted. It is relevant to real symmetric sparse positive-definite systems, not a general nonsymmetric solver. The wrapper calls Discretize%On_Sparse_Matrix itself, replacing/allocating A/X/B; it then checks and deallocates A/X/B before returning, so these are not returned solution arrays for user consumption. The first P-transpose-A-P division has no initial-zero-residual or breakdown guard, and the beta denominator is floored at 1e-12. No INFO or achieved iteration count is returned; printed diagnostics and a post-solve check are the public result. Review covers this pedagogical CG path, not the incomplete-preconditioner variants or a proof the generated system is always SPD.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `52d5c8ca86481b3af36df74bb2260a098dbb5826`.

[README.md](https://github.com/vtopt/vtdirect95/blob/52d5c8ca86481b3af36df74bb2260a098dbb5826/README.md)

**G2i — source-reviewed**

VTdirect normalizes the finite box, samples its center, selects potentially optimal rectangles by size/value (or the aggressive option), samples displaced centers on longest dimensions and dispatches thirds-based subdivision. The inspected serial driver scales final X back and returns the best sampled value. G2i records deterministic derivative-free global box search, not a finite-budget proof of the global minimum or an audit of parallel/checkpoint modes. OBJ_FUNC returns a value and IFLAG; undefined samples become HUGE rather than a validated feasible solution. R8=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(13), N>=2, strict finite L<U and valid callback values are required. MAX_ITER/MAX_EVL are mutable controls/results; evaluation limits are checked after a batch/iteration and can be exceeded by that batch. Normal statuses are 1..4 stopping rules, not a conventional STATUS=0 success check. Shared global box bookkeeping prevents assuming reentrancy. No DIRECT search, regression or stopping-limit behavior was executed.

```fortran
use REAL_PRECISION, only: r8
```

**J — source-reviewed**

wavelet removes the mean, optionally pads with zeros, FFTs and normalizes the signal, multiplies by scale-dependent daughter wavelets, and inverse-transforms into wave(time,scale). The inspected Morlet branch uses the positive-frequency Gaussian and reports Fourier-equivalent periods and a cone of influence. J records a continuous wavelet service, with no dedicated wavelet child in this taxonomy; significance testing and other mother-wavelet branches are outside the claim. Scratch arrays have fixed length 65535, but only npad<n is checked: require 0<n<=npad<=65535 and positive dt/s0/dj/jtot yourself. mother may be replaced by a default and negative param is overwritten, so pass variables. No status or transform accuracy is returned/established; npad<n prints a diagnostic and leaves outputs unset. The FFTPACK dependency is declared by an unpinned refactor branch. No transform or significance test was run.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use wavepack, only: wavelet, rk
integer, parameter :: n=128, jtot=16, npad=128
integer :: i, mother
real(rk) :: y(n), dt, param, s0, dj, scale(jtot), period(jtot), coi(n)
complex(rk) :: coefficients(n,jtot)
dt=1.0_rk; mother=0; param=6.0_rk; s0=2.0_rk; dj=0.25_rk
do i=1,n
  y(i)=sin(2.0_rk*acos(-1.0_rk)*real(i-1,rk)/16.0_rk)
end do
call wavelet(n, y, dt, mother, param, s0, dj, jtot, npad, &
             coefficients, scale, period, coi)
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build the module, chisqr module and matching FFTPACK dependencies; complex(rk) must match the source DOUBLE COMPLEX ABI. Bound npad at 65535 even though source does not enforce the upper limit. This is an evenly spaced time series; npad=n retains periodic FFT edge effects and the cone-of-influence output helps interpretation, not an accuracy guarantee. Significance levels and statistical assumptions were not reviewed.

**E1 — source-reviewed**

The standard rank-one Jiang-Shu interpolation path combines candidate polynomial stencil values with normalized nonlinear smoothness weights. Inspected S=3 tables provide three candidate stencils on five equispaced point values; alpha uses kappa/(eps+beta)**S and weights divide by SUM(alpha). E1 records univariate interpolation, scoped to interpolator-JS at a cell interface, not a general scattered-grid API, a fixed spline or a whole conservation-law solver. X_TARGET is relative to the center cell in units of grid spacing, not an absolute coordinate. No coordinate array is accepted, so uniform spacing and stencil/ghost data are caller responsibilities. The debug overload leaves SI unassigned and reconstruction overloads on this concrete interpolator are empty; use the standard rank-one path. No formal-order, nonoscillation or interpolation result was verified by execution.

**J2 — source-reviewed**

ATROUSWV forms adjacent smoothed image levels using separable dilated five-tap B-spline convolutions, with coefficients proportional to [1,4,6,4,1] and endpoint replication. The native Fortran control code dispatches the C ATRousstep_02 kernel along rows/columns. With CJ1MODE false it copies the original image and computes both smoothing levels; their difference supplies the associated detail image. The returned CJ1/CJ arrays themselves are smooth levels, not automatically thresholded wavelet coefficients. This concrete convolution component supports J2; it is not a claim of orthogonal/downsampled wavelet normalization or reconstruction correctness. The scratch pencils have fixed bounds -8191:24576, so dimensions, dilation and all padded indices must fit; use positive compatible scale/dimensions. The C bridge expects default Fortran REAL/INTEGER compatible with C float/int and matching symbol naming. Full image-detection/FITS/classification application paths are outside this review.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `92a2d45b0566452666f69277e470b03209e90286`.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

RandomNumberGenerator%random_uniform dispatches to a xorshift64star state update using shifts 12,25,27 and an explicit base-2**16 multiplication modulo 2**64. It then assembles a floating-point fraction from the four words. L6a21 records uniform-output sampling; state must be seeded to a nonzero C_INT64_T bit pattern, since zero is absorbing. Scalar and rank-one through rank-three wrappers share this state. Conversion to C_DOUBLE can round a high unsigned fraction to 1, despite the intended [0,1) range; callers must not assume a strict upper bound. The OpenMP critical region serializes scalar draws but does not establish independent parallel streams. No sequence, endpoint or reference comparison was run.

**L6a14 — source-reviewed**

The public random_normal generic uses the Box-Muller transform of two uniform draws, returning one sine component and saving the cosine component. This supports normal random-variate generation L6a14. A SAVE cache/has_cache belongs to the procedure, not each RandomNumberGenerator; interleaving two objects can return a cached value derived from the other object, and reseeding an object does not clear it. OpenMP marks the cache threadprivate, not per object. LOG(u(1)) is unguarded for a zero uniform output. This source mapping records the implemented transform and lifecycle limits, not independent streams or a verified normal law. No sample was run.

**L6a21 — source-reviewed**

For typ_xoshiro256star2 the integer overload computes the star-star scrambler and advances the four-word recurrence once. The inherited real overload calls that integer overload, advances again, and converts its buffered output to an IEEE binary64 52-bit grid in [0,1). Thus real draws consume two recurrence steps whereas integer draws consume one; they are not interchangeable streams. set_state copies only MIN(source,destination) entries without rejecting wrong lengths or all-zero states; provide exactly four nonzero-in-total words. Integer scrambler products assume wrapping signed arithmetic. L6a21 records this uniform-output path, not reference equivalence, quality, jump-ahead or all nine variants. No sequence was run.

**D — source-reviewed**

The external routine named ZOLOPD in zolopd.f90 actually implements QR-based dynamically weighted Halley polar iteration, with a Cholesky/positive solve branch once the iterate is sufficiently conditioned. It is distinct from PZOLOPD1, which dispatches Zolotarev coefficients and communicator-split rational work. This mapping records matrix polar decomposition under broad linear algebra D, not QR as an end product or a singular-value decomposition inferred from the repository name. Although the header permits M>=N, important operations use N-by-N dimensions, so the sketch is deliberately square. POLAR=T additionally forms the symmetrized Q-transpose*A factor in WORK2. Descriptor layouts, local leading dimensions, two workspace buffers and BLACS/MPI initialization are prerequisites. Error state is overwritten across dependency calls and the main loop has no visible hard iteration cap. Source review is not a polar residual or distributed convergence check.

**D4a1 — source-reviewed**

ZOLOEIG computes a partial real symmetric eigendecomposition given a polar factor of A-sigma*I. PQDWHSUBIT subtracts I and halves Q, estimates the projector rank from its squared Frobenius norm, forms a randomized invariant subspace and compressed matrix, then ZOLOEIG calls PDSYEVD and back-transforms selected vectors. The executable projector is (Q-I)/2 despite a nearby comment saying (Q+I)/2, so do not infer a selected side from the comment alone. The computed RK is local and printed rather than returned by ZOLOEIG; callers cannot safely infer the number of valid returned eigenpairs from INFO alone. Q/AS/work buffers are overwritten. Subspace iteration has a two-step limit, and downstream INFO overwrites require review. This is prototype subset-symmetric functionality, not full-spectrum, nonsymmetric or generalized eigensolving.
